description: Linear A lexicon: one entry per word, logogram or sign group, with its reading, meaning, root, cognates, confidence tier and attestations. Readings are di Mino's unless the source field names another scholar.

confidence_levels.CONFIRMED: Ideographic + phonetic + mathematical convergence (e.g., KU-NI-SU next to WHEAT ideogram)
confidence_levels.PROBABLE: Gordon reading with external attestation or strong structural evidence
confidence_levels.CANDIDATE: A close root match or strong contextual support, not yet independently confirmed
confidence_levels.SPECULATIVE: Analogical reconstruction or weak match, included for completeness

entries.meaning: blood (with case ending -i)
entries.note: ZA 21a is a tablet: *118-MI 2 closes a quantity list (PI-MU 40, TE 2, PA 5, TA-MA-PI 3). ṭa-mi ~ Heb. דָּם dam 'blood' (HALOT 224), Ug. dm (DULAT 270), with ṭ for plain d. Rival: √ṭ-m-m with the emphatic (Harding tmm 'a kind of grass?'; Ar. ṭamma 'overflow'). A counted entry favours a commodity. One attestation, two signs. || Case unassigned: nothing here selects it (Fischer 2002, §140).

entries.meaning: commodity ideogram; probably a Pistacia/terebinth product (resin, mastic, or nuts)
entries.note: Commodity status is secure; the exact identification remains PROBABLE. It occurs in 29 contexts on 26 documents. Three forms occur on damaged HT123+124b: *188-*308 (11), *188-DU (10), and *188 (1). Their relation cannot be recovered by simply summing the preserved quantities. *308 also modifies OLIV and may denote a processed or oil product. *188 co-occurs with VIN on HT98b, appears on Khania roundels, and occurs in ritual context on PSIZa1. The proposed Pistacia identification compares Hebrew boṭnā (Gen 43:11), Akkadian buṭnu, and Arabic buṭm. PA₃-*188 is compatible with a /b/-initial reading only if PA₃ is a phonetic complement; it cannot independently prove that value. The proposed CH 009 vessel/container ancestry (Ferrara et al. 2022, Pasiphae XVI) likewise establishes neither the commodity nor its name.

entries.meaning: processed Pistacia/terebinth product, perhaps oil
entries.note: Compounds proposed commodity *188 with modifier *308, which also occurs with OLIV on HT123+124a and may denote an oil or processed product. The exact lexical reading and process are not independently established. HT123+124b is damaged, and its preserved quantities do not transparently reconstruct the closing totals.

entries.meaning: wheat; rivals ḫaṭṭu 'sceptre', ḥaṯ 'unleavened bread'
entries.note: KH 88 QA-NU-MA · *21F-*118 · NI 10, before figs; ZA 5a heads a ration list, *21F-*118 · VIN-SU over KI-NI-MA 7 and O-TA-NI-ZA-SE 6; ZA 14 an entry of 1. Ug. ḥṭt 'wheat' (DULAT 372), Heb. ḥiṭṭâ (HALOT 306), the final -t unwritten; *21F writes ḥ. Rivals: ḫṭ 'sceptre, rod' (DULAT 410; Akk. ḫaṭṭu), and ḥṯ 'unleavened bread' (DULAT 373) with *118 = ṯa.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Addu lives'

cognates.Amorite: ḪAJJ-A + DN names (Gelb AS 21 nos. 1651–1653); names in -Addu written -A-DU: LI-MA-A-DU (no. 4368), NI-MA-A-DU (no. 5057)

entries.note: HT 84: *21F-JA-DU heads the tablet over NU-TI · VIR+[?]. ḥayya + Addu, 'Addu lives', cf. Amorite ḪAJJ-A + DN names (Gelb AS 21 nos. 1651–1653) and A-DU, A-DU-NI-TA-NA. Weak point: *21F as an optional H-sign; no Ḫayya-Addu is attested. Rival: a heading or place over the men. One attestation.

entries.meaning: bridegroom, son-in-law (or: the bridegroom)
entries.note: Most frequent *21F form (3×). √ḫ-t-n 'bridegroom, son-in-law' is pan-Semitic: Akkadian ḫatānu (CAD Ḫ 149–151), Ugaritic ḫtn (DUL 414), Hebrew ḥātān (HALOT 364–365), and Arabic ḫatan (Lane 697). Syllabic controls include Ugaritic {LU₂}ha-ta-nu and Neo-Assyrian ha-tu₂-nu /hatunu/ (WVDOG 152, P514187.11.1); the latter closely parallels the Linear A spelling, though it is much later. Read ha-tu-ne as /ḫatun-/ with final E as a dead vowel. All three Linear A attestations occur as administrative rubrics or personnel categories. Near-anchor for *21F=/ha/, not independent proof of the sign value.

entries.meaning: pastureland, pastoral product (commodity logogram: nawum in administrative register, nawā in ritual/general)

cognates.Akkadian: nawûm 'steppe, uncultivated pastureland' (CAD N/1, 249–51)—administrative land-use category in OB economic texts
cognates.Amorite: nawûm 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)' (Huffmon, APNM 237); nawijum 'nomadic encampment' (Gelb, AS 21)
cognates.Hebrew: nāweh 'habitation, pasture-land' (KB); cultic sense 'shrine, temple' at Exod 15:13 (ʾel nəwēh qodšeḵā 'to Thy holy shrine')

entries.note: 238 standalone occurrences (82% of all *301 uses), concentrated at Haghia Triada on nodules and tablets. Appears in the same commodity-label position as GRA (dagān), OLE (šamnu), VIN (wayn), CYP (copper). *301 is the pastoral commodity sign—the missing category in the Aegean Bronze Age commodity system. Two registers: (1) ADMINISTRATIVE: nawum (with archaic mimation), the Akkadian-parallel land-use category marking goods from uncultivated pastureland—livestock, wool, dairy, as opposed to cultivated cereals (GRA) and orchard products (OLE, OLIV, VIN). The 232 standalone nodules at HT use this sense. (2) RITUAL: nawā 'dwelling, abode'—the sacred-dwelling sense, cognate with Greek ναός 'temple.' Attested in the compound *301-WA = nawā at Iouktas peak sanctuary. The dual economic/sacred semantics is intrinsic to the root: pastureland and divine dwelling are the same word because pastoral economy and temple economy are the same institution. Syllabic value /na/ is acrophonic (first syllable of nawā(n)), paralleling cuneiform acrophony (É = bītu 'house' → syllabic /bi/). This dual function explains why the scribe uses *301 rather than plain NA in the formula verb A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA: the sign carries both phonetic /na/ and semantic resonance with the √NWY root of the verb itself.

entries.meaning: light, radiance (personal name or epithet)
entries.note: HT115a accounting tablet with GRA+BOSm. √NWR 'to shine, give light' is pan-Semitic (Hebrew נוּר nūr, Arabic nūr, Ugaritic nrt 'lamp'). As a personal name element 'Light' is extremely common across Semitic onomastics. The r alternative (r-u-ra) produces awkward reduplication. || Huehnergard: Ug nwr /nāra/ ~ /yanūr-/ "G: to be/become bright, shine"; I-n / hollow-looking w root. G suffix nāra, prefix yanūr-. BH cognate: nēr "lamp" (Huehnergard 2012, p. 50 (line ref.); cf. BH [9]) In erasure on HT 115a.2 (GORILA I, 188–91).

alternative_readings.note: servant, retainer (root n-ʿ-r): Heb. נַעַר naʿar 'lad, servant, retainer'. Suits a tablet listing people and grain just as well.

entries.meaning: oil/fat-register commodity; possibly fat, lard, or tallow
entries.note: Non-phonetic commodity ideogram: 42 occurrences on 38 tablets; 25 stand alone, 24 directly before quantities, regularly among GRA, OLE, OLIV, and related commodities. The tentative comparison is Central Semitic *pidr- 'fat' (Hebrew peder, Judaic Aramaic pidrā, Arabic fidra), consistent with but not proven by the oil/fat register. *304+PA may add a phonetic complement or commodity qualifier.

entries.meaning: administrative heading or transaction marker; exact function unknown
entries.note: All three attestations are on LM IB Haghia Triada tablets, where *326 is isolated by dividers at or near the opening of an allocation list. This distribution supports an administrative or transactional function, but neither a phonetic value nor a specific operation can yet be assigned.

entries.meaning: *304 oil/fat-register commodity with PA adjunct; exact commodity and function of PA uncertain
entries.note: The *304 commodity logogram carries a PA adjunct in seven administrative attestations. PA may be a phonetic complement or a commodity qualifier, paralleling other logogram-plus-sign compounds, but it does not independently establish the proposed reading *pidr- 'fat, tallow.' The commodity classification is secure; the lexical identification and the function of PA remain CANDIDATE.

entries.meaning: personnel-category logogram; exact class unknown
entries.note: Dual-function sign: a logogram in standalone quantified contexts and a possible syllabogram in embedded groups. Its logographic personnel function is secure from HT89, where *305 23 belongs to the exact headcount 23+22+24+13+5=KU-RO 87, and HT100, where it is a subcategory within a personnel total. Uchitel 2006, 75 independently proposes an age group; Montecchi 2008, 315 a group of persons, never with fractions. The former ḎABBĀḤŪ 'sacrificers' expansion is retained only as a superseded hypothesis: it derived the logographic meaning from the proposed syllabic /ḏa/ value and then used that meaning to support the value. No phonetic complement on HT89 establishes √ḏ-b-ḥ. The syllabic /ḏa/ or /da/ question remains separate and CANDIDATE.
entries.source: Corpus distribution; Montecchi 2008, 315; Uchitel 2006, 'Listing by Age and Occupation in Minoan Linear A,' Kadmos 45: 73–81

entries.meaning: seed-grain; rival a personal name
entries.note: HT 10a .3–4 *305-RU 2½, whole and undotted at the end of .3, the side written over an erasure (GORILA I 21), in a KU-NI-SU (emmer) list. Ug. d/ḏrʕ 'seed-grain' (DULAT 277–278), Heb. zeraʿ, OSArb. ḏrʾ (HALOT 282), the ʿ unwritten. Rivals: dr 'association' (DULAT 277), a personal name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: thus, likewise (ditto heading); rivals kaṯ 'flask, jar', a personal name

cognates.Hebrew: zeh 'this', with Ug. d and Arb. ḏā (HALOT 264)

entries.note: HT 9b .2 KA-*305 ·, unnumbered, below the ruling, over a roster that repeats the names of HT 9a in whole units (KU-RO 24); *305 drawn whole at the edge of worn surface, undotted (GORILA I 19). k 'like, as' (DULAT 415) with the demonstrative ḏā 'this' (Heb. zeh, Ug. d, Arb. ḏā; HALOT 264), as Arb. kaḏā 'like this, thus' (Lane 948): a ditto heading over the repeated roster. The ḏ- demonstrative is a West Semitic innovation. Rivals: kaṯ 'flask, bottle, jar' (DULAT 466) with *305 = ṯa; KA with the logogram *305; a personal name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: gift, offering (votive label)
entries.note: Not √ʿ-t-y 'to come': 'come' is aleph-initial, PS *ʾtw (Heb. ʾātā, Aram. ʾătā, Arab. ʾatā, Ug. ʾtw), so it does not corroborate *306=ʿA. Sole word on one inked object from Arkhanes (ARKH Zc 8; FO Zc 1 is the same object): a votive label. TA covers ṭ; III-weak noun *ʿaṭāy- with the glide written JE. Root attested in Arabic only (semitic_roots 857): SPECULATIVE.

entries.meaning: the ancient, the noble; or 'became fertile' (t-stem heading)
entries.note: Uses resolved *306=/ʿa/. HT4: heads a short allocation list (DU-RI-TE 2, PA-RE, TA-PI-SI-DI 1). NWS √ʿ-t-q 'to be old, noble' (Hebrew ʿātīq, Arabic ʿatīq); the +are ending may be a nominal suffix. Rival reading covers the full sign sequence with no leftover suffix: Sabaic ʿtkr 'become fertile (of land)' (Beeston 1982 p. 14, Ry 522/2)—a t-infix stem of √ʿ-k-r, so ʿa-ti-ka-(a)-re = ʿ-t-k-r exactly. A 'yielded/became fertile' heading over an allocation list is contextually viable; the ʿ-t-q reading leaves -RE unexplained but has the broader NWS pedigree.

entries.meaning: pressed oil, oil derivative—commodity modifier indicating oil extraction from base commodity
entries.note: Oil derivative modifier. HT123+124a places *308 after OLIV; the three securely evaluable pairs give a stable 26.6–28.3% ratio, while the third fraction is damaged. Always in oil/liquid commodity neighborhoods (OLE+X, CYP, VIN). Three-site attestation (HT, KH, ARKH). Possible reading šamnu 'oil' (Akk. šamnu, Heb. šemen), but the lexical identification is less secure than the commodity function, and OLE also carries šamnu.

entries.meaning: flax/linen—dual-use crop: fiber for textiles (TELA+*312), linseed for food/oil (standalone with small quantities)
entries.note: Logogram. TELA+*312 (HT38) ties it to cloth, and KI-TA-NA 'linen' is spelled out on PEZb3. Standalone with 1–2 units at four sites (HT49a, HT123+124b, KH8, ARKH3a). Inside a word it writes KI, the first syllable of kitnu, as *307 writes DU in *307-PU₂-RE: *312-TE-TE = kitītu (HT26a). *312-TA (HT10b.2, 6½) is the garment with feminine -t, as in Heb. kuttōnet. ZA6b *312-TA₂ GRA+PA 40 is an entry receiving grain, set out like I-KU-JU-TI-*28B GRA+PA 50¼ above it, not a grain heading. MU-*312 (HT78) stands alone on a fragment.

alternative_readings.note: measure, portion, allotment (root m-n-y); SPECULATIVE. Evidence: fractional counts (*312-TA 6½, *312 1¾) and entries beside several commodities.

entries.meaning: fine cloth (Akk. kitītu "fine, lit. linen-like, wool")

cognates.Akkadian: kitītu A "fine (lit. linen-like) wool", Mari (CAD K 466); kitû "flax, linen" (CAD K 473)

entries.note: HT26a.1: unquantified after the vessel heading *406VAS+KE, before TA-TI 21 and MI-KI-SE-NA 15. *312 writes KI, the first syllable of the linen word (TELA+*312, HT38, KI-TA-NA, PEZb3), as *307 writes DU in *307-PU₂-RE, and TE-TE writes the rest, E for I as in U-TA-I-SE ~ U-TA-I-SI. Akk. kitītu at Mari: 1 TÚG ki-ti-tum (ARM 7 90:2), a kitītu garment for a woman (ARM 9 129:1f.), and Malku VI 85 ki-ti-tum = lubuštu "garment" (CAD K 466). TE-TE does not write a geminate, since the doubling in kuttōnet is secondary (HALOT 505).

alternative_readings.note: hammered, crushed (root k-t-t); confidence SPECULATIVE (secondary). Evidence: Ugaritic ktt is attested of hammered/broken copper, but HT26a lacks the copper and weight context found in those texts.

entries.meaning: seal, signet; or 'he sealed' (3ms perfective); rival buṭma 'pistachio'
entries.note: Contingent on *314 = ḤA. Phaistos roundel (MMII)—sole word on the roundel. √ḥ-t-m 'to seal, stamp': Hebrew ḥōtām (חותם) 'seal, signet ring' (HALOT 300), Arabic ḫatama 'he sealed' (Lane 702); Akkadian ḫatāmu means only 'to muzzle, block' (CAD Ḫ 152). Either the noun 'seal' (labeling the administrative sealing device itself) or the 3ms perfective verb 'he sealed' (performative inscription). A word meaning 'seal' inscribed on a seal—contextually perfect. Pan-Semitic root attested from Old Akkadian through Modern Hebrew; Egyptian ḫtm 'seal, contract' extends the family Afroasiatic-wide. Weaker Egyptian rival ḥtm 'provide, supply' would suit a roundel-as-receipt, but the Semitic root carries the exact pharyngeal ḥ that *314 encodes. || TA is dotted (GORILA II 94). Rival with *314 = bu, a PU₂ variant: bṭm 'pistachio' (DULAT 249), Arb. buṭm 'fruit of the terebinth' (Lane 219), a roundel commodity, cf. *188 BUṬNU.

entries.meaning: bean or legume; food commodity in ration allocations
entries.note: Commodity ideogram *316 (6 att., Khania + Phaistos). KI complement on nodules KHWa1001/1002 gives initial syllable /ki/. Akk kiššanu 'bean' (CAD K 454). On KH91, positioned between VIN (wine) and NI (figs) in a rations list alongside GRA and *401+RU/RO—food commodity context. On PH1a, allocated to named individuals (DI-RA-DI-NA, JA) with CYP—three independent contexts across two sites and three document types. Akkadian-only attestation; no Hebrew or Ugaritic reflexes confirmed.

entries.meaning: unresolved logogram; A542 on HT89 is a personnel-class composite

cognates.Akkadian: leqû, laqû "to take, receive" (CAD L 138); liqtu "collection, gleaning"

entries.note: The previous LUQḤU 'receipts/offerings' reading depended on treating JU and QE in HT89 JU+*317+QE as phonetic complements. SigLA analyzes that written unit as the single composite logogram A542, and Uchitel's personnel-list analysis places its count of 22 among four other human categories. HT89 therefore cannot establish an l-...-q frame and is removed from the isolated *317 attestation list. The remaining *317, *323-*317, and *317-QE-*353 occurrences warrant separate study; √l-q-ḥ survives only as a rejected historical proposal, not a reading.

entries.meaning: personnel-category composite A542; exact class unknown
entries.note: GORILA decomposes the unit as JU+*317+QE; SigLA catalogs it as the single composite sign A542. On HT89 it labels 22 persons within the exact total 23+22+24+13+5=87. Its components are not independently shown to be phonetic here. The former LUQḤU 'receipts/offerings' reading is withdrawn for this composite.

entries.meaning: personnel-class logogram, counted beside VIR (men); class unknown
entries.note: HT 97a .1–2 *327 33 after VIR+KA 82 under KA-RU · *307+*307 (foot broken, no KU-RO). HT 119 .1 *327 34 beside VIR 68; the entries sum to 159 with *327 against KU-RO 160, so it counts persons (Montecchi 2008, 317: summed with VIR/MUL). Cf. *327-JU 8 (HT 119 .4–5), 'forse un gruppo sillabico' (Montecchi 2008, 318). A closed rectangle, left upright projecting, crossing interior strokes (GORILA I 159, 203); what it depicts is not determinable. No Linear B counterpart (Montecchi 2024, 172). No sound value.
entries.source: HT97a; HT119; GORILA I 159, 203; Montecchi 2008, 317–18; Montecchi 2024, 172

entries.meaning: aromatic preparation, compounded ointment—commodity ideogram for perfumed/refined oil products
entries.note: Commodity ideogram with two phonetic complements: +RU (×7, all Khania) and +RO (×3, KH31/KH91/MI2), plus compound +*304 (×2, HT33/KH12). PS S15 √r-q-ḥ "to mix aromatics, compound ointment": Akk. ruqqû "perfumed oil" (CAD R 418), rāqiḫu "ointment-mixer"; Heb. rōqēaḥ "perfumer, apothecary" (BDB 955), riqqūḥīm "spices, perfumes" (Song 8:2); Ug. rqḥ "perfumer" (DUL 738), mrqḥt "mixed spices"; Phoen. rqḥ "perfumer" (DNWSI 1082). +RU = ru- initial → ruqqû "perfumed/refined oil"; +RO = rō- initial → rōqēaḥ "compounded ointment". Both subtypes appear on KH91 proving distinct products. +*304(pidru) compound = fat-based aromatic preparation. Co-occurrence profile: CYP (cyperus), OLE (olive oil), *308 (šamnu), *304 (pidru)—exclusively aromatic/oil register. Fractional quantities (¹⁄₅, ¹⁄₁₆) = concentrated aromatic. 13/15 attestations at Khania, paralleling Pylos as Mycenaean perfume center (PY Un 267).

entries.meaning: cup, drinking vessel—commodity ideogram for a specific vessel type, with KE phonetic complement indicating initial syllable of Semitic *kaʾs-
entries.note: Vessel ideogram (*406VAS) with phonetic complement KE, functioning as tablet header on both sides of HT26 (Haghia Triada, Villa Magazine, LMIB). The VAS sign is pictographic—a vessel drawing—probably a compound or ligature component, not a phonetic sign. The +KE complement narrows the generic vessel ideogram to a specific type, paralleling Linear B vessel ideogram + phonetic complement conventions. PS #297 *kaʾs- "vessel for beer, bowl" (Akk. kāsu, Heb. kōs, Arab. kaʾs): the medial aleph triggers vowel fronting in NWS, yielding *kēs → KE as initial syllable complement. KA-SI (skeleton k-s) attested on HTWa1027 (Haghia Triada nodule)—same site, same consonantal skeleton, possibly the same word spelled syllabically on a different document type. HT93a has the bare form *406-VS (without KE complement) alongside DA-RI-DA with quantity 2, confirming the sign functions as a vessel-class commodity marker across multiple tablets. HT26b opens with *406VAS+KE followed by VIR+[?] 9 and named allocations (RO-NI 3, KA-U-ZU-NI 4, KI+MU 12)—a personnel/commodity distribution ledger organized by vessel type.

entries.meaning: large open bowl or basin for liquids; wine bowl
entries.note: Commodity ideogram. *412+E (×3, Malia MA10) + TI+*412VAS (×1, MA10b) + *412-VS-VIN (×1, Phaistos PH9b). VIN at PH9b confirms wine-vessel function. Distinct from *406VAS = kās 'cup'—ʔaggān is larger basin type || ETYMOLOGY: PS *ʔigān- 'cup, bowl' (PS #1358): Akk. agannu 'basin', Heb. ʔaggān (Exod 24:6, Song 7:3, Isa 22:24), Arab. ʔiggānat-. Arabic preserves /i/-class vowel; NWS /i/→/ē/ lowering yields /ʔēgān/; aleph drops → complement E = /ʔē-/ || TI+*412VAS = subtype (possibly ṭīn- 'clay bowl')

entries.meaning: transaction/account marker; possible account or register logogram
entries.note: Administrative logogram, identified by SigLA as a transaction sign on HT118. Ten occurrences across Haghia Triada, Khania, and Zakros; nine stand alone, several head quantified entries, and two occur on sealed Khania roundels. SI-*516 may be an /s/-onset phonetic complement, permitting comparison with Akkadian šipru 'work, message, record', Hebrew sēfer/sōfēr, and Ugaritic spr. The value remains CANDIDATE because no full phonetic spelling is attested.

entries.meaning: Dikte; opening of a damaged name or title

cognates.Ugaritic: dqt 'female goat, young she-goat' (DUL 280); theonym Diqatu attested in offering lists (KTU 1.148:3)
cognates.Hebrew: Not directly attested as theonym; cf. se'îrāh (שְׂעִירָה) 'she-goat' and se'îrîm (שְׂעִירִים) 'goat-demons' (Lev 17:7, 2 Chr 11:15)
cognates.Akkadian: diqāru 'cooking pot' (unrelated); goat-deity pattern parallels Amurrite theophoric names
cognates.Arabic: No direct reflex; goat-deity pattern preserved in Yazidi Melek Tawus traditions

entries.note: PKZa12 preserves A-DI-KI-TE-[ without a following divider, so it may open a longer Diktaian name or title; neither an independent word boundary nor a vocative use is established there. Palaikastro lies beneath the Dictaean mountains. Compare complete A-DI-KI-TE-TE on PKZa11 and JA-DI-KI-TU elsewhere. || COGNATES: those of JA-DI-KI-TU, the same name (Diktu/Dikte).

entries.meaning: Addu/Haddu; alternatively an administrative work assignment or stint

cognates.Ugaritic: hd(d) 'Haddu (Hadad), storm god, byname of Baal'
cognates.Akkadian: Adad (OB Addu) 'storm god'; adû 'a (day's) work, stint'
cognates.Amorite: Haddu/Addu as a divine name and theophoric element (Huffmon; Howard)
cognates.Hebrew: Hădad (הֲדַד) 'Hadad' in names: Ben-Hadad, Hadadezer 'Hadad is help'

entries.note: A-DU occurs in 8 documents at two sites, regularly in initial or administrative-heading position. This establishes its heading or entity function but not its semantic identity, and the spelling may be homographic across contexts. Gordon's Addu/Haddu remains viable: the spelling fits Old Babylonian Amorite/Akkadian Addu without initial h, and second-millennium syllabic forms such as eh-li-a-du independently preserve the divine element (Howard 2023). Alternatively, Akkadian adû 'a (day's) work, stint' is independently attested and fits allocation and roster contexts (ORACC ARM/EP). HT92 places A-DU between TE and commodities, slightly favoring a named recipient such as Addu, but the administrative distribution cannot confirm that interpretation.
entries.source: Corpus distribution; Gordon 1966; ORACC ARM/EP; Huffmon 1965; Howard 2023

entries.meaning: Addu's sanctuary (Storm God + doubled sanctuary sign)
entries.note: HT85a.1: A-DU · *307+*307 · VIR+[?] ·, heading a personnel register with 66 workers. The middle sign is *307 written twice, joined by a top bar (A 638; GORILA I 131); Montecchi 2008, 316 n. 30 also reads A 638 as doubled *307. KA-RU · *307+*307 · VIR+KA heads HT97a. || Word-field notation: 'A-DU *307+*307' records a two-element phrase (theonym A-DU + the doubled *307) as attested on HT85a; not split into separate entries to avoid breaking the attested-phrase citation.

entries.meaning: Addu has sheltered (compound theophoric PN)

cognates.Amorite: KMN verbal root in names: Ka-mi-nu-um (Gelb 1980, no. 3970), Ia-ak-me-ni Yakmin- (no. 2909)
cognates.Hebrew: כמן hiphil 'to hide' (Mishnaic; HALOT 481); cf. צְפַנְיָה Ṣəpanyāh 'Yahweh has hidden' (HALOT 1049)
cognates.Aramaic: kmn 'to hide oneself, lie in wait'; Christian Palestinian kymn 'ambush' (HALOT 481)

entries.note: ZA 10a: a roster name counted 1, beside A-KU-MI-NA from the same verb. A-DU (Addu) + √k-m-n 'hide, shelter', built like A-DU-NI-TA-NA 'Addu has given'. KU for ka as in Linear B ku-mi-no = kamūn-. Not 'Addu's cumin': cumin is always measured (MY Ge 605 ku-mi-no Z 2), and KU-MI-NA 'cumin' is a homograph. Weak point: KU for ka. Rival: A-DU + KU-MI-NA 'cumin', which a roster count of 1 argues against.

entries.meaning: given by Addu (compound theophoric PN)

cognates.Akkadian: nadānu N innadin 'was given'; active names Adad-iddinam, Bēl-ittannu
cognates.Amorite: yantin-DN 'DN gave' (active prefix conjugation; Gelb AS 21)

entries.note: Arkhanes tablet. Compound theophoric: A-DU (Hadad/Addu storm god, the dominant theophoric in the corpus) + NI-TA-NA (nittāna, N-stem perfect of √n-t-n 'to give', < *nintan 'was given'). Parallels: Amarna EA Addu-dāni, OB Addu-nārī. Both root elements independently attested in corpus: A-DU heads HT88 register; √n-t-n underlies NA-TU-*301-NE (SKOZc1). Single attestation. Both constituent elements independently attested: A-DU (CANDIDATE, 8 documents at two sites) and √n-t-n (via NA-TU-*301-NE at SKOZc1, PROBABLE). ZA10a demonstrates A-DU as detachable theophoric prefix (A-DU-KU-MI-NA ~ A-KU-MI-NA). Active parallels: Akkadian Adad-iddinam, Iddin-Dagan; West Semitic Adda-natan (SAA 14 014), whose G perfect natan the NI- spelling does not fit. One attestation. Member of the Arkhanes ration-formula family (named recipient + GRA/*131B-must + quantity; ARKH2, ARKH5 ↔ ARKH3a/b)—the recipient slot on ARKH5. NB: the recurring element across ARKH2+ARKH5 is *131B, not this name; attestation remains ARKH5 only.

entries.meaning: possible divine name or liturgical predicate: Haya/Aya, or "(the) Living One; Life"
entries.cognates: PS *ḥayy- "to live, be alive; life" (#2760). Hebrew חַי ḥay "alive", חַיִּים ḥayyīm "life"; Ugaritic ḥyw "to live"; Mari West Semitic ḥaya "lives" is written both ha-ia- and a-ia-; Late Old Babylonian Alalakh likewise alternates ha-ia- and a-ia- in the same name (Weeden 2009, 96–100). The Mesopotamian god Haya is written dḫa-ià; Aya is an independently attested goddess.
entries.note: A-JA is complete at PE Zc 4 and SY Za 2; MA 4b reads A-[?]-[?]-[?]-JA and is not an attestation. The closest spelling control is Old Babylonian Mari, where West Semitic ḥaya "lives" appears as both ha-ia- and a-ia-; Weeden suggests that a-ia- may attempt to reproduce an unrepresented /ḥ/. At Alalakh VII, a-ia-/ha-ia- alternate in the same name (Weeden 2009, 96–100). This makes A-JA compatible with /ḥaya/ or /ḥayyā/ without treating pharyngeal /ḥ/ as ordinary /h/. Linear B omission of Greek /h/ is an independent Aegean orthographic control only. The divine name Haya is attested as dḫa-ià from Early Dynastic Fara onward and in the Old Babylonian Hymn to Haia for Rim-Sin, whose line 59 calls him the god who loves the petition "Give me life!" (ORACC AMGG, "Haya"; ETCSL 2.6.9.2.59). Keep three analyses separate: Haya; Semitic /ḥaya/ or /ḥayyā/ "(the) Living One/Life"; and the independently attested goddess Aya. Their historical relationship is disputed. Davis's "much" remains a structural rival.

entries.meaning: island
entries.note: THEZb7 (Thera, clay vessel): sole word on vessel—inscribed on an island, possibly labeling origin or dedication. Dialectal variant of I-JA /ʾiya/ (Knossos) and I-JA-TE /ʾiyyate/ (Phaistos): A-JE spelling at Thera vs I-JA at Eastern Cretan sites may reflect regional vowel variation, parallel to the Phaistos-vs-Eastern Crete dialectal patterns observed in the libation formulae.

entries.meaning: cup, bowl
entries.note: Hebrew/Aramaic ʾaggān 'bowl'. Gordon §119: 'opens with the word a-ka-nu = Hebrew and Aramaic ʾaggan bowl, which happens to be applied specifically to a magic bowl in an Aramaic incantation.' Self-referential vessel label: the bowl names itself. II,2 = KNZc7 (Brice/GORILA concordance). GORILA writes A-KA-NU-ZA-TI as one sign group, but Gordon segments A-KA-NU as a standalone noun. GORILA IV, 125 begins the diplomatic transcription directly with complete A-KA-NU-ZA-TI and marks no opening lacuna; no lost word should be supplied before it. The following ZA-TI may be /zāt/ 'this' (historically perhaps /zāʾt/), giving ʾagānu zāt 'this bowl.' Hebrew zō(ʾ)t supplies the closest lexical parallel. Phoenician ʾGN is feminine, and FK D 35 has the postposed demonstrative construction hʾgn hz, 'this bowl' (Krahmalkov 2000, 31), so feminine agreement is independently plausible. The alternative single-word √k-n-s verbal parse is weak because that root is consistently written KA-NA-SI elsewhere. The segmentation remains analytical: ZA-TI is a hapax, its first sign is disputed ZA/ZE, and final TI = /t/ with a nonphonemic support vowel is not an established Linear B rule.

entries.meaning: field or estate heading; possible Ugaritic Ugaru theonym

cognates.Ugaritic: ugr 'field, soil' (DULAT); DN Ugaru, paired with Gapnu as gpn-w-ugr 'Vine and Field'

entries.note: Linear A writes A-KA-RU, hence Agaru; Ugaritic supplies Ugaru (ugr II), 'Field,' paired with Gapnu ('Vine') as one of Baal's two messenger-deities (DULAT 27; KTU 1.3; 1.5). A-KA-RU heads accounts at HT2 and HT86a/b as a field or estate heading; on HT86a its section stands beside one headed A-DU (Addu), so a divine or cult-institutional sense remains possible. Initial a/u remains unexplained. Akkadian ugāru is usually derived from Sumerian A.GÀR, so the term may be a Wanderwort rather than an inherited ʾ-g-r root.

entries.meaning: I shelter (verbal PN)

cognates.Amorite: Ia-ak-me-ni Yakmin- (Gelb 1980, no. 2909), prefix form of KMN
cognates.Aramaic: kmn 'to hide oneself, lie in wait' (HALOT 481)

entries.note: ZA 10a: a roster name counted 1, beside A-DU-KU-MI-NA from the same verb. First-person ʾa- + √k-m-n 'hide, shelter', the counterpart of Amorite Yakmin-. Not 'he of cumin': cumin is always measured (MY Ge 605 ku-mi-no Z 2). Weak point: KU for ka. Rival: A- + KU-MI-NA 'cumin'.

entries.meaning: people, kinfolk—social/kinship term
entries.cognates: Hebrew ʿam "people, nation" (HALOT 837), Ugaritic ʿm "people, kinsmen" (DUL 169), Akkadian ummānu "people, army" (CAD U/W 106), Phoenician ʿm "people" (Tomback 255)
entries.note: PS #44/#99 *ʕamm- "relative, uncle, ancestor" + PS #S10 *ʕamam- "people, nation, kinfolk". 3 attestations across 3 geographically dispersed sites. On MA1b, A-MA appears alongside QE-DE-MI-NU (Qadmīnu "primordial/eastern", cf. Kadmos)—a kinship term adjacent to a recognized Semitic PN parallels NWS naming formulae (ʿAmminadab, ʿAmmiśaday). 2-consonant skeleton is underdetermined: competing roots include *ʔamm-at- "cubit" (#1156), *ʔam(a)t- "maidservant" (#2783). The *306=/ʿa/ vs standard A ambiguity also applies.

entries.meaning: handmaid (of the goddess)
entries.note: Ug. amt aṯrt 'handmaid of Asherah' (Gordon p. 91). On the Zakros tablet ZA10b, A-MI-TA 3 in a quantified list of names. Pan-Semitic root: Akk. amtu, Heb. ʾāmāh, Ug. amt. || Huehnergard: Ug àmt /ʾamatu/ "woman slave, handmaid"; Feminine biradical nominal; listed alongside yd /yadu/ "hand," qšt /qaštu/ "bow," šnt /šantu/ "year," dlt /daltu/ "door". BH cognate: ʾāmā "maid, handmaid" (feminine ending reduced/lost relative to Ug. -atu) (Huehnergard 2012, p. 41) || Mari attests the exact formation—ʾAmat-ʿAštar-an (Gelb AS 21 no. 782), ʾAmat-Labwa (no. 783), 'handmaid of Ashtart / of the Lioness'. LB a-mo-ta rejected (Greek harmota 'wheels').

entries.meaning: grace, favor
entries.note: Split from JA-SA-RA-A-NA-NE (GORILA reads as one word). A- writes /ḥa/ with guttural dropping. qatāl nominal pattern from geminate root. In prayer context on KNZc7: yašara ḥanān = 'righteous grace.'

entries.meaning: the crosser (√ʿ-b-r 'to cross over,' cf. ʿibrī 'Hebrew') OR creator (√b-r-ʾ 'to create,' Gen 1:1)

cognates.Hebrew: ʿābar (עָבַר) 'to cross over' → ʿibrī (עִבְרִי) 'Hebrew'; bārāʾ (בָּרָא) 'he created' (Gen 1:1)

entries.note: HT96a+b (Scribe 8, Casa Room 7, LMIB). HT96b heads major institutional allocation: QA-*118-RA-RE (qaṭara 'incense') + *516 (SIPRU) + GRA 40¾ + OLE+U 4 + NI 2. Short form PA-RA-NE attested on HT115a/b (same scribe) || TWO COMPETING ETYMOLOGIES: (1) √ʿ-b-r + -āne agentive = 'the crosser/one from beyond' (= ʿibrī 'Hebrew'). Dual reading requires PA→BA neutralization. (2) √b-r-ʾ + -āne = 'creator' (aleph drops) || REJECTED: Aaron (ʾAhărōn)—PA ≠ /ha/, fatal mismatch || Amorite Ḥa-pí-ra-an (Huffmon APNM p. 36; element ḤPR ḥapir-, *ʿapir- = the ʿApiru/Ḥabiru word, p. 202) matches A-PA-RA-NE (initial A = ʿa) with -ān; cuneiform ḫ writes ʿ. AP-RA-AN (Gelb AS 21 no. 863) is a separate name, normalized ʾApran; cuneiform AP- writes ʾ and ʿ alike. Root disputed: Borger (via Huffmon p. 202) derives ʿapīru from ʿ-p-r 'dust', not ʿ-b-r 'cross'; PA writes p and b alike.

entries.meaning: my servant

Amarna.note: ʿAbdi-X theophoric pattern is the most common WS PN type in Amarna (ʿAbdi-Aširta, ʿAbdi-Ḫeba, ʿAbdi-Milki, etc.). Confirms √ʿ-b-d as productive WS root in Bronze Age onomastics.

entries.note: PS *ʕabd- 'slave, servant'. Uses *306=ʿA. With 1sg possessive -ī. PN or title.

entries.meaning: personal name; Ugaritic ålnr (Hurrian), Linear B a-ra-na-ro
entries.note: HT 1 A-RA-NA-RE 105, the last of the counted names, whole (GORILA I 3). Ugaritic ålnr, a personal name classed Hurrian and set beside Linear B a-ra-na-ro (DULAT 57); first element allai 'the Lady' (Laroche, GLH 42–43), as in Allan-šeridani at Ugarit (Kinlaw 1967, 19). Hurrian r and l alternate; RA writes r here, as the same scribe writes RA₂ for la in QE-RA₂-U. Linear B a-ra-na-ro is a man, VIR 1, on KN As 1516.11. HT 47b ]RA-NA-RE[, room for one sign before (GORILA I 91), is the same name if the lost sign is A. Rival: Gordon's Egyptian ꜥꜣ-rn-Rꜥ 'Great-is-the-name-of-Re' (Gordon 1966 §127).
entries.source: di Mino; DULAT 57; Laroche 1980; KN As 1516.11; Gordon 1966 §127

entries.meaning: earth (feminine noun—PS *ʾar(V)ṣ̂- "earth")

cognates.Akkadian: erṣetu(m) "earth, land, ground"—standard citation form erṣetum carries feminine mimation, supporting ʾarṣ̂atum as regular East-Semitic-style case marking

entries.note: ZA7a (Zakros stone vessel allocation): A-RA-TU 4, A-RE-TU-MI [broken]. PS *ʾar(V)ṣ̂- "earth" (PS #768) with ṣ̂ (emphatic lateral) dropped—same ṣ̂-loss as A-RE-TU-MI (ʾarṣ̂-ummī "Earth is my mother," CANDIDATE). The -TU = feminine ending -at(u). Vowel /a/ in A-RA-TU preserves absolute state *ʾarṣ̂atu, while A-RE-TU-MI shows /e/ reduction in construct (bound) form before -ummī. Co-occurrence on ZA7a forms a semantic cluster: the noun "earth" alongside the theophoric compound "Earth is my mother." Allat reading REJECTED: the script distinguishes RA (/ra/, AB27) from RA₂ (/la/, AB76), and ʾAllāt requires /l/. The scribe wrote RA, confirming /r/ not /l/. || MIMATION NOTE: A-RA-TU-ME (hapax heading on roundel HTWc3024) would be ʾarṣ̂atum—a feminine noun with mimation. The corpus-derived mimation rule says functional mimation marks masculine absolute-state nouns only (14 feminine -at tokens, none mimated). This is the sole feminine mimation candidate. AKKADIAN DEFENSE: Akkadian feminine nouns take mimation routinely—erṣetum itself is the standard citation form. If Minoan mimation is East-Semitic-style case mimation (both genders) rather than the masculine-only absolute marker, ʾarṣ̂atum is regular. This reading would require revising the mimation rule to allow both genders, which must be weighed against the 14 unmimated feminines. The -TU/-TU-ME alternation is noted as an unresolved suffix pair pending resolution of the mimation scope question.

entries.meaning: earth (feminine noun with mimation—cf. Akk. erṣetum)

cognates.Akkadian: erṣetum "earth, land, ground"—standard fem. citation form with mimation (ORACC freq. 62)

entries.note: Hapax heading on roundel HTWc3024. Mimated form of A-RA-TU (CANDIDATE, ZA7a). Akk. erṣetum shows regular feminine mimation; if Minoan uses East-Semitic-style case mimation (both genders), ʾarṣ̂atum is regular. Sole feminine mimation candidate in corpus (14 fem. -at tokens otherwise unmimated). Context: roundel = sealed receipt, heading = citation form where mimation expected.

entries.meaning: Earth is my mother (NWS theophoric compound PN; pre-Greek Artemis)

cognates.Ugaritic: ʾarṣ 'earth'; ʾum 'mother'—X-ummī theophoric pattern attested: ʾaḫ-ummī, ʾil-ummī (DUL)
cognates.Greek: Ἄρτεμις (Artemis)—widely agreed pre-Greek; no convincing Greek etymology
cognates.Lydian: Artimuś (dat. artimuλ)—u after the m, not in TU's slot; Aramaic (Letoon) ʾrtmwš likewise
cognates.Linear B: a-te-mi-to (PY Es 650, genitive)—drops pre-consonantal /r/ per standard LB orthography
cognates.Etruscan: Artumes (oldest), Artam[e]s, Aritimi, gen. Artmsl (Nielsen & Rathje 2009: 261–262)—u before the m, as in TU-MI; Cristofani's cited Aretume unverified

entries.note: ZA7a (Zakros stone vessel allocation): U-JU 5 · A-RA-TU 4 · A-RE-TU-MI [broken]. Parse ʾarṣ̂-ummī 'Earth is my mother': √ʾ-r-ṣ̂ 'earth' (PS *ʾar(V)ṣ̂- PS #768) + ʾummī 'my mother'. Spelling: A = /ʾa/, RE = /r(e)/, TU = /ṣu/ (T-series writes emphatic ṣ, as TE = /ṣe/ in TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU √r-ṣ-y; glottal of ʾummī elided in sandhi), MI = /mmī/ (gemination unmarked). Open point: the RE vowel—A-RA-TU on the same tablet writes A-RA-. X-ummī sentence names are productive (Mari Eštar-ummī, ARM 23 610:7; Ugaritic ʾaḫ-ummī, ʾil-ummī). Variant grid, slot 2 (TU's vowel) unstable, slots 1 and 3 stable: LB a-te-mi-to / a-ti-mi-te (e/i; r omitted per LB orthography); Greek Ἄρτεμις / West Greek Ἄρταμις (Cretan has Ἄρτεμις) / Pamphylian Ἀρτιμι-; Etruscan Artumes (oldest), Artam[e]s, Aritimi, gen. Artmsl; Lydian Artimuś and Aramaic (Letoon) ʾrtmwš; Lycian Ertẽmi; Carian ŕtmi. Beekes (Pre-Greek 2014: 8, 25) explains such e/i, e/a scatter as adaptation from an a/i/u vowel system—the Semitic triangle. The u stays beside the m outside Greek: before it in TU-MI and Etruscan Artumes, after it in Lydian Artimuś and ʾrtmwš (vowel metathesis across the labial, or a Lydian stem vowel). Greek -is/-it- is the nominative and t-stem added to the borrowed -mi.

entries.meaning: healer, Rephaim (√r-p-ʾ) OR clouds (√ʿ-r-p, Baal epithet rkb ʿrpt)
entries.note: Ug. rpum KTU 1.20–22 (Rephaim as ancestral healers/shades); alt. Ug. ʿrpt 'clouds' from rkb ʿrpt 'Rider of Clouds' (Baal epithet, = Ps 68:5). PE2 Petras. Guttural ʿ drops transparently.

entries.meaning: Eshmun (healing deity)
entries.note: Hapax on ZAZb3 (Zakros, LMIB). Skeleton (ʾ)-š-m-n matches Sidonian healing deity Eshmun (Phoenician ʾšmn). Archaic /a/-initial vocalism (ʾAšmūn) vs. later Greek Asklepios syncretism. Same root as šmn 'oil'—the deity name may derive from the anointing/healing substance. VIN 32 co-occurs, consistent with libation/offering context. Competing commodity reading 'oil, fat' considered but divine name preferred: Eshmun is well-attested as a Phoenician export deity with Sidonian cult center, and theophoric names are common in Linear A administrative texts. Rival: Woudhuizen (2016, 229–230) reads Akkadian assammû 'a large drinking vessel' (CAD A/2 339–340), the pithos's own name. || PKZa12 A-NE (damaged surface between A and NE; sign loss not established) is possibly A-[SA-MU]-NE, a vocative in the libation formula; A-[KO-A]-NE (PKZa11) is the likelier restoration.
entries.phonological_notes: Initial A- = laryngeal (ʾ). SA = /šV/ under sibilant neutralization. MU = /mū/ (long vowel). NE = /n/ with dead vowel. Archaic /a/-vocalism preserved in Linear A spelling.

entries.meaning: captives, bondsmen put to work (heading: captives of the sanctuary); rival aššum šarra 'concerning the queen'

cognates.Ugaritic: åsr 'prisoner, captive', pl. åsrm (KTU 4.382:6; 2.31:24); RS Akk. LÚ a-sí-ru
cognates.Akkadian: asīru 'prisoner of war, captive used as worker' (OB administrative and western texts, Mari to Boğazköy); bīt asīri 'prisoner compound', kurummat bīt asīri 'food rations for the prisoner compound'

entries.note: HT89 A-SA-RA₂ · *307 (dubur 'sanctuary') heads five personnel classes, KU-RO 87, then rations of cyperus, figs and wine. Written as one group, with no divider or space between A and SA (GORILA I 141). /ʾasīr-/ 'captive(s)': Ug. åsr (DULAT 111); Akk. asīru, a western word of administrative lists, with rations for the prisoner compound (CAD A/2 331–32). Captives of the sanctuary, cf. the Gibeonites made hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of God (Josh 9:23, 27) and the captives given to the Levites (Num 31:47); compare MA-I-MI, TA-RA. Rival: A + SA-RA₂ 'concerning the queen', A as abbreviated Akkadian aššum (EA 287:34; Huehnergard 2008: 285, 399), a cut the tablet does not mark. One witness.
entries.source: HT89; GORILA I 141; DULAT 111; CAD A/2 331–32; Josh 9:23, 27; Num 31:47; Montecchi 2008, 321; Huehnergard 2008: 285, 399

entries.meaning: uprightly (variant of yaššaram, ʾa- for ya-)

cognates.Hebrew: yāšār (יָשָׁר) 'upright, straight, righteous' (Deut 32:4, Ps 119:137, 1 Kgs 9:4, Prov 2:7); yōšer (יֹשֶׁר) 'uprightness, equity' (Ps 111:8, Prov 2:13); √y-š-r 'to be straight'; Yeshurun (יְשֻׁרוּן) poetic name for Israel = 'the upright one' (Deut 32:15, 33:5, 33:26, Isa 44:2); cf. Num 23:10 yĕšārīm (Balaam's pun on Yeshurun)
cognates.Ugaritic: yšr 'straight, upright' (DUL 928); yšr in ritual context = moral/cultic fitness
cognates.Akkadian: ešēru 'to be/go straight, prosper' (CAD E 354); išaru 'straight, just, normal'; mīšaru 'justice, equity' (CAD M/II 116)—Hammurabi's mīšarum edicts: royal debt-release decrees that 'set things straight'
cognates.Arabic: yasara (يسر) 'to be easy, smooth'; yasār 'ease, prosperity'

entries.note: Iouktas and Prassa variant (on PRZa1 RA is drawn reversed, the A802 form, and normalized RA in GORILA IV 48) with ʾA- prefix instead of JA- (ya-). The prefix alternation JA-/A- parallels the formula verb (A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA vs. JA-TA-I-*301-U-JA), suggesting these are person markers or article variants, not different roots. Huehnergard: /yušru/ "uprightness" (yuCCu nominal pattern); confirms adverbial accusative with -m. || COGNATES: those of JA-SA-SA-RA-ME, whose reading this spelling shares.

entries.meaning: fine flour, semolina
entries.note: Skeleton syk against šwq: š is written s and ḳ is written k. HT28a context is decisive: A-SI-JA-KA heads a list with GRA+QE 5, OLE+U 2, OLE+KI ½, OLE+MI 1, OLE+TU, VIN 3—mixed grain and oil commodities. A flour category in a commodity allocation tablet is semantically coherent. Arabic sawīq (parched barley meal) preserves the ancient trade commodity.

entries.meaning: I make myself a dwelling (Palaikastro dialect variant, 1cs tG-stem middle-reflexive of √NWY)

cognates.Hebrew: nāweh (נָוֶה) 'comely habitation, pasture' (Exod 15:13, Ps 23:2 [nĕʾōt, pl. construct], Isa 33:20, Jer 25:30); nāʾwāh (נָאוָה) 'comely' (Song 1:5); √n-w-y 'to dwell, settle'
cognates.Amorite: nawûm 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)' (Huffmon, APNM 237); nawijum 'nomadic encampment' (Gelb, AS 21)
cognates.Akkadian: namû A (nawû) 'pasture land … and its population and flocks; outlying area around a city' (CAD N/1, 249–51)
cognates.Arabic: nawā (نوى) 'to intend, settle toward'; nawāh 'dwelling-place, destination'
cognates.Greek: ναός (naos) 'temple' < *nawos, same √n-w-y (Bernal 1987, Rendsburg 1989); cf. Exod 15:13 nəwēh qodšekhā 'Thy holy shrine'

entries.note: Monophthongized Palaikastro dialect variant of A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA. The -WA-E ending replaces -WA-JA, showing /ay/ → /ē/ monophthongization characteristic of the Palaikastro scribal tradition. || COGNATES: those of A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA, whose reading this spelling shares.

entries.meaning: I make myself a dwelling (1cs tG-stem middle-reflexive denominative of √NWY)

cognates.Hebrew: nāweh (נָוֶה) 'comely habitation, pasture' (Exod 15:13, Ps 23:2 [nĕʾōt, pl. construct], Isa 33:20, Jer 25:30); nāʾwāh (נָאוָה) 'comely' (Song 1:5); √n-w-y 'to dwell, settle'
cognates.Amorite: nawûm 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)' (Huffmon, APNM 237); nawijum 'nomadic encampment' (Gelb, AS 21)
cognates.Akkadian: namû A (nawû) 'pasture land … and its population and flocks; outlying area around a city' (CAD N/1, 249–51)
cognates.Arabic: nawā (نوى) 'to intend, settle toward'; nawāh 'dwelling-place, destination'
cognates.Greek: ναός (naos) 'temple' < *nawos, same √n-w-y (Bernal 1987, Rendsburg 1989); cf. Exod 15:13 nəwēh qodšekhā 'Thy holy shrine'

entries.note: The core libation formula verb. 11 attestations across 5 peak sanctuary sites (Iouktas, Kophinas, Troullos, Palaikastro, Syme). Morphology: A- 1cs prefix, -TA- tG prefix, I epenthetic /i/; *301-WA-JA = root √n-w-y (*301 = /na/): /ʾatainawaya/ (di Mino, Ya Diktu). tG-stem (middle-reflexive) of √NWY 'to dwell, settle'—the worshipper actively positions herself at the sanctuary before the deity. Hebrew keeps the tG only in relics such as tirgaltî (Hos 11:3; Hutton & Marzouk 2012), and Moabite has Gt wʾltḥm 'and I fought' (KAI 181:11, 15); the act matches Hebrew wāʾetnappal 'and I prostrated myself' (Deut 9:18), a Hitpaʿel. Same paradigm: A-TA-I-*301-WA-E (PK Za 11a), JA-TA-I-*301-U-JA (AP Za 1, 3ms). A-TA-I-*301-DE-KA and TA-NA-I-*301-(U-)TI(-NU) share the frame but are √ʿ-n-y 'answer' (di Mino, Ya Diktu). Root noun *301-WA = nawā 'dwelling' attested at IOZa4 || STEM SEMANTICS: Middle-reflexive, NOT causative. The causative ('I cause the deity to dwell') would require the Š-stem (Shafel/Hiphil), not the tG. The tG/hitpael is the Semitic liturgical stem for what the worshipper does to herself in the divine presence—denominative from nāweh 'abode': 'I make myself a dwelling,' the same pattern as hitnabbēʾ 'make oneself a prophet' from nābîʾ. Closest NWS cognate utterance: Exod 15:2 (Song of the Sea) zeh ʾēlî wə-ʾanwēhû—1cs √n-w-y with deity as object, oldest stratum of Hebrew poetry; Targum Onkelos renders it wə-ʾebnē lēh maqdəšā 'I will build Him a sanctuary,' an ancient witness to the habitation reading (rival sense: 'beautify/praise him,' cf. parallel colon wa-ʾărōməmennhû; HALOT files it under II נוה 'glorify,' and the Peshitta and Palestinian Targumim read 'praise'). Frame parallel: wāʾetnappal lipnê YHWH (Deut 9:18) = 'I prostrated myself before YHWH'—same sentence frame (1cs reflexive verb of self-positioning + 'before the deity'). The prefixed -t- (A-TA-I-, not *A-I-TA-) follows the West Semitic pattern (Hebrew hitpael, Arabic Form V ta-faʿʿala, Ge'ez tä-qätlä), not the Akkadian Gt infix—the earliest epigraphic witness to the East/West Semitic split in -t- morpheme placement || BIBLICAL ATTESTATION SET: nāweh (נָוֶה) 'comely habitation, pasture'—Exod 15:13 (holy nāweh), Ps 23:2 (green nĕʾōt), Isa 33:20 (Zion as unshaken nāweh), Jer 25:30 (YHWH roars from His holy māʿôn, against His nāweh), Ezek 34:14 (good nāweh on the mountains of Israel). Semantic field consistently pairs divine habitation with pastoral landscape—same conceptual frame as the peak sanctuary formula, where the worshipper settles herself at the mountaintop sanctuary. AMORITE: nawûm 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)' (Huffmon, APNM 237)—the pasture-to-settlement step in second-millennium West Semitic || DIALECT EVIDENCE: Palaikastro A-TA-I-*301-WA-E weakens JA to E, as in A-SA-SA-RA-ME and A-DI-KI-TE-TE there (di Mino, Ya Diktu). The verb opens the prayer as an act of ritual self-positioning—the worshipper takes up dwelling before the deity. See TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU (pos 7) for the closing acceptance petition Davis 2026 functional gloss: 'gives' (in Salgarella & Petrakis eds., The Wor(l)ds of Linear A, pp. 43–60)

entries.meaning: ʾAtanat, 'She-who-gives'—feminine of √y-t-n 'to give' with regular I-y > ʾ weakening; the etymon of Athena (di Mino, Ya Diktu p. 20)

cognates.Linear B: a-ta-na-po-ti-ni-ja (KN V 52)—divine offering list alongside e-nu-wa-ri-jo, pa-ja-wo-ne, po-se-da-o-ne
cognates.Greek: Ἀθάνα (Doric), Ἀθήνη (Ionic/Attic)—universally pre-Greek, no established etymology (Beekes 2010)
cognates.Hurrian: Atana—PN attested at Nuzi, but lacks Hurrian morphology; likely substrate borrowing, not Hurrian origin
cognates.Phoenician: ytn 'give, present' (Krahmalkov 2000); cf. BʿLYTN Baʿal-yatōn 'Baʿal has given'

entries.note: Root √ʾ-t-n (lexicalized divine name from √y-t-n after y > ʾ weakening). Feminine *yātanat > ʾAtanat. Phoenician preserves the y-initial verbal form: BʿLYTN = Baʿal-yatōn 'Baʿal has given' (KAI). Greek receives the post-weakened form: Mycenaean a-ta-na-po-ti-ni-ja (KN V 52), Classical Ἀθάνα (Doric) / Ἀθήνη (Ionic). Beekes (EDG 2010): no IE etymology, classified pre-Greek. Founding myth preserves the etymology: Athena wins Athens by GIVING the olive tree. Six √y-t-n / √n-t-n forms across the corpus (JA-TA-NO and A-TA-NO are Gordon's misreadings of the formula verb and do not count). ZA9 reads /ʾAtanat/ 'She-who-gives' (di Mino, Ya Diktu p. 20). The A-/∅ alternation (A-TA-NA-TE vs TA-NA-TE on ZA10a) follows the same scribal convention as 4 other corpus pairs (A-PA-RA-NE/PA-RA-NE, A-MI-TA/MI-TA, A-SA-SA-RA-ME/SA-SA-RA-ME, A-DU/DU). ZA9, the only witness, reads A-TA-NA-[·] (GORILA III 166–67: "A-TA-NA-TE possible"): the last sign is lost and no divider follows NA, so ZA9 most likely writes A-TA-NA-TE as on ZA10a, and the bare stem stands only inside A-TA-NA-TE and A-TA-NA-JE. || CONTEXT: A-TA-NA-TE on ZA10a and A-TA-NA-JE on THEZb6 have their own entries. ZA9 lists names with QI+SI and *21F amounts under NU-TI—RO-SI-RA QI+SI 4, A-TA-NA-[·] QI+SI 2, [·]-MA-JU *21F 2, WI-RA-RE-MI-TE *21F 1—where the name reads most naturally as a person named for the goddess, not the goddess herself.

entries.meaning: Athirat (divine name: the Goddess)
entries.note: ZU is the only available /ṯ/-carrier in the syllabary; its /u/ vowel is a dead vowel—the consonant is the semantic carrier (Gordon §147). The spelling does not specify the middle vowel, so the Ugaritic vocalization ʾAṯirat- (with /i/) is adopted as the best-attested form. Final -t (feminine marker) implied but unwritten per CV orthography. The preserved interdental /ṯ/ is the key: Akkadian Aširat- (OB onward) and Hebrew ʾĂšērā already show the sibilant shift ṯ→š. The Minoan form aligns with Ugaritic ʾAṯirat- in retaining /ṯ/, and may predate the shift.

entries.meaning: luminous one (feminine)
entries.note: From √ʾ-w-r 'to shine, be light' (Hebrew ʾōr < *ʾawr 'light') + feminine -ēt ending. Personal name or epithet on a Khania cyperus distribution tablet. || 'Feminine' rests on the name slot: -t also forms abstracts and unit nouns (Fischer 2002, §64), so ʾawrēt may equally be 'light'.

entries.meaning: possible opening 'our beloved …' (fragmentary and doubtful Linear A)
entries.note: DRA Zg 1 is a five-sign retrograde graffito on a clay reel from Drama-Kajrjaka, Bulgaria: DA-DU-*301̣-[?]-[?]. Only the first three signs have been compared with Linear A; the final two remain unread, and RILA-S1 D 24 classifies the inscription as doubtful. DA-DU recurs initially in KN Zf 31 and HT 95. With *301 = /na/, Amorite dādum/dawdum 'beloved' plus Ugaritic 1cp /-nā/ after the case vowel (cf. /malku-nā/ 'our king') permits /dādu-nā-/ 'our beloved ….' No boundary follows *301, so the sequence may instead begin a longer name and cannot be treated as a complete prayer or epithet.
entries.source: Fol and Schmitt 2000, 56–62; Gelb 1980; Huehnergard 2012, 33–34; RILA-S1 D 24

entries.meaning: settlement(s), district (heading of a grain list); rival 'beloved land'

cognates.Akkadian: dadmū pl. tant. 'the inhabited world (settlements and inhabitants)' (CAD D 18)
cognates.Amorite: dadmum, fem. dadmītum (Gelb 1980, 17); PN Da-ad-mi-tum (Gelb 1980, no. 1394)

entries.note: HT 95a .1 DA-DU-MA-TA · GRA, heading the grain list DA-ME 10, MI-NU-TE 10, SA-RU 20, KU-NI-SU 10, DI-DE-RU 10, QE-RA₂-U 7; HT 95b gives the same list under A-DU ·. A band of lost surface between MA and TA is wider than the other gaps but holds no sign position. dadmatu 'settlement(s)', feminine of PS *damdam- 'inhabited land': Akkadian dadmū 'the inhabited world (settlements and inhabitants)' (CAD D 18), Amorite dadmum and fem. dadmītum (Gelb 1980, 17), the Mari name Da-ad-mi-tum (Gelb 1980, no. 1394); cf. Punic ʔdmt 'land, country'. Woudhuizen (2016, 226–227) reads the same word but takes it as 'goddesses of the dwellings'. The U of DU echoes no vowel of the word. Rivals: dādu-mātu 'beloved land' (√d-w-d + Akk. mātu), though both languages put the head noun first (māt dādi); Hadad-mattān 'gift of Hadad', parallel to A-DU on side b, with Ha- lost and final -n unwritten. Hapax.

entries.meaning: good, sufficient—commodity quality designation on oil/fat allocation tablets
entries.note: PS *day- 'good, sufficient'. Cross-site: HT12 (50 units, oil/fat inventory) and KH13 (3 units, after *304-CYP fat/cypress compound). Both contexts pair with *304 (fat/tallow) and CYP (cypress) commodities. Large quantity range (3–50) suggests a bulk commodity or quality grade. Hebrew day 'enough, sufficiency', Aramaic day.

entries.meaning: fish
entries.note: 5× sole word on HT nodules = commodity label; Heb. דָּג, Ug. dg; g→KA standard voicing neutralization.

entries.meaning: personal name, probably derived from Dagan/Dagon; cf. attested Daguna
entries.note: DA-KU-NA corresponds exactly, allowing Linear A stop neutralization, to syllabic Da-gu-na. Daguna is attested as an Old Akkadian personal name and later as an Akkadian divine name. Because HT103 is a counted administrative list, an anthroponym or recipient is safer here than a direct reference to the god. The connection with Dagan/Dagon is probable but does not determine the bearer.
entries.source: Gordon 1966; Old Akkadian Da-gu-na attestations; ORACC Daguna

entries.meaning: probable Hurrian-style personal name; compare Boğazköy Tagu(b)-šini, Ugaritic Taki-šenni
entries.note: No exact Dakušenni is attested in the Nuzi Personal Names corpus. Nuzi does attest Aku-šenni, Takku (Ta-ak-ku, Ta-a-ku, Ta-ku, Ta-gu), and Takuja (Ta-ku-ia; variant Da-ku-a-a): Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, s.vv. AKU-ŠENNI, TAKKU, TAKUJA. The closest full compound is Boğazköy Tagu(b)-šini (KBo XXII 114, 7), under the themes tagi- and tagu- (Laroche 1980, 250); Ugaritic tgḏn, syllabic ta-gi₅-ŠA-na, is analyzed as Hurrian Taki-šenni (NPN p. 262, printed Tgz̄n; Tropper 2000, 119, §32.144.35). Hurrian šēna ‘brother’ with the individualizing -ni, šen=ni, accounts for the onomastic element -šenni (Giorgieri 2000, 199, 202; Wilhelm, Hurrian, 103; Laroche 1980, 225–26, s.v. šeni); the first element remains unexplained. Linear A DA-KU spells /ta.ku/ under stop neutralization, with the u of tagu-; /Takušenni/ is a comparative reconstruction, not an exact external attestation. HT 103 .4–5 DA-KU-SE-NE 1 (on .2–3 a break follows NE) and extended DA-KU-SE-NE-TI on HT104 support an entity or name. The pair favors suffixation, but GORILA I 171 allows final TI to be an ideogram or classifier; Finkelberg 2002/03, 96–97 instead proposes a dative/recipient function.
entries.source: Gordon 1966; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943; Tropper 2000; Laroche 1980; Giorgieri 2000; Wilhelm, Hurrian

entries.meaning: blood (ritual allocation category); rival dimtu 'district'

cognates.Akkadian: damu 'blood' (CAD D 75); dimtu 'tower; fortified area; district' (CAD D 144–147), rival

entries.note: HT 95a/b and HT 86a: DA-ME with MI-NU-TE, always together, in the set SA-RU, KU-NI-SU, DI-DE-RU, QE-RA₂-U (QA-RA₂-WA on HT 86a). HT 120: DA-ME GRA+K+L 74, GRA+PA 62⅕, beside DA-U-*49, KI-RE-TA-NA and PA-I-TO. PS *dam- 'blood' (Ug. dm, Heb. dām, Akk. damu), which DA-ME spells: a ritual category drawing grain. Rival: Akk. dimtu 'tower; district' (CAD D 144–147), Ug. dmt 'tower' (DULAT 272), which fits the place names on HT 120 but needs DA for di and lacks the -t. Four attestations, all Haghia Triada.

entries.meaning: pot, vessel (for grain storage)
entries.note: Skeleton dqr, the emphatic ḳ of *diḳar- written q. HT120 shows DA-QE-RA heading a list with GRA+K+L 74, GRA+PA 62—grain commodities measured in vessels. A vessel category heading in a grain allocation tablet is semantically strong. HT57a is fragmentary (DA-QE-RA 1 A ¹⁄₈). The Akkadian diqāru is well-attested as a large storage vessel for grain and liquids.

entries.meaning: dwelling or estate; administrative unit
entries.note: Attested across Haghia Triada and Palaikastro as a recurring administrative label with variable quantities. Compare Arabic dār and Aramaic dārā(ʾ) 'house, dwelling'; this supports a possible dwelling or estate term, not the more specific gloss 'granary.' Its association with grain and personnel may reflect an administrative unit, but the function is not independently established. The unrelated Ugaritic drʾ /ḏirāʾu/ 'arm' does not explain the contexts.
entries.phonological_notes: Skeleton d-r, as in dār. Dead vowel on RE. No neutralization required.

entries.meaning: those of Acacia (gentilic, a roster unit); rival the unglossed Dasiṭa

cognates.Proto-Semitic: *šint- 'acacia' (semitic_roots no. 3629), a loan from Egyptian šnd.t
cognates.Hebrew: šiṭṭâ, pl. šiṭṭîm 'acacia' (HALOT 1473); place names Beth-Shittah (Judg 7:22), Abel-Shittim (Num 33:49)

entries.note: HT 13 DA-SI-*118 19 (wine list, beside KU-ZU-NI 18); HT 85a 24 (men, under A-DU · *307+*307, beside KU-ZU-NI 5); HT 122a 2 (men); HT 99b 2. Three scribes count it as a unit, not a person. ḏā 'those of', as in DA-NA-SI Ḏā-Naśiʾ, + ši-ṭa, Heb. šiṭṭâ 'acacia', the n of *šint- unwritten or assimilated. *118 = ṭa: s-t and s-d give no acacia. DA first and *118 third show *118 is not DA.

entries.meaning: the enduring one (personal name)
entries.note: Retained CANDIDATE name from DA-U-*49: Dawmi, 'the enduring one,' compared with √d-w-m 'endure, remain,' Hebrew Dūmah and Assyrian Adummatu. The reading requires *49 to carry the candidate syllabic value /mi/ and U to represent the medial glide /w/; neither step is independently settled. The sign's official semantic reading is PALM/TREE, with TAMIR its proposed Semitic lexical name, so an unresolved DA-U-PALM/TREE analysis remains available.

entries.meaning: nobles, assembly of elders, council

cognates.Akkadian: adāru 'to be afraid, to fear' (semantic shift from 'awe-inspiring')

entries.note: DI-DE- renders the Semitic geminate -dd- in ʾaddīr-. Always co-occurs with SA-RU in the formulaic allocation set. 3 tablets, all Haghia Triada LMIB. Cross-tablet allocation series (HT86a/95a/95b)—consistent ordering and quantities. It co-occurs structurally with SA-RU, MI-NU-TE, QE-RA₂-U.

entries.meaning: personal name ("El judges"—Ugaritic hero-king Dāniʾēlu)

cognates.Ugaritic: Dāniʾēlu—hero-king of KTU 1.17-19 (Tale of Aqhat). √d-y-n "to judge" + ʾēl "God."
cognates.Hebrew: Dāniyyēʾl (דָּנִיֵּאל)—Ezekiel 14:14, 14:20, 28:3; likely same figure as Ugaritic Danel

entries.note: Hapax on HT108 (Scribe HT2, LMIB). Grain ration list headed by KI-RE-TA-NA ('Cretan,' CONFIRMED gentilic): DI-NA-RO receives 2 units, DU-SU-NI 5, RA₂-TI 10 || ETYMOLOGY: Skeleton d-n-r → d-n-l via R-class liquid neutralization (RO=/lo/). √d-y-n + theophoric ʾēl contracted to -lo. Morphological parallel: DI-NA-U (Dīnāyu, hypocoristic PN, CANDIDATE, 6 att.) shares same √d-y-n base with 1pl possessive suffix. Vowel indifference DI=/di/ for expected DA=/da/ within documented tolerance (cf. KI-RO/KU-RO per Gordon §147) || Both Ugaritic epic root names (Keret + Danel) appear on same tablet HT108—administratively coincidental but onomastically notable

entries.meaning: personal name: hypocoristic of a √d-y-n name ('Judge')
entries.note: 6 attestations across Haghia Triada and Knossos. Not 'our judge': 1cp is -nā/-nū (Fischer 2002, §268; Heb. -nû), and no Semitic 1cp is -āʾu. -U after NA writes the hypocoristic -āyu/-āʾu (Amorite -ay-um: ʾAhlul-ay-um, Gelb 1980, no. 690; cf. Diyn-i-Baddu, no. 1512). Appears in personnel lists (HT25a: names × 1, appears twice on same tablet) and commodity allocations (HT9a: VIN context, DI-NA-U 4; HT9b: AROM context, DI-NA-U 4; KNZb27: VIN 17). Cross-site distribution (HT + Knossos) confirms a stable common NWS name. Note: √ʾ-d-n 'lord' with laryngeal loss gives the same d-n skeleton (ʾadōnū 'our lord'), but the extra assumption makes it less parsimonious. AMORITE CORROBORATION: Huffmon APNM p. 182 glossary — DN dyn 'judge' (Common Semitic), an onomastic element at Mari: G imperfect Ya-di-nim (yaqtil class), precative La-di-nam, I-di-AN; Noth IPN 187-88, Stamm ANG parallels. The root is a productive name-former in the closest NWS onomasticon upstream of Linear A.

entries.meaning: mighty is the judge (compound sentence name); rival a simplex recipient name

cognates.Hebrew (PN): עַדְרִיאֵל Adriel (1 Sam 18:19), אֲבִידָן Abidan (Num 1:11), דָּנִיֵּאל Daniel

entries.note: Both constituent roots have their own lexicon entries: DI-DE-RU = ʾaddīru (PROBABLE, √ʾ-d-r), DI-NA-U = dīnāʾu (CANDIDATE, √d-y-n), DI-NA-RO = Dānīlu (CANDIDATE). NWS sentence-name formation: predicate adjective + agent noun. Hapax, a recipient of ½ on HT98a: ʾaddīr requires DI for /ʾad-/ with its vowel unwritten.

entries.meaning: households, granaries (grain recipient); rivals the Amorite place name Dīr, a personal name

cognates.Amorite: dīrum (noun), Dīr, Dīrum (GN), Dīrītum (DN), under DWR 'to turn around' (Gelb 1980, AS 21, pp. 17–18)

entries.note: A grain recipient in two Scribe 5 lists: HT 93a DI-RI-NA · DA+RE+SE 43½; HT 102 DI-RI-NA 10, beside SA-RA₂ GRA 976, PA₃-NI, VIR, MA-ZU and I-KA. DI-RI = dīr-, the base of Amorite dīrum and Dīr under √d-w-r (Gelb AS 21, 17–18); -NA = masculine plural -īna: households. Rivals: the place name Dīr ('the people of Dīr'), a personal name. Two attestations.

entries.meaning: that, of (relative pronoun)
entries.note: Relative/determinative from PWS *ḏū; Akkadian ša kept apart. Open question: the corpus attestations are list entries with their own quantities—HT122a '*306-TU 1 / DU 1 / KU-PA₃-NU 1' (list totalled KU-RO 31), ZA10b 'TA 2 / DU 1', ZA31 'DU 2' (HT47a's ]DU 2̣0[ ends a word begun on the line before, GORILA I 91)—a slot for a name or abbreviation, with no clause for a relative to head. Gordon's reading rests on II,2:1; the roster DU is uninvestigated (cf. KI's accounting use)

entries.meaning: sanctuary, inner sanctum; proposed variant spelling of DU-PU₂-RE
entries.note: Preferred as a word-specific variant of DU-PU₂-RE, attested in the same ritual corpus at PKZa15 and HTZb160. Facchetti (1999, 132) and Davis (2013, 44 n. 46) identify *314 here as an orthographic variant of PU₂; Thomas (2020, 8) cautiously accepts the comparison. On di Mino's Semitic reading, dubur means 'sanctuary, inner sanctum' (√d-b-r; cf. Hebrew dəbīr), forming dubur ʾIda, 'the sanctuary of Ida.' This is a word-specific equation, not a value assigned to every *314. RI would yield √d-r-r comparanda but no secure contextual parse. GORILA IV 20 dots DU and RE; *314 is whole.
entries.source: Facchetti 1999, 132; Davis 2013, 44 n. 46; Thomas 2020, 8; di Mino

entries.meaning: sanctuary, inner sanctum (dubur)

cognates.Linear B: da-pu₂-ri-to-jo po-ti-ni-ja (KN Gg 702), identified with λαβύρινθος (Chadwick–Baumbach 1963, p. 216)

entries.note: di Mino's hypothesis linking three orthographic strategies: *307 alone, *307-PU₂-RE, and DU-PU₂-RE. The phonetic spelling, Hebrew dəbîr 'inner sanctuary' and Linear B da-pu₂-ri-to-jo po-ti-ni-ja (KN Gg 702) make /dubur/ a strong candidate. The equivalence is not epigraphically automatic in every *307 occurrence: on HT89, *307 is an uncomplemented heading sign and does not independently establish 'sanctuary.' No independent evidence shows that the three spellings are semantically identical. DU-PU₂-RE never stands alone: it is written inside JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-DU-PU₂-RE (PK Za 15) and PA-TA-DA-DU-PU₂-RE (HT Zb 160). PK Za 11 reads A-DI-KI-TE-TE-[··]-RE (GORILA IV 34), two signs lost before RE, the slot DU-PU₂ fills on PK Za 15.

entries.meaning: freedom, release
entries.note: Akkadian darāru means 'become free, move about freely, run off,' while (an)durāru denotes remission, manumission, or release from imposed service (CAD D, 109, s.v. darāru A; CAD A/2, 115–17, s.v. andurāru). Hebrew dĕrōr denotes liberty or release (HALOT, 230, s.v. III דְּרוֹר). These sources support 'freedom/release,' not the former contextual glosses 'deliverance' or 'purity.' DU-RA on MA2a and the -RA-RE sequence in QA-*118-RA-RE (HT96b) are formal comparanda only; neither independently establishes the meaning. On KN Zc 7 its exact syntactic relation to A-KA-NU ZA-TI remains uncertain.

entries.meaning: the Levite (ethnonymic designation)
entries.note: HT 25a .4, at the end of the line after ZU-JU-PU₂ 1, with no numeral. WI is complete at the preserved right edge, and .5 opens with I-KI-RA 1. The scribe carries DI-NA-U's 1 from .2 to .3, so DU-RU-WI-I-KI-RA may be one name. DU = ḏu 'the one of' + RU-WI /lēwī/; U-RE-WI on the same tablet spells the element RE-WI. Niesiołowski-Spanò (2020) argues Levites = Mycenaean ra-wo (λαοί). Rival: ḏurwī, from √ḏ-r-w 'to scatter, winnow' (Arabic ḏarā, Ugaritic dry, Hebrew zārâ), whose vowels fit no participle.

entries.meaning: copper, bronze (commodity category)

cognates.Hebrew: neḥōšet (נְחֹשֶׁת) "copper, bronze" (BDB 638); nāḥāš (נָחָשׁ) "serpent" (Gen. 3:1); neḥushtan (נְחֻשְׁתָּן) "the bronze serpent" (2 Kings 18:4)

entries.note: KH7a (Khania, LMIB): section heading for 10 copper-workers (VIR+*313b 10) receiving ½ unit CYP+D. Three named worker groups on the tablet, each with CYP+D copper allocation || ETYMOLOGY: Skeleton n-s against PS *naḥaš- 'snake', with interior ḥ unwritten (no *314 sign on any KH tablet). Prosthetic E- not standard for this root (Hebrew neḥōšet has no initial vowel)—possible adjectival/nisbe naḥāšī 'of copper' or dialectal prosthesis before initial nasal || The dual meaning 'serpent/copper' (shared shininess) is pan-Semitic; Hebrew neḥushtan collapses both into Moses' bronze serpent (Num 21:9). Structural parallel to KU-NI-SU: Semitic commodity term as administrative category label

entries.meaning: parīsu, the half-gur grain measure (CAD P 186; DULAT 671–672 prś)
entries.note: GRA ideogram + PA, the initial of parīsu, attested at four sites and often assigned large dry-measure quantities: Akkadian parīsu B '(a measure of capacity) one-half of a gur' (CAD P 186), Ugaritic prś/prs, a dry measure of half a gur (DULAT 671–72), and Biblical Aramaic pĕrēs 'half-portion' (Dan 5:28). HT102 has PA₃-NI GRA+PA 33 and, after a lacuna, VIR GRA+PA 33; the source reads ]VIR, not VIR+[?]. HT120 distinguishes GRA+PA from GRA+K+L and GRA+B.

entries.meaning: flour/meal as a grain subtype; processed grain product for rations and offerings
entries.note: GRA ideogram + QE complement (4 att., all Haghia Triada). PS *qamāḥ- 'to grind, mill': Akk qēmu(m) 'flour, meal' (CAD Q 254), Heb קֶמַח qemaḥ (Gen 18:6, Num 5:15), Ug qmḥ (KTU 1.14 ii:29). QE = /qe/ = initial syllable of qemāḥu. GRA+QE appears with dry-measure bulk quantities (5, 20, 40 units) in multi-commodity allocation tablets alongside OLE+KI, OLE+MI, VIN, and plain GRA. On HT36, *307+*387-GRA+QE 44½ (20 erased from 64½) records a flour allocation to a dubur sanctuary—the largest attested quantity. GRA+QE is distinct from plain GRA (whole grain) as a processed subtype.

entries.meaning: Ida, 'the Hand' (sacred mountain—toponym/theonym)
entries.note: Attested as a complete sign group on ritual stone vessels across 3 sites (Nerokurou, Palaikastro, Zakros); in PKZa18 it alone is bounded by dividers between the broken groups ]-TE and JA-JA-[…. Distribution + dedicatory genre fit a sacred-mountain name (cf. Mt. Ida / Idaean cave). I-DA-MA-TE (ARZf1–2) is prothetic ʾi- + DA-MA-TE 'the tower' (√d-m-t), not an Ida compound, and lends no support here. The toponym class is behavior-supported; the specific Ida identification is the speculative element. || PH6 (MM IIB, Phaistos): earliest attestation, within the fused prepositional phrase I-DA-PA₃-I-SA-RI = ʾIdā bi-ʾišarī—Phaistos lies directly under the mountain. || ROOT: Ida = 'the Hand', PS *yad- ~ *ʾid- (semitic_roots 2046); Linear A writes the *ʾid- variant, with the initial i of Akkadian idu, Soqotri ʔed, Tigre ʔǝde. Per the Ya Diktu grammar's footnote (Chantraine, DELG s.v. Ἴδη, calls Ἴδη pre-Hellenic): the Idaean Daktyls, 'fingers', are the Greek doublet—'fingers of the hand' (Pollux, Onom. 2.156)—and the gentilic JE-DI yedī 'the Idaean' (HT8a, HT36, HT122b, HT140) may corroborate.

entries.meaning: of Ida (preferred diptotic genitive after DU-*314-RE); alternatively, toward Ida

cognates.Hebrew: hāhārāh (הָהָרָה) 'toward the mountain' (Gen 19:17, the hē locale -āh); yad (יָד) 'hand, arm' (H3027)
cognates.Ugaritic: ʾugarita, diptotic genitive 'of Ugarit' in ḥmyt ugrt /ḥāmiyātu ʾugarita/ 'the walls of Ugarit'; yd 'hand'

entries.note: Preferred as the diptotic genitive in dubur ʾIda, 'the sanctuary of Ida.' Compare Ugaritic /ḥāmiyātu ʾugarita/ 'the walls of Ugarit,' where a diptotic place-name has genitive -a (Huehnergard 2012, §IV.B.3, p. 40). 'Toward Ida' remains possible by comparison with Ugaritic directive -h /-ah(a)/ and Hebrew -āh, but final A alone does not prove that analysis. Bare I-DA is independently attested; Ida's proposed connection with PS *yad- ~ *ʾid- remains interpretive.

entries.meaning: the tower (DA-MA-TE with prothetic I-)
entries.cognates: Cf. Ugaritic dmt "tower", in "the tower of the mother of(?) the god[s(?)" (KTU 2.31:46), and dmtqdš "Tower" (DULAT 272); Akkadian dimtu "tower; fortified area, settlement; district" (CAD D, 144–147; Huehnergard 1997). The unprefixed DA-MA-TE is independently attested at KY Za 2.
entries.note: AR Zf 1 and AR Zf 2 are separate one-word inscriptions on metal objects from Arkhalkhori. Their I-DA-MA-TE form stands in a formal I-/zero alternation with DA-MA-TE at KY Za 2. This supports prothetic I- before the same lexical base and rules out the syntactically reversed Akkadian construct Ida-māt, "Land of Ida." The lexical identification remains CANDIDATE because the inscriptions supply no sentence-level context.

entries.meaning: tower; the unprefixed base of I-DA-MA-TE
entries.note: KY Za 2, a stone vessel from Kythera, DA-MA-TE alone. The base of I-DA-MA-TE (AR Zf 1, 2), read 'the tower': Ug. dmt (I) 'tower', in 'the tower of the mother of(?) the god[s(?)' (KTU 2.31:46; DULAT 272), Akk. dimtu 'tower; fortified area; district' (CAD D 144–147). Rival: a personal name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Waters of Ida—sacred springs and caves of the Idaean sanctuary
entries.note: Hapax at Syme, position-2 slot in the libation formula (after A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA). I-DA = Mount Ida (the sacred mountain, cf. I-DA-A on KOZa1); -MI = √m-y-y 'water' (Hebrew מַיִם mayim, Ugaritic my). 'Ida-waters'—a reference to the sacred springs and caves of the Idaean sanctuary. The Dictaean and Idaean caves are famously associated with water sources (the Dictaean cave has an underground lake; the Idaean cave complex is spring-fed). Alternative reading: -mī as 1cs possessive suffix 'My Ida'—the worshipper claiming personal relationship with the mountain-deity. Parallels each peak sanctuary naming its own sacred mountain in position 2: JA-DI-KI-TU (Dikte) at Iouktas, I-DA-A (Ida) at Kophinas, I-DA-MI (Waters of Ida / My Ida) at Syme.

entries.meaning: island
entries.note: KN Za 10 preserves only right-broken I-JA[, so it does not attest a complete standalone word or support ‘of the island.’ CR(?)Zf1 supplies the complete I-JA form in minimal context. Homograph risk remains: I-JA could be the Semitic ‘island’ word, a demonstrative or personal-name element, or—on CR(?)Zf1—a shortened vocative for Yamm. Cf. Ugaritic rbt ʾaṯrt ym and the cross-Semitic vocative particle *yā*. The proposed relation to A-JE /ʾaye/ remains dialectal and CANDIDATE.

entries.meaning: and behold (contracted conjunction + h-n presentative)

cognates.Hebrew: hinnēh (הִנֵּה) "behold" (< *han + emphatic); ha- definite article (< *han with n-assimilation)

entries.note: Working vocalization /wannā/ 'and behold,' comparing Ugaritic w hn beside contracted wn (KTU 1.23:46; 1.4 IV 50; Watson 1996, 285–87; Sivan 2001, 34, 186) and Lipiński's *wa-hanna/u > wn (1997, §27.25). The initial w- already contains the conjunction, so */u-winnā/ is excluded. Alphabetic Ugaritic does not determine the vowels; /winnā/ remains possible, and Tropper 2000, §33.142.23 permits */wa-hinnV/ > /winnV/ while preferring w + enclitic -n. Hebrew wəhinnē retains /h/. The Linear A equation remains a project hypothesis, not an Ugaritic vocalization.

entries.meaning: progenitress, sister-in-law (divine epithet of Anath)
entries.note: Ug. ybmt limm 'Progenitress of Heroes'—Anath's primary epithet alongside btlt. Near-exact 4-syllable match at Khania, the most Semitic-looking Linear A site. All shifts regular: y→y, b→p, m→m. || Huehnergard: Ug ybmt /yabam(a)tu/ "sister-in-law, kinswoman"; Feminine noun. ybmt limm /yabam(a)tu li-ʾēmima/ "kinswoman to the terrible ones(?)" — epithet of Anath. Possible Št stem: pštbm. BH cognate: yəbāmā "sister-in-law" (levirate context) (Huehnergard 2012, p. 87 (epithet))

entries.meaning: island (genitive after SI-MA 'name of'; -i written with an E-series sign)
entries.note: PHZb4 (Phaistos, clay vessel): SI-MA 𐄁 I-JA-TE = šima ʾiyyate "name of the island." Feminine construct ʾiyyat- with -e vowel. Morphology: base ʾiyy- + feminine -at + construct -e (cf. Hebrew construct ʾiyyat- in toponym formation). Dialectal pair with A-JE /ʾaye/ (Thera) and I-JA /ʾiya/ (Knossos): spelling variation may reflect regional vowel shifts across Phaistos, Thera, and Eastern Crete, parallel to the JA-SA-SA-RA-ME / A-SA-SA-RA-ME dialectal split.

entries.meaning: farmer, plowman (recipient)
entries.note: HT 91 opens with I-KA over grain and small rations of oil, olives, figs and wine; HT 102 I-KA 5 (KA dotted) in a personnel total (KU-RO 1060). Akk. ikkaru 'farmer', Heb. ʾikkār, Syr. ʾakkārā; geminate and final r unwritten. Rival: the personal name Ikkaru (ORACC QPN).

entries.meaning: at the horn / promontory (toponym?)
entries.note: HT90 (Haghia Triada): heads GRA 20, OLE+DI 3 distribution. Skeleton i-k-r-n—initial I- could be locative prefix ("at/in"). If √q-r-n, reads as "at the horn"—a promontory toponym. Alternatively a personal name built on √q-r-n. The k-r-n element echoes KA-RO-NA on HT11a. || If I- is a preposition, its noun is genitive *qarni*, not -NA (Fischer 2002, §292); the toponym reading avoids this.

entries.meaning: behold, the reverence of… (broken)

cognates.Proto-Semitic: *yarVʾ- 'to fear, be afraid, revere' (cf. Ugaritic yrʾ DUL 976, Hebrew yārēʾ HALOT 432)
cognates.Hebrew: hēn yirʾat (הֵן יִרְאַת) "behold, the fear of" (Job 28:28); yārēʾ (יָרֵא) "to fear, revere" (HALOT 432); yirʾā (יִרְאָה) "fear, reverence, awe"

entries.note: AP Za 2 .2 I-NA-JA-RE-TA[ ]QA; no divider follows TA, and the word may run on across the lacuna. If it ends at TA, hinna yirʾat… 'behold, the reverence of…' (Job 28:28; di Mino, Ya Diktu), with I-NA- as in I-NA-JA-PA-QA hinna yapqaḥ (PK Za 11). Rival: a toponym.

entries.meaning: my Anat—theonym plus 1cs -ī; proposed "She Who Answers" (√ʿ-n-y)

cognates.Ugaritic: ʿnt /ʿanatu/ "Anat"; syllabic ᵈa-na-tu₄ = /ʿanatu/; btlt ʿnt "the young woman Anat"
cognates.Hebrew: ʿAnāt (עֲנָת) in Shamgar ben Anath (Judg 3:31); Beth-Anath (Josh 19:38); Anathoth (Jer 1:1)
cognates.Egyptian: ꜥntjt "Anat" (NK warrior goddess, adopted from Canaan)
cognates.Amorite (Mari): Ḫanat (cult goddess at Mari, early 2nd millennium, with initial ḫ- instead of ʿ-)

entries.note: IOZa6 position 2. The vessel is chipped, but the complete group I-NA-TA-I-ZU-DI-SI-KA has no internal lacuna. Proposed segmentation: I-NA-TA-I + ZU-DI + SI-KA, 'my Anat, Breast-Who-Gives-Drink.' Initial I may be laryngeal-bearing rather than a separate particle: Ugaritic has three vowel-conditioned aleph signs (Huehnergard 2012, 21), and syllabic Ugaritic writes ᵈa-na-tu₄ for /ʿanatu/ and ša-i for /šāʿi/ (Huehnergard 2008, 18 n. 78, 208, 249). This is an orthographic parallel, not proof of the Linear A value; final I is tentatively the 1cs suffix -ī. IOZa8 is not counted: ]A-NA-TI-*301-WA-JA[ is broken at both edges.

entries.meaning: my Anat, Breast-Who-Gives-Drink—theonym plus compound divine epithet

cognates.Ugaritic: ṯd "breast" (KTU 1.23: b-ṯd aṯrt 'at the breast of Athirat'; yiṯdyn 'they suckle')
cognates.Akkadian: šaqû "to give to drink, to irrigate" (CAD Š2 20)

entries.note: Complete, undivided IOZa6 group, tentatively segmented I-NA-TA-I + ZU-DI + SI-KA. Ugaritic btlt ʿnt 'the young woman Anat' (KTU 1.3 III 11; Huehnergard 2012, 86) and Middle Babylonian Ištar-ṣēri provide deity-plus-epithet controls. ZU-DI = ṯudī 'breast'; SI-KA = šiqā 'she who gives drink.' KTU 1.23 has b-ṯd aṯrt, 'at the breast of Athirat,' supplying the same divine nursing context. The segmentation and exact vocalization remain project hypotheses.

entries.meaning: Who Gives Drink (proposed second member of a divine epithet; participial/verbal noun of √š-q-y)

cognates.Hebrew: hišqā (הִשְׁקָה) "to give drink, to water" (HALOT 1640); šiqqūy (שִׁקּוּי) "drink, watering"; mašqeh (מַשְׁקֶה) "cupbearer, drink"
cognates.Akkadian: šaqû "to give to drink, to irrigate" (CAD Š2 20); šāqû "cupbearer"
cognates.Arabic: saqā "to water, give drink" (BK 1 1076); sāqī "cupbearer"; siqāya "the providing of water" (Q 9:19 siqāyat al-ḥājj)

entries.note: Ritual homograph, kept separate from administrative SI-KA √š-k-n (HT nodules, KH5). In the undivided IO Za 6 group I-NA-TA-I-ZU-DI-SI-KA, it is tentatively segmented after ZU-DI and read as the second member of ṯudī-šiqā, "Breast-Who-Gives-Drink." The root and divine-epithet syntax are Semitically plausible, but Linear A supplies neither a divider before SI-KA nor independent confirmation of this vocalization.

entries.meaning: in the presence of

cognates.Hebrew: pānīm (פָּנִים) 'face, presence' (Gen 32:31, Exod 33:14–15, Lev 1:3–4, Ps 19:15, Mal 1:8); lipnê (לִפְנֵי) 'before the face of' = standard cult-approach formula; √p-n-y 'to turn, face'
cognates.Ugaritic: pnm 'face, presence' (DUL 666); pn ilm 'face of the gods' in ritual texts
cognates.Akkadian: pānu 'face, front, presence' (CAD P 92); ina pāni 'before, in the presence of'
cognates.Arabic: fanā' (فناء) 'courtyard, forecourt'; related to approaching a presence

entries.note: Four complete attestations occur at three peak-sanctuary sites (Iouktas, Kophinas, Vrysinas), with damaged sequences at Troullos (TLZa1 […]NA-MA) and Apodoulou and only I-PI[ preserved at the broken end of PKZa8. The PKZa8 fragment supports membership in this formula family by position but does not attest a complete standalone I-PI or the restoration I-PI-NA-MA by itself. In APZa2, I-PI-NA-MA reaches a broken edge and no following divider is preserved; it therefore supports recurrence of the sequence but not its completeness or complement there. Skeleton pnm compares with Hebrew pānīm and Ugaritic pnm 'face, presence.' Biblical cultic language pairs approach before the divine presence with acceptance (Lev 1:3–4; Ps 19:15; Mal 1:8), providing a structural comparison for I-PI-NA-MA beside the proposed √r-ṣ-y verb in the fuller formula. The precise preposition and vowels remain reconstructed. PI writes pin- against Hebrew pānīm and Akkadian pānu: one root, a different vowel, as the cognate languages show among themselves, e.g. PS #3001 *zVrVḳ- 'blue, bright (of the eyes)', Akkadian zarriqu (CAD Z 69), Syriac zārqā (Payne Smith 121), Arabic zurqa, azraq. Hebrew shifted *a > *i more than once (Suchard 2020, 189). The noun's own vowel varies: Punic writes Tinnit's epithet pn bʿl as Θινιθ-Φανεβαλ and Θεννειθ-Φενηβαλ (Krahmalkov 2000, 398, 495), and SED reconstructs *yad- 'hand', of the same noun pattern as *pan-, 'with a variant *id- … probably for PS too' (SED I, p. CXXX). Davis 2026 instead proposes the functional gloss 'a favor/blessing' (in Salgarella & Petrakis eds., The Wor(l)ds of Linear A, pp. 43–60).

entries.meaning: face, presence (of)—expanded variant of I-PI-NA-MA

cognates.Hebrew: pānīm (פָּנִים) 'face, presence' (Gen 32:31, Exod 33:14–15, Lev 1:3–4, Ps 19:15, Mal 1:8); lipnê (לִפְנֵי) 'before the face of' = standard cult-approach formula; √p-n-y 'to turn, face'
cognates.Ugaritic: pnm 'face, presence' (DUL 666); pn ilm 'face of the gods' in ritual texts
cognates.Akkadian: pānu 'face, front, presence' (CAD P 92); ina pāni 'before, in the presence of'
