cognates.Arabic: fanā' (فناء) 'courtyard, forecourt'; related to approaching a presence

entries.note: Reduplicative expansion of I-PI-NA-MA (=ipinama, √p-n-m 'face/presence', PROBABLE). Co-occurs with the core libation formula (A-TA-I-*301-WA-E, SA-SA-RA-ME) on Palaikastro stone vessels (PKZa10, PKZa11). Reading inherits from I-PI-NA-MA. || COGNATES: those of I-PI-NA-MA, whose reading this spelling shares.

entries.meaning: section heading over mixed commodities
entries.note: Heads a mixed commodity section on both tablets: HT 44a I-QA-*118 · GRA, OLE+KI, OLE+U, OLE+RA, OLIV, NI, VIN; HT 131a I-QA-*118 GRA 58, OLE 12½, *304 12¾. If *118 = ṭa, cf. Arabic iqṭaʿ, imperative of √q-ṭ-ʿ 'cut, divide', with final ʿ unwritten. Weak point: *118 = ṭa is speculative. Rivals: a personal or institutional name. Two attestations.

entries.meaning: goddess; rival ʾila 'god'
entries.note: HT Wa 1006–1013: eight sealings bearing only I-RA₂, in two hands (scribes 52 and 53), from one deposit, Portico 11 and Room 13, LM IB. One context. I = /ʾi/, RA₂ = /la/. PS *ʾil- 'god', feminine *ʾilat- 'goddess' (Akk. ilat, Ug. ilt), final -t unwritten. Rival: masculine ʾila 'god', the Amorite name element *ilāh, almost always first in a name (Huffmon 1965, 165: I-la-sa-lim, Sa-mu-ū-i-la). || Huehnergard: Ug il /ʾilu/ "god; El (supreme deity)"; Biradical qil nominal. Pl. ilm /ʾilūma/. BH cognate: ʾēl "God, El" (Canaanite Shift ī > ē) (Huehnergard 2012, p. 41, §II.F)
entries.phonological_notes: I = /ʾi/ (initial laryngeal). RA₂ = /la/ (CONFIRMED). Quiescent feminine -t not written—NWS ʾilāt → ʾilā in absolute state.

entries.meaning: O Diqqitu! (vocative invocation of the proposed goat-goddess Diqqitu)

cognates.Ugaritic: dqt 'female goat, young she-goat' (DUL 280); theonym Diqatu attested in offering lists (KTU 1.148:3)
cognates.Hebrew: Not directly attested as theonym; cf. se'îrāh (שְׂעִירָה) 'she-goat' and se'îrîm (שְׂעִירִים) 'goat-demons' (Lev 17:7, 2 Chr 11:15)
cognates.Akkadian: diqāru 'cooking pot' (unrelated); goat-deity pattern parallels Amurrite theophoric names
cognates.Arabic: No direct reflex; goat-deity pattern preserved in Yazidi Melek Tawus traditions

entries.note: Peak sanctuary libation formula position 2. Syllabary spells DI-KI-TU (/diktu/), not Greek Δίκτη (Dikte)—the -TU vowel is explicit. JA- = vocative particle ya-. The mountain-goddess is named at position 2 as the vocative addressee of the self-positioning verb at position 1 (ʾata-inawaya 'I make myself a dwelling')—the worshipper settles before the deity. Pattern: each peak sanctuary invokes a sacred mountain-deity (Diktu at Iouktas/Palaikastro, Ida at Kophinas/Syme) || ASTOUR ETYMOLOGY: Ugaritic dqt 'female head of small cattle for sacrifice' (Gordon UT §19.695), pronounced *daqqatu/*diqqatu. dqt appears as a divine name in a Ugaritic god-list (Astour, 'New Evidence for the Semitic Derivation of the Greek Name of the Mountain Dikte,' 1966). Hesiod (Theog. 481–482 [West]) calls the same mountain Αἰγαίῳ ἐν ὄρει, Aigaion oros ('Goat's Mountain')—a Graeco-Semitic onomastic doublet. Egyptian scribal list of Amenhotep III spells it Di-qa- with determinative 'high' (Astour, 'Aegean Place Names,' 1966). Clay goat figurines are the most common votive offering at peak sanctuaries || GREEK RECEPTION: Amalthea, the goat who nursed infant Zeus in the Dictaean Cave—demotion from sovereign deity to wet-nurse || DIALECT: Variant A-DI-KI-TE(-TE) at Palaikastro shows the split: -TU (Iouktas, standard) vs -TE (Palaikastro, Proto-Phoenician). Vocative form JA-DI-KI-TE-TE attested on PKZa15 (JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-DU-PU₂-RE 'O Diktēt of the sanctuary') and PKZa8 (JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-*307-PU₂-RE, same compound with *307=DUBUR logogram)
entries.source: di Mino; Astour 1966 (New Divine Names, Aegean Place Names)

entries.meaning: personal name: Amorite-type yaqtul name + feminine -at (cf. Yadwiratum, Gelb 1980, no. 3209; Ya-du-ra-an, Ya-du-ri-im, Huffmon 1965, 38)

cognates.Amorite: JA-DWIR-AT-UM Yadwiratum (Gelb 1980, no. 3209); JA-DWIR-UM, JA-DWIR-I, JA-DWIR-AN (nos. 3210–3214); Ya-du-ra-an, Ya-du-ri-im (Huffmon 1965, 38); element jadūr (Gelb glossary)

entries.note: Verso of KN1 tablet. Format: WORD + E + QTY (105); the recto JA-KU-TI · E · 240 has the same layout, so both are names. Not 'I purified': a ya- prefix cannot carry a perfect person suffix (Fischer 2002, §§207, 211). ya- patterns 'figure almost exclusively in animal, plant, and personal names' (Fischer 2002, §66d). JA-DU-RA-TI = Yadurat-i matches feminine Amorite Yadwiratum except for the case ending.

entries.meaning: O Radiant One (vocative + elative of √n-w-r 'light'), divine epithet
entries.note: Hapax, SYZa4 word 2 (deity or recipient slot after the formula verb). RILA-S1 p. 84 reads JA-I-NWA-RO with RO underdotted, and rates GORILA's JA-I-NWA-ZA 'moins probable' (cf. SY Za 11; for ZA cf. KN Zf 31). Sign 3 is NWA (AB48) in both RILA-S1 lines, its only occurrence in the corpus; the value nwa is inherited from Linear B B48 (pe-ru-si-nwa ~ pe-ru-si-nu-wa). JA = vocative ya, as in JA-DI-KI-TU. I- writes the aleph, here ʾa (cf. I- for ʾu in I-KU-JU-TI); NWA writes the cluster /nw/; -RO writes final /-ru/. ʾanwaru is the ʾaqtal elative of √n-w-r: Arb. 'hāḏā ʾanwaru min ḏāka' (al-Zamakhsharī, Asās al-Balāgha, s.v. nwr). The epithet stands before PA₃-NI-WI 'the Builder', as Ugaritic pairs El's titles ṯr il dpid // bny bnwt 'Builder of Built (Ones)' (KTU 1.4 III 30–32; Smith & Pitard 2009, 39, 447). Same root as NU-RO nūr; Akkadian nawir 'is bright' of a god in OB names (Ilšu-nawir, Nawir-bēlī). Rival: ʾaṣwaru 'Fashioner' (√ṣ-w-r; Q 59:24 al-muṣawwir beside al-bāriʾ), which needs AB48 = a sibilant + w sign. The ya-inwā-ṣa reading stays withdrawn: it needed ZA. GORILA form JA-I-NWA-ZA.

entries.meaning: damaged theonym or divine epithet; possibly 'the Living One'
entries.note: Fragment entry, not a complete lexical word. In PKZa18 it follows the fully delimited I-DA on a ritual stone vessel; in SYZa8 it follows the recurring libation-formula opener A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA. Those two positions support classification as a theonym or divine epithet. Comparison with Semitic √ḥ-y-y 'live; life' permits the contextual restoration 'the Living One,' but both witnesses break immediately after the second JA, so the complete form, ending, and vocalization remain unknown. No HA sign precedes JA-JA. Aegean spelling nevertheless permits unexpressed /h/: Linear B e-qe-ta /hekwetās/ and e-qe-ta-i /hekwetāhi/, a-mo-ta /harmota/, and a-u-po-no /ahupnos/ all omit an etymological /h/ (Chadwick and Baumbach 1963, s.vv. ἕπομαι, ἅρμα, ἀ-/ἀν-). These Greek parallels establish an orthographic possibility only; they do not prove Semitic /ḥ/ here.
entries.phonological_notes: Only /ja-ja-/ is graphically preserved. HA is absent; an initial /ḥ/ and every sign after the second JA remain hypothetical.

entries.meaning: personal name, Amorite type (yaqtul of √m-w-t)

cognates.Amorite: IA-MU-UT-DA-DU, IA-MU-UT-LI-IM (Gelb 1980, nos. 3370, 3375)

entries.note: MA 2c: ]-U-NA-NA 3, then JA-MA-U-TI 6. Yamūt + -i, cf. Amorite JA-MWUT names (Gelb 1980, nos. 3370, 3375); MA-U writes the -mw- of *yamwut-, and -TI is the ending of JA-KU-TI and JA-DU-RA-TI. Weak point: MA-U for mū has no second case. Rival: JA- + Egyptian mꜣʿt 'Maat'. One attestation.

entries.meaning: He-from-the-hand-of-Re (Egyptian theophoric)
personal name ("he shines"—Amarna Yapaḫu)

cognates.Amarna: Yapaḫu (EA 297-300)—ruler of Gezer; cuneiform -ḫ- renders ʿ, √y-p-ʿ "he shines/appears"
cognates.Hebrew: yāpaʿ (יָפַע) "to shine forth" (Hiphil hôpîaʿ, Deut 33:2); PN Yāpîaʿ, king of Lachish (Josh 10:3)
cognates.Amorite: JPʿ "to shine" (B stem jāpaʿ); bare name IA-A-PA-AH Yaypaʿ at Mari, beside Yaypaʿ-Addu, Yaypaʿ-Lim (Gelb 1980, nos. 2792–2794, p. 595)

entries.note: ZA 4a .3-4 JA-PẠ 1̣[, PA dotted, numeral dotted and broken after (GORILA III 149). One witness. Standalone JA-PA on ZA4a (Zakros). Of 6 corpus occurrences of JA-PA, only ZA4a is standalone—extended forms JA-PA-QA, I-NA-JA-PA-QA, JA-PA-RA-JA-SE are likely different words/roots. Skeleton y-p maps to √y-p-ʿ with guttural ʿ dropping (standard in Linear A); the Amarna spelling Yapaḫu writes ʿ with cuneiform -ḫ-, and Hebrew preserves the PN as Yāpîaʿ (Josh 10:3). Amarna Yapaḫu (EA 297-300, ruler of Gezer) is the closest Bronze Age parallel; the Amorite name family Jāpuʿ/Jēpaʿ (√JPʿ) carries the same element. ARKH3b […]-JA-PI is a damaged ending and no longer supplies an independent inflectional parallel.

entries.meaning: he instructs/directs (impf. 3ms of √y-r-h)
entries.note: Standalone word on MMIIIB roundel at Knossos. Skeleton yr; compare yrḥ. || Huehnergard: Ug yrḥ /yariḥu/ or /yarīḥu/ "month; moon"; qatil nominal. Pl. /yarāḥūma/. byrḥ /bi-yarḥi/ "in the month" (prepositional). BH cognate: yāreᵃḥ "moon," yéraḥ "month" (Huehnergard 2012, pp. 42, 87)

entries.meaning: personal name, '(DN) is exalted' (Amorite type)

cognates.Amorite: JA-RWIM names, IA-RI-IM-LI-IM Yarim-Lim, IA-RI-IM-D-IM (Gelb 1980, nos. 3432–3442)

entries.note: HT 87: JA-RE-MI 1 in a roster of men under *21F-TU-NE · MA-KA-RI-TE. Yarīm, the yaqtul of √r-w-m, a hypocoristic of the Amorite Yarim-DN names (Gelb 1980, nos. 3432–3442: Yarim-Lim, Yarim-Addu); cf. Heb. Yirmᵉyāhû. Weak point: RE for /ri/. Rival: √y-r-ḫ 'moon', the god Yariḫ (Huehnergard 2012, 42, 87). One attestation.

entries.meaning: righteous, upright (clipped form of yasaramu; may converge with *y-s "to heal" in onomastic contexts—cf. Greek ἰάομαι, Iāsōn, no secure IE etymology)
entries.note: 2 standalone attestations across 2 sites (Malia, Phaistos). MAZb8: bare JA-SA on a clay vessel. PH16b: JA-SA on a fragmentary lame. IOZa12 and SAMWa1 are excluded as the libation formula: IOZa12 = JA-SA-SA-RA-ME whole on one line (Karetsou, Godart & Olivier, Kadmos 24, 1985, 143); SAMWa1 = JA-SA SA-RA (syllable sequence JA-SA-SA-RA = formula without terminal -ME, on a nodule with TE 10 ¹⁄₁₆). Clipped form without mimation (-amu); functions as independent verbal adjective or epithet in short votive inscriptions. Huehnergard: /yušru/ 'uprightness' (yuCCu pattern); confirms adverbial accusative with -m || POLYSEMY HYPOTHESIS: LA sibilant merger (SA writes both /s/ and /š/) leaves standalone JA-SA ambiguous between √y-š-r 'righteous' and *y-s 'to heal.' Full formula JA-SA-SA-RA-ME locks to √y-š-r (7 CONFIRMED sites). Standalone JA-SA at Malia (MAZb8) or fragmentary Phaistos (PH16b) could in principle preserve the healer reading, but neither site has specific Iasion cult associations. The Samothrace attestation (SAMWa1), which would have been the strongest anchor for the healer hypothesis, is now identified as the formula. Greek ἰάομαι 'to heal' has no secure IE etymology (Beekes: possible substrate); Iāsōn and Iasion both derive from it (Astour, Hellenosemitica 276–282). NWS -ān agentive suffix (Gordon §155) would produce *yasā-ān > Iāsōn, parallel to Rpan (√r-p-ʾ + -ān, Astour 252). LB i-ja-te (iatēr 'surgeon') at Pylos confirms the root in Mycenaean but not the PN. Cf. SI-RU-TE polysemy (√š-r-t / √š-y-r)—same sibilant merger, same root convergence

entries.meaning: 'He hears'—yaqtal hypocoristic personal name with frozen nominative -ū

cognates.Hebrew: יִשְׁמָעֵאל (Yišmāʿēl / Ishmael) = "El hears"—√š-m-ʿ + ʾēl; שִׁמְעוֹן (Šimʿōn / Simeon) = "hearing"; שְׁמוּאֵל (Šəmūʾēl / Samuel) = "name/heard of El"
cognates.Ugaritic: yšmʿ—theophoric PN element in KTU personal names; šmʿ "to hear" in Ba'al cycle
cognates.Akkadian: šemû "to hear"; Šamû-Adda (EA 325) = "Addu has heard"—same root reversed
cognates.Punic: √š-m-ʿ in ŠMʿ-BʿL "Baal has heard" (Benz 1972); one of the productive PN roots in Carthaginian epigraphy
cognates.Amorite: Ya-ás-ma-ḫu-um, Yasmaḫ-Addu (Mari, APNM p. 132)

entries.note: Zakros wine allocation list (ZA15a, stone vessel). JA-SA-MU receives 5 units alongside SI-PI-KI and SA-MI-DA-E (both read as Semitic). Proto-NWS sibilant merger (SA writes both /s/ and /š/) leaves the reading ambiguous: *yasamu* (with sāmek) or *yašmuʿ* (with šīn + ʿayin dropping). √š-m-ʿ "to hear" is the strongest parse—most productive NWS theophoric root in this shape, and the guttural-dropping rule accounts for the missing final radical. The Ishmael parallel is direct: Yišmāʿēl = yišmaʿ + ʾēl "El hears"; JA-SA-MU is the bare verbal element without the deity complement—a standalone sentence name "he (the god) hears." This is the first Linear A attestation of √š-m-ʿ, one of the most productive NWS theophoric roots. Secondary parse: Ya-ʾAšmu, Eshmun hypocoristic (ʾŠMN → ʾŠM- short form)—less likely because ya- prefix is not standard for Punic ʾŠMN short forms (which use ʾŠM-, not *YŠM-). Huehnergard: infinitive replacing imperative /šamāʔu/ "hear!"; alternative parsing as jussive or infinitive-as-imperative. || The form fits the yaqtal theme-vowel class with frozen nominative *-ū, the citation form of an independent name (APNM pp. 104–15). Guttural-final root: cuneiform must write it (Ya-ás-ma-aḫ-{d}IM), Linear A must drop it—JA-SA-MU is the predicted Linear A shape of the Yašmaʿ hypocoristicon, APNM p. 132 Ya-ás-ma-ḫu-u[m]. Refines the earlier yaqtul parse (yašmuʿ); both are G imperfects with identical Linear A surface. Fourth data point for the Yašmaʿ type at Zakros, independent of WI-JA-SU-MA-TI-TI/yašmaṭu (HTZd157+156).

entries.meaning: righteous, upright (proposed adjective modifying A-NA-NE)
entries.note: PS #1446 *yašar- "straight, right." In KN Zc 7 the sequence is written continuously as JA-SA-RA-A-NA-NE; the proposed segmentation JA-SA-RA | A-NA-NE gives *yašara ḥanān*, "righteous grace." Because no divider marks the boundary on this inked vessel, both the segmentation and adjectival syntax remain provisional. A verbal jussive, "may she make right," is a possible rival but is not the preferred translation.

entries.meaning: line-broken first portion of JA-SA-SA-RA-ME / yaššaram 'uprightly; in righteousness'; not independently attested as a bare lemma
entries.note: IO Za 16, a fragmentary square serpentine libation table from the Iouktas peak sanctuary (HM 5317), reads JA-SA-SA-RA- / -ME across a line break without a divider. The break is word-internal, so this is evidence for JA-SA-SA-RA-ME /yaššaram/, not an independent bare lemma or divine epithet. PK Za 4 likewise preserves only A-SA-SA-RA-[ at a broken edge. Compare Amorite IA-SA-RA-AM (Gelb 1980, no. 3448).

entries.meaning: in righteousness indeed; uprightly indeed
entries.note: KN Za 10 writes JA-SA-SA-RA-MA / NA across the side break without a divider, so the sequence is one graphic word. Amorite IA-SA-RA-AM directly attests accusative /yašaram/ (Gelb 1980, no. 3448), permitting the Semitic manner accusative ‘uprightly, in righteousness.’ NA is provisionally an emphatic/topical clitic =na, compared with Ugaritic -n or -(Vn)na (Tropper §§89.1–2). No exact /yašaram=na/ is externally attested, and regular Semitic dual/plural endings do not produce -MA-NA. The former √m-n-y compound ‘righteous portion/Righteous Allotter’ is withdrawn.

entries.meaning: in righteousness (adverbial accusative in -am of √y-š-r; also 'righteously'); rival: substantivized "the upright/proper [thing]" in an object slot. Polysemic layer: masculine divine name Yasharam (Akk. Mīšarum, Phoen. Misor)

cognates.Hebrew: yāšār (יָשָׁר) 'upright, straight, righteous' (Deut 32:4, Ps 119:137, 1 Kgs 9:4, Prov 2:7); yōšer (יֹשֶׁר) 'uprightness, equity' (Ps 111:8, Prov 2:13); √y-š-r 'to be straight'; Yeshurun (יְשֻׁרוּן) poetic name for Israel = 'the upright one' (Deut 32:15, 33:5, 33:26, Isa 44:2); cf. Num 23:10 yĕšārīm (Balaam's pun on Yeshurun)
cognates.Ugaritic: yšr 'straight, upright' (DUL 928); yšr in ritual context = moral/cultic fitness
cognates.Akkadian: ešēru 'to be/go straight, prosper' (CAD E 354); išaru 'straight, just, normal'; mīšaru 'justice, equity' (CAD M/II 116)—Hammurabi's mīšarum edicts: royal debt-release decrees that 'set things straight'
cognates.Arabic: yasara (يسر) 'to be easy, smooth'; yasār 'ease, prosperity'

entries.note: √y-š-r 'to be straight, upright, righteous.' SA writes /š/ (cf. SA-SA-ME HT23a = sesame: LB sa-sa-ma, Ug. ššmn); SA-SA writes the geminate /šš/ (di Mino, Ya Diktu), not a shin marker; the same root takes one SA, with no gemination written, in JA-SA-RA (KNZc7) and I-MI-SA-RA (HT27a). Vowels: Amorite JAŠAR-AM, IA-SA-RA-AM (Gelb 1980, no. 3448), base *yašar-. Spelling encodes accusative -am: RA = /ra/ (not RU = /ru/ for nominative -um), ME = mimation. Primary reading: accusative *yaššaram* 'uprightly'; the long vowel of earlier *yašāram* is dropped for want of independent support. Amorite IA-SA-RA-AM is classed accusative (Gelb 1980, no. 3448). Davis and Thomas's 'offering' is a syntactic rival (object slot), not a lexical value. Davis 2026 functional gloss: "an offering/dedication" (in Salgarella & Petrakis eds., The Wor(l)ds of Linear A, pp. 43-60). Huehnergard: /yušru/ "uprightness" (yuCCu nominal pattern); confirms adverbial accusative with -m. PL Zf 1 preserves JA-SA-SA-RA followed only by a damaged vertical trace; [ME?] is a probable formulaic restoration, not an independent full attestation, and NE cannot be excluded. IO Za 2 preserves JA-SA-SA-RA-[, ME restored by GORILA (V 19), and IO Za 9 only ]JA-SA-SA-, RA-ME restored (V 33). PK Za 14 ends JA-SA-SA-[ at the broken edge (IV 40), probably the same word. Intact on IO Za 6 (V 25), PS Za 2 (IV 54) and TL Za 1 (IV 59). IO Za 12 has it whole on one line, second SA and ME dotted (Karetsou, Godart & Olivier, Kadmos 24, 1985, 143).

entries.meaning: O Šumāt! (vocative particle yā + proper name; possibly *šum- ‘name, posterity’ + plural *-āt)
entries.cognates: Amorite Šumat-Yaraḥ, Šumat-ʾIlī, Šumatān, and Šumatānum (Gelb 1980, AS 21, nos. 5581–5582, 5588–5589); Common Semitic *šum-/šim- ‘name’ and Amorite sum- ‘name (> posterity)’ (Huffmon 1965, pp. 247–249, 252).
entries.note: Segment JA | SU-MA-TU: JA = Semitic vocative yā, internally paralleling JA-DI-KI-TU /yā Diktu/ in the same formula position. Huffmon lists Amorite sumat- as an unexplained name element but reports Birot's proposal that it is a plural of sum- ‘name (> posterity)’; the resulting analysis is *šum- + *-āt → Šumāt. SU-MA-TU can write /šu-mā-t/, with TU carrying a dead vowel after final /t/ and vowel length unmarked. The derivation and the human or divine identity of the addressee remain uncertain. Amorite independently attests the element in Šumat-Yaraḥ, Šumat-ʾIlī, Šumatān, and Šumatānum (Gelb 1980, AS 21, nos. 5581–5582, 5588–5589; Huffmon 1965, pp. 57, 247–249, 252). Epigraphic caveat: GORILA V 64–65 and Davis read the following sign as OLIV, yielding yā Šumāt | OLIV 1; Metaxa-Muhly 1984 and Finkelberg 1990 read it as syllabic RE, which may extend the name.
entries.source: di Mino; Birot, TEM III, p. 29, apud Huffmon 1965, p. 252; Gelb 1980
entries.root_meaning: name, posterity (proposed Amorite plural; Birot, apud Huffmon 1965, p. 252)

entries.meaning: gentilic 'the Idaean' (of Mount Ida); rivals the personal name 'He knows' and the gentilic 'Judean'

cognates.Hebrew: yād 'hand', if Ida relates to *yad; for the rivals, Yĕdîʿăʾēl (יְדִיעֲאֵל), a y-d-ʿ name (1 Chr 11:45; 26:2), and yehūdī (יְהוּדִי) 'Judean'
cognates.Amorite: for the rival, JDʿ 'to know' as a name element (Gelb 1980, glossary); JADAʿ+JAT-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 3168)

entries.note: HT 8a: JE-DI OLE+KI 10, heading the list; HT 36: JE-DI GRA+QE 44½; HT 122b: JE-DI · *346 · VIR+[?], heading a roster of men; HT 140: JE-DI · OLE+KI 1½ in mid-line, damaged JE, with a sign possibly lost before it. A recipient on three tablets. Read as yedī 'the Idaean,' gentilic of Mount Ida; if Ida relates to Semitic *yad 'hand,' the Idaean Daktyls are 'fingers of the hand' (di Mino, Ya Diktu). Rivals: yēdīʿ 'he knows' as a personal name, with ʿ unwritten (Hebrew Yĕdîʿăʾēl, 1 Chr 11:45; Amorite JDʿ in names, Gelb 1980); yehūdī 'Judean', which leaves the ū of -hū- unwritten (U writes /hu/ in U-NA, so the expected spelling is JE-U-DI) and needs Judah, first attested under Tiglath-pileser III (c. 734 BCE), some 700 years after LM IB.

entries.meaning: He gave (PN, qatal 3ms of √y-t-n 'to give')—straight theophoric truncation: Yatana-DN 'DN-gave,' same formation as Hebrew Nāṯān, Ugaritic Yattin-Haddu, Amorite Yattan-Dagan
entries.note: Skeleton ytn. It stands in a name or title slot, not a verb's: it may be a theophoric PN element. Huehnergard: G /yatana/ 3ms, prefix /yittinu/ (n-assimilation); BH nātan. || Not 'she gave': NWS 3fs prefix-forms take t-, never y- (she gave = ta-ttin/tētin; qatal 3fs yātinat), and a single sign JE cannot encode a /ye/-feminine vs /ya/-masculine switch. JE-TA-NA occurs once, HTWa1020; HT88 has none. Gloss describes the name's formation, not the bearer's gender. || JE conventionally gives /ye/, but the Semitic reconstruction demands /ya/—the JE sign likely covers /ya/ here, the way Linear B je covers both values. In Ugaritic the root is ytn (not n-t-n as in Hebrew), so the 3ms perfect is yatana. Masculine counterpart of A-TA-NA (ʾAtanā > Athena), which is the feminine form of the same root with regular I-y > ʾ weakening. The root has 5 entries in the lexicon.

entries.meaning: wine-lords, wine-stewards (personnel category)
entries.note: Compound: yīnu (wine, √y-y-n) + mārē (lords/sons, √m-r-y). Appears exclusively on wine distribution tablets at Zakros (3× with quantities 6, 13, 20). Functions as a personnel category label alongside personal names and SI-PI-KI 'pressings'. Wine-steward officials who administer palace wine allocations. The main support for *28B = JI, a proposed value; WE (wēnu-mārē, wēnu < *wayn) reads the word as well as JI. Negri (SMEA 43/1, 2001, 82) assigns i-nu-ma-re to personal names, from its recurring slot beside SI-PI-KI.

entries.meaning: food, provisions (section heading)
entries.note: Heads ZA6b's first section over GRA+PA 50¼, VIN+RA 40, VIN+KA 10; *312-TA₂ heads the second. KU-JU writes /kul/ (JU = /lu/, as in KU-RE-JU); initial I- writes /ʾu/. The corpus token is I-KU-JU-TI-*28B: the word spans a fragment join, with a gap at the crack in the diplomatic copy (GORILA III 158–159), and *28B is taken as a separate sign before GRA+PA. Cf. AB 28 (I), a different sign, as a single or transaction sign before GRA+PA (Salgarella 2020, 73 n. 55; Steele 2024, 58).

entries.meaning: until, as far as (preposition)

cognates.Ugaritic: ʿd /ʿad(ē)/ 'up to, as far as, until' (Huehnergard 2012)
cognates.Hebrew: ʿad (עַד) 'until'; ʿad ʾăšer dāq 'until it was fine' (Exod 32:20, Deut 9:21)

entries.note: Opens register .2 of KNZc6 after QI-TI-RI and governs DA-KI-TI: ʿadi daqqati '(ground) until fine', the Hebrew ʿad … dāq of grinding to powder. Evans (PoM I 615 n. 1) reports a dividing mark before DA, which GORILA IV 121 does not print. Initial A- writes ʿa- (ʿ drops).

entries.meaning: fine (powder), ground fine

cognates.Hebrew: daq, f. daqqâ (דַּקָּה) 'fine, crushed': qəṭōret sammîm daqqâ 'finely ground sweet incense' (Lev 16:12); hādēq 'very fine', of the sanctuary incense (Exod 30:36)

entries.note: KNZc6 register .2, after QI-TI-RI 'my incense' and A-DI 'until': incense ground fine, the Hebrew qəṭōret … daqqâ (Lev 16:12). Written as one unit with PA-KU 'flask' (DA-KI-TI-PA-KU, closed by a divider before NI-JA-NU). QI-TI-RI is masculine, so DA-KI-TI is a noun 'fine powder', not an adjective agreeing with it. Alternative: genitive of the divine name, 'of Daqqatu' (Ugaritic dqt, DN 'the Little One', CUC), cf. JA-DI-KI-TU and A-DI-KI-TE-TE. Younger reads A-DI-DA-KI-TI-PA-KU as a muddled A-DI-KI-TE. SKOZc2 ]DE-KI-TI[ (Skoteino cave, painted vessel) may be the same word, broken on both sides and not counted.

entries.meaning: thin bread, wafers (qualifier of *309C KIKKARU)

cognates.Arabic: ruqāq (الرُقاق) 'thin bread'; ruqāqa 'a single thin, round cake of bread' (Lane 1131)
cognates.Hebrew: rāqîq (רָקִיק) 'wafer', beside kikkar leḥem 'round of bread' (Exod 29:23)
cognates.Akkadian: raqqatu D '(a type of bread)', Emar (CAD R 171)

entries.note: TY 2 .5 *309C-[?]-RU-KA 30, one of eight qualifiers joined to *309; the AB53 hook on top of *309C is unread, and if it is a syllabogram RU-KA is not the whole qualifier. RU-KA writes ruqāq, the final q unwritten. Exod 29:23 sets rāqîq beside kikkar leḥem, the pairing TY 2 shows; Akk. raqqatu, a bread at Emar (CAD R 171). Sign order follows GORILA's facsimile, RU over KA (GORILA I 324–325). Depends on *309 = KIKKARU, unconfirmed. Rival: a place or recipient name, as the other qualifiers may be. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name ('Where are you?')

cognates.Amorite: ʾAjak-u, written A-JA-KU (Gelb 1980, no. 320); ʾAjak-um, A-IA-KU-UM (no. 300); the ʾAja- 'where?' names, nos. 285–319

entries.note: KN Zf 13, the last four signs of an undivided 19-sign spiral, ending at the centre of the bezel; the start of the word is not marked and KU is underdotted (GORILA IV 152–153). Amorite ʾAjak-u (Gelb 1980, no. 320). Rival: Akk. ajakku, a temple structure (CAD A/1, 224–25).

entries.meaning: personal name ('the Ka is praised'—Egyptian theophoric); rival kabsi 'young ram'
entries.note: Contingent on *314 = ḤA. Phaistos roundel (MMII), alongside *320 || EGYPTIAN READING: kꜣ 'ka, spirit/vital force' + ḥs.j 'praised one, favored one'—standard Middle Kingdom theophoric name pattern. Phonetic mapping: KA = kꜣ (velar onset), ḤA = ḥs (pharyngeal onset), SI = .j (adjectival suffix) || Egyptian contact with Crete in MMII is well attested. Less phonetically exact than PI-ḤA (Luwian) or RA-ḤA-RA (Egyptian), but the name pattern is standard || All three signs whole and undotted (GORILA II 94). Rival with *314 = bu, a PU₂ variant: kabsi 'young ram', Akk. kabsu (CAD K 23), Heb. kebeś, Arb. kabš (HALOT 459), a roundel commodity.

entries.meaning: Cadmos + -ān suffix
the Canaanite (ethnonymic designation)
entries.note: KHWc2005 Khania roundel, standalone. -NI-TI = nisbe gentilic suffix -ītī. Exact morphological parallel to DU-RU-WI = ḏu-lēwī 'the Levite.' ʿayin guttural-transparent. Hebrew כְּנַעֲנִי kĕnaʿanī, Akkadian Kinaḫḫi, El Amarna 'Canaan.' Administrative roundel context—ethnic designation for trade/personnel tracking.

entries.meaning: emmer (cereal grain)
entries.note: Skeleton knt. Second cereal term alongside CONFIRMED KU-NI-SU (k-n-š "emmer wheat"). It stands in a name slot, where commodity terms often appear on ledgers.

entries.meaning: entity, institution, or settlement; perhaps village
entries.note: Six Haghia Triada attestations. First word on HT 102 (SA-RA₂ GRA 976 follows; KU-RO 1060), HT 94a (VIR+[?] 62 follows on the line; KU-RO 110), HT 6a (divider, then DA-TA-RA) and HT 105 (broken after PA; VIR+[?] 234 below). An entry with ½ on HT 8b and HT 140; KA-PA-QE 5¾ on HT 6a. Hebrew and Aramaic kĕpar 'village', with final /r/ unwritten; the ½ entries make an institution or entity the rival to a place. Rival: Akkadian gabbu 'all' (Gordon, via Rendsburg 1996, 38), spelt ka-pa-šu-nu and qa-pa-šu-ma at Nuzi, where it follows a total of men (Gordon 1934, 20 §100). It fits the heads of HT 94a and HT 105, but not the ½ entries, and HT 94a closes with KU-RO.

entries.meaning: great one (Kabeiri divine epithet); rival kōper 'ransom'

cognates.Akkadian: kabru 'fat, thick, large' (CAD K 22); also kuppuru 'to purify' (CAD K 178) if √k-p-r
cognates.Hebrew: kabbîr 'mighty, great' (HALOT 458); also kōper 'ransom' (HALOT 495), kippēr 'to atone' (HALOT 493) if √k-p-r
cognates.Arabic: kabīr 'great' (Lane 2585); also kafara 'to cover, conceal' (Lane 2620) if √k-p-r

entries.note: HT 115a .5 KA-PO-RU 1, whole and undotted, one of several sign groups with small quantities (NA-*21F-NE-MI-NA 1, SE-KU-TU ½, PA-RA-NE 1) on a palimpsest side (GORILA I 189). kabīru 'great one' (b→p). Rival: √k-p-r, Hebrew kōper 'ransom' (HALOT 495), kippēr 'to atone' (HALOT 493), Akkadian kuppuru 'to purify' (CAD K 178); both roots give the skeleton kpr. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name/gentilic
entries.note: Hapax recipient of ¼ on HT98a. KA-RI-IN-I = karīn+ī, contingent on *310 = IN; no root identified.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'horn'
entries.note: HT11a (Haghia Triada, Villa Magazine, LMIB): A-RU-RA-[·] ]3, KA-RO-NA 2, *322-RI 1, KU-RO 10, three entries in one total, so a recipient. KA = /qa/ under Gordon's stop neutralization. Horn names are common across Semitic: Amorite Qar-ni-li-im (Huffmon 1965, 58; element qarn- 'horn, strength', 259); Middle Babylonian Qarni-Ana (ORACC P503266), Middle Assyrian Qarna-Adad (ORACC P282214), Neo-Assyrian Qarnaya (ORACC P336263); Hebrew Qeren-happûk, a daughter of Job (Job 42:14).

entries.meaning: carafe, drinking vessel (Akkadian karpatu; Ugaritic krpn)
entries.note: Gordon's etymology holds via intervocalic lenition. Gordon (§163) read ka-ro-pa = karpu (Akkadian karpatu, one of the most common vessel terms in cuneiform). PA₃=/ba/ shifts surface skeleton k-r-p → k-r-b, but the underlying PS root √k-r-p is preserved: simplex *p→b is regular intervocalic lenition in Minoan phonological adaptation (V_V environment: /o_a/). Preceded by *416-VS vessel ideogram on HT31 (qty 10). Part of Gordon's HT31 vessel quartet (§163). Stieglitz (1971) independently confirmed the identification citing Gordon and the Akkadian/Ugaritic cognates. Rendsburg (forthcoming Ugaritic Dictionary) cites 'Min. ka-ro-pà (HT 31.3) (Gordon, EML, 26, 30, 39; Stieglitz 1971)' as cognate to Ugaritic krpn 'carafe, goblet, flagon.' The Ugaritic evidence (6 passages: El blessing Kirta, ʿAnat drinking wine, Baʿal's feast) narrows the semantic range to a drinking vessel, not a generic pot. The Ugaritic form krpn carries an affirmative -n suffix (Dahood 1965) absent from the Minoan bare root karp-.
entries.source: Gordon 1966 §163; Stieglitz (Kadmos 10, 1971, 110); Rendsburg (Ugaritic Dictionary, forthcoming); di Mino

entries.meaning: Kothar (divine craftsman god)

cognates.Hebrew: kōšēr (כּוֹשֵׁר) "skill, success" (Eccl 2:21, 4:4; BDB 507); keter (כֶּתֶר) "crown" (Esth 1:11, 2:17; Kabbalistic Keter, highest sefirah)

entries.note: KH41 (Khania, clay tablet, LMIB): 3·KA-TA-RE·[break]. Skeleton k-t-r. Number preceding divine name follows HT86a allocation pattern || KOTHAR VS QOTAR PHONOLOGY: Initial KA (not QA—Q-series available and used for √q-ṭ-r in QI-TI-RI), medial TA (not *118/ṬA—emphatic available for /ṭ/) favor √k-ṯ-r (Kothar) over √q-ṭ-r (incense). The ṯ→t neutralization is expected: no /ṯa/ sign exists in the grid (ZU covers only /ṯu/), so TA is the default approximation. Khania = western Crete's second major archive with strong Near Eastern exchange evidence || ROOT MERGER HYPOTHESIS: √k-t-r (crown) and √k-ṯ-r (craft) may derive from biconsonantal *K-T via sibilant extension, parallel to √k-n-s / √k-n-sh. LA TA neutralizes ṯ/t, so KA-TA-RE may preserve the pre-split form || One attestation, broken at both ends (]KA-TA-RE[).

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Disk, Round loaf'

cognates.Amorite: KAKKAR-I (KA-KA-RI), personal name (Gelb 1980, AS 21, no. 3957)
cognates.Akkadian: kakkaru 'metal disk (a talent); round loaf' (CAD K 49)

entries.note: HT 94b under KI-RO: TU-MA 1, PA-TA-NE 1, DE-DI 1, KE-KI-RU 1, SA-RU 1, KU-RO 5, one unit each with no commodity sign: a name. The noun kakkaru 'disk, round loaf' (CAD K 49) as a name, as Amorite KAKKAR-I (Gelb AS 21 no. 3957). Weak points: KE and KI for ka-ka. Rival: a title. KI-KI-RA-JA (HT 85b) is on the same root. One attestation.

entries.meaning: lyre (Hebrew kinnōr כִּנּוֹר)
entries.note: Qty 1 on inventory tablet. KI-IN-RE = ki+in+re → kinnār. Anchor reading for *310=/in/. Hebrew kinnōr is the ancient stringed instrument played by David.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Dark' (√ḳ-d-r 'be dark'; cf. Hebrew Qēdār)

cognates.Hebrew: Qēdār (קֵדָר) 'Kedar', son of Ishmael, an Arabian people (H6938); qādar (קָדַר) 'be dark, mourn' (H6937)

entries.note: PREFIXED FORM: A-KI-DA-RO (KH Wa 1002, Khania)—A- as NWS article *ha-* or prosthetic aleph on commodity noun: *ʾa-qidrū* 'the earthenware.' || Personal name Qidaru, √ḳ-d-r 'be dark'; rival PS *ḳidr- 'earthenware' (Arabic qidr, Hebrew qǝdērā, Aramaic qidrā). Both attestations are lists of people: HT117a's SA-TA roster counts KU-KU-DA-RA, KO-SA-I-TI, DA-MI-NU, DA-NE-KU-TI and KI-DA-RO once each; HT47a lists KU-PA₃-NA-TU 20, DU 20, PI 10, KI-DA-RO 5. Cf. Hebrew Qēdār, Ishmael's son and an Arabian people (Gen 25:13), from qādar 'be dark, mourn'.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'protection (of the god)' (Akk. kidinnu)

cognates.Akkadian: kidinnu "divine protection"; OB personal names Ki-din-Amurrum, Ki-di-nu-um (CAD K 342–343)

entries.note: HT93a .3 KI-DI-NI 5 J H, in a grain list of recipients with DI-RI-NA, A-SE, SA-RA₂ and QA-QA-RU. Akkadian kidinnu 'divine protection', in Old Babylonian personal names Ki-din-Amurrum and Ki-di-nu-um (CAD K 342–343). Rival: kittini 'linen' (Akk. kitû, Ug. ktn), which needs DI for ti and a textile in a grain list. One attestation.

alternative_readings.note: linen: Akk. kitû "flax, linen" (CAD K 473); Ug. ktn "a type of tunic" (DULAT 464); Heb. kuttōnet (Gen 3:21; 37:3). Needs DI for ti and a textile entry in a grain list.

entries.meaning: priests (plural + mimation)
entries.note: h guttural-transparent; Heb. kōhănīm; ZA5a Zakros. Medial h drops, same pattern as RA-ME /raḥmē/, E-NA-SI /naḥāši/, JA-JA /ḥayyā/. Huehnergard: CāCiCu pattern /kāhinu/, pl. /kāhinūma/; BH kōhēn exact cognate.

entries.meaning: possibly garden/orchard; alternatively liquid bitumen
entries.note: KI-RA occurs on HT103 with 5½ and opens ZA8 before A-TA-RE, which is followed by NI ‘figs’ ½. The former gloss ‘balance’ was inferred from resemblance to KI-RO, but HT103 provides no balancing equation: NI 40 is not marked as a total, and no KU-RO occurs. Akkadian kirû(m) ‘garden, orchard’ (base kiri-; Huehnergard 1997, 126) fits the horticultural contexts, although KI-RA does not reproduce its inflection exactly. Akkadian qīru ‘liquid bitumen,’ attested syllabically as qi-ra, is formally closer but requires KI to represent /qi/ and fits ZA8 less well. ‘Garden/orchard’ is the preferred candidate; the entry remains unproved.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA I 170–171; Huehnergard 1997, 126; ORACC qīru attestations

entries.meaning: Kret (eponym of Crete)
entries.note: Cf. Ugaritic Epic of Kret (KTU 1.14-16). Corpus form uses TA₂ sign variant (AB66), distinct from plain TA (AB59) used in the gentilic KI-RE-TA-NA. The Semitic verb √k-r-t 'to cut, make a covenant' has PS *t (plain dental) across all branches: Akkadian karātu, Ugaritic krt (with t, not ṯ—Ugaritic distinguishes them), Hebrew כָּרַת with ת (taw). PS *ṯ → Hebrew š, so if the root had *ṯ, Hebrew would show *כרש not כרת. The TA₂ spelling on Crete may therefore point to: (1) a Cretan dialectal pronunciation preserving a phonetic distinction (interdental, aspirated, or palatalized) in the island's own name that was normalized to plain /t/ in foreign traditions; or (2) a pre-Semitic substrate toponym with an original non-dental stop that was later folk-etymologically conflated with √k-r-t 'to cut/covenant.' The scribes on Crete—who knew the local pronunciation—used the marked sign; Ugaritic and Hebrew scribes, hearing a foreign name, fitted it to their standard /t/. RE/RI alternation with KI-RI-TA₂. || Huehnergard: Ug krt /kirta/ "Kirta (royal protagonist PN)"; lkrt /li-kirta/ "belonging to the story of Kirta." Huehnergard rejects vocalization "keret" as non-Ugaritic [p. 68]. BH cognate: kərētī "Kerethite" (but vocalization differs) (Huehnergard 2012, pp. 60, 68) || Corpus spelling KI-RE-TA₂ (GORILA, HT 85b and 129).

entries.meaning: Cretan (gentilic: 'of Crete')
entries.note: Cf. Hebrew Kerethite (כְּרֵתִי). -ān gentilic suffix. 4 tablets, all HT. See also KI-RE-TA₂ (2×) and KI-RI-TA₂ (2×) short name forms. || Huehnergard: Ug krt /kirta/ "Kirta (royal protagonist PN)"; lkrt /li-kirta/ "belonging to the story of Kirta." Huehnergard rejects vocalization "keret" as non-Ugaritic [p. 68]. BH cognate: kərētī "Kerethite" (but vocalization differs) (Huehnergard 2012, pp. 60, 68)

entries.meaning: Kret (variant spelling)
entries.note: Variant spelling of KI-RE-TA₂ with RE→RI vowel alternation. Both tablets pair it with SA-RA₂ in an identical administrative template; SA-RA₂ is read as a recipient or institution, provisionally the queen or royal establishment. Corpus form uses TA₂. Huehnergard gives Ugaritic krt /kirta/ 'Kirta' and lkrt /li-kirta/ 'belonging to the story of Kirta,' while rejecting 'keret' as a Ugaritic vocalization (2012: 60, 68). Biblical Hebrew kərētī 'Kerethite' differs in vocalism.

entries.meaning: owed, outstanding balance (deficit)—transaction term heading deficit sections
entries.note: Function CONFIRMED from independent arithmetic and structural controls: (A) corpus complementarity—KU-RO functions as 'total' and KI-RO as 'owed/outstanding'; KI-RA is excluded because its relationship to KI-RO remains unproved; (B) HT15 arithmetic forcing case—684 + 570 = 1254 ≠ 400, so KI-RO 400 cannot be a total, but reads cleanly as 'owed/outstanding 400'; (C) structure—KI-RO heads sections that END in KU-RO with exact sums (HT88: six 1s = KU-RO 6 ✓; HT117a: ten × 1 = KU-RO 10 ✓; HT94b: five × 1 = KU-RO 5 ✓); a total cannot head a list. HT1 supplies a further control: KI-RO 197 is not the total of the four following quantities, which sum to 336. HT30's KI-RO section re-lists the main section's commodities with smaller quantities—the delivered/outstanding split; HT34's mid-list KI-RO 30 (a 7 erased) sums nothing visible || Not kuro/kiru √k-l-l 'all, total' (Gordon 1966 §163): that conflates it with KU-RO through the Gordon KI=/ku/ sign alternate, whose only evidence was this very word. Under primary KI=/ki/, KI-RO ≠ KU-RO phonetically and the two terms are cleanly complementary. Fongaro kirru 'container' recorded as a possible ETYMOLOGY only (excluded as the function—a container cannot head the HT88/HT117a/HT94b recipient lists). The function stands independently of the etymology || Usage: KI-RO quantities are NOT summed into KU-RO checks; residuals compute as (delivered − owed) where the tablet marks the split. What would flip it: a tablet where KI-RO's quantity equals the exact sum of the items above it (none among the 13). || ETYMOLOGY (CANDIDATE): √k-l-ʾ 'hold back, withhold'. KI-RO = *kilʾu (R-series writes l; the glottal stop is unwritten; -u case ending), the qitl noun preserved in Hebrew keleʾ 'restraint' (< *kilʾ): 'what is held back', the amount outstanding. Cognates: Hebrew kālāʾ 'withhold, keep back' / keleʾ (H3607/H3608), Akkadian kalû 'detain, hold back', Syriac klʾ 'restrain', Geʿez kalʾa 'retinuit, denegavit'. The pair KU-RO *kull- 'all' (√k-l-l) / KI-RO *kilʾ- 'withheld' (√k-l-ʾ) differs in vowel and third radical—which explains Gordon's conflation of the two.

entries.meaning: personal or clan name, 'Kishite(s)'
entries.note: KH 6: KI-SA-NE CYP+D ½, a recipient of a vessel. Qīš + -āne, cf. Heb. Qîš (1 Chr 23:21). Weak points: KI for /q/, where QI exists; -āne as a gentilic has no second case. Rival: a Hurrian name in -nni, as DA-KU-SE-NE. One attestation.

entries.meaning: cumin (Cuminum cyminum)

cognates.Akkadian: kamūnu / kammūnu—OB ration lists, medical texts
cognates.Linear B: ku-mi-no (𐀓𐀖𐀜)—Knossos/Pylos palatial spice inventories, 15th c. BCE

entries.note: One of the strongest cross-script cognates: LB ku-mi-no is a universally recognized Semitic loanword and KU-MI-NA is its Linear A precursor (exact skeleton). Culture-word chain (Wanderwort): Sumerian U.GAMUN → Akkadian kamūnu → Ugaritic kmn → Linear B ku-mi-no → Greek κύμινον. On the HT Wc 3014 roundel, KU-MI-NA (side a) and QE (side b, the standalone qab-measure √q-b-b before the CAP caprid logogram) are separate entries—QE is not bound to cumin (a Semitic measure precedes its noun in construct, qê kamūni, and coordination is the proclitic wa-, never a postposed -qe). HT 54a.2 reads ]KU-MI-NA-QE[, broken at both ends (GORILA I 105). A-KU-MI-NA and A-DU-KU-MI-NA on ZA10a are names from the homograph √k-m-n 'hide, shelter' (HALOT 481), not cumin.

entries.meaning: emmer wheat
entries.note: Akkadian loanword kunāšu. Co-occurs with GRA ideogram. GRA+KU (7 att., HT61, HT128a ×3, HT128b ×3) is the logographic abbreviation: GRA ideogram + KU complement = initial syllable of kunāšu. On HT128a, GRA+KU co-occurs with GRA+PA as distinct grain subtypes in a distribution tablet.

entries.meaning: priestess (fem. singular)
entries.note: KH 92 .1 A-DA-QIf-RI · KU-NI-TE 10[ (Younger): a counted entry, with ]NA-KI 1 on .2. Punic khnt 'priestess' (Krahmalkov); Ugaritic khn 'priest'. Part of the √k-h-n group with KI-NI-MA and KA-NU-TI. Weak point: KU for the ā of kāhin-.

entries.meaning: personal name (hypocoristic in -aya), cf. Amorite Kubbiya

cognates.Amorite: KUBB-IJA (KU-UB-BI-IA), Mari (Gelb AS 21 no. 4149); KUBB-AN-UM (no. 4148)

entries.note: HT 116a: KU-PA-JA GRA 16, first of six grain recipients under U-TA-RO · TE ·, with PU-RA₂, SI+SE, PI-*34-TE, SI-KI-NE and QA-NU-MA. KU-PA-JA writes Kubbaya, the geminate unwritten, -aya the hypocoristic ending; cf. Amorite KUBB-IJA at Mari, KUBB-AN-UM (Gelb AS 21 nos. 4148–4149). Rival: KU-PA quppa 'box, basket' (HT 110a, KH 29, ZA 11a/b) with -ya; or a name on Kubaba (Gelb's Kupapa). One attestation.

entries.meaning: great ones (Kabeiri, pl./oblique); rival kᵉpārîm 'villages'
entries.note: PE 1 KU-PA-RI VIR 50, GRA+PA 26½, parallel to E-KA VIR 72, GRA+PA 36: two groups of men, each drawing about half a unit of grain per man. kubīri, plural/oblique of kabīru 'great one' (cf. KA-PO-RU). Rival: Hebrew kāpār 'village', pl. kᵉpārîm (Song 7:12; 1 Chr 27:25, the king's stores 'in the cities and in the villages'). One witness.

entries.meaning: devotee(s) of Kubaba (Kubaba + -ān- + feminine -atu), a counted personnel group

cognates.Anatolian/North Syrian: Kubaba, divine name (Ugarit, Carchemish); Hurrian Kubaba (Laroche 1980, 150)
cognates.Amorite: Kupapa, fem. DN (Gelb glossary); ʾAlli-Kupapa, Baʿli-Kupapa (nos. 708, 2094); short base in Kubb-ān-um (no. 4148) and Kuba-ʾEl (nos. 4099–4100), which Gelb segments kubb-, kuʾb-
cognates.Akkadian: ištarītu 'a priestess', named from Ištar; Kubabat (Old Assyrian); rival gubnatu 'cheese made from sheep milk', CAD G 117, Late Babylonian and labeled an Aramaic loanword

entries.language_layer: Anatolian/North Syrian theonym with Semitic derivation
entries.note: Feminine of KU-PA₃-NU Kubānu, on the base of KU-PA₃-PA₃ Kubaba (HT88, where KU-PA₃-NU also stands). HT119 KU-RO 160 includes *327 34 and VIR 68, so KU-PA₃-NA-TU 7 counts persons. HT47a KU-PA₃-NA-TU 20[ is broken. Amorite has the short base with the same -ān- in Kubb-ān-um (Gelb, AS 21, no. 4148), and in Kuba-ʾEl (nos. 4099–4100), so the name need not write Kubaba's second BA. Akkadian ištarītu, a priestess named from Ištar, is the same type. APZa2 I-KU-PA₃-NA-TU-NA-TE carries the stem. Rival: gubnatu 'cheese(s)', which HT119's personnel total excludes there.
entries.source: di Mino, Ya Diktu; Gelb 1980, AS 21, nos. 708, 2094, 4099–4100, 4148; Laroche 1980, 150; CAD G, 117, s.v. gubnatu; Leslau 1987, 178; Thomas 2020, 10–11; Furumark 1988, 63, 67 (cited by Sucharski 2002, 28); Jiménez Delgado 2024, 439

parallels.linear_a: Both administrative attestations are quantified: 20 on broken HT47a and 7 on HT119, where KU-RO 160 includes *327 34 and VIR 68, so the entry counts persons. The base KU-PA₃- takes -NU (KU-PA₃-NU), -NA-TU and -RI-JA (KU-PA₃-RI-JA); HT88 has KU-PA₃-PA₃ Kubaba beside KU-PA₃-NU. Thomas treats the longer APZa2 sequence as an inflectional variant of this base.
parallels.semitic: With PA₃ = /ba/ and K-series voicing left open, KU-PA₃-NA-TU can spell /gubnatu/: KU = /gu/, BA closes /gub/ with a dead vowel, followed by NA-TU. CAD records Akkadian gubnatu 'cheese (made from sheep milk)' in explicitly numbered allocations.
parallels.derivation: Furumark analyzes KU-PA₃-NA-TU-NA as an ethnic adjective, 'from/belonging to Kupanatu.'
parallels.linear_b: Mycenaean ku-pa-nu-we-to may belong to the same Aegean onomastic family (Jiménez Delgado 2024, 439).
parallels.apza2_preferred: The damaged APZa2 sequence is preferably segmented I- + KU-PA₃-NA-TU + -NA + -TE: a derived or inflected Kupanatu form, with initial I- and final -TE unresolved.
parallels.apza2_alternative: Alternatively, I-KU-PA₃ + NA-TU-NA-TE permits comparison of the second member with reconstructed Semitic *natūnāt 'given/dedicated persons or things' from √n-t-n; no divider or independent I-KU-PA₃ confirms this split.

entries.meaning: devotee of Kubaba (Kubaba + -ān-), personal name or title; rival Ugaritic Gupana/Gupan

cognates.Anatolian/North Syrian: Kubaba, divine name; base of Kubānu
cognates.Amorite: Kubb-ān-um (Gelb, AS 21, no. 4148)
cognates.Ugaritic: rival {m}gu-pa-na, personal name (RS 11.839 r.8); gpn/Gupan, messenger-deity

entries.language_layer: Anatolian/North Syrian theonym with Semitic derivation
entries.note: Kubānu 'devotee of Kubaba', masculine of KU-PA₃-NA-TU Kubānatu, the counted personnel group of HT119 (di Mino, Ya Diktu). HT88 sets it beside KU-PA₃-PA₃ Kubaba. Amorite has the short base with this ending, Kubb-ān-um (Gelb, AS 21, no. 4148), so the form need not write Kubaba's second BA. Eight occurrences across seven inscriptions make name or title status probable. Rival: Gupana/Gupan, from Ugaritic syllabic {m}gu-pa-na and alphabetic Gupan, with Linear B ku-pa-nu-we-to. HT101.4 has KU-PA₃-[…] in an entity-heading position; KU-PA₃-[NU] is the strongest restoration but is not counted as an attestation.
entries.source: di Mino, Ya Diktu; Gelb 1980, AS 21, no. 4148; RS 11.839 r.8; KTU 1.3 III:36, VI:6; Jiménez Delgado 2024, 439

parallels.linear_a: Shares KU-PA₃-N- with the independently attested Kubānatu. HT101.4 preserves the damaged entity heading KU-PA₃-[…] before OLE+U 2. KU-PA₃-[NU] is the strongest internal restoration, but the lost ending is not counted as an attestation.
parallels.linear_b: Mycenaean ku-pa-nu-we-to may be related to KU-PA₃-NU or KU-PA₃-NA-TU (Jiménez Delgado 2024, 439).
parallels.amorite: Kubb-ān-um carries the short base with the same ending (Gelb, AS 21, no. 4148).
parallels.ugaritic: Rival: syllabic {m}gu-pa-na is an attested personal name at Ugarit (RS 11.839 r.8; ORACC P503288); alphabetic gpn, Gupan, is one of Baal's messenger-deities (KTU 1.3 III:36, VI:6). The comparison depends on the value of PA₃.
parallels.gordon: Gordon compared Ugaritic Gupanu, now the rival.

entries.meaning: Kubaba (Anatolian/North Syrian divine or personal name)

cognates.Amorite: Kupapa 'divine name' (Gelb)
cognates.Akkadian: Kubabat (ku-ba-ba-at) 'Kubaba', with the Semitic feminine -t (Old Assyrian, Kanesh; see parallels)

entries.note: Layer 3 contact name. Conditional on PA₃ = /ba/, KU-PA₃-PA₃ spells Kubaba exactly. The name is externally attested both for the goddess and in personal names; HT88's one-unit roster therefore does not decide whether the referent is the goddess, a woman bearing the name, or a cult institution. The reading and the PA₃ value must not be used circularly to prove one another. Kubaba and Phrygian Cybele are distinct deities in current scholarship.

parallels.sumerian_king_list: Queen Kubaba of Kish (Early Dynastic III, c. 2500 BCE)—only female ruler in the SKL
parallels.kanesh: Kubabat (ku-ba-ba-at) with Semitic feminine -t suffix, Old Assyrian period c. 1950–1750 BCE. Priests (kumrum/GUDU₄) attested. (Kryszat 2006, p. 112; Taracha 2009, p. 29)
parallels.alalakh: Theophoric names Ili-Kubaba and Ini-Kubaba attested in legal texts, c. 1780–1600 BCE (Lauinger 2015, p. 297; Frayne 1990, pp. 781, 789)
parallels.carchemish: Tutelary goddess by c. 1770 BCE—cylinder seal of princess Matrunna, daughter of king Aplahanda. One of three principal deities alongside Nergal and Nubandag. (Marchesi & Marchetti 2019, pp. 527, 532)
parallels.ugarit: Listed in offering ritual RS 24.261 (bilingual Ugaritic-Hurrian); two theophoric names under king Arḫalba c. 1315–1313 BCE (Pardee 2002, pp. 93–95; van Soldt 2016, pp. 101, 106)
parallels.emar: Theophoric names attested; Hurrian text alongside Carchemish, Išḫara, and Ebla (Beckman 2002, pp. 45, 51)
parallels.hattusa: In kaluti (offering lists) of Ḫepat, alongside Adamma and Hašuntarhi (Taracha 2009, p. 96)
parallels.kizzuwatna: Hurrian religious context, dyad with Adamma (Archi 2013, p. 15)
parallels.cybele_note: Current consensus (Rutherford 2020, Hutter 2017, Oreshko 2021): Kubaba and Cybele are DISTINCT goddesses whose cults partially overlapped in Lydia. Kubaba was civic, never 'Mother,' no mountain associations. Cybele is Phrygian Matar Kubeleya, from Mount Kubela near Pessinus.
parallels.chronological_overlap: Alalakh attestations (c. 1780–1600 BCE) in northwest Syria—a known Minoan trade zone with Minoan pottery finds—predate LM IB by 150–200 years. Kubaba cult active in Levantine coastal corridor during exact period Haghia Triada tablets were written.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Vineyard' (√k-r-m)
entries.note: HT117a (Haghia Triada, Casa Room 9, LMIB): one of ten entries counted 1 each under MA-KA-RI-TE 'merchants' (KU-RO 10), a name on the noun 'vineyard', as Tēnā 'Fig' (TE-*301). Skeleton k-r-m matches PS *karm- "mountain with vineyard." Hebrew kerem is the exact cognate.

entries.meaning: total, sum (accounting term)
entries.note: Function confirmed corpus-internally by final or section-final position and arithmetic. HT89 supplies an exact control: 23+22+24+13+5=87. The comparison with Semitic *kull- 'all, entirety' is an etymological hypothesis rather than the basis of the decipherment. Linear B normally writes TO-SO for 'total'; no Linear B KU-RO cognate should be claimed. Complements KI-RO 'owed/outstanding' in Linear A accounting.
entries.source: Corpus-internal arithmetic; Gordon 1966 for the Semitic comparison; Duhoux 2012

entries.meaning: saffron, crocus (PN from plant term)
entries.note: Hapax; personnel list, Scribe 9; exact match to PS *kurk- 'saffron' base: *kurkum- Starling #2657; Akk kurkānū CAD K; Heb כַּרְכֹּם karkōm Song of Songs 4:14; Greek κρόκος is Semitic loanword; CROC ideogram on 59 Linear B tablets at Knossos; Xeste 3 saffron-gathering frescoes.

entries.meaning: vineyard / mountain with vineyard
entries.note: HT 115b, in a list of entries with small quantities (PA-RA-NE ½, DU-PA₃-NA 1, *306-TU-JA 1). √k-r-m: kurma or gurma 'vineyard', a place, or a name drawn from it.

entries.meaning: water(-men), water-drawers of the sanctuary; rival Anatolian 'grown-ups'

cognates.Ugaritic: mh/y 'water', pl. mym; tkmt my 'who carries water on her shoulders' (KTU 1.19 II 6)
cognates.Hebrew: מַיִם mayim 'water'; שֹׁאֲבֵי מַיִם 'drawers of water' (Josh 9:21, 27; Deut 29:10)

entries.note: HT89 MA-I-MI 24, third of five classes under A-SA-RA₂ · *307 (dubur 'sanctuary'), KU-RO 87. /mayimi/ 'water' (DULAT 529): the sanctuary's water-drawers, cf. Josh 9:27 and Ezra 7:24 (gatekeepers, Nethinim); compare TA-RA. Rival: Uchitel 2006, 75, Anatolian 'grown-ups' from mai- 'to grow'; but Hittite makes the participle mi(y)ant- (EDHIL 541–42), and the -mi participle is Luwian (Finkelberg 1990/91: 80 n. 86), which has no verb mai- (Melchert 1993, 146). One witness.
entries.source: DULAT 529; KTU 1.19 II 6; Josh 9:27; Ezra 7:24; Uchitel 2006, 75; Finkelberg 1990/91: 80 n. 86; Kloekhorst, EDHIL 541–42; Melchert 1993, 146

entries.meaning: infants or young dependents (personnel category)

cognates.Ugaritic: mṯ (I) 'infant, baby boy' (KTU 1.69:2; 1.5 V:22; 3.7:15; Copenhagen Ugaritic Corpus/DULAT)

entries.note: HT102 counts MA-ZU 3 within an administrative list. Ugaritic mṯ 'infant' is the closest lexical and contextual comparison; in KTU 1.5 V:22 it follows yld 'give birth.' ZU can represent the interdental /ṯ/ under the proposed sign system. The vocalization /maṯu/ and final -u are reconstructed from the Linear A spelling because alphabetic Ugaritic records only mṯ. As a Linear A hapax, the term remains SPECULATIVE and should not replace MA-ZU in an unqualified translation.

entries.meaning: magical protection, protective amulet/rite (Egyptian loanword)
entries.cognates: Egyptian mk.t 'protection, magical protection' (Wb II 161); from √mk 'to protect'. Cross-register: appears on both administrative tablets and stone ritual vessels
entries.note: Egyptian mk.t 'magical protection' (Wb II 161, √mk 'to protect'). Cross-register: PK1 (tablet, Palaikastro—personnel list, all qty=1) and ZA5b (stone vessel, Zakros—with qty 3 alongside SI-PI-KI 'libation pourings'). Skeleton mkt has no close NWS or Proto-Semitic match, confirming Layer 3 (Egyptian contact). The -TA suffix preserves the Egyptian feminine -t intact as a commodity/category label. Compare MA-KA-I-SE (ZA8), which re-derives from the same *makī-* base using a NWS agentive suffix *-šē*: the -TA form functions as a ritual commodity ('magical protections: 3' on ZA5b), while the -SE form functions as a personal name ('protector') in a personnel list. This contact-layer morphological hybridization—Egyptian loanword preserved intact alongside a Semitized derivation—parallels Amarna Canaanite patterns. The onomasticon's competing MLK reading (*Malkīta* 'Queen') is weakened by the same objection raised against MA-KA-I-SE: the skeleton is m-k, not m-l-k (no /l/ sign).

entries.meaning: Tax-man, Customs Official (professional-title PN, maqtil pattern)
entries.cognates: PS *mak(i)s- "customs dues, customs official"; Heb. מֶכֶס mekes "tax/levy" (Num 31:28); Akk. miksu "customs duty"; 1 Kgs 4:9 Māqaṣ (Solomon tax district)
entries.note: The Egyptian reading (mk + agentive -šē) is rejected as hybrid; PS *mak(i)s- fits consonant for consonant. The -I- is the regular epenthetic vowel in the maqtil noun pattern (instrument/place noun from √m-k-s): /makis/ → MA-KA-I-SE. The -SE is the final root consonant /s/ with dead vowel, not a gentilic suffix. Context: ZA8 allocation tablet—a tax document with personnel receiving numbered portions. Professional-title PN "Tax-man" on a tax list is semantically ideal.

entries.meaning: merchants (heading of a roster of men); rival 'red (wool)'

cognates.Ugaritic: mkr 'merchant, commercial agent', pl. mkrm, counted in rosters: ʿšr mkrm 'ten merchants', spr mkrm 'list of traders', ġr mkrm 'total of merchants' (DULAT 537); syllabic ma-ka-ri 'to trade' (Huehnergard 2008, 146)
cognates.Akkadian: makāru B 'to do business', OA and Ras Shamra (CAD M/1 126); mākiru, makkāru 'trader' (CAD M/1 129, 131); tamkāru 'merchant' (CAD T 125); tamkārūtu 'commercial transaction; (collective) merchants' (CAD T 141); rival makrū, fem. makritu 'red', of wool (CAD M/1 138)
cognates.Egyptian: *mākiruyu 'merchant', a Semitic loan after swty 'trader' (Hoch 1994, 169, no. 223)

entries.note: HT 87: *21F-TU-NE · MA-KA-RI-TE ·, then six men at 1 each. HT 117a: MA-KA-RI-TE · KI-RO · U-MI-NA-SI ·, then ten men at 1 each, KU-RO 10: 'merchants: owed'. One sign-group in both, divider after TE. √m-k-r 'to trade': Ugaritic counts mkrm in rosters with a total (ġr mkrm, DULAT 537), Akkadian has mākiru and makkāru 'trader', Punic mkr. TE writes the -t of a class noun, cf. the Akkadian collective tamkārūtu 'merchants' (CAD T 141). Weak point: no -t form of mkr is attested. Rival: makritu 'red', of wool (CAD M/1 138), which suits a commodity, not a roster of men.

entries.meaning: mina, portion (weight/measure unit)
entries.note: Ligature on Khania roundels (administrative context). Akkadian manû 'to count, allot', Hebrew māneh 'mina' (standard weight unit across the ANE from Ur III through Persian period). The mina as commodity label on administrative roundels is contextually ideal.

entries.meaning: loin, hip meat—choice cut on sacrificial fat allocation tablet
entries.note: HT 41a, unquantified before PA-JA 2 on a tablet of *304 (fat) allocations: MI-DA-NI PA-JA 2, a weight. PS *matn- 'loins' (Heb. māṯnayim). Weak points: MI for ma, DA for t. Rival: a heading or title before PA-JA. One attestation.

entries.meaning: water
entries.note: SYZa5 stone libation vessel at Syme peak sanctuary—object-label match; Ug. my/mw, Heb. mayim, Akk. mû.

entries.meaning: coverings, blankets
entries.note: HT26a: MI-KI-SE-NA 15 under the *406VAS+KE heading, after *312-TE-TE (linen item) and TA-TI 21. miqtal of √k-s-y: *miksay- > miksē (Heb. miksê), SE a sounded ē; -NA the plural *-īna. KI echoes the preceding i. Not MI-KI-SA-NE (ARKH1a), read as MI + KI-SA-NE.

alternative_readings.note: levy, tax on produce (√m-k-s): Akk. miksu, makāsu (also at Ugarit), mākisu 'tax-collector'; Heb. mekes (Num 31:28); Phoen. MKS 'customs official'. Fits the ledger slot, not the e-vowel.

entries.meaning: amount, number; counting, reckoning

cognates.Akkadian: minūtu 'amount, number; contingent; standard of coinage' (CAD M/2 98); minûtu, cross-reference to manûtu (CAD M/2 99); manû 'count'
cognates.Arabic: Manāt, a remote divine-name comparison from the same apportioning semantic field

entries.note: Four Haghia Triada attestations (HT86a, HT95a, HT95b, HT106). Akkadian minūtu is the closest independent formal and semantic parallel: CAD M/2 98 gives 'amount, number,' and the spellings mi-nu-te occur in administrative or reckoning contexts (Ebeling, Parfümrez. p. 26 ii 20; AKA 143 iv 33). This makes 'count/reckoning' preferable to a goddess Minut. Linear A does not mark vowel length, and final TE may carry a support vowel. Linear A writes i where Amorite has a: MI-NU-TE against Ma-nu-tum (Gelb no. 4528), as I-PI-NA-MA against pān-. Arabic Manāt remains a remote comparison, not the primary identification.

entries.meaning: personal name (Mitanni Indo-Aryan type)

cognates.Nuzi: Mittar-atti (Mi-it-ta-ra-at-ti), name element mittar- (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, s.v. MITTAR-ATTI)
cognates.Amarna: Ša-mitta, filed with Indo-Aryan su- (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, element list, s.v. šu)

entries.note: Personal name on HT128a, with GRAIN. The closest name is Nuzi Mittar-atti, element mittar- (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, s.v. MITTAR-ATTI), which Gelb sets among the non-Hurrian names with apparent Kassite features (ibid., 196) and Gentile analyses as Mitanni Indo-Aryan *mitra-atthi- 'having Mitra [or a friend] as his guest' (Gentile 2019, 157); no Kassite element list has mittar- (Clay 1912, 36–41; Pinches 1917, 111–113). Rival: Indo-Aryan -mitta, as Amarna Ša-mitta (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, element list, s.v. šu). Bare MI-TA occurs only on HT128a; SI-MI-TA (HT96a), A-MI-TA (ZA10b) and the Troy whorls contain the string but are separate words. Cross-reference: SI-MI-TA, MI-DA (t/d variant), A-MI-DA-O.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943; Gentile 2019; Clay 1912; Pinches 1917

entries.meaning: personal name, 'dead one' (?)

cognates.Amorite: rival: MUT-UM 'man' in names (Gelb 1980, nos. 4827–4831)

entries.note: HT 117a: MI-TU 1, a recipient in the roster under MA-KA-RI-TE · KI-RO, with U-SU, KU-PA₃-NU and TE-JA-RE. mītu 'dead one', a name of the substitute type. HT 135a ]-MI-TU is the end of a longer word. Weak point: two signs. Rival: Amorite mutum 'man', which needs MU. One attestation.

entries.meaning: prefect, administrator (heading of a wine issue); rivals mōgun- 'regalement, gift', Dagan

cognates.Canaanite: su₂-ki-na 'prefect', gloss in EA 362 (ORACC aemw/amarna P270873)
cognates.Akkadian: sākinu 'a high official', Alalakh, Boğazköy, Ras Shamra (CAD S 76)

entries.note: ZA 15a .1 *47-KU-NA SA-VIN, all four signs whole and undotted (GORILA III 183), heading a wine issue with libation portions (SI-PI-KI) and groats. With *47 = so: sōkina 'prefect', the vowels of the Canaanite gloss su₂-ki-na (EA 362), with the ō of the Canaanite shift. Rivals: mōgun- 'regalement, gift' with *47 = mo, /m-g-n/ 'to wine and dine, regale' (DULAT 525); Dagan with *47 = do (DULAT 265). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Vow' (√n-d-r); rival Egyptian PN 'of-the-hand-of-Re'
entries.note: From √n-d-r 'to vow'. Also read as Egyptian PN by Gordon. Huehnergard: G /nadara/, prefix /yaddur-/ (n-assimilation); impersonal 3mp attested; BH nādar. || Attested on the HT117a personnel list (qty 1, beside MI-TU, KU-PA₃-NU, TE-JA-RE); Amorite NDR 'to vow' (Gelb AS 21 §0.7)—nadir- 'vowed one' as PN fits the roster slot. LB no-da-ro (KN As(1) 609, personnel) preserves the n-d-r frame.

entries.meaning: damaged final sequence; possible nasīʾ 'chief, prince'

cognates.Hebrew: nāśīʾ (נָשִׂיא) 'prince, chief, tribal leader' (HALOT 724); Num 1:16, Ezek 44:3

entries.note: APZa2 line 1 begins at a broken edge with ]NA-SI and preserves a divider after SI. The sequence could be complete, but its beginning and syntactic role are unknown. Comparison with Semitic nasīʾ 'chief, prince' remains possible; it cannot be translated as the subject of a reconstructed offering clause. KH7a attests the distinct form E-NA-SI, not an independent NA-SI witness, and therefore no longer counts as an attestation.

entries.meaning: Dual reading: (A) the dedicated one (passive participle qatūl of √n-t-n 'to give' + -ān suffix); (B) the giver (active participle qātāl + -ān), a theophanic title parallel to A-TA-NA = ʾatanā 'She-who-gives' (Athena)

cognates.Hebrew: nātīn (נָתִין) "temple servant, dedicated one"—singular of Nĕtīnīm (נְתִינִים), Ezra 2:43, 8:20; 1 Chr 9:2. Passive participle of √n-t-n. The Levites themselves called nĕtūnīm nĕtūnīm "given, utterly given" (Num 3:9)
cognates.Ugaritic: ytn / ntn "to give"—one of the most common Ugaritic roots
cognates.Phoenician: Mattan (מתן) "gift"—common PN element (Mattan-Baal); institutional parallels in Phoenician temple servant classes
cognates.Athena: A-TA-NA = ʾatanā 'She-who-gives' (lexicon PROBABLE)—NWS feminine of √y-t-n (> ʾ- via I-y weakening). NA-TU-NA-NE with initial n- preserves √n-t-n; the coexistence of both allomorphs points to a pre-split isogloss stage

entries.note: Skoteino Cave inked inscription (fragmentary—lacuna on both sides). With *301=NWY logogram (CONFIRMED, phonetic /na/), full reading is NA-TU-NA-NE || DUAL ANALYSIS: (A) PASSIVE—natūn (qatūl passive participle of √n-t-n 'to give') + -ān = natūnān 'the dedicated one.' TU vowel matches /ū/ of the passive participle exactly; dead vowel -e on final NE closes the syllable: na-tū-nā-n(e). BIBLICAL PARALLEL: Hebrew nĕtūnīm (Num 3:9) 'given ones'—Levites as persons dedicated to sanctuary service. Post-exilic Nĕtīnīm (Ezra 2:43, 8:20; 1 Chr 9:2) are temple servants from √n-t-n; the institution is pre-Israelite, traced to the Gibeonites (Josh 9:27). (B) ACTIVE—nātān (qātāl active participle) + -ān = nātānān 'the giver.' Parallels A-TA-NA = ʾatanā < *yātanat 'She-who-gives' (proposed NWS etymology of Athena, √y-t-n). If active, natūnān qaqqatī = 'The Giver at the Peak'—theophanic title for the Goddess at a cave sanctuary. A-TA-NA/NA-TU-NA paradigm would attest both feminine divine epithet and masculine/neuter cultic title from the same root || Both readings contextually strong: sanctuary dedicatee (passive) or divine epithet (active) at a sacred cave. *301=NWY is CONFIRMED across 288 occurrences at 16 sites. || Huehnergard: Ug ntn, ttn /tatinū/ "to set, put; to give"; I-n verb; preterite yaqtul 3mp: ttn /tatinū/. Assimilation of /n/ standard for I-n verbs. BH cognate: nātan "to give" (Huehnergard 2012, p. 52 (paradigm); pp. 6-7 (Appendix C))

entries.meaning: offspring, descendants, posterity

cognates.Hebrew: nîn ‘offspring, descendants’ (Gen 21:23; Isa 14:22; Job 18:19); cf. the extended -ūn formation Yəšūrūn ‘Jeshurun, the Upright One’
cognates.Hebrew verb: rare n-w-n ‘produce shoots, get descendants’ at Ps 72:17; HALOT leaves open whether the noun derives from the verb or the verb is denominative
cognates.Semitic morphology: masculine nominative plural *-ūna (Huehnergard 2019, 60–61); Arabic indefinite nominative -un (Fischer 2002, §§141, 147)

entries.note: PL Zf 1 hapax. Its position after the proposed imperative-object phrase /tannî qînâ/ favors a noun or noun phrase—contextually a vocative ‘offspring/descendants’—over a second finite verb. Hebrew nîn securely means ‘offspring, descendants.’ The three N-series signs can be accounted for exactly as /nīn-ūn/: NI /nī/, NU /nū/, and final NI /n/ with a dead vowel; alternatively /nīn-un/ would contain Arabic-type nominative nunation. Both are grammatically regular Semitic analyses: -ūn may represent plural or collective morphology (compare masculine nominative plural *-ūna with loss of the final vowel, and the Hebrew -ūn formation Yəšūrūn), while -un is a regular indefinite nominative ending in Arabic. The uncertainty concerns which ending NI-NU-NI encodes and whether the noun functions as a vocative here, not the grammatical validity of the formation. Because this exact inflected form is unattested for nîn and NI-NU-NI is a hapax, the identification remains speculative. The rare Hebrew verb n-w-n (Ps 72:17) supplies a semantic association with descent but no matching finite paradigm.

entries.meaning: O Sukar—proposed Minoan rendering of Egyptian Sokar
entries.note: Hapax in the deity-address slot at Troullos. O may be the vocative /ʾō/ rather than a prosthetic vowel; Geʿez ʾo- 'O …!' supplies a later structural parallel (Leslau 1987, 1), not proof of the Bronze Age form. SU-QA-RE supplies /sukar/, with final E as the dead spelling vowel after /r/; its s-k-r skeleton supports comparison with Egyptian Skr/Zkr 'Sokar.' The divine identification and exact vowels remain CANDIDATE.

entries.meaning: DI-oil subtype; perhaps honeyed oil
entries.note: OLE ideogram + DI adjunct: 12 tokens on 8 Haghia Triada tablets. Akkadian dišpu(m) and Hebrew dǝbaš mean 'honey,' so DI could abbreviate a honey-related modifier; Ugaritic normally uses nbt for honey. The corpus securely establishes an oil subtype, not the expansion dišpu or an exact ancient 'honey-oil' expression. Co-occurrence with OLE+MI is administrative evidence for distinct oil classes, not by itself proof of ritual use.

entries.meaning: compound oil category; perhaps honeyed or syrup-infused
entries.note: Hapax. SigLA catalogs the glyph as the single logogram A623, while GORILA decomposes it as OLE+QE+DI. OLE makes an oil category secure. DI permits comparison with Akkadian dišpu and Hebrew dǝbaš 'honey/syrup,' as in the recurrent OLE+DI subtype, but the precise product is unknown. QE is not independently established here as Akkadian qû 'capacity measure,' so the expansion 'qû-measured honey-oil' does not hold.

entries.meaning: oil subtype; perhaps standard or genuine-grade oil
entries.note: OLE ideogram + KI adjunct (21 tokens at Haghia Triada, Tylissos, and Zakros). Akkadian kīnu 'true, genuine, legitimate' and Hebrew kēn 'correct, right' provide a plausible quality term, and Linear A KI-NU may preserve the full word, although its personal-name interpretation remains viable. No exact ancient collocation 'genuine oil' has been identified, so the subtype is secure but 'standard/genuine grade' remains tentative.

entries.meaning: oil subtype; perhaps anointing or ceremonial oil
entries.note: OLE ideogram + MI complement (19 att., Haghia Triada + Tylissos). Northwest Semitic √m-š-ḥ 'anoint' is attested in Ugaritic mšḥ (DUL 585) and Hebrew māšaḥ. Biblical cult inventories repeatedly use שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה šemen ham-mišḥā 'the anointing oil' (Exod 25:6; 29:7; 31:11); Exod 30:25, 31 has שֶׁמֶן מִשְׁחַת קֹדֶשׁ šemen mišḥat qōdeš 'holy anointing oil.' This supplies a precise commodity-plus-MI structural parallel. Akkadian provides only a semantic control—pašāšum 'anoint' with šamnum 'oil' (Huehnergard 1997, §5.5)—not an m-š-ḥ cognate. MI may therefore be a phonetic complement for mišḥ-, but does not prove the reading. OLE+MI co-occurs with OLE+U and OLE+KI on allocation tablets (HT42+59, HT91, TY3a) and appears with PA as PA-OLE+MI (TY3b). Confidence remains CANDIDATE.
entries.source: Hebrew Bible, Exod 25:6; 29:7; 30:25, 31; 31:11; DUL 585; Huehnergard 1997, §5.5; corpus distribution

entries.meaning: oil designated for ritual libation; sacred oil poured as an offering
entries.note: OLE ideogram + NE complement (5 att., Haghia Triada + Tylissos). Exclusively very small quantities (¾, ≈⅙, 2 units)—consistent with measured ritual portions, not bulk commodity || ETYMOLOGY: Akk nasāku 'to pour a libation' (CAD N/II 26), Heb נֶסֶךְ nesek 'libation, drink offering' (Num 15:5, Isa 48:5), √n-s-k. NE = /ne/ = initial syllable of neseku || DISTRIBUTION: HT32—allocated under *307 (dubur 'sanctuary') heading, explicitly sacred. HT23a—OLE+NE ≈⅙ in a group of four oil preparations (OLE+NE, OLE+TU, OLE+RI, *308) all at identical ≈⅙ quantities, suggesting a ritual recipe or sacred oil blend formula. TY3b—minor complement (2 units) alongside massive OLE+MI (anointing oil) quantities || Alternative: nēru 'lamp' (√n-w-r) → lamp oil, but tiny quantities and sanctuary contexts rule it out || HT32 places it under a dubur sanctuary heading.

entries.meaning: aromatic/fragrant olive oil preparation
entries.note: OLE ideogram + RI complement (4 att., Haghia Triada + Khania). Akk riqqu 'aromatic substance' (CAD R 371). RI = /ri/ = initial syllable of riqqu. Co-occurs with OLE+NE and OLE+TU on HT23a (all in fractional quantities ≈⅙). Cf. *401=RUQQÛ (√r-q-ḥ 'perfumed oil')—related aromatic register but different root (√r-q-q vs √r-q-ḥ). || Myrrh co-occurs on 3 of 4 tablets, independent contextual evidence.

entries.meaning: fine-grade olive oil; 'good oil' as an administrative quality designation
entries.note: OLE ideogram + TA complement (8 att., Haghia Triada + Khania). PS *ṭayb- 'good, pleasant': Akk ṭābu, Heb ṭōb, Ug ṭb. TA = /ṭa/ via T-class neutralization = initial syllable of ṭābu. Direct Ugaritic administrative parallel: šmn ṭb 'good oil' (KTU 4.14, 4.91, 4.158). Small fractional quantities (⅕, 𐝓) suggest a premium grade distributed in measured amounts. || Huehnergard: Ug ṭyb (ṭb) /ṭaṭib-/ (D-stem) "to make good, return"; D-stem: tttb, ṭtb /ṭaṭib-/ "make good." PS *ṭayb- "good". BH cognate: ṭōb "good" (< PS *ṭayb-) (Huehnergard 2012, paradigm section)

entries.meaning: sanctuary oil
entries.note: Compound logogram: OLE + DUBUR. Oil for sanctuary use at Petras.

entries.meaning: Phaistos (place name)
entries.note: Same spelling in Linear B—direct overlap.

entries.meaning: Sukrita (place name; Linear B su-ki-ri-ta)
entries.note: PH Wa 32, a Phaistos nodule: SU-KI-RI-TA alone, four signs, undotted (GORILA II 90). HT Zb 158b, a jar: SU-KI-RI-TE-I-JA, the gentilic in -TE-I-JA. Linear B spells the place su-ki-ri-ta in the Knossos sheep tablets (KN Da 1091, Db 1324, 1327, Df 1325, Dn 1092, Dv 5232), with the ethnic su-ki-ri-ta-jo (KN C 911); DMic II 303 n. 6 records Godart's reading of su-ki-ri-ta on this Phaistos sealing (PP 31, 1976, 42 ff.) and the scribe's change of su-ki-ri-ta to pa-i-to on KN Da 1163. Identified with Σύβριτα in the Amari valley; Chadwick takes the name as not Greek (DMic II 303 n. 5). Semitic etymology, SPECULATIVE: √s-g-r 'shut, bolt' on Ventris and Chadwick's Sugrita, the vowel of KI dead: Heb. sāgar 'shut' (BDB 688), Akk. šigaru 'bolt' (HALOT 742), Pun. sgr 'lock'. Ugaritic personal name śgryn /Sugriyānu/ (KTU³ 4.825 i 13), s̀ an allograph of {s} (Tropper & Vita 2019, §2). Rival: SU- + KI-RI-TA qrt 'town' (Phoen., Pun. qrt, HALOT 1142; Syr. ḳerīt-, Brock. 695), SU- unexplained; Greek writes Semitic q as κ, and Σύβριτα has β/γ.

entries.meaning: of Sukrita (Sybrita): origin label on a jar
entries.note: HT Zb 158b, a jar: the only word on side b (GORILA IV 65); side a reads [·]-TU-SE-SU-KI. Gentilic on SU-KI-RI-TA (PH Wa 32), the vowel of KI dead before RI; Linear B has the ethnic su-ki-ri-ta-jo (KN C 911). Davis (Aura Suppl. 13, 46) pairs the two forms as alternating endings. -I-JA is the Semitic nisba *-iy- (fem. *-iyya), the gentilic suffix of Ugaritic ugrty /ʾugaritiyyu/ 'man of Ugarit' (Fischer §116). Rival: Anatolian -iya-. -TE-I-JA has no other Linear A witness; SE-TO-I-JA (PR Za 1) shares -I-JA. One document.

entries.meaning: He (of) Re: Egyptian personal name Pꜣ-Rꜥ (Gordon's Pꜣy-Rꜥ); Linear B pa-ja-ro
entries.note: The four Linear A occurrences behave as a personal name. Linear B pa-ja-ro is a masculine personal name in the Knossian roster KN As(2) 1519.6, and DMic compares it with Linear A PA-JA-RE; Davis 2026 likewise treats the pair as Minoan. Gordon reads Egyptian Pꜣy-Rꜥ 'He-of-Re' (Gordon 1966a, 31, §127). PNM v6 has the man's name pꜣ-rꜥ 'he (of) Ra' (Ranke I, 114.11, as PNM cites it), used from Thutmose III to Amenhotep III and spelled pꜣjj-rꜥ under Hatshepsut, the date of the LM IB tablets (Ilin-Tomich 2025, personal_names_id 142613047); JA writes the jj. Rival: a Minoan name, as Davis treats it.
entries.source: Gordon 1966a, 31 (§127); Ilin-Tomich 2025 (PNM v6), s.v. pꜣ-rꜥ; DMic II; Davis 2026

entries.meaning: daughters (fem. pl.) / portions / Kubaba devotees (cf. KU-PA-NA-TU)
entries.note: Standalone on KH7b vessel allocation tablet (Khania) || THREE READINGS: (1) banātu 'daughters' (P→/b/, Akk. fem. pl. of bintu, Ug. bnt, Heb. bānōt)—personnel category. (2) panātu 'faces/portions' (Akk., Heb. pānîm)—share categories. (3) (Ku)bānatu—tail of KU-PA-NA-TU (Kubaba feminine form attested in lexicon), possibly standalone devotee title || Khania's Anatolian contact layer supports reading (3). Distinct from KU-PA-NA-TU which carries a KU- prefix. Dual registration per di Mino

entries.meaning: short form of A-PA-RA-NE—'crosser' or 'creator' (without initial guttural prefix)
entries.note: HT115a: PA-RA-NE receives quantity 1 in GRA+BOSm list alongside *301-U-RA (naura 'light'), SE-KU-TU, KA-PO-RU, RI-SU-MA. HT115b: receives ½. Both by HT Scribe 8. Short form of A-PA-RA-NE (HT96a/b, same scribe): the A- prefix = initial ʿayin (√ʿ-b-r) or prosthetic aleph (√b-r-ʾ). Same dual reading as A-PA-RA-NE but without the guttural initial. || Amorite Ḥa-pí-ra-an (Huffmon APNM p. 36; element ḤPR ḥapir-, *ʿapir- = the ʿApiru/Ḥabiru word, p. 202) and ʾAPR-AN AP-RA-AN (Gelb AS 21 no. 863) match the short form with -ān; cuneiform ḫ writes ʿ. Root disputed: Borger (via Huffmon p. 202) derives ʿapīru from ʿ-p-r 'dust', not ʿ-b-r 'cross'; PA writes p and b alike.

entries.meaning: Ptah-theophoric personal name: Ptaḥ-di(w) 'Ptah-gives/Ptah-given'
entries.note: PH(?)31a.3–4, after KU-PA₃-NU SUS+SI+RE 1, broken after; HTZb160 clay-vessel label PA-TA-DA-DU-PU₂-RE 'Patada: to the sanctuary' (scriptio continua, PN + dubur). Phonologically ambiguous with NWS √p-t-ḥ 'to open.' -DA element: Egyptian dj/di(w) 'give(n)' — Ptaḥ-di(w) 'Ptah-gives/Ptah-given.' The DN-first order follows the standard NK verbal template Ptḥ-ms (Ptahmose 'Ptah-is-born') and Ptḥ-ḥtp (Ptahhotep 'Ptah-is-content'); the deity-last worry applies only to the Late-Period P3-dj-DN type, not to this one. Secondary option: hybrid Egypto-Semitic Ptaḥ-dād 'Beloved-of-Ptah,' a calque of Mry-Ptḥ (Merneptah) with NWS √d-w-d (cf. corpus DA-DU-*301 dāduna 'our beloved'). || Huehnergard: Ug ptḥ /pat(a)hī/ "to open"; Strong/final guttural verb. G imperative fs: pth /pat(a)hī/. BH cognate: pātaḥ "to open" (Huehnergard 2012, paradigm section)

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Viper'; rival Ptah-theophoric
entries.note: HT 94b (KI-RO · TU-MA 1, PA-TA-NE 1, DE-DI 1 …), HT 122a (PA-TA-NE 1 after KU-PA₃-NU 1, in a roster with JA-MI-DA-RE) and the nodule HT Wa 1019 (PA at the edge). On HT 122a SigLA labels the second sign ri; its own tracing, GORILA's facsimile and the photo show TA. *patn- 'viper' as a name; no name of that form is attested. Rivals: Ptah with ḥ unwritten and -ānu, 'devotee of Ptah'; √p-t-ḥ 'open' with -ānu.

entries.meaning: a kind of *402 cup, Aramaic pitqa 'winecup' compared
entries.note: HT 31 vessel inventory, written on the *402-VS cup logogram, qty 3000—the largest allocation on the tablet. Two competing Semitic etymologies: (1) Astour proposed Akkadian patāqu 'to cast metal,' reading PA-TA-QE as 'metal vessel' (JAOS 87, 1967, 292 n. 13). (2) Stieglitz preferred Aramaic pitqa 'winecup' (Lewy, Chaldäisches Wörterbuch) and Akkadian naptaqu 'smelting-jar' (AHw). Root skeleton p-t-q is an exact match. The -QE ending may correspond to Semitic -ey (archaic Hebrew plural -êy or Ugaritic dual construct -ê), per Stieglitz's morphological analysis of HT 31 case endings. Part of Gordon's HT 31 vessel inventory (§163), confirmed by both Astour and Stieglitz as Semitic.

entries.meaning: terebinth (phonetic complement confirming /b/-onset)
entries.note: PA₃ = /b/ phonetic complement (dash notation). Confirms commodity name starts with /b/. HT8b Villa Magazine, qty 2.

entries.meaning: cattle, heifers (fem.pl.)
entries.note: PS *baḳar- 'large cattle'. Hebrew bāqār. Fem.pl. -āti. Livestock allocation term.

entries.meaning: builder or personnel designation
entries.note: The comparison is the Semitic active participle of √b-n-y 'build', *bāniyu > bānī in a weak-final form. Its personnel sense suits HT102, but the bare form is lexically ambiguous and the proposed relation to PA₃-NI-NA does not by itself establish the reading.

entries.meaning: our builder
entries.note: √b-n-y 'to build' + 1pl possessive -na. Personnel designation. Huehnergard: III-y verb; participle /bāniyu/ → construct /bny/ "creator". Validates participial reading.

entries.meaning: the builder (nisba/gentilic)
entries.note: √b-n-y "to build" + NWS gentilic suffix *-iy (written -WI). Syme peak sanctuary libation context, alongside A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA and JA-I-NWA-RO. RILA-S1 p. 84 underdots WI and rates PA₃-NI-PI less plausible. Same -WI nisba morpheme as DU-RU-WI (*ḏu-lēwī "the Levite") and U-RE-WI (*ʾūr-lēwī). PA₃-NI-WI = "the builder" parallels DU-RU-WI = "the attached one/Levite"—both are occupational nisba adjectives from the NWS gentilic *-iyy-, preserved in Linear A where the /iy/ diphthong writes as WI (glide preserved, not collapsed to Hebrew long -î). The Merarite Levite בָּנִי Bānî bears this exact name. Huehnergard: III-y verb; participle /bāniyu/ → construct /bny/ "creator". Validates participial reading.

entries.meaning: balsam, spice (aromatic resin)
entries.cognates: Hebrew bōśem (בֹּשֶׂם) 'spice/perfume'; beśāmīm (בְּשָׂמִים) 'spices' (pl.); Ugaritic bšm 'spice' (offering lists); Akkadian basmu 'fragrant plant'; Aramaic busmā (בּוּסְמָא) 'aromatic'; Arabic balsam (بلسم) with l-infix → Greek βάλσαμον → English 'balsam'; Ethiopic baśam 'to be fragrant'. Pan-Semitic root. Minoan form ba-si-mo preserves the archaic triradical without Arabic l-infix.
entries.note: Anchor reading for *47=MO. Hebrew bōśem (בֹּשֶׂם) 'spice, balsam, perfume'. Single-word vessel inscription from Miletos—a Minoan trade colony on the Anatolian coast. Balsam was among the highest-value aromatics in Bronze Age Mediterranean trade. PA₃=/ba/, SI=/si/, *47=/mo/.

entries.meaning: face, front, portion
entries.note: Same root as I-PI-NA-MA (/ipinama/ "face, presence"). At Zakros before OLIV · 2. PI-IN-A = pīnā or pinā.

entries.meaning: damaged sequence; possible mnt/mināt 'portion, allotment'; rival minḥâ 'offering'

cognates.Hebrew: mānā (מָנָה) 'portion, share' (HALOT 600); mān (מָן) 'manna' (Exod 16:15); mānāh 'to count, allot'
cognates.Arabic: manāt 'fate, destiny; that which is allotted' (the goddess Manāt, Quran 53:20)

entries.note: APZa2 line 2 preserves ]PI-MI-NA-TE from a broken left edge to a divider after TE; PI and MI are written over an erasure (GORILA IV 5). Because no beginning is preserved, PI cannot securely be isolated as a preposition, and the sequence is not a complete attestation of *mināt. Ugaritic mnt (I) 'portion, ration' (DULAT 558) and Semitic √m-n-y 'count, allot' remain possible lexical comparisons only. Rival: Hebrew minḥâ 'gift, offering' (Lev 2:1), Ugaritic mnḥt 'tribute' (DULAT 556); the spelling drops ḥ. Younger restores I-]PI-MI-NA-TE and compares PI-*34-TE (HT 116a); no I survives before PI.

entries.meaning: provisions, provisioning (allocation entry); rivals bayti 'house', a recipient name
