entries.note: HT 116a PI-*34-TE GRA 5, then OLE 5, OLE+MI 1, *OLIV+TU 2: one of six entries under U-TA-RO · TE, each a sign group with GRA and a number, as KU-PA-JA, PU-RA₂, SI+SE, SI-KI-NE and QA-NU-MA. Read PI-QI-TE with *34 = QI, a speculative value. Akkadian piqittu(m), oblique piqitti, sense 1 'provisioning, provisions' (CAD P 388), from paqādu(m) 'entrust, assign, inspect' (Huehnergard 1997, pp. 104, 614); the entry draws grain, oil and olives. Rivals: bayti 'house; temple, household, estate' (DULAT 243; HALOT 124; CAD B 282) with *34 = ai, Linear B a₅ /hai/, an institution among recipients that include PU-RA₂ and SI+SE; a recipient name, as its neighbours. Younger compares ]PI-MI-NA-TE (AP Za 2.2), with *34 for MI-NA. One witness. Weak point: *34 = qi is speculative.
entries.source: Huehnergard 1997, pp. 104, 614; CAD P 388; di Mino

entries.meaning: virgin, maiden (divine epithet)
entries.note: HT 96a .4 PI-TA-RA · 1, whole, a recipient in a grain list after SI-MI-TA GRA 5, RU-SA 4, *323-*317 1 (GORILA I 157). Ug. btlt 'virgin' (btlt ʿnt; DULAT 248); b→p, l→r. Rival: a personal name. The slot gives no divine cue. One witness.

entries.meaning: grandtotal (lit. 'daughter of all')

cognates.Hebrew: bat kol (בַּת כֹּל) 'daughter of all'—compound accounting term
cognates.Akkadian: napḫar napḫāri 'total of totals' (different idiom, same concept)

entries.note: Gordon reading: PO-TO-KU-RO = bat kol, compound of bat 'daughter' + kol 'all' = grandtotal. Structural parallel to KU-RO (kull 'total'). On HT122b, PO-TO-KU-RO 97 follows KU-RO 65—a grandtotal that sums the subtotal with additional items. Rendsburg includes this in his survey of Gordon's confirmed readings. Skeleton ptkr maps to bt+kr via dead vowels. || PROVEN by cross-tablet arithmetic: HT122a KU-RO 31 + KU-DA 1 + HT122b KU-RO 65 = PO-TO-KU-RO 97 EXACT—the first demonstrated inter-tablet summation.
entries.source: Gordon 1966; Rendsburg confirms in survey of Gordon's readings

entries.meaning: allocation heading; possibly Baal, 'Lord'

Amarna.meaning: lord, master / lord of the houses
Amarna.note: Baal theophoric ubiquitous in Amarna (Šipti-Baʿla, etc.). bʿl t bbtm "lord of the houses" (EA 11 n.22) parallels institutional usage.

entries.note: PU-RA₂ occupies an allocation-heading position on HT28b and HT116a. Gordon's comparison with Baʿl/Bōl is semantically apt and uses di Mino's proposed PU=/bV/ and RA₂=/l/ correspondences, with loss of ʿayin. It nevertheless requires an acknowledged U/O correspondence and dead-vowel spelling, while RA₂=/l/ and the Baal identification partly support one another. Retain Baal as a candidate, not a confirmed reading. ZA6a ]PU₂-RA₂ GRA+PA 20 may be the same name at Zakros, with PU₂ = /bu/, in the same name-with-grain slot; the line is broken before PU₂, so a longer word is not excluded.
entries.source: Gordon 1966 §150; HT28b and HT116a corpus contexts

entries.meaning: incense, incense-offering (Semitic cultic term)
entries.note: Contingent on *118 = ṬA. HT96b (Haghia Triada, Casa Room 7, LMIB)—commodity tablet header. Full line: A-PA-RA-NE 𐄁 QA-*118-RA-RE 𐄁 *516 𐄁 GRA 𐄁 40¾ | OLE+U 4 | NI 2 1/16. A major commodity allocation (40¾ units grain, 4 olive oil). √q-ṭ-r "to smoke, burn incense"—Hebrew qeṭōret (THE ritual incense term in Biblical Hebrew), Arabic qaṭara "to drop, distill." The -RA-RE suffix could render the final root consonant + case ending, or a Semitic noun pattern like qaṭṭāra. "Incense" as a commodity header on a grain-and-oil ledger is semantically perfect. *118 = ṭa is speculative; √q-ṭ-r is well attested.

entries.meaning: its portion (a measured share); rival qadaša 'holy portion'

cognates.Arabic: qaṭīʿa 'portion (of land) held in fee', VIII 'took a portion' (Lane 2990)

entries.note: HT 70 .2 ]QA-*118-SA 2¼, broken before QA, part of *118 dotted (GORILA I 123), after NI · TE 30 and before I 3. With *118 = ṭa there is no q-ṭ-s root; QA-*118 (KH 10) with the suffix -ša 'its, her' gives qaṭʿ-ša 'its portion' (Lane 2990), a pre-*s > *h suffix. Rival: qōdeš 'holy portion' (HALOT 1076), which needs plain d, a value only possible for *118. A lost sign before QA would change the word. One witness.

entries.meaning: smith or cultic administrator; occupational title

cognates.Sabaic: qyn 'administrator, governor,' including an administrator of a god or king (Biella 1982, 454)

entries.note: 4× at Haghia Triada in administrative lists. QA-*310-I = QA-IN-I /qaynī/, using the proposed VC sign *310=/in/. Arabic qayn means 'smith, artisan'; Sabaic qyn denotes an 'administrator, governor,' including an administrator of a god or king (Biella 1982, 454). The Linear A distribution therefore supports a recurring occupational or administrative title. Hebrew qēnî 'Kenite' is formally comparable, but the historical relation among the smith, administrator and ethnonymic senses is not established; 'possessor' from √q-n-y is not required.

entries.meaning: personal name, Hurrian type in -šenni 'brother'

cognates.Hurrian: šēna 'brother' with the individualizing -ni, šen=ni, onomastic -šenni (Giorgieri 2000, 202; Wilhelm, Hurrian, 103; Laroche 1980, 225–26): Adal-šenni (RS 11.0839, a-dal-ŠEŠ) and Tulbi-šenni (RS 19.0063+, tul₂-bi-ŠEŠ) at Ugarit; Aku-šenni at Nuzi (NPN, s.v.)

entries.note: CR(?) Zf 1, a gold pin: A-MA-WA-SI · KA-NI-JA-MI · I-JA · QA-KI-SE-NU-TI · A-TA-DE. The name stands before the 1cs verb A-TA-DE, as the one who makes the pin ready. The second sign is KI, with GORILA IV 146–47, Younger and the photograph; it is not DE. KN Wb 33 joins QA-KI[ (a) and NU-SE (b, read leftward) as QA-KI-SE-NU-[ (Younger, Linear A Texts, other texts). Pattern of DA-KU-SE-NE /Takušenni/ (HT 103) beside DA-KU-SE-NE-TI (HT 104), with the same final -TI; the first element is unexplained, and QA, for a /q/ Hurrian lacks (Wilhelm, "Hurrian," 98–99), puts it outside Hurrian: a mixed name with Hurrian -šenni. Rival: Amorite two-element name, kakka + sanati.
entries.source: di Mino; Younger, Linear A Texts; Laroche 1980; Giorgieri 2000; Wilhelm, Hurrian; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943

entries.meaning: the top, head (?)
entries.note: SKO Zc 1, painted on a chalice rim in two non-joining fragments, order uncertain: NA-TU-*301-NE (natūnān, di Mino, Ya Diktu) and QA-KI-TI. Akkadian qaqqadu 'head; top (of a field, a city)' (CAD Q 100, 108); Hebrew qodqōd, Ugaritic qdqd. Weak points: KI for q beside QA, T for d, i for a; CAD gives no mountain-top sense. QA-QA-DA (PE 2) writes qaqqadu with QA and DA. One attestation.

entries.meaning: goblet, cup (vessel term on HT31 inventory)
entries.note: Gordon (§163) read qa-pa = kappu (√k-p-p 'palm/vessel'). PA₃=/ba/ changes the surface consonant to /b/. Written on the *402-VS vessel logogram on HT31 (qty 10). Part of Gordon's HT31 vessel quartet (§163) || LENITION ARGUMENT: Unlike SU-PA₃-RA and KA-RO-PA₃, lenition does NOT restore Gordon here: kappu has geminate /pp/, and geminates resist intervocalic voicing cross-linguistically (cf. begadkephat: post-vocalic /p/→/f/ but /pp/ stays). The scribe wrote PA₃ because the word genuinely had /b/ || Hebrew qubaʿat (קֻבַּעַת, Isaiah 51:17,22) 'goblet/cup'—an actual vessel term with original /b/. ʿAyin drops per 99.3% convention
entries.source: Gordon 1966 §163; di Mino; cf. Stieglitz (Kadmos 10, 1971, 111) who proposed Akkadian qapūtu / Hebrew qūpāh as alternative

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Ground' (Akkadian qaqqarum)

cognates.Akkadian: qaqqaru(m) 'ground, earth, territory, plot of land'
cognates.Ugaritic: qqr not attested; arṣ 'earth' is the common word

entries.note: A recipient or listed person at all three intact witnesses: HT93a QA-QA-RU · I GRA+PA 5; HT118, 6 pigs with KI 4; HT122b, 2 in a personnel list totalled KU-RO 65. HT111a ]QA-QA-RU 8 is broken before. Ebla has the noun as a personal name: ga-ga-lum = qaqqarum 'ground' (ARET 8 539 v. 9, 13′), and gar₃-ga-ri₂ = qarqari, both on the base qarqar- (Pagan 1998).

entries.meaning: parched (roasted) grain; rival Ugaritic qrwn 'offering'
entries.note: HT 86a, intact: QA-RA₂-WA 10, where HT 95a/b write QE-RA₂-U (qelwu 'parched grain') in the same set (KU-NI-SU, SA-RU, DI-DE-RU, DA-ME, MI-NU-TE). With RA₂ = /la/, PS √q-l-w 'roast': Geʿez qalawa, Heb. qālî (Lev 23:14; Ruth 2:14), Aram. qəlā. Rival: Ugaritic qrwn 'offering' (DULAT 703; KTU 1.127:10–11), with RA₂ = /ra/ and final n unwritten. Cf. LB qa-ra₂-wo, a personal name (KN Ce 50; DMic II). One attestation.

entries.meaning: city of (Phoenician construct form)
entries.note: Skeleton qrt = Phoenician qart- 'city (of)'. PS #2772 *milk-qart- 'Melqart (king of the city)' confirms the Phoenician construct. Uses unambiguous RE (not RA₂), providing a comparison for RA₂=/ra/ in QA-RA₂-WA and QE-RA₂-JA. On HT132 in commodity allocation context with *305. Huehnergard: fem. /qar(i)yatu/, construct /qart-/; BH qiryā.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Easterner' or 'Ancient one'

cognates.Ugaritic: qdm 'east' (Huehnergard 2012, glossary); qdmy 'ancient; ancestral' (DULAT 684); personal name Qdmn (Astour 1965, 152)
cognates.Hebrew: qedem 'east, ancient time' (HALOT 1069); qadmōnî, the Kadmonites (Gen 15:19; HALOT 1071)

entries.note: MA 1a and 1b, the faces of one bar from the Malia palace: I-DU-WI · *47 · QE-DE-MI-NU and A-MA · *47 · QE-DE-MI-NU (GORILA I 268–269). QE-DE-MI-NU writes Qadmīnu, √q-d-m 'front, east, early' with -īnu, beside KA-DU-MA-NE Kadumānu (HT 29) with -ānu. Astour sets Kadmos, Kadmōn and Kadmaiōn beside W-S qdm and the Ugaritic name Qdmn (Hellenosemitica 152); Heb. qadmōnî names the Kadmonites (Gen 15:19). Weak point: QE for qa. Rival: a non-Semitic name, or a title after *47. One bar.

entries.meaning: parched (roasted) grain
entries.note: Heads HT1 (KI-RO 197, ZU-SU 70, DI-DI-ZA-KE 52, KU-PA₃-NU 109, A-RA-NA-RE 105), a list with no commodity logogram. Closes the fixed set DA-ME, MI-NU-TE, SA-RU, KU-NI-SU 'emmer', DI-DE-RU on HT95a (under DA-DU-MA-TA · GRA) and HT95b; QA-RA₂-WA closes the same set on HT86a. PS *ḳVlVw- 'roast': Hebrew קָלִי 'parched grain', listed with wheat, barley and flour (2 Sam 17:28; Lev 23:14); Syriac qelyātā, Geʿez qēlēw 'roasted' (HALOT s.v. קָלִי); Akkadian qalītu 'parched grain' (CAD Q 59), verb qalû 'burn, roast' (CAD Q 69; OB to NA, Boğazköy and El-Amarna included). QE writes the e of qelyātā and qēlēw; RA₂ = /la/; U = /wu/. As a grain product it gives the HT95 set a second commodity beside KU-NI-SU, which bears on SA-RU and DI-DE-RU as recipients.
entries.source: HALOT s.v. קָלִי; CAD Q 59, s.v. qalītu; Dillmann 1865; di Mino

entries.meaning: bow, incised on the Malia palace wall; alternative 'throne, seat' (PS *kussīʾ-)

cognates.Akkadian: qaštu 'bow' (CAD Q 148); rival kussû 'chair, throne' (CAD K 587)
cognates.Hebrew: qešet 'bow' (קֶשֶׁת, HALOT 1155); rival kissēʾ 'throne, seat' (כִּסֵּא, HALOT 487)

entries.note: MA Ze 11, incised in the Malia palace south of the north-west court (GORILA IV 140), complete. QE-SI-TE writes qašt 'bow', the feminine -t in TE: Akk. qaštu, Ug. qšt, Heb. qešet, Geʿez qast. Not variants: KN Ze 49 (KE-SI-TE) and KN Ze 45 (KA-SI-A-TE) are masons' marks; THE Zb 13 reads 77-08-41-[[?-?-04]] (Karnava & Nikolakopoulou); KO-SA-I-TI (HT 117a) is a name. QE-SI-TE follows Heb. qéšet: QE writes qe, TE the -t; SI for še is a vowel mismatch only. Rival: kussīʾ 'throne, seat' (Akk. kussû, Ug. ksu, Heb. kissēʾ), which suits a palace but has no -t for TE. One attestation.

alternative_readings.note: throne, seat (root k-s-ʾ); Akk. kussû, Ug. ksu, Heb. kissēʾ. Fits a palace label, but the word has no -t for TE and QE must stand for k.

entries.meaning: in the charge of (list heading); Akk. qātu 'hand; charge'
entries.note: HT 7a: QE-TI · VIR+[?] heads a list of five men with numbers. Akk. qātu 'hand; custody, charge' (CAD Q 183), the word that marks whose charge a list records; QE writes qā. Cf. QẸ-TI-RA-DU · VIR+[?] (HT 58), in the same slot. Rival: a personal name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: small (portions)
entries.note: HT 41a .2 QE-TU 10, complete at the start (GORILA I 79), over *305 ·, *304 10, RE · *304 10, MI-DA-NI · PA-JA 2. QE-TU writes qaṭun 'small', the final n unwritten; QE-TU-NE (HT 12) writes it out. Weak point: QE for qa. Rival: Ug. qṭ 'flax, flaxseed (?)' (DULAT 708), a commodity; or a heading over the *304 entries. One attestation.

entries.meaning: small, fine (amounts)—quality term over the QA₂-ligature entry
entries.note: HT 12: QE-TU-NE · QA₂+[?]+PU 1, after QA-TI-DA-TE · OLE+DI 5 and *304 5, before E 30 and MA+RU · *118 5 (GORILA I 25). QE-TU-NE writes qaṭunē, *qaṭun- 'small, thin' with -ē: Heb. qāṭōn, qāṭān; Akk. qatnu 'thin, fine'; Ug. qṭn. QE-TU (HT 41a) is the form without the ending. Weak point: QE for qa. Rival: a heading or name over the QA₂ entry. One attestation.

entries.meaning: my incense (ritual term)
entries.note: Written *34-TI-RI, with *34 read QI. Hebrew qiṭṭēr 'to burn incense', qeṭōret 'incense'. TI for /ṭi/ via T/Ṭ neutralization. Register .1 of KNZc6, an ink-inscribed clay cup from a sanctuary deposit above the Basement of the Monolithic Pillars, Knossos; followed by A-DI DA-KI-TI 'until fine' (Lev 16:12 qəṭōret … daqqâ). 1cs possessive suffix -ī.

entries.meaning: Ra-Horus (Egyptian theophoric personal name); rival raḥil 'ewe-lamb'
entries.note: HT Wc 3006, a roundel: WA-O-MI RA-*314-RA. Egyptian Rꜥ-Ḥr(w) 'Ra-Horus': RA writes Rꜥ, *314 the ḥ of Ḥr, RA its r. Rivals: rāḥēl 'ewe' (HALOT 1216), Arb. riḫl, raḫil 'ewe-lamb' (Lane 1059), Akk. laḫru (CAD L 42), a roundel commodity; a local name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: to, for, as (preposition)
entries.note: RE read as /le/ not /re/—preposition function. EXCLUDED as commodity logogram. 62% numeral-following rate is a syntactic artifact—le- 'to, for' introduces allocation quantities on administrative tablets. The standalone occurrences outside HT 27 read grammatically. On HT 27a–b RE n is a counted entry (27a RE 20[; on 27b paired with SA, SA 4 RE 70 on one line), not le-; no reading there. HT32: OLE+NE RE 104 = 'libation oil for 104.' Methodological note: prepositions introducing quantities are a known confounder for the %Num commodity diagnostic.

entries.meaning: dance (√r-q-d); rival raqqitt- 'female dancer'

cognates.Akkadian: raqādu 'to dance' (CAD R 166); raqqidu, f. raqqittu 'dancer' (CAD R 171); riqittu 'dance' (CAD R 367)

entries.note: PO Zc 1, inked: RI-QE-TI-A-SA-SA-RA-[·]. Akk. riqittu 'dance' (ri-qi-it-tum), from √r-q-d with the d assimilated to t; QE writes qi. The same root gives raqqittu 'female dancer' (raq-qit-tum), with RI for ra. The pair matches U-QE-TI · JA-SA-SA-RA-ME on PL Zf 1, a -QE-TI word before the Asasara name. Rival: RI- + QE-TI, the element of HT 7a. Weak point: the cut before A-SA-SA-RA is analytical. One attestation.

entries.meaning: head, chief quality; first quality
entries.note: Akk. rēšum, Ug. rʔiš, Heb. rōʾš; -MA preserves archaic nominative mimation -um; HT81+HT115a allocation contexts with GRA+BOSm, KA-PO-RU; related: RE-SU 1× HT37, A-RI-SU 1× HT118 in list summing to KU-RO 30. || Huehnergard: Ug riš /raʾšu/ "head"; qatl nominal (triradical CvCC, sound root). Pl. rāšm /raʾāšūma/ and rāšt/rišt /raʾ(a)šātu/. BH cognate: rōʾš < *rāšu < *raʾsu "head"; pl. rāʾšīm < *rəʾāšīm < *raʾasima (Huehnergard 2012, pp. 41-42)

entries.meaning: setting, arrangement; a set/group (of vessels)—deverbal noun from √ś-y-m 'to place, set'

cognates.Amarna: sīm 'placing', under West Semitic influence (Moran, EA 155 n. 1); sīm lēb (EA 139 n. 8)

entries.note: HT 31 .3, after *416-VS-KA-RO-PA₃ 10: SA-JA-MA 30[, two tens visible and the surface lost after them. MA is the last sign. The five vessel names on the tablet stand over their logograms; SA-JA-MA stands without one, as KI-DE-MA-*323-NA does on .4. A noun /śaymā/ of √ś-y-m 'to set, place' (Heb. śîm, Amarna sīm); JA writes the y, so not the perfect śām. Gordon (1975, 153 n. 13) read sa-ya-ma-n[a] 'silver', after Aramaic סים: the tablet has no NA, and Jastrow (1903, 980) derives סִימָא 'silver' from Persian. Rival: a vessel name written without its logogram. Hapax.

entries.meaning: Samarō, personal name; compare Northwest Semitic √š-m-r and Egyptian smr

cognates.Amorite: samar, a name element 'guard, watch' (Huffmon 1965, 251)

entries.note: HT 88, one of six one-unit entries in the KI-RO roster. √š-m-r 'guard', the Amorite name element samar (Huffmon 1965, 251). Rival: Egyptian smr 'courtier'. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Harnessed'(?); cf. Amorite Ṣamidum

cognates.Amorite: ṢAMID-UM (ZA-MI-DU-UM), a woman's name (Gelb AS 21 no. 6398); ṢMD 'to bind, to harness' (p. 34)
cognates.Akkadian: rival samīdu B '(a type of groats)' (CAD S 115)

entries.note: HT 39 .3 SA-MA-TI 10, then KU-RE[ (GORILA I 75), complete at the left edge. The list runs TA-I-*123 10[, KU-RE-JU 8, KU[, SA-MA-TI 10, KU-RE[, then KU-RO *414+A 100[. SA-MA-TI takes no commodity sign and stands among names. It writes Ṣamidi, cf. the Amorite name ṢAMID-UM and Amorite ṢMD 'to harness' (Gelb AS 21 no. 6398, p. 34), Ug. ṣmd 'yoked pair'. Weak point: TI for di. Rival: Akk. samīdu B, a groats (CAD S 115), which needs a commodity slot. One attestation.

entries.meaning: groats, semolina, processed grain
entries.cognates: Akkadian samīdu/samiddu 'groats, coarse meal, semolina' (temple ration lists); related to SA-MA-TI (HT39) from same root
entries.note: Both attestations on Zakros stone vessels (ZA5a, ZA15a). Compare PS *samid-. The -E suffix may be a Minoan grammatical ending on a borrowed Akkadian commodity noun. Related to SA-MA-TI (HT39) only if that word is a commodity, which its slot does not show; shares the smt skeleton with JA-SU-MA-TU. Receives quantity 4 on ZA15a. || Huehnergard: Ug ṣmd /ṣimdu/ "pair, yoke, team (also: pairs of wheels)"; CiCCu noun pattern. Pl. ṣmdm /ṣimadūma/. BH cognate: ṣémed "pair, yoke" (segolate pattern) (Huehnergard 2012, pp. 130-135 (line 202)) || ONOMASTIC ALTERNATIVE—the X-dāʿ paradigm: Šumī/Šammī-dāʿē 'my Name knows', of the kinship-theophoric X-dāʿ name type beside A-MI-DA-U/A-MI-DA-O (ʿAmmī-dāʿ) — the -U/-E endings would need a final-vowel variation; Howard (JSS 68.1) documents /u/ > /a/ only in √ypʿ names (Niqmī-yapuʿ > Niqmēpaʿ). Amorite template fit 0.0 (sammi opener ×catalog, daʿi final, Gelb AS 21); biblical template ʾĂbîdāʿ/ʾEldāʿā (Gen 25:4). Context split: ZA15a quantity 4 favors the commodity; ZA5a list slot (after KI-NI-MA 7, O-TA-NI-ZA-SE 6) admits either.

entries.meaning: personal name, from √š-q-l 'to weigh'
entries.note: HT11b SA-QE-RI · KA 30, the last of five KA entries summed to KU-RO 180: a recipient, so a name, not the unit 'shekel'. Skeleton s-q-r matches š-q-l via the Linear A r/l merger. Names on the root: Amorite ŠIQL-AN-U, ŠIQL-AN-UM, ŠIQL-IM (Gelb 1980, nos. 5881–5883; glossary ŠQL 'to weigh'); Akkadian Šaqilia (ORACC P514274) and Šiqila (ORACC Q003427, Q006330).

entries.meaning: queen, princess (feminine of šarru)
entries.note: Feminine counterpart of SA-RU = šarru 'king'; the -u/-a terminal vowel is the Semitic masculine/feminine marker. The only bare SA-RA is SAMWa1 (Samothrace nodule), JA-SA SA-RA TE 10 ¹⁄₁₆, whose edition is untraced; it may be JA-SA-SA-RA across a line break, as IO Za 12 writes JA-SA / SA-RA-ME and IO Za 16 JA-SA-SA-RA / ME. HT 62 .1 has [·-·]-SA-RA, broken before (GORILA I 117). The same family is written SA-RA₂ (20 HT tablets), A-SA-RA₂ (HT 89) and SA-RA-RA (HT 30, the geminate written out). Hebrew Sarah (שָׂרָה) 'princess' (Gen 17:15) keeps the feminine form.

entries.meaning: queen/princess; by metonymy the queen's or royal establishment (recipient/institutional heading)

cognates.Linear A: SA-RU /šarru/ 'king/prince' and SA-RA /šarra/ 'queen/princess' are proposed members of the same title family

entries.note: 20 Haghia Triada accounting-tablet witnesses: 19 preserve the complete group, while HT125a has ]SA-RA₂ at a broken left edge and cannot independently prove that the group was complete there. Distribution strongly disfavors the šeʾāra 'remainder/surplus' analysis. HT105 places KA-PA and SA-RA₂ in parallel before VIR totals 234 and 235; HT100 and HT94a place SA-RA₂ after a completed KU-RO and before a new commodity section; HT30 and HT34 already use KI-RO for an actual deficit; HT97b preserves SA-RA₂ alone as a plausible docket or recipient label. Montecchi independently excludes a transactional meaning and identifies SA-RA₂ as probably a sender, recipient, personal name, or local name. Within the Semitic hypothesis, the SA-RA/SA-RU title family makes /šarra/ 'queen/princess' the strongest positive candidate; in administrative contexts this may refer metonymically to the queen's establishment, or more broadly the royal establishment. This remains CANDIDATE rather than PROBABLE: exact Akkadian šarratu would require an unwritten final /t/, and RA₂'s value is not securely /ra/ (proposals include /rya/, /rra/, /lya/, and /lla/). The √š-ʾ-r derivation is rejected because positional recurrence alone did not establish the semantics 'surplus.'
entries.source: Corpus distribution; Montecchi 2008, 321; comparative Akkadian šarratu and Hebrew śārâ

entries.meaning: royal allocation/account (the King's entry—šarr- royal-title family)
entries.note: Three convergent supports for the royal reading: (1) the šarr- family is independently established: SA-RU = šarru 'king, prince' (CANDIDATE), SA-RA₂ = šarra 'queen' (CANDIDATE); (2) on HT42+59 the SA-RO block (OLE+KI 8, OLE+U 2) is structurally coordinate with the preceding Šapšu block (OLE+KI 8, OLE+U 7)—recipient behavior, goddess then crown, not a section marker; (3) SA-RO carries its own quantities on HT17 (10) and HT19 (5½), natural for a beneficiary/account line, awkward for a marker; the rival *šārû 'opening of account' is moreover an inferred noun—the attested Akkadian form is šurrûm 'to begin'. Against it: no case ending yields -o, and the RO beside SA-RU is unexplained (the lexicon has no same-root RO/RU pair)—hence the gloss commits to royal semantics, not the vocalization *šarrō.

entries.meaning: king, prince (administrative title/category)

cognates.Hebrew: sǝrānīm 'city-princes' (KB 727); śar 'prince, chief' belongs with Akkadian šarru

entries.note: HT 86a and 86b (A-KA-RU · KU-NI-SU GRA+K+L 20, SA-RU 20, DI-DE-RU 20, QA-RA₂-WA 10), HT 95a (DA-DU-MA-TA · GRA, SA-RU 20 among DA-ME, MI-NU-TE, KU-NI-SU, DI-DE-RU and QE-RA₂-U) and HT 95b (A-DU · SA-RU 10, the same list): an entry in grain lists. HT 123+124a SA-RU OLIV 16, *308 4, beside KI-TA-I, PU-VIN and DA-TU; HT 94b SA-RU 1, one of five entries totalled KU-RO 5. A native reflex of PS *sVrw- 'chief, prince' (Ug. srn, Heb. sǝrānîm) or Akkadian šarru (Heb. śar). Rival: śaʿru 'barley' (Woudhuizen 2016, 226; Heb. śəʿōrâ, Ug. šʿrm, Old Aramaic šʿrh), ʿ unwritten, a grain kind beside KU-NI-SU 'emmer' and QE-RA₂-U 'parched grain'; it fits the four grain lists but not the olive and roster entries.

entries.meaning: uprightly (= JA-SA-SA-RA-ME with JA- prefix dropped in Palaikastro dialect)
entries.note: Palaikastro dialect variant. At PKZa11, the preceding token is standalone 'A' followed by a line break then SA-SA-RA-ME—the scribe split A-SA-SA-RA-ME across lines, with A- on one line and SA-SA-RA-ME continuing. The JA- prefix drops in Palaikastro proto-Phoenician dialect (cf. PKZa27 which retains JA-, standard register). Same reading as JA-SA-SA-RA-ME: *yaššaram* 'uprightly' (accusative -am). Huehnergard: /yušru/ "uprightness" (yuCCu nominal pattern); confirms adverbial accusative with -m.

entries.meaning: tribute, gift—logographic abbreviation of šay(u); administrative category marker for goods designated as tribute/gift offerings

cognates.Hebrew: šay (שַׁי) tribute, gift, present. Ps 68:30—tribute brought to the Temple; Ps 76:12—tribute brought to the Awesome One; Isa 18:7—tribute brought to YHWH Ṣebaʾôt. √š-y biconsonantal root

entries.note: 112 attestations across 3 distributional patterns, structurally parallel to TE (terûmā): (1) On tablets in position SI · NUMBER (10 occurrences: HT, KH, PH, GO)—marks a quantity as tribute: on HT106, MI-NU-TE · CYP · 6 · SI · 5½ · SI · 1 · DA · 8 · SI · 3 = tribute sub-quantities within a CYP reckoning (MI-NU-TE). On HT30, SI · 4 opens a multi-commodity summary. (2) Standalone on 93 nodules (all HT)—category stamp marking sealed goods as 'tribute.' Part of the single-sign nodule classification system: *301 (231), KU (152), KA (150), SI (93), RO (91), ZE (46), TE (27), I (25). (3) In compound logograms: SI+SE (3 tablets), QI+SI (ZA9), SI+ME, SI-CYP (HT130). The SI-CYP compound = 'tribute-cypress' parallels VIN+TE = 'wine-offering.' All three Hebrew attestations of שַׁי describe tribute brought to a temple or divine authority—mapping precisely onto a Minoan palace-sanctuary category stamp. SI and TE form a natural administrative pair: TE = terûmā 'sacred contribution/heave-offering' (voluntary donation to sanctuary), SI = šay 'tribute/gift' (obligatory or diplomatic gift).

entries.meaning: the account/record (phonetic complement + logogram)
entries.note: SI prefix = phonetic complement marking /s/-onset of logogram *516=SIPRU. Parallel to PA₃-*188 (marking /b/-onset of BUṬNU). Single attestation on HT34. Huehnergard: /sipru/ qitl pattern, pl. /siparūma/; BH sēper.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Arranger'

cognates.Akkadian: sadāru 'to do regularly; to be lined up' (CAD S 11)

entries.note: HT 17: SI-DA-RE 5 after SA-RO 10 under RA-*164-TI · TE · VIN 38. HT 122a: SI-DA-RE 1 in a roster of men, KU-RO 31. √s-d-r 'to set in order' (Akk. sadāru, Heb. sēder); SI-DA-RO (GO 2r) and JA-SI-DA-RA[ (PH 7a) are on the same signs. Weak point: the -E. Rival: √s-t-r 'to hide', Heb. Sitrī (Exod 6:22). Two attestations.

entries.meaning: personal name; etymology uncertain
entries.note: Probable personal name in the damaged HT126a administrative list, immediately followed by 1. Ugaritic alphabetic śdy is attested as a PN in šmbʿl bn śdy (BAH 214, 7, o 14), and syllabic {m}ša-di-ia occurs at Ugarit in RS 15.0173, r. 2′. The first-vowel difference prevents treating the syllabic spelling as identical, but the consonantal and onomastic agreement is strong. The former derivation 'of Shaddai' is withdrawn; comparison with the Semitic field/estate root remains a lexical rival, not the adopted name etymology.

entries.meaning: which goes out (disbursement marker)—relative particle šī + 3ms imperfect √y-ṣ-ʾ "to go out"

cognates.Hebrew: אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵא ʾašer-yēṣē "that which goes out" (2 Kgs 12:13, Temple expenditure)
cognates.Akkadian: ṣītu "expenditure, disbursement"; wāṣītu "outgoing goods" (OB/MB palace archives)
cognates.Phoenician: š- relative particle (< PS *ḏū)—diagnostic Canaanite feature

entries.note: Productive suffix on pithos labels: A-NA-NU-SI-JA-SE (HTZb159), KI-TA-NA-SI-JA-SE (PEZb3). Parsed as two-morpheme relative clause: šī (Phoenician-type relative particle, cf. MLK Š-PʿL) + yāṣē (3ms impf. √y-ṣ-ʾ with ʾaleph-III loss, > *yiṣʾaʾu > yāṣē). Tags commodity nouns as outgoing disbursements. || Structural parallel: Hebrew אשר-יצא (2 Kgs 12:13) uses the identical construction (relative + impf. √y-ṣ-ʾ) in Temple accounting to mark expenditures. Akkadian ṣītu is the standard administrative term for disbursements, contrasted with erēbu/ēribu "income." || Diagnostic value: if SI = š(ī) is the relative particle, Minoan clusters with Canaanite (š-type) rather than Ugaritic/Aramaic (d-type). || Bare yāṣē (without the relative šī) now also read within JA-PA-RA-JA-SE = yapʾara yāṣē (SYZa9, Syme libation vessel): the same morpheme in liturgical register—the libation as "that which goes out." Component broken out as its own JA-SE entry.

entries.meaning: Seat of Righteousness (toponym/institutional name)

cognates.Akkadian: kummu A 'cella, private room (of a temple or palace)' (CAD K 533)
cognates.Hurrian: Kummi, the city of Tešub (Hitt. Kummiyaš); Kummeni, epithet of Tešub (Laroche 1980, 154)

entries.note: NWS √ṣ-d-q 'righteous' (SI=ṣi via S-class neutralization) + Akkadian kummu A 'cella, private room (of a temple or palace)' (CAD K 533). Institutional name at Haghia Triada. *34=QI (K-class: covers /qi/, /gi/, /ki/). || Huehnergard: Ug ṣdq /ṣidqu/ "rightness, legitimacy"; qiCCu noun pattern. ṣdqh /ṣidqi-hū/ "his legitimate/rightful". BH cognate: ṣēdeq "righteousness" (Ug. i/u vowels vs. BH development) (Huehnergard 2012, p. 87) || Rival: 'Ṣidq of Kummi', with Kummi the city of Tešub, Hitt. Kummiyaš, and Kummeni his epithet (Laroche 1980, 154). DDD s.v. Ṣedeq: deity name (Melchizedek, Adoni-ṣedeq, Philo Sydyk)—theophoric "Shrine of Ṣedeq" also possible.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD K; Laroche 1980; Huehnergard 2012

entries.meaning: dwelling/sanctuary (√š-k-n) or covered booth (√s-k-k, cf. sukkā); administrative: steward/prefect office

cognates.Hebrew: šākan "to dwell" (HALOT 1496); šĕkīnā "Shekhinah"; OR sukkā (סֻכָּה) "booth, tabernacle" (√s-k-k "to cover"); Sukkot (סֻכּוֹת) festival of booths
cognates.Akkadian: šakānu "to place, set, establish" (CAD Š1 115); šaknu "governor"

entries.note: 7 attestations across 2 sites (IOZa6 SI-KA is a separate homograph from √š-q-y, not this entry): (1) six identical HT nodules from Portico 11/Room 13—administrative sealings, plausibly institutional stamps from a steward/prefect office; (2) A-DA-KI-SI-KA at KH5. The administrative analysis compares √š-k-n and the title family represented by Ugaritic skn /sākinu/ 'prefect,' Amarna sū-ki-ni /sōkini/, and SI-KI-NE Sikinet; the precise truncation or suffixation remains unresolved. An alternative compares √s-k-k 'cover' and Hebrew sukkā 'booth.' The older divine-dwelling/Shekhinah comparison is only a late semantic parallel and does not establish the word's function.

entries.meaning: stewardess or female administrator; compare masculine prefect/commissioner

Amarna.meaning: commissioner, one who provides (glossing Akk. rābišu)
Amarna.moran_page: Intro p. xxvi n.70; EA 287 n.22
Amarna.note: Moran: West Semitic *sōkinu (Hebrew sōkēn), 'one who provides.' Durand proposes 'resident.' These administrative title readings are the primary comparison.

cognates.Hebrew: sōkenet (סֹכֶנֶת), Qal participle fs, of Abishag (1 Kgs 1:2, 4)

entries.note: Strong root and title candidate. The displayed reading Sikinet, vocalized /šikinēt/, follows SI-KI-NE syllable for syllable and requires only an unwritten feminine final /t/. Ugaritic šknt is tentatively vocalized /sākinat-/ 'female administrator, stewardess' (Tropper 2000, 180, KTU 4.135:2; škn 4.36:3), and Hebrew has the same feminine participle, sōkenet, of Abishag (1 Kgs 1:2, 4), while later Akkadian šakintu, oblique šakinte, denotes a female official or governess. The masculine comparison is independently strong: Ugaritic skn /sākinu/ means 'prefect' and is written syllabically sā-ki-ni, while Amarna Canaanite sū-ki-ni /sōkini/ denotes a prefect or commissioner. Thus 'stewardess' is preferred, with 'prefect/commissioner' retained as the economical title comparison. The exact historical vowel pattern remains a project reconstruction. The older 'Shekhinah/divine dwelling' interpretation survives only as a weak root-level association: the specialized divine-presence sense is much later and is not independently established here.
entries.source: Huehnergard 2012, p. 212; Lipiński 1997, §21.12; Tropper 2000, 180; CAD Š/1

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Hired' (√ś-k-r 'to hire'); rival šēkār 'strong drink'
entries.note: HT 8a: JE-DI · OLE+KI 10, then PA₃-KA-RA-TI 1½, PA 3½, TE-*301 2, QA-*310-I ¾, SI-KI-RA ¼, KI-RE-TA-NA ½; a recipient of KI-oil beside Tēnā 'Fig', the smith and the Cretan. √ś-k-r 'to hire' (Ug. /š-k-r/ I, DULAT 804; Heb. śākār 'wages', HALOT 1330): at Mari Sa-ki-rum and the woman's name Sa-ki-ra, under *škr 'hire, reward, favor' (Huffmon, APNM 245–46), Sa-ki-rum compared to Hebrew śākîr 'hired; hireling' (APNM 145); Gelb, AS 21, no. 5400 ŠAKIR-U (SA-KI-RU). Rival: Hebrew שֵׁכָר šēkār 'strong drink' (HALOT 1501; Lev 10:9), √š-k-r 'to become intoxicated' (Ug. /š-k-r/ II, DULAT 804). A-SI-KI-RA (KH 20) stands in the entry slot before CYP+E, parallel to ]DU-RE-ZA. One witness.

entries.meaning: name, renown, progeny (common noun in construct state; also attested as personal name Šima = Shem)

cognates.Akkadian: šumu "name, offspring, progeny" (CAD Š/III 281); Amorite PN element: Sumu-abum "Progeny of the Father" (founder of 1st Dynasty of Babylon, c. 1894 BCE), Sumu-la-El "Progeny of God"

entries.note: PHZb4 (Phaistos, clay vessel): SI-MA 𐄁 I-JA-TE. Dual function: (1) common noun šima "name of" in construct state; (2) personal name Šima = Shem, meaning "Name/Renown/Progeny." On a vessel, the PN reading is more natural — a person identified on a commodity vessel, paralleling DI-NA-U 𐄁 VIN on KNZb<27>. The Amorite onomastic parallel is exact: šumu- is the most productive name element in Old Babylonian Amorite onomastics (Sumu-abum, Sumu-la-El, Šumu-ditāna in Hammurabi's genealogy). Pan-Semitic noun, no root dispute. || Case unassigned: nothing here selects it (Fischer 2002, §140).

entries.meaning: pourings, libation portions (wine administration term)
entries.cognates: Akkadian šapāku 'to pour, heap up'; Hebrew šāpak (שָׁפַךְ) 'to pour out, shed'; Ugaritic špk 'to pour'
entries.note: Fixed co-occurrence with JI-NU-MA-RE (wine-stewards, PROBABLE) on all 3 Zakros stone vessels (ZA4a, ZA5b, ZA15a). On ZA5b followed by MA-KA-I-TA (makita 'magical protection'). Wine distribution context makes 'pourings/libation portions' semantically strong. Receives quantities (5, 1.5, 2.5) consistent with commodity allocation.

entries.meaning: sacred song, hymnody (proposed abstract in -ūt of √š-y-r "sing")

cognates.Akkadian: non-cognate semantic and morphological controls in -ūtu: kalûtu "the lament-singer's craft/repertoire," zammārūtu "music," and Old Babylonian nārūtu "musicianship"

entries.note: Preferred */šīrūt/*, a regular but unattested abstract in pan-Semitic -ūt from √š-y-r 'sing', rendered 'sacred song' from its exclusively ritual distribution; 'sacred' is not a separately written adjective. Ugaritic syllabic ši-i-ru /šīru/ 'song' secures the root and /šī-/ in the Bronze Age (Huehnergard 2012, 158). Secondary: /šīrōt/ 'songs' (Amos 8:3), but its ancestor *šīrāt predicts SI-RA-TE and shifted /šīrōt/ predicts SI-RO-TE; Linear A has distinct O and U series (Steele 2024, 17), and the stone has RU, not RO, wherever the sign survives (IO Za 2, KO Za 1, SY Za 3, VRY Za 1). Rival, same consonants and vowels: */širrūt/* 'cultic service' (√š-r-t), ancestor of MHeb. *šêrût*, JArm. *šêrûtā* 'service, worship' (HALOT 1661). The root is Canaanite: Levites 'stand before YHWH to minister to him' (*lĕšārĕtô*, Deut 10:8; 18:7) and singers 'ministered before the tabernacle with song' (*mĕšārĕtîm … baššîr*, 1 Chr 6:17); Ph. *pʿl mšrt ʾt pn gw* 'performed service before the community' (KAI 60.7–8); Pu. 'any person who shall not serve, Our Lady Tinnit-Phanebal and the Lord Baalhammon shall bind' (CIS i 5510.4–6, Carthage 406 BCE); NPu. *rʾš ʿm šrt* 'head of the service personnel' (KAI 136.4–5) (Krahmalkov s.vv. MŠRT, Š-R-T I, ŠRT II; Tomback s.v. MŠRT). Ugaritic *šrd* 'to serve' is doubtful, 'more likely' Š of √yrd (Huehnergard 2012, 157), so */širrūt/* would be the Bronze Age ancestor of the Canaanite word. Final E may be a support vowel after /t/. 7 tokens on stone vessels at 5 peak-sanctuary sites (Iouktas, Kophinas, Syme, Troullos, Vrysinas); several are fragmentary (IO Za 14, IO Za 15, TL Za 1; PK Za 11 shows only SI-RU-[). || After I-PI-NA-MA a genitive *šīrūti* is expected (Fischer 2002, §292); the same TE spelling recurs in genitive position in APZa2 and PHZb4, against ZA-TI (KNZc7).

entries.meaning: vessel (pot)
entries.note: Gordon's etymology holds via intervocalic lenition. Gordon (§163) read su-pa-ra = sēpel (Hebrew ספל 'bowl'), treating PA=/p/ and RA=/l/. PA₃=/ba/ (a proposed value) shifts surface skeleton s-p-r → s-b-r, but underlying PS root √s-p-l is preserved: intervocalic *p→b is regular lenition in Minoan phonological adaptation (V_V environment: /u_a/), l→r = standard liquid mapping || SEMANTIC CONFIRMATION: Vessel meaning independently secured—*402-VS logogram (pictographic vessel determinative) + position in HT31 vessel inventory (alongside QA-PA₃, SU-PU, KA-RO-PA₃) + V&C independent identification. Part of Gordon's HT31 vessel quartet (§163): 4 of 5 vessel names identified as Semitic || The scribe writes PA₃ precisely because the word was pronounced with /b/ in Minoan—supporting rather than undermining PA₃ = /ba/

entries.meaning: bowl, basin (the vessel named on HT31)
entries.note: On HT31, the vessel tablet, the word is written into a vessel sign: *415-VS-SU-PU 10, beside *416-VS-KA-RO-PA₃ 10 (the jar, Akkadian karpu) and *402-VS-QA-PA₃ 10. Every cognate names a bowl or basin (Hebrew sap, Ugaritic sp, Phoenician sp), which also keeps HT31's two vessels distinct.

entries.meaning: bowl of terebinth (pistachio) nuts (commodity measured in bowl-units)
entries.note: SU-PU₂ = /sapu/ 'bowl, basin' (see SU-PU). Commodity *188 = buṭn- 'terebinth/pistachio nuts' (Hebrew boṭnîm, Gen 43:11; Ugaritic bṭm) in bowl-units. HT8b Villa Magazine, qty 1.

entries.meaning: may you (f.) be favorable toward us (N-stem of √r-ṣ-y + indicative -u + analogical 2fs subject clitic -tī + 1cp object -n; energic -n the alternative)

cognates.Hebrew: rāṣāh (רָצָה) 'to be pleased with, accept favorably' (Lev 1:4, Ps 19:15, Mal 1:8, Ezek 20:40–41, 43:27); rāṣōn (רָצוֹן) 'favor, acceptance, goodwill' (Prov 11:1, Ps 5:13); √r-ṣ-y 'to accept, be pleased'
cognates.Arabic: raḍiya (رضي) 'to be pleased, satisfied, accept'; riḍā 'acceptance, divine pleasure'

entries.note: IOZa2 line 2, in the frame TA-NA-[X]-U-TI-NU shared with IO Za 6 (X = I-*301) and IO Za 11 (]U-TI-NU). TA- = 2fs prefix; -NA- = N-stem n-, unassimilated before /r/ (later Hebrew תֵּרָצֶה tērāṣeh; Lipiński §41.16); RA-TE = √r-ṣ-y 'be acceptable' (Hebrew Niphal, Lev 1:4; TE = ṣ unproved); U = indicative -u of the yaqtulu conjugation, preceding the subject pronoun (Ugaritic ʾargmk /ʾargumu-kī/, KTU 1.3 III 21; modal 'may' sense, cf. Huehnergard 2012, 55–56; -u "remains attached directly to the verbal base, and pronominal object suffixes follow it," Bjøru and Pat-El 2021, 56), the least secure element; TI = archaic 2fs nominative subject clitic (subject clitics from the nominative pronouns, usable on other bases: Pat-El 2025, 330, 332), extended analogically to a finite host; NU = 1cp object 'us' (PS *-na, Ugaritic -n/-nā), energic n-extension the alternative. Controls: Enūma eliš I 119–20 ul taremmināsi 'you (f.) do not love us'; Josh 2:18 hôradtēnû; Ugaritic tšqy-n (KTU 1.19 IV 53). Principal objection: ordinary 2fs *taqtulīna, with -na after gender-number suffixes (Bjøru and Pat-El 2021, 48), a Central Semitic innovation beside shared -u (Bjøru and Pat-El 2021, 66).

entries.meaning: may [it] be drunk for you (f.)—N-stem 3fs imperfective of √š-t-y 'to drink' + 2fs pronominal suffix -kī
entries.note: Hapax. Position 1 on PRZa1 (Prassa stone vessel, LMIA), occupying the formula verb slot. Followed by SE-TO-I-JA (toponym?, hapax) and A-SA-SA-RA-ME (formula word, RA drawn reversed). TA-NA = N-stem 3fs imperfective prefix (same structure as TA-NA-RA-TE from √r-ṣ-y): ta- (3fs) + na- (N-stem). SU = C₁ (š, sibilant merger), TE = C₂ (t), KE = 2fs pronominal suffix -kī 'for you (f.)' addressing the Goddess; weak C₃ (y) drops as expected for lamed-he verbs. Morphological parallel to TA-NA-RA-TE is exact: both N-stem 3fs imperfective with root starting after TA-NA. Semantics: the vessel addresses the Goddess—'may [the offering] be drunk for/by you.'

entries.meaning: Tanit variant—TNT goddess at Haghia Triada (a-vowel pattern). Dual etymology: (A) √t-n-n feminine 'she-dragon', (B) t-ʿAnatu (Hvidberg-Hansen 1979). Context: HT49a alongside KU-PA₃-NU (Kubānu, a probable name or title) and TU-SU-PU₂ (Teshub).
entries.note: 4× at HT (HT7a, HT10b, HT49a, HT98a). Support: (1) significant frequency, (2) HT49a context with known Layer 3 names, (3) Hvidberg-Hansen 1979 scholarly framework, (4) Zakros variant TA-NA-TE reinforces the TNT goddess identification.

entries.meaning: may you (f.) be gracious/favourable (if TA begins the word)
entries.note: GORILA IV, 8–9 prints ]TA-NU-MU-TI; the initial break is of indeterminate extent, so this analysis applies only if TA begins the word. Proposed G u-class /ta-nʿum-u-tī/: Arabic naʿuma/yanʿumu supports the u-vocalism; Sabaic n²m ‘be favourable, prosper’ supplies the closest semantics (Beeston et al. 1982, 90); Hebrew nāʿamt (Song 7:7) is a 2fs semantic/person control. The ʿ is unrepresented, and -tī is di Mino's analogical 2fs subject clitic rather than an independently attested prefix-conjugation ending; Thomas's plural-agreement reading remains a rival. The former √t-n-m ‘I dedicated’ and tD */tanaʿʿamti/ analyses are withdrawn.
entries.source: GORILA IV, 8–9; Beeston et al. 1982, 90, s.v. N²M; Fischer 2002, §162f; Harding 1971, 139; di Mino

entries.meaning: chant a dirge! (proposed internal segmentation)

cognates.Hebrew: Piʿel √t-n-y ‘recount, recite’ (Judg 5:11; 11:40), including a proposed association with repetition in antiphonal performance (HALOT, 1759–60)
cognates.Northwest Semitic: Hebrew qînâ ‘funeral song, dirge’; Syriac qintā ‘hymn, lament’ (HALOT, 1097)

entries.note: PL Zf 1 hapax on a silver pin from a funerary context. Proposed internal segmentation TA-NU-NI / KI-NA = /tannî qînâ/, naturally ‘chant a dirge!’: /tannî/ is the expected 2fs Piʿel imperative of √t-n-y ‘recount, recite,’ while /qînâ/ is the standard Hebrew funeral song or dirge. The English ‘chant’ reflects HALOT's proposed repetition in antiphonal performance; the stricter lexical gloss is ‘recite/repeat.’ TA-NU-NI can preserve the doubled middle radical with a dead vowel in NU, while KI-NA can represent /qînâ/ without vowel length or final /h/. The principal cost is epigraphic: no divider occurs between NI and KI, so the two-word segmentation is proposed rather than written.

entries.meaning: gatekeepers (of the sanctuary); rival Akkadian tārû 'child-minder'

cognates.Ugaritic: ṯġr (II) 'gatekeeper', pl. ṯġrm, in personnel and ration lists (KTU 4.126:22; 4.141 III 2; 4.128:11)

entries.note: HT89 TA-RA 5, last of five classes under A-SA-RA₂ · *307 (dubur 'sanctuary'), KU-RO 87. /ṯa(ġ)ra/ from *ṯaġr- 'gate', ṯ written in the T-series before a and ġ unwritten: Ug. ṯġr 'gatekeeper', a personnel class with grain rations (DULAT 888); the gatekeepers of the house of God beside MA-I-MI's water-drawers (Ezra 7:24). Cf. TA 4, last entry before KU-RO on HT 94a (entries 111 against KU-RO 110), and ]TA 4 before ]KU-RO 129 on HT 109, broken on the left. Rival: Akkadian tārû 'child-minder' (CAD T), which predicts TA-RU. One witness.
entries.source: HT89 list structure; DULAT 888; Ezra 7:24; Uchitel 2006, Kadmos 45: 73; Militarev and Kogan 2005, SED II no. 232: 297–98; CAD T s.v. tārû

entries.meaning: father (Luwian tati-)
entries.note: Exact predicted Linear A rendering of CL Luwian tati- 'father' (Melchert 1993 p. 209). Also embedded in Troy compound forms PI-MI-TA-TI-RA₂ (TROZg1) and DU-MI-TA-TI-RA₂ (TROZg2). Currently unclassified in onomasticon. The Luwian identification is speculative: TA-TI could equally be a NWS form or abbreviation. However, the Anatolian geographic association of the Troy compounds and the exact phonological match support monitoring this as a Luwian contact candidate.

entries.meaning: proposed Semitic lexical name of the PALM/TREE sign
entries.note: Official semantic reading of *49 (AB049): PALM/TREE, based on its pictorial form and counted administrative contexts. TAMIR is the retained Semitic lexical identification: Proto-Semitic *tam(V)r- 'date palm,' Hebrew tāmār, Ugaritic tmr and Arabic tamr. The associated syllabic value /mi/ remains CANDIDATE, not established: TO-*49-RE yields the attractive skeleton t-m-r only if /mi/ is first assumed, while Linear B writes *49 beside ordinary MI in tu-*49-mi. ZA10b preserves complete U-*49; HT126a has ]U-*49 after a left break and cannot establish the compound or an initial conjunction. DA-U-*49 remains the candidate name Dawmi. Four *49 occurrences survive across three sites.

entries.meaning: administrative transaction or category marker; perhaps contribution or offering

cognates.Ugaritic: trmt 'offering' (KTU 1.43:3; 1.6 VI:44; Copenhagen Ugaritic Corpus lexicon)
cognates.Akkadian: tāmartu 'gift, present (to temple or king)'—a functional parallel, not a cognate

entries.note: TE occurs in 56 documents at six identified sites plus AN Zb 1, whose site is unrecorded in the corpus. Commodity-number entries and 25 one-sign HT nodules securely establish an administrative category or transaction function. Hebrew terûmā 'contribution' and Ugaritic trmt 'offering' support the proposed sense, but Linear A TE does not spell the full word and no TE-RU-MA form is attested. Terûmā therefore remains a proposed acrophonic or logographic value, not a lexical identification. VIN+TE may be a compound commodity marker but does not independently prove 'wine-offering.'
entries.source: Corpus distribution; Hebrew terûmā; Ugaritic trmt (KTU 1.43:3; 1.6 VI:44)

entries.meaning: Fig (personal name); a recipient in allocation lists
entries.note: A recipient on both tablets: HT8a TE-*301 2 in the OLE+KI list between PA 3½ and QA-*310-I ¾ (QA-*310-I receives again on HT8b); HT98a TE-*301 ¾ between DI-RE-DI-NA and RO-KE. Hebrew təʾēnāh 'fig tree' (HALOT 1675), contracted in Mishnaic Hebrew tīnā and Aramaic tyn; Akkadian tittu (tiʾittu), pl. tinātu, with an Old Assyrian 'Month of Figs' (CAD T 435); Arabic tīn. A fruit-tree name as a personal name, as Hebrew Tamar 'date palm' (HALOT 1756) and Ugaritic tmr (DULAT 859). No fig-name is attested elsewhere. NI (AB30) remains the fig ideogram.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Bull' (PS *ṯawr-)

cognates.Hebrew: šôr (שׁוֹר) "bull, ox" (BDB 1004); from PS *ṯawr- via ṯ→š

entries.note: HT117a (Haghia Triada, Casa Room 9, LMIB): one of ten entries counted 1 each, KU-RO 10, under the MA-KA-RI-TE heading ("merchants," CANDIDATE); a name on the noun 'bull', as Tēnā 'Fig' (TE-*301). Alongside KU-RA-MU (Kurmu 'Vineyard'), KU-PA₃-NU (Kubānu, PROBABLE), NA-DA-RE (Nadr 'Vow', PROBABLE). The NWS w→y shift turns *ṯawr- into tayr-: JA renders the /y/. The initial /ṯ/ is written with TE because no /ṯe/ or /ṯa/ sign exists—only ZU=/ṯu/. This ṯ→T neutralization before non-/u/ vowels independently confirms ZU's vowel-specific function. Bull-horn dyad with KA-RO-NA (qarna "horn") on HT11a—same archive, same period. Ugaritic El is ṯr ʾil "Bull El"—the bull as divine epithet. PY Ta 711 (Linear B) qo-u-ka-ra = gʷou-kara ("bull-headed") ritual vessels belonging to the wanassa.

entries.meaning: Tinit (goddess, = Phoenician Tanit)

cognates.Phoenician: tnt 'Tanit' (Sarepta, KAI 285, 7th c. BCE: dedication to Tanit-Astarte)
cognates.Punic: tnt 'Tinnit' (Carthage stelae: lrbt ltnt pn bʿl 'to the Lady Tinnit, face of Baal')
cognates.Punic in Greek letters: ΘΙΝΙΘ Thinith 'Tinnit' (El-Hofra stele, Constantine: ΘΙΝΙΘ ΦΑΝΕ ΒΑΛ)

entries.note: On HT27a, TI-NI-TA appears directly before *307 (= DUBUR, sanctuary). Pattern "Goddess + Sanctuary" = Linear A equivalent of Linear B Potnia Daboritu. Variant TA-NA-TI (4 attestations: HT10b, HT49a, HT7a, HT98a) is more frequent. || Vocalization: the Greek transcription ΘΙΝΙΘ Thinith records i–i, not conventional 'Tanit'—the same vowels as TI-NI-TA, a vocalic match across a millennium, not consonants alone. Against the Berber-origin view of Tanit (t…t feminine pattern of Tamazight names): an LM I attestation a millennium before Carthage favours a Levantine–Aegean origin.

entries.meaning: Tinit of the Sanctuary (Goddess + Sanctuary pattern)
entries.note: HT27a: TI-NI-TA *307 = 'Tinit of the Sanctuary.' Three-script chain: Linear A TI-NI-TA *307 = Linear B Potnia da-pu2-ri-to-jo = Hebrew Baʿalat ha-Dəḇîr. || Word-field notation: 'TI-NI-TA *307' records the attested epithet phrase (goddess name + sanctuary logogram) as it appears on HT27a; not split into separate entries.

entries.meaning: palm/tree or date-palm produce
entries.note: PE2 commodity tablet at Petras. With the official PALM/TREE semantic reading, the entry plausibly denotes palm or date-palm produce. Reading *49 syllabically as /mi/ gives TO-MI-RE and the exact consonantal skeleton t-m-r, comparable to Proto-Semitic *tam(V)r-, Hebrew tāmār, Ugaritic tmr and Arabic tamr. This supports TAMIR as a candidate lexical identification but does not independently prove /mi/, because the same word supplies the proposed value. Final RE may support coda /r/.

entries.meaning: our purification (genitive + 1cp -nā)
entries.note: The main support for *21F = /ha/, a speculative value. √ṭ-h-r 'to be clean, purify'—pan-Semitic: Ugaritic ṭhr 'to purify' (DUL 872), Hebrew ṭāhēr 'to be clean, pure' (HALOT 369), Arabic ṭahura, Aramaic ṭǝhar. Central to temple/ritual vocabulary across all Semitic traditions. TU writes /ṭu/ (T/Ṭ not distinguished in Linear A). -NA is the 1cp possessive -nā after the genitive -i, since Linear A has no definite article; cf. lə-ṭohŏrātô 'for his purification' (Lev 14:23). Rival: emphatic enclitic =na (Tropper 2000, §89). || Huehnergard: Ug ṭhr /ṭuhūru/ < *ṭahūru "pure"; II-guttural adjective. qutūl < qatūl pattern (vowel raising before guttural). BH cognate: ṭāhōr "pure, clean" (Huehnergard 2012, p. 42). In context, grain 40½ and three oils (OLE+DI 1, OLE+KI 6, OLE[) stand under the heading on HT129: the offering of Hebrew ṭohŏrâ, where on 'the day of his purification' (bəyôm ṭohŏrātô, Lev 14:2) the man brings fine flour mixed with oil and a log of oil (Lev 14:10, 21) 'for his purification' (lə-ṭohŏrātô, Lev 14:23). TU- fits the u of Ug. /ṭuhūru/ and Heb. ṭohŏrâ. Ugaritic ṭhrm 'pure' occurs in KTU 1.4, 1.24, 2.39.

entries.meaning: my wholeness, my completeness (noun *tumm- + 1cs -ī)
entries.note: Two damaged witnesses give the group in full. PK Za 8 (GORILA IV 24–26) secures the start with a divider before TU, but ME is partial and I survives only as the tops of three prongs at the broken corner, with no divider preserved before JA-SA[ on the next face. Younger regards only TU as secure. PK Za 14 (IV 40) secures the end, ]-TU-ME-I · JA-SA-SA-[, but breaks before TU. Hebrew תֻּמִּי tummī 'my wholeness/integrity' (Ps 7:9; 26:1) supplies the exact nominal shape. On both vessels √t-m-m 'wholeness/completeness' stands before a √y-š-r word (JA-SA[, JA-SA-SA-[), cf. Job 1:1 tām wə-yāšār, Ps 25:21 tōm wāyōšer (di Mino, Ya Diktu), which supports 'my wholeness, [in righteousness]' while keeping the two roots distinct. A D-stem imperative 'be made whole' is less likely: a regular factitive imperative would ordinarily preserve more of the stem. Alternative roots √d-m-m/√d-m-y (TU≠DU) and √ṭ-m-ʾ (wrong sign, vocalism, and semantics) remain disfavored.

entries.meaning: judge (title)
entries.note: PORZf2 (Poros Herakleiou, metal object): sole inscription—single word stamped on bronze, consistent with authority token or judicial seal || ETYMOLOGY: PS #987 *tVpVṭ- 'judge': Ug. ṯpṭ (Yamm's epithet ṯpṭ nhr 'Judge River'), Heb. šōpēṭ 'judge' (√š-p-ṭ, with ṯ→š in Hebrew), Arab. ṣabiṭ || PHONOLOGY: Three neutralizations: T→ṯ, P→p (trivial), T→ṭ. Initial TU (not ZU) expected: ṯāpiṭu starts with /ṯā-/, and ZU=/ṯu/ only writes /ṯ/ before /u/. Before /ā/, the /ṯ/ neutralizes to T-series—same pattern as TE-JA-RE (tayru 'bull') where /ṯ/ before /a/ → TE. Independently confirms ZU's vowel-specific function

alternative_readings.note: sacred precinct / place of judgment (root ṯ-p-ṭ (same root)). Cognates: Heb. תֹּפֶת tōpet (2 Kgs 23:10, Jer 7:31–32); Punic tpt (Carthaginian sacred precinct for votive deposits) tōpet may itself derive from √ṯ-p-ṭ: 'place of judgment' where the deity accepts/rejects the offering. If so, ṯāpiṭu and tōpet are cognate derivatives of the same root, and the two readings collapse: 'judge' (title) → 'place of judgment' (sacred precinct). Both senses fit a metal votive object at a harbor sanctuary.

entries.phonological_notes: Skeleton tpt requires T→ṯ (interdental), P→p (trivial), T→ṭ (emphatic). TU writes /ṯā/ because ZU=/ṯu/ is vowel-locked to /u/. PI = /pi/. TA = /ṭu/ with dead vowel.

entries.meaning: Shield, Protector (invoked in formula position two); the name Tursha

cognates.Egyptian: twršꜣ Tursha, a Sea People, under Merneptah and at Medinet Habu (di Mino, Ya Diktu)

entries.note: KO Za 1, formula position two, before DU-*314-RE · I-DA-A dubur ʾIda 'the sanctuary of Ida'. √t-r-s 'to shield, protect' (Ar. turs; Lane 302); the shield-bearing Kouretes of Ida, and the Sea People Tursha, named from the same root (di Mino, Ya Diktu). One attestation.

entries.meaning: Teshub (Hurrian storm god theophoric PN)

cognates.Hurrian: Teššub/Tešub 'storm god'—supreme deity of Hurrian pantheon (Laroche 1980, 263; Hittite Tarhunt)
cognates.Ugaritic: tṯb, the Hurrian storm god in Ugaritic texts (DULAT 870)

entries.note: HT49a personnel register: name + 1 unit allocation alongside KU-PA₃-NU, TA-NA-TI, and 8 other PNs. Hapax || HURRIAN READING: Skeleton t-s-p matches Tešub (b/p₂ neutralization). Hurrian PN layer expected given archaeological Hurrian contact (faience, cylinder seals) || PARADIGM: TE-SU is the predicted rendering of Teššub; TU-SU-PU₂ (HT49a) is the only attested one.

entries.meaning: and (conjunction)

cognates.Hebrew: wə- (וְ) 'and'; û- (וּ) before b, m, p and shewa (Gesenius §104e)

entries.note: Second allomorph wa-: WA-DU-NI-MI 'and (to) the lord(s)' (HT6b, HT85b; see DU-NI-MI). Prefixed u-: U-DI-RI-KI. || Gordon's only citation, Brice I,14 (*ya-ta-no-x u ya-[*), is a ghost—in GORILA the U sits inside the formula verb JA-TA-I-*301-U-JA (AP Za 1). GORILA has standalone U after a number on ARKH 4b (RE 10 U DE-MI 10) and HT 56a (… 11 ½ U [). HT126a has U[ broken after the sign and cannot establish an independent particle; HT47a's U̥[ is likewise dotted and broken after (GORILA I 91). "And" fits but is unproven: Linear A accounts do not otherwise join entries with a conjunction. Other support: prefixed U-DI-RI-KI and the WA- allomorph (WA-DU-NI-MI).

entries.meaning: mother; or capital (Akk. ummu 'capital'); rival u- 'and' + PALM/TREE
entries.note: ZA 10b .3 U-*49 6, in a list of entries with numbers. *49 writes mi, as in DA-U-*49 Dawmi and TO-*49-RE tamir; U-MI ʾummi 'mother', or Akk. ummu 'initial investment, capital' (CAD U/W 120), an account term. Rival: u- 'and' + *49 PALM/TREE, though *49 never stands alone. HT 126a ]U-*49 1 is broken before U. One witness.

entries.meaning: My mother is chief/exalted (sentence name)
entries.cognates: Ugaritic ʾum "mother", našaʾa "to lift, raise"; Hebrew nāśīʾ (Gen 23:6 nəśîʾ ʾĕlōhīm); Amorite mother-element in Ummum-ka-abī (Gelb AS 21 nos. 6246–7, FN) and Našiʾ name element (NIQM-I·LA·NAŠIʾ, no. 5051); = *301-SI nāśī (PROBABLE)
entries.note: Sentence name: ʾummī 'my mother' (geminate mm spelled with a single sign) + naśiʾ 'chief, exalted one' (√n-ś-ʾ 'lift'; the title independently PROBABLE at *301-SI). Both attestations stand in the header, outside the count: on HT117a (MA-KA-RI-TE KI-RO U-MI-NA-SI) the roster's ten qty-1 entries sum exactly to KU-RO 10 with U-MI-NA-SI excluded—the responsible party, not a counted worker; on HT28b it stands in the header pair with A-SI-JA-KA before the commodity block. U- is radical, not the proclitic 'and': bare MI-NA-SI and DI-MI are unattested anywhere in the corpus, and the tablet's other U- words resolve as radical—U-SU (ʾUšu, mainland Tyre) and U-DI-MI (ʾUdumī, man of Udum), both Amarna-anchored origin labels—leaving no conjunctive u- on HT117a. The mother-element is attested in Amorite feminine names (Ummum-ka-abī 'the mother is like my father'); a mother-exalting name suits a goddess-primary administration. ALTERNATIVE (superseded reading): u-Minasī 'and-Minasī'—MI-NA-SI sign-for-sign = Neo-Assyrian Mi-na-si-i (Manasseh), √m-n-n with mnn→mnš dissimilation, beside MI-NA-NE (CONFIRMED); requires the conjunction, the dissimilation, and an eight-century reach to the Neo-Assyrian match—retained as the recorded rival. || The Ugaritic mnn → mnš pair is not attested in the Copenhagen Ugaritic Corpus or DULAT; the Ugaritic tribute word is mnḥ (KTU 3.8:21, 3.10:1; mnḥy 'offering' KTU 1.2 I 38). The dissimilation support is withdrawn.

entries.meaning: So, behold my gathering! (conjunction + presentative + G verbal noun kanāsī + 1cs -ī)

cognates.Hebrew: kānas (כָּנַס) 'to gather, assemble' (Esth 4:16, Ezek 22:21, Neh 12:44); knesset (כְּנֶסֶת) 'assembly, gathering'; √k-n-s 'to gather'
cognates.Akkadian: kamāsu A 'to gather, store' (CAD K 114–117); earlier form of Hebrew kns via m~n interchange (Greenfield 2001, 840–846)
cognates.Aramaic: knaš (כנש) 'to gather, assemble'; kiništu (NB/LB loan) 'priestly college' (AHw 480a; Greenfield 2001)
cognates.Arabic: kanasa (كنس) 'to sweep, collect'; kanīsah (كنيسة) 'synagogue, church' (< Aramaic knš)

entries.note: U-NA is provisionally /wannā/ 'and behold,' comparing Ugaritic w hn ~ wn and Lipiński's *wa-hanna/u > wn; the alphabetic spelling does not fix the vowels, and /winnā/ remains possible. KA-NA-SI = *kanāsī, a regular but unattested G verbal noun + 1cs -ī; Aramaic-shaped alternative *knāšī (knāš 'gathering'); Syriac knšy 'gather!' (Peshitta Jer 10:17) is a live verbal rival. The -ī suffix is 1cs possessive, consistent with 1cs A- at Position 1. Translate the proposed action noun as 'my gathering'; reserve 'assembly' for a lexicalized collective formation. IO Za 2 and IO Za 9 are restored or partial witnesses; the group is intact on KO Za 1, PK Za 8, SY Za 2 and TL Za 1.

entries.meaning: and behold, may my gathering [take place] (proposed precative lū)

cognates.Hebrew: kānas (כָּנַס) 'to gather, assemble' (Esth 4:16, Ezek 22:21, Neh 12:44); knesset (כְּנֶסֶת) 'assembly, gathering'; √k-n-s 'to gather'
cognates.Akkadian: kamāsu A 'to gather, store' (CAD K 114–117); earlier form of Hebrew kns via m~n interchange (Greenfield 2001, 840–846); lū 'may, indeed'—the precative/asseverative particle written by -RU- (akk_hg_0642)
cognates.Aramaic: knaš (כנש) 'to gather, assemble'; kiništu (NB/LB loan) 'priestly college' (AHw 480a; Greenfield 2001)
cognates.Arabic: kanasa (كنس) 'to sweep, collect'; kanīsah (كنيسة) 'synagogue, church' (< Aramaic knš)

entries.note: Normalized formula, not an independently complete spelling in the listed witness. PKZa12 preserves U-NA-RU-KA-[?]-JA-SI, with JA legible (GORILA IV 38). The lost sign is restored as NA from the formula, and NI fits the trace equally (Soldani 2012, 221–22 n. 129). NA-JA recurs in I-NA-JA-PA-QA on PK Za 11, which makes JA a Palaikastro spelling. Soldani's KA-NI-JA- beside KA-NI-JA-MI (CR Zf 1) would make SI an ending, not a radical. IO Za 16 is only a structural comparator: it ends U-NA-RU-KA[ and does not preserve -NA-SI or -NA-TI. PKZa11 independently preserves U-NA-RU-KA-NA-TI. Proposed analysis: U-NA /wannā/ 'and behold' + RU /lū/ 'may' + KA-NA-SI /kanāsī/ 'my gathering.' Akkadian lū can introduce a positive injunction in a verbless clause (Huehnergard 1997 §22.2), but Duhoux 1992, 69–70 and Thomas 2020 establish only that -RU- is a morphological variant; its value and function remain uncertain.

entries.meaning: the burning one (f.); name or epithet

cognates.Hebrew: yqd 'to burn' (HALOT 430); yōqedet 'burning' (f. ptc., Isa 65:5); môqēd 'hearth, burning' (HALOT 560)

entries.note: PL Zf 1, a silver pin from beside Platanos Tholos A: ]TA · WI-TE-JA-MU · U-QE-TI · JA-SA-SA-RA-ME (GORILA IV 161). Feminine participle of √w-q-d 'to burn': U writes w-, as in U-NA-KA-NA-SI wannā; QE the qe of Heb. yōqedet; the d before t unwritten; TI the feminine -t. Initial w- where Hebrew and Aramaic have y-. Rival: U- + QE-TI, the element of HT 7a, HT 58 and PO Zc 1. Weak point: one attestation.

entries.meaning: light of the Levite (compound PN)
entries.note: HT25a personnel roster alongside DU-RU-WI, qty 1. U = /ʾūr/ 'light/flame' (√ʾ-w-r) + RE-WI = /lēwī/. Parallel to Hebrew אוּרִיָּה ʾŪriyyāh 'flame of Yah.' Both -RE-WI and -RU-WI terminals on same tablet suggest ethnonymic element.

entries.meaning: sanctuary personnel
entries.note: Compound logogram: VIR + DUBUR. Temple workers receiving rations at Khania.

entries.meaning: VIR-class personnel qualified by *313; exact class unknown
entries.note: VIR establishes the human referent, and the quantified occurrences establish a personnel category. Three palaeographic variants (a/b/c) occur in comparable list contexts. No phonetic complement identifies *313. The former RĀQIḪŪ 'perfumers/aromatic workers' expansion relied on commodity co-occurrence and remains an archived conjecture, not a reading; CYP and other aromatics are not exclusive to these tablets, and on HT89 CYP occurs only after the personnel total in a separate section.

entries.meaning: personnel class marked by the KA complement; possibly Akkadian kāribū
entries.note: VIR securely marks personnel; KA is a written complement. Akkadian kāribu(m) 'one who blesses, intercessor, dedicant' supplies a plausible expansion, but HT88 writes neither RI nor BU, so 'intercessory priests' is not established by the spelling. Translate VIR+KA as a personnel class and retain kāribū as the leading lexical hypothesis. HT97a counts 82, HT100 counts 58, HT88 counts 20, and HT28a has VIR+KA-VIN 6. Alternative: Akkadian kallu 'temple servant.'

entries.meaning: Beloved of the Deep (title or name)

cognates.Arabic: widd 'love' (Lane 2931); names of wdd + a god: wddʾl, wddʿm (Harding 1971, 637)
cognates.Ugaritic: thm 'ocean', thmt 'Primordial Ocean' (DULAT 851); ydd il ġzr 'beloved of El, the hero' (DULAT 943)

entries.note: PL Zf 1, a silver pin from beside Platanos Tholos A: ]TA · WI-TE-JA-MU · U-QE-TI · JA-SA-SA-RA-ME (GORILA IV 161). WI = wid(d)-, as in WI-DI-NA Widdīna, dd unwritten before t; TE-JA-MU = ti(h)āmu, h unwritten, JA the glide. Construct 'beloved of the Deep', the title type of Ug. ydd il. Sign dispute: GORILA reads WI and MU, both doubtful; a second reading of the facsimile takes the fourth sign as RU, which gives no reading. Weak point: -MU where the construct wants the genitive -MI. One attestation.

entries.meaning: this (f.sg. demonstrative)

cognates.Hebrew: zō(ʾ)t 'this' (f.sg.), from an earlier interdental demonstrative base; closest lexical parallel (Huehnergard 2023, 46)
cognates.Phoenician: ʾGN n.f. 'bowl'; FK D 35 hʾgn hz 'this bowl,' with a postposed demonstrative (Krahmalkov 2000, 31)
cognates.Ugaritic/Arabic: dāti/ḏāti is an inflected genitive relative/possessive form with a phonemic final /i/; it is retained only as the rejected rival analysis

entries.note: Fills the gap Gordon (1966 §156) marked between A-KA-NU and DU-RA-RE. ZA-TI may write /zāt/ (historically perhaps /zāʾt/), with TI exposing final /t/ and a nonphonemic support vowel. Hebrew zō(ʾ)t is the closest lexical parallel. Phoenician ʾGN is feminine, and FK D 35 hʾgn hz 'this bowl' provides an independent noun + postposed demonstrative parallel. Because Semitic places the demonstrative after its noun here, the natural English rendering of A-KA-NU ZA-TI is simply 'this bowl'; 'this very bowl' would add emphasis not established by the form. This reading is preferable to /ḏāti/ 'of': Ugaritic dāti and Arabic ḏāti have a live genitive /i/ and require an agreement frame absent here. Caution: ZA-TI is a hapax, GORILA and SigLA disagree on ZA/ZE, and final TI = /t/ is a proposed Linear A spelling rather than a demonstrated Linear B rule.

entries.meaning: breast (√ṯ-d-y, PS *ṯad-); at IOZa6 first member of ZU-DI SI-KA (ṯudī-šiqā)

cognates.MSA: Mehri ṯódi, Harsusi ṯōdi, Soqotri tódi "breast, bosom"

entries.note: IOZa6: first member of the compound epithet ZU-DI SI-KA (ṯudī-šiqā, 'Breast-Who-Gives-Drink'), following I-NA-TA-I (ʿInatī, 'my Anat'). The -ī on ZU-DI is treated as a construct/bound vowel linking to SI-KA, not the possessive suffix on the preceding theonym. MSA cognates (Mehri ṯódi, Harsusi ṯōdi) are close; compare Ugaritic KTU 1.23 b-ṯd aṯrt, 'at the breast of Athirat.' ZU-DI-RA occurs on HTWc3011–3012.

entries.meaning: breast (woman's)
entries.note: Ug. ṯd, Heb. šād, Ar. ṯady-. Biconsonantal root. Fractional quantities (5/8, 1) suggest commodity subdivision.

entries.meaning: Bull- (personal name)
entries.note: KN Zb 52, a clay vessel: ZU-RI-NI-MA alone. √ṯ-w-r 'bull' with -īn and mimation -MA. Cf. I-ZU-RI-NI-TA (PH 6), with feminine -TA. Weak point: ZU = /ṯu/ is a proposed value. One attestation.

entries.meaning: conjunction u- "and" + dirik "way, path"—Hebrew derek דֶּרֶךְ, Akkadian darāku "to tread"; cross-ref DA-RE-KU (ZA18a, same √d-r-k skeleton, different vowel class)
entries.note: Mari name Dark-i-Ma (Gelb AS 21 no. 1497) attests drk as a name-former; DA-RE-KU (ZA18a) is an independent √d-r-k token at Zakros.

entries.meaning: head, top, capital (Akkadian qaqqadu(m))

cognates.Akkadian: qaqqadu 'head; top; original amount, principal' (CAD Q 100, 108–109)

entries.note: PE 2, among fractional entries: A-RI-PA ¼, QA-QA-DA ½, TO-ME ⅓. QA-QA-DA writes qaqqada, the geminate unmarked, as QA-QA-RU qaqqaru. Akk. qaqqadu 'head; original amount, principal' (CAD Q 100, 109). Rival: a personal name, as on the neighbouring entries. One attestation.

entries.meaning: all, totality, everything (administrative category: miscellaneous/general allocation; section subtotal)
entries.note: 168 standalone attestations (152 single-sign HT nodules HTWa1471–1622, plus 16 multi-word tablets across 5 sites). Second most common nodule category after *301 (226). On HT127b, KU 72 appears as one sub-category alongside *307, VIR+*313c, KI+MU, *301—all summing to KU-RO 292 (the sum includes the erased KI+MU 14, GORILA I 219). This confirms KU is a CATEGORY LABEL, not an abbreviation of KU-RO. On HT42+59, KU directly precedes OLE ("all oil"). On HT131a, KU 353 is the largest number (subtotal). On HT45b, KU ¼ appears 3×. The semantic distinction kull "all/section" vs kull-rōʿu (KU-RO) "grand total" parallels administrative subtotal vs grandtotal conventions. Alternative: kōhēn "priest"—rejected (152 nodules too many for personnel; full spelling KI-NI exists separately). Huehnergard: /kalīlu/ "entirety", /kullu/ "all" CuCC pattern; BH kālīl.

entries.meaning: palm-measure, bowl (unit of dry/liquid measure; administrative commodity category)

cognates.Akkadian: kappu 'palm of hand, bowl, pan; a small unit of measure'
cognates.Hebrew: kap (כַּף) 'palm, hollow of hand, bowl, pan, spoon'

entries.note: 149 single-sign HT nodules (HTWa1322–1470) plus ~12 multi-word tablet appearances across 4 sites (HT, KH, Milos, Gournia). Third most common nodule category after *301 (226) and KU (152). HT11b is decisive: *86 · KA 40 · KA 30 · KA 50 · RU-ZU-NA KA 30 · SA-QE-RI · KA 30 · KU-RO 180—sum is exact, KA is a COMMODITY allocated in quantities of 30–50 to named recipients. On HT140, KA alternates with OLE+U (oil) in a ratio pattern (KA 1 · OLE+U 1). On GO2r, KA ⅛—fractional quantity consistent with a unit of measure. On HT85b, KA 1 in a personnel list (one unit per person). Metrological function is consistent across all contexts. Alternatives considered: kaspu "silver" (strong but abbreviation to first syllable weakens it), Egyptian ḫꜣw "goods" (too generic).

entries.meaning: shone forth (causative of y-p-ʿ 'rise, shine forth')

cognates.Hebrew: הוֹפִיעַ hôpîaʿ "shone forth" (hiphil; Deut 33:2, Ps 50:2; HALOT 424)

entries.note: KN Zf 31 · A-WA-PI ·, undotted, between dividers (GORILA IV 155). Causative with ʾa-, inflected as I-w (aw), final ʿ unwritten. Heb. hôpîaʿ, the theophany verb (Deut 33:2; Ps 50:2; 80:2), whose ô is old aw (HALOT 424); Ug. /y-p-ʿ/ 'go up, rise' (DULAT 958). JA-WA-? on PE Zb 7 may be the prefix form if its third sign is PI. Rival: ʿawp 'bird' (Heb. ʿôp), which would need *306 for ʿa.

entries.meaning: unresolved entity or commodity category; comparative /qanūma/ 'reeds'
entries.note: Two administrative attestations, HT116a and KH88. Ugaritic alphabetic qnm is explicitly reconstructed as /qanūma/ < *qanawūma 'reeds' (Huehnergard 2008, p. 291), with Eblaite qā-nu-wu / qā-nu-um comparisons; this is the closest exact vocalic parallel. 'Reeds' does not fit the HT116a allocation-heading slot transparently. A separate comparison with √q-n-y 'acquire, possess' could yield an acquisition category, but the proposed nominal formation and mimation are not independently attested. Preserve both comparisons and leave the contextual meaning unresolved.

entries.meaning: verbal ending: indicative -u + 2fs -tī + -n(u) 'us'
entries.note: Ending of the petition verb: TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU (IO Za 2), TA-NA-I-*301-U-TI-NU (IO Za 6), ]U-TI-NU · I-NA-I-DA-[ (IO Za 11, broken before U). Davis, Thomas and Monti isolate it (Monti 2022, 111–112). U = indicative -u, TI = 2fs -tī, NU = -n(u) 'us' (di Mino, Ya Diktu). Rival: -NU the precative particle (cf. Heb. nāʾ, Ps 119:108). U-TI-NU never stands free (Thomas 2020).

entries.meaning: Pitrī/Puṭrī (personal name; perhaps 'my release')

cognates.Amorite: PTR 'solve, redeem'; Annu-puṭri, Ištar-puṭri

entries.note: Hapax on PK Za 11. Davis (2013, 42–43) and Thomas (2020, 8–10) place PI-TE-RI A-KO-A-NE in the subject/dedicant slot but infer two names without identifying either. DULAT 677 lists Ugaritic pṭry as a Semitic personal name; syllabic Ugaritic /piṭru/ 'loosening, release' supplies the qitl base, and Amorite has PTR 'solve, redeem' plus -puṭri in Annu-puṭri and Ištar-puṭri (Gelb 1980, 339; Nakata 1995, 244). Rival: Gordon (1966, §124) reads . pi-te za . 'this engraved monument', the table naming itself, after Phoenician ptḥ 'inscription, engraving' with z 'this' following, as in pthy z 'this inscription of mine' (KAI 10.3–5, 14; Krahmalkov s.v. PTḤ III); the third sign is a loop on a long stroke, between RI and ZA (GORILA dots RI), but no divider stands between TE and it, and Ugaritic ptḥ means only 'open' and 'door'. Preferred as a personal name in apposition to A-KO-A-NE 'the priest.' Common-noun /piṭrī/ 'my release/opening' and a 2fs imperative 'release!' remain morphological alternatives. Pidray (pdry; syllabic pi-id-ra-yu) is cultically attractive but requires unproved TE = /d/.

entries.meaning: the priest (proposed title after PI-TE-RI)
entries.note: Hapax on PK Za 11; damaged A-[?]-NE may recur in the corresponding slot on PK Za 12 but does not establish the restoration. Proposed as a singular title in apposition: PI-TE-RI A-KO-A-NE, 'Pitrī, the priest.' The root is secure (Ug. /kāhinu/, Heb. kōhēn; Phoenician khn), and Canaanite ha- is a Common Central Semitic article historically related to *han. Exact vocalization and the underrepresentation of /h/ remain uncertain. The former /ha-kōhānē/ 'O priests' is withdrawn: Hebrew kōhănê is construct plural, Ugaritic plural is /kāhinūma/, and no direct vocative plural in -ē is attested. Rivals are a second personal name (Davis/Thomas), Akkadian/Nuzi Aḫūni 'our brother,' and Arabic ʾaḫawāni 'two brothers'; the latter two fit the signs poorly.

entries.reading: wannā lū kanasti / winnā lū kanasti
entries.meaning: so, behold, may you gather!

cognates.Hebrew: כְּנֶסֶת kəneset 'assembly' (later Hebrew); כָּנַסְתִּי qānastī 'I gathered' (Eccl 2:8)
cognates.Akkadian: kamāsu A 'to gather, store' (CAD K 114–117); earlier form via m~n interchange (Greenfield 2001)

entries.note: Segmentation: U-NA /wannā/ or /winnā/ 'so, behold' + RU /lū/ 'may' + KA-NA-TI /kanasti/, 2fs suffix form of √k-n-s 'gather': 'so, behold, may you gather!' (di Mino, Ya Diktu). The coda /s/ is unwritten, per the Linear B rule that drops syllable-final s before a stop (Ventris & Chadwick 1956, 45; pa-ka-na /phasgana/). Hebrew has the same opening sequence: הֵן לוּ יְהִי hēn lū yəhî 'behold, may it be' (Gen 30:34). Distinct from KA-NA-SI /kanāsī/ 'my gathering.' Rivals: a K-N-S-T feminine collective */kanast/*, 'may there be a gathering,' with lū introducing a verbless injunction as in Akkadian (Huehnergard 1997 §§22.2, 29.3; compare later Hebrew kəneset 'assembly'); and /qānastī/ 'I gathered,' exactly paralleled by Biblical Hebrewכָּנַסְתִּי (Eccl 2:8), a 1cs verb.

entries.meaning: you (f.) gathered (2fs suffix form; after lū 'may you gather'); rival K-N-S-T feminine collective 'assembly'

cognates.Hebrew: כְּנֶסֶת kəneset 'assembly' (later Hebrew); כָּנַסְתִּי qānastī 'I gathered' (Eccl 2:8)
cognates.Aramaic: kənaš 'to assemble' (Dan 3:2); Syriac knuštā 'congregation, synagogue' (Peshitta, Acts 6:9)
cognates.Linear B: pa-ka-na /phasgana/ and PA-I-TO /Phaistos/ illustrate non-writing of /s/ before a stop

entries.note: Written KA-NA-TI in U-NA-RU-KA-NA-TI (PK Za 11). Linear B omits /s/ before a stop (pa-ka-na /phasgana/), and the Linear A/B place-name PA-I-TO /Phaistos/ supplies the closer Aegean control; KA-NA-TI may therefore spell */kanasti/, the 2fs suffix form of √k-n-s, with /s/ unrepresented before /t/ (Ventris and Chadwick 1956, 45, 80; Meissner 2024, 121–23); after RU /lū/ it reads 'may you gather!' (di Mino, Ya Diktu). Rival: a feminine collective */kanast/*, with final I as a support vowel; the consonantal formation K-N-S-T is comparable to later Hebrew כְּנֶסֶת kəneset and Aramaic/Syriac knuštā 'assembly,' but the exact Bronze Age noun and its vocalization are unattested. Rival: phonetic -TĪ permits /qānastī/ 'I gathered' (Eccl 2:8).

entries.meaning: Behold, he opens (his eyes)!—theophanic epiphany closure
entries.note: Proposed I-NA hinna 'behold!' + JA-PA-QA, 3ms yaqtul of √p-q-ḥ 'open (the eyes).' It closes the damaged PKZa11 prayer; JA-PA-QA is independently attested on PKZa12. Hebrew hinnēh/hēn and Ugaritic hn support the presentative, while Isa 42:7 supplies the 'open eyes' usage. IOZa6 is no longer counted as a bare-I-NA control: I-NA-TA-I-ZU-DI-SI-KA is preferred there as ʿInatī ṯudī-šiqā, though hinna remains a rival segmentation.

entries.meaning: he opens (the eyes)?

cognates.Hebrew: פָּקַח pāqaḥ "to open (eyes)" (Isa 42:7 lipqōaḥ ʿēnayim ʿiwwərōt "to open blind eyes")
cognates.Ugaritic: pqḥ not attested; pqd 'to command' is a distinct competing root

entries.note: Complete final group on PKZa12 and also attested after I-NA on PKZa11. Candidate 3ms yaqtul from √p-q-ḥ 'open (the eyes)': Proto-Semitic *paqaḥ-, Hebrew pāqaḥ, and Aramaic pqḥ. The final laryngeal would be unrepresented. JA- is masculine /ya-/, so the subject cannot simply be identified as the goddess without further explanation; the damaged context may have lost its subject. No secure Akkadian cognate or Ugaritic pqḥ attestation has been identified. √p-q-d is weaker because it requires an absent final /d/.

entries.meaning: behold! (presentative particle)

cognates.Arabic: ʾinna (إنّ) "indeed, behold" (later form, ʾ for h)

entries.note: Proposed presentative hinna 'behold!' (Hebrew hinnēh/hēn; Ugaritic hn), the bare counterpart of U-NA = u=hinna. It is proposed in PKZa11 I-NA-JA-PA-QA and may occur in APZa2. Akkadian ina 'when, in' remains an alternative in suitable contexts. IOZa6 is excluded from the positive attestation list: its complete middle group is now preferred as ʿInatī ṯudī-šiqā, with initial hinna retained only as a rival segmentation.

entries.meaning: O Dikte, she of [the Dubur] (name + determinative de)

cognates.Ugaritic: dqt 'female goat, young she-goat' (DUL 280); theonym Diqatu attested in offering lists (KTU 1.148:3)
cognates.Hebrew: Not directly attested as theonym; cf. se'îrāh (שְׂעִירָה) 'she-goat' and se'îrîm (שְׂעִירִים) 'goat-demons' (Lev 17:7, 2 Chr 11:15)
cognates.Akkadian: diqāru 'cooking pot' (unrelated); goat-deity pattern parallels Amurrite theophoric names
cognates.Arabic: No direct reflex; goat-deity pattern preserved in Yazidi Melek Tawus traditions

entries.note: Palaikastro variant of JA-DI-KI-TU (Iouktas). A-DI-KI-TE + TE: the name Diqqite + determinative de "she of", before [dubu]re (A-DI-KI-TE-TE-[DU-PU₂]-RE). The second TE stands only before dubur (PKZa8, PKZa15, PKZa11); the name alone has one dental (JA-DI-KI-TU, A-DI-KI-TE[, LB di-ka-ta-). TE = determinative de, cf. DU du; Ug. il d pid "El, the one of the heart" (KTU 1.4 IV 58–59). de CANDIDATE. PKZa12 A-DI-KI-TE[ is broken after TE. Davis 2026 parses A- as prepositional prefix "to/for the Diktaian" (in Salgarella & Petrakis eds., The Wor(l)ds of Linear A, pp. 43-60). || COGNATES: those of JA-DI-KI-TU, the same name (Diktu/Dikte).

entries.meaning: (Man) of the throne-house, crown dependant (title); rival Hurrian PN Pidi-kešḫi

cognates.Akkadian: bīt kussî, É.GIŠ.GU.ZA, '1. royal property (real estate), 2. royal service' (CAD K 593); PN and PN ša GIŠ.GU.ZA 'belonging to the crown' (Alalakh 7:26; CAD K 592)
cognates.Hurrian: kešḫi 'siège, trône', ki-iš-hi = Akk. kussû (Laroche 1980, 143–44), rival

entries.note: HT 87 PI-TA-KE-SI 1, first of six one-unit entries under MA-KA-RI-TE in a roster of men. bīt-kissi, construct + genitive, as Akk. bīt kussî 'royal property, royal service' (CAD K 593): '(man) of the throne-house', as the šūt GIŠ.GU.ZA 'those of the throne' of an Old Akkadian roster of men (CAD K 592). The house itself heads HT 21 as PI-TA-KA-SE. Rival: Hurrian Pidi-kešḫi, kešḫi 'throne' (Laroche 1980, 143–44) with pidi/u- unglossed (1980, 200).

entries.meaning: Dikise (personal name; possibly related to Hurrian tagiše/tegiše 'beautiful; beauty')

cognates.Hurrian: tagi 'beautiful'; tagiše/tegiše 'beautiful' or 'beauty', written t/da-a-ki-ši and ta-(a)-ki-(e)-še (Laroche, Glossaire hourrite, pp. 249–50)
cognates.Amarna: Tagi (EA 264–66), mayor of Gintikirmil—Hurrian name, same root

entries.note: Personal-name candidate. Laroche directly records Hurrian tagi 'beautiful' and the theme tagiše/tegiše 'beautiful' or 'beauty', written t/da-a-ki-ši and ta-(a)-ki-(e)-še (Glossaire hourrite, pp. 249–50). These forms are closer controls than an internally reconstructed tagi + -šše analysis. DI-KI-SE can approximate tagiše/tegiše through Linear A stop and sibilant neutralization, though its vowels are not exact. Tagi is independently attested as a Hurrian personal name in EA 264–66. Keep Dikise untranslated as a name.

entries.meaning: group of daughters (Hurrian collective)

cognates.Hurrian: šāl=ardi 'group of daughters' (Wilhelm, "Hurrian," 103); šalardi 'qualité de fille', ša-la-ar-di, Mari 5, 11; RS h. 5, 12 (Laroche 1980, 213); šal(a)=arde 'Tochterschaft' (Wegner 2000, 51; Richter 2012, 344)

entries.note: HT 27a .5 ]SA-RA-DI 5, broken directly before SA (GORILA I 49), a counted row in the personnel tally under TI-NI-TA · *307 (KU-RO 335). Hurrian šāl(a)=ardi, šāla 'daughter' with the collective -ardi, the thematic vowel lost before it: šāl=ardi 'group of daughters' (Wilhelm, "Hurrian," 103); ša-la-ar-di at Mari and Ugarit (Laroche 1980, 213); šal(a)=arde 'Tochterschaft' (Wegner 2000, 51). ša-la-ar-di gives SA-RA-DI sign for sign: coda r unwritten, RA for /la/. Laroche and Wegner gloss an abstract, 'qualité de fille,' 'Tochterschaft'; Wilhelm's collective fits a counted row. The break allows a longer compound, as Mari sindišalardi 'Siebentochterschaft' (Richter 2012, 388). One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; Wilhelm, Hurrian; Laroche 1980; Wegner 2000; Richter 2012

entries.meaning: Iruja (personal name; Hurrian hypocoristic of Irup-tešup)

cognates.Nuzi: Iruja (I-ru-ia, E-ru-ú-ia, I-ru-ú-ia), hypocoristic of Irup-tešup (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, s.v. IRUJA; 220)

entries.note: HT 7a .2 I-RU-JA 3, all three signs whole and undotted, the first entry under .1 QE-TI · VIR+[?], before DU-JA 4 (GORILA I 15). Nuzi Iruja, I-ru-ia, var. E-ru-ú-ia, I-ru-ú-ia: the son of Ziqaya bears both Iruja and Irup-tešup, and the element list gives iruja as the "Hypocoristic for Irup-tešup" (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, s.v. IRUJA, IRUP-TEŠUP; 220). The element ir- is Hurrian; Speiser's gloss 'aid' is uncertain (ibid., 220). I-ru-ia gives I-RU-JA sign for sign.
