A three-sign match with one witness; chance is a live alternative.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943

entries.meaning: Ipšaja (personal name; Hurrian hypocoristic)

cognates.Nuzi: Ipšaja (Ip-ša-a-a, Ip-šá-a-a), probably hypocoristic of Ipša-halu (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 220)

entries.note: KH 10 .3 I-PA-SA-JẠ · QA-*118, JA dotted on both copies, before A-KI-PI-E-TE GRA 90 (GORILA III 37). Nuzi Ipšaja, Ip-ša-a-a, Ip-šá-a-a, "Probably hypocoristic for Ipša-halu" (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 220); the element ipš- is Hurrian (ibid., 220). The coda p takes a dead A: Ip-ša-a-a gives I-PA-SA-JA. JA is dotted and there is one witness.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943

entries.meaning: sorcerer, diviner (occupational title or PN)

cognates.Akkadian: kaššāpu/qaššāpu 'sorcerer, practitioner of witchcraft' (Maqlû passim); kašāpu 'to bewitch' (CAD K 282)
cognates.Hebrew: mǝkaššēp 'sorcerer' (Exod 22:17, 7:11); mǝkaššēfīm = palace cult specialists (Exod 7:11); qōšēp (Deut 18:10)
cognates.Amarna: Not attested as Canaanite gloss; but cf. EA 35:26 kaššāpu in Akkadian matrix
cognates.Hurrian: kaššapte 'magie', a transcription of Akkadian kaššaptu (Laroche 1980, 138)

entries.note: √k-š-p / √q-š-p 'to practice sorcery.' Akk. kaššāpu/qaššāpu 'sorcerer' (qattāl agent noun), Heb. mǝkaššēp / qōšēp (Exod 22:17; Deut 18:10). Sibilant merger š→S; geminate šš simplified (no gemination in LA). QE writes /q/ (emphatic velar, its primary value)—this disambiguates from √k-s-p 'silver' (kaspu), which would spell KA-SA-PU with plain /k/. On HT87 cult personnel register: occupational title in name-slot with 1-unit allocation, among Hurrian PNs (PI-TA-KE-SI, DI-KI-SE) and NWS PNs (JA-RE-MI). Structural parallel: Exod 7:11 lists mǝkaššǝfīm alongside ḥakāmīm and ḥarṭummīm as palace cult specialists—identical genre to HT87. Rival reading kaspu 'silver' excluded: (a) QE ≠ KA, (b) commodity noun doesn't fit personnel register, (c) silver requires weight/quantity not 1-unit allocation.

entries.meaning: burnt offering
entries.note: √ʿ-l-h 'go up' → ʿōlâ 'burnt offering' (Lev 1:3), Ugaritic ʿlt /ʿōlatu/. ZA 7a (tablet): U-JU 5 · A-RA-TU 4 · A-RE-TU-MI[, a counted list. Weak point: U-JU lacks the feminine -t. DU-JU[ (ZA 22, tablet, beside OVISf) may share the root.

entries.meaning: fine flour, semolina
entries.note: Skeleton s-l-t exact match to √s-l-t *sult- (Heb. sōlet, Phoen. slt). KN22a lames tablet: SU-JU-TA 20 KA-JE. Qty 20 consistent with bulk commodity allocation. Biblical sōlet is the primary offering flour (Lev 2:1, Ex 29:2).

entries.meaning: possible entity or place name heading the NI (fig) entry on HT103
entries.note: Hapax opening HT103 before the divider and NI 40. Its position favors an entity, institution, recipient, or place name associated with the fig entry. Uta is attested as a much later Akkadian personal name; Uda is a Middle Babylonian geographical name attested at Ugarit. Either is compatible with Aegean stop neutralization, but neither identifies the Linear A form or supplies its etymology. NI 40 is an item, not a marked total.
entries.source: di Mino; GORILA I 170–171; ORACC Uda comparison

entries.meaning: additional, surplus, or excess (administrative heading)
entries.note: Hapax heading before the TE transaction sign on HT116a. Akkadian watrum (stem watar-) means 'additional, in excess,' and substantivized watartum/watarti means 'excess, surplus, extra' (Huehnergard 1997, §10.1). This provides a closer consonantal and administrative comparison than the former *ʿattāru 'supplicant.' U may represent /wV/ and final RO may contain a dead vowel, but the precise form and syntax remain uncertain. Hebrew √ʿ-t-r 'entreat' is genuine (Gen 25:21; Judg 13:8), yet the proposed agent noun and donor interpretation are unattested and survive only as a weak rival.

entries.meaning: unidentified administrative entity or category; speculative comparison with Šapšu
entries.note: HT 116a: SI+SE GRA 16, OLE+KI 1, OLE+MI 6, OLIV 3, a recipient among KU-PA-JA, PU-RA₂, PI-*34-TE, SI-KI-NE. HT 42+59: TA · SI+SE · TE · OLE+KI 8, OLE+U 7, beside SA-RO. Ug. Šapšu (špš, DULAT 824), taking the ligature's outer consonants š…š. Weak points: no other ligature abbreviates this way, and the medial p is unwritten. Rival: a syllabic še, as in SI+SE-RA+KA (HT Wa 1021), a name or office. SI+SE-NI (HT 99b) is a separate word. Two attestations.

entries.meaning: levy, gift—fiscal category on a commodity nodule

cognates.Akkadian: širku B 'gift; (a tax)', at Ugarit with the tithe and toll of a town (RS 16.276:10; CAD Š/3 111); širiktu, also šeriktu, 'grant, gift' (CAD Š/3 103); šarāku A 'to dedicate, to give' (CAD Š/2 40)

entries.note: HT Wa 1021, a nodule: *188-DU · ¾ · SI+SE-RA+KA, a commodity, a fraction and a word. With SI+SE as še, SI+SE-RA+KA writes šeraka: Akk. širku 'gift; a tax', levied at Ugarit with a town's tithe and toll (CAD Š/3 111), and širiktu, also šeriktu, 'grant, gift' (CAD Š/3 103), of šarāku 'to dedicate, to give'. Weak points: SI+SE for še; RA+KA a ligature, read in sign order. Rival: a personal name, the official of the sealing. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Her Ka endures' (Egyptian)

cognates.Egyptian: Ḏd-kꜣ-Rꜥ, Djedkare (ORAEC oraec2777, oraec3547); ḏd 'enduring', kꜣ 'ka'

entries.note: ZA Zb 3: DI-DI-KA-SE before A-SA-MU-NE, Eshmun, under VIN 32. Egyptian ḏd-kꜣ + -s 'her', the pattern of Djedkare; DI-DI writes ḏd, as on DI-DI-ZA-KE (HT 1) and DI-DI-KO-RA-ME-TA₂ (ZA 11a). Weak point: no private Egyptian name ḏd-kꜣ.s is attested. Rival: Semitic dādī-kussē 'my beloved is the throne', which needs DI-DI for dādī. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Strong One (El epithet)

cognates.Hebrew: אָמֵץ ʾāmēṣ 'be strong' (Deut 31:7, Josh 1:6); אַמִּיץ ʾammîṣ 'mighty', said of God (Job 9:4; Isa 40:26)

entries.note: CR(?)Zf1 (unprovenanced metal object), word 1 of 5: A-MA-WA-SI · KA-NI-JA-MI · I-JA · QA-KI-SE-NU-TI · A-TA-DE. Paired with KA-NI-JA-MI 'Creator of the Sea' as an El epithet. Weak point: ʾammîṣ predicts A-MI-SI; the -WA- is unexplained. Rival: a personal name.

entries.meaning: Creator of the Sea (El epithet)

cognates.Ugaritic: qnyt ʾilm 'Creatress of the Gods' (KTU 1.4 III 26)—standard epithet of Athirat/Asherah
cognates.Hebrew: קֹנֵה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ qōnēh šāmayim wāʾāreṣ (Gen 14:19)—epithet of El ʿElyon; also קֹנֵה qōnēh alone as divine title
cognates.Phoenician: ʾl qn ʾrṣ 'El Creator of the Earth' (KAI 26 III 18, Karatepe bilingual)
cognates.Amarna: EA 266:16—Canaanite vassal invokes qny in theophoric context
cognates.Amorite: qanij(ān)um 'to create' (QNJ; Gelb 1980, glossary p. 29)

entries.note: CR(?)Zf1 (unprovenanced metal object), word 2 of 5. Masculine construct participle qāniy (Amorite qanijum) + genitive yammi 'of the Sea'; KA writes /q/. √q-n-y is a Bronze Age divine epithet: Ugaritic qnyt ʾilm of Athirat (KTU 1.4 III 26), Hittite Elkunirša (= ʾil qōnē ʾarṣ, husband of Asherdu), Karatepe ʾl qn ʾrṣ (KAI 26 A III 18), Gen 14:19. El's Ugaritic creation epithet is bny bnwt (KTU 1.4 II 11). Rival: -MI as mimation.

entries.meaning: I make ready (1cs prefix form; proposed)

cognates.Hebrew: ʿātîd "ready, prepared"; Piel ʿattᵊdāh "make it ready" (Prov 24:27)

entries.note: Divider-bounded hapax on the gold pin CRZf1. 1cs prefix form ʾa-ʿtid- of √ʿ-t-d 'to be ready, prepare', ʿ dropped: a-ta-de sign for sign. A suffix-form 1cs would need -t- (Heb. ʿātadtî). Final DE is confirmed in GORILA V's AB45 variant table. The sequence AU-TA-DE occurs within undivided KO(?)Zf2 and is a formal comparison, not a second attestation of A-TA-DE or proof of its meaning.

entries.meaning: mantle (ʾaddart-); or the Mighty One (divine epithet)
entries.note: (A) ʾaddart- 'mantle': Heb. ʾadderet (Gen 25:25; Josh 7:21, beside silver and gold; 1 Kgs 19:13 bə-ʾaddartô; Zech 13:4); Ug. adrt 'of good quality' (DULAT 22). A garment word on a silver dress pin; A-DA-RA's a-a vowels fit ʾaddar(t), final -t unwritten. (B) ʾaddīr 'mighty' (Ps 8:2, 93:4; Ug. adr), which needs ī where the spelling has a. Spelling: ʾ dropped, single DA.

entries.meaning: Addar, 'Mighty' (personal name)

cognates.Hebrew: ʾAddār (אַדָּר), son of Bela (1 Chr 8:3; HALOT 17); place names ʾAddārâ (Josh 15:3), Ḥăṣar-ʾAddār (Num 34:4)

entries.note: Recipient slot on ARKH 5, parallel to A-DU-NI-TA-NA: A-DA-RO GRA 40[+, the entry wrapping past the broken edge to *131B 6 at the start of .3 (GORILA III 16–17). Final -O is a dead vowel; GORILA dots RO, and the .3 logogram is written over an erasure. Cf. A-DA-RA (KN Zf 31). Rival: Akk. adru 'threshing floor' (CAD A/1 129), against which one entry carries both grain and must (cf. Num 18:27). One attestation.

entries.meaning: my Creator (divine epithet)
entries.note: ZAZb34 (Zakros clay vessel) PU₂-RE-JA · KO-MU · RU-DI. Hebrew בָּרָא bārāʾ "to create" (Gen 1:1); Arabic baraʾa. PU₂=/bu/ as in DU-PU₂-RE=dubur. Final ʾ drops (guttural rule). -JA = -yā 1cs suffix "my." PK Za 16 ]TO-SA · PỤ₂-RE-JẠ[, no divider between PU₂ and RE, broken after JA (GORILA IV 42), is a damaged second witness, so the tier stays SPECULATIVE; the base PU₂-RE stands alone on PKZa28. Rival: PU₂-RE + -JA on that Palaikastro base; √p-r-y "fruit" (*puriyya).

entries.meaning: cella, inner sanctuary

cognates.Akkadian: kummu "cella, inner room of a temple"

entries.note: Akkadian kummu 'cella, inner room of a temple'; cf. DU-PU₂-RE dubur 'sanctuary'. ZA Zb 34 PU₂-RE-JA · KO-MU · RU-DI (clay vessel). Weak point: KO for /ku/. Rival: √q-w-m 'arise', qūmū (imperative plural).

entries.meaning: Rule! / may you rule (jussive/imperative)
entries.note: Hebrew רָדָה rādâ "to rule, have dominion" (Gen 1:26, Ps 72:8, 1 Kgs 5:4). Prayer-command on the Zakros clay vessel ZAZb34, after PU₂-RE-JA · KO-MU. Also HT141 (Haghia Triada tablet) after A-RI (harrī 'mountain of'). Weak point: the imperative of √r-d-y is rdī; RU writes the u.

entries.meaning: She-of-the-Lion (feminine gentilic—priestess/cult title; cf. I-ZU-RI-NI-TA She-of-the-Bull)

cognates.Hebrew: ari lion (Gen 49:9 gur aryeh Yehudah; Num 23:24; Judg 14:8)

entries.note: Feminine gentilic from pan-NWS ari lion: ari + -nit = arInit She-of-the-Lion. Morphological paradigm with I-ZU-RI-NI-TA = i-thawrInit She-of-the-Bull (same -NI-TA suffix on animal root). Bull and lion are the two central sacred animals in Minoan iconography. Attested at HT25a and ZA8 (two independent sites). || 'Priestess/cult title' rests on -t alone; -īt also forms feminine relational adjectives, abstracts and collectives (Fischer 2002, §§64, 116).

entries.meaning: farmer, tenant farmer (occupational title)
entries.note: HT 25a personnel list, I-KI-RA 1. Akkadian ikkaru 'farmer, plowman' (ORACC); Hebrew ʾikkār (Isa 61:5; Jer 14:4). Cf. I-KA ʾikkār (HT 91, HT 102), with final r unwritten; here r is written with a following vowel. Rival: a personal name.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'he knew him'

cognates.Amorite: JADAʿ names, IA-DA-AḪ-…, IA-DA-DINGIR (Gelb 1980, nos. 3168–3178)

entries.note: KH 74: ]-SỊ · JA-DA-SU, then ]SỊ-*805-MI, both broken before. Yadaʿ + -šu 'he knew him', √y-d-ʿ, ʿ unwritten; cf. Amorite JADAʿ names (Gelb 1980, nos. 3168–3178), Ug. ydʿ (DULAT 942), Heb. Yədaʿyāh. -šu is the old 3ms suffix that Akkadian keeps and NWS turns to -hu (Huehnergard 2019: 51–52). Weak point: no West Semitic name ends in -šu. Rival: a JADAʿ name with an unknown second element. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name (f.), 'she who judges'

cognates.Ugaritic: dnty, wife of Danel (KTU 1.17 V 16; DULAT 274); dn 'judgment' (DULAT 273)

entries.note: ARKH 6: DA-NA-TU · KU heads the tablet, TE-RI on the next line. Feminine participle dānat- + -u, √d-y-n 'to judge'; cf. Ug. dnty, Danel's wife (KTU 1.17 V 16), Heb. Dînāh, and DI-NA-U. Weak point: -t may make an abstract 'judgment' as well as a feminine. Rival: dannatu 'hardship; fortress' (CAD D 87), a heading. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, recipient of 8 (q-ṭ-l)
entries.note: ZA 14: ME-KI-DI 1, *21F-*118 1, PU-NI-KA-*363 3, QA-TI-JU 8, KU-PI 1, TU-MI-TI-ZA-SE 45: a name slot among recipients. Word-internal JU = /lu/: qa-ti-lu, a qātil form of q-ṭ-l (Heb. qāṭal, Aram. qṭl 'kill'); ṭ in the T-series. QA-TI-DA-TE (HT 12) and QA-TI-KI (KH 7a) share two signs only. Rival: qāḍīyu 'judge' (Arab. qāḍī), which reads JU as /yu/. || Case unassigned: nothing here selects it (Fischer 2002, §140).

entries.meaning: Tanāt—the Serpent-Goddess (= Punic Tanit/TNT). Feminine of *tannīn* with -t suffix; or related to A-TA-NA-TE (ʾAtanat, √y-t-n), which follows it on ZA10a.

cognates.Punic: TNT (Tanit/Tinnit); Greek transliteration Θινιθ/Θεννειθ at El-Hofra
cognates.Greek: θύννος "tunny" (BDB: Phoenician loanword from same root)

entries.note: Cf. LB ta-na-to (KN De 1618). Related to A-TA-NA-TE (ʾAtanat, √y-t-n), or else √t-n-n (Tinit) (di Mino, Ya Diktu, there ṯ-n-n); Ugaritic tnn and Punic tnt write t, and Linear A writes ṯ with ZU. The a-vocalization (*Tanāt*) reflects the archaic form; TI-NI-TA (*Tinnīt*) reflects the Punic vowel-raising shift (*a > i* in geminate -nn- environment), attested in El-Hofra Greek-Punic bilinguals (Θεννειθ alongside Θινιθ). Three TNT-family forms span HT and ZA.
related_forms: Θηναί (Thenai, Cretan toponym near Amnisos)—Greek rendering with ṯ→θ
Θινιθ/Θεννειθ (El-Hofra Greek-Punic bilinguals)—Greek rendering of TNT

entries.meaning: ʾAtanat, 'She-who-gives'—feminine reflex of √y-t-n 'to give'
entries.note: Feminine reflex of √y-t-n 'to give', final E a dead vowel after /t/; the etymon of Greek Ἀθήνα; cf. LB a-ta-na-po-ti-ni-ja (KN V 52) (di Mino, Ya Diktu). ZA9 A-TA-NA-[·] (GORILA III 166–67: "A-TA-NA-TE possible") is probably the same word. On ZA10a it follows TA-NA-TE, related to it or else √t-n-n (Tinit).

entries.meaning: Beloved of Minos (theophoric PN)

cognates.Ugaritic: dd 'love, loved one' (DULAT 262); ydd 'loved' (DULAT 943); lydd il 'to the beloved of El' (KTU 1.4 VII 46)
cognates.Hebrew: dōd 'beloved' (HALOT 215); Yədîdyāh 'beloved of Yah' (2 Sam 12:25; HALOT 390)
cognates.Hurrian: tad- 'to love', tadi-/tadu- in names (Laroche GLH 248); Tadu-Ḫepa (TLHdig KBo 27.93+)

entries.note: KN Zf 31, a silver dress pin from a Mavro Spelio tomb: DA-DỤ-MI-NE between ]SỊ-ZẠ-NE-*310 and QA-MI-*47-NA-RA, DU dotted (GORILA IV 155). DA-DU 'beloved' + MI-NE, Minos (√m-n-y 'to allot'). 'Beloved of DN' is a name type: Heb. Yədîdyāh (2 Sam 12:25), Ug. ydd il (KTU 1.4 VII 46). Hurrian builds the type on tad- 'to love'; DA writes /da/ and /ta/. Weak point: MI-NE as Minos stands on this word alone (TRYZb1 ]MI-NE[ ≈ ]NE-MI[ is broken both sides). Rival: a Hurrian tadu- name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: the Lady (divine title; personal-name element)

cognates.Sabaic: mrʾt 'woman, girl; lady, divine or human' (Biella 1982, 283)

entries.note: Second element of HT 90 SI-RU-MA-RI-TA₂, written as one word (GORILA I 143): Ṣill-marʾita 'Shade of the Lady', the Amorite pattern of Ṣill-Haddu. PS *marʾ-at- 'woman, lady', feminine of *marʾ- 'lord': Sabaic mrʾt 'woman, girl; lady, divine or human' (Biella 1982, 283), Akkadian mārtu (marʾatu, merʾatu) (CAD M/1 300), Aramaic mārtā 'lady' (the name Martha), Arabic marʾat-. The glottal stop is unwritten, and TA₂ gives final -ta as in KI-RE-TA₂.

entries.meaning: bull, cattle (logographic abbreviation of ṯawr; administrative commodity category for bovine livestock/products)

cognates.Ugaritic: ṯr 'bull' (KTU 1.10 iii:35, 1.12 i:30); epithet of El: ṯr ʾil 'Bull El'

entries.note: Two complete witnesses: HT 49a .8 TU 4 (GORILA I 93) and KH 91 .3 TU ¹⁄₁₆ (V 45). The fraction on KH 91 marks a measured commodity, not a person. Every other TU is broken or dotted: HT 55a ]TU 1[ (I 107), HT 79+83 ]TU-[·] 3 (I 127), HT 98a ]TU 1 (I 161), HT 126b ]TU 6 (I 217), KH 2 TU-[ (III 23), KH 51 TU[ (III 75), KH 57 ]TU[ (III 79), ZA 12b ]TỤ[ (III 177), PH(?) 31b TU-[ (I 319). Spelling: ṯ→TU under the interdental mapping (as ZU = /ṯu/), √ṯ-w-r → ṯawr → TU, first-syllable abbreviation. || Huehnergard: Ug ṯwr /ṯōru/ < *ṯawru "bull"; II-w qatl nominal. Pl. /ṯōrūma/ or /ṯarūma/(?). Also √ṯwr "mountain": /ġūru/ < *ṯuwru (qutl pattern). BH cognate: šōr "bull, ox" (< *ṯawr- with interdental > sibilant shift) (Huehnergard 2012, p. 42)

entries.meaning: figs—commodity ideogram (FIC)

cognates.Linear B: NI ideogram = figs, anchored by the phonetic descriptor su-za on KN F 841 (V&C 1956: σῦκον 'fig'); the Fs ration series HORD+NI+OLE(+VIN) directly continues the LA GRA+NI+OLE+VIN lists (KN Fs 2/4/8/17, PY Fn 187, PY Fg 253)

entries.note: Commodity identity CONFIRMED on the footing of GRA/OLE/VIN—four independent lines: (A) LB ideogram continuity with the su-za/σῦκον anchor on KN F 841—LA→LB commodity-logogram continuity (OLE, VIN, GRA, VIR, OLIV) is foundational, and NI shifting meaning between the scripts would be a singular exception; (B) acrophony—/ni/ abbreviates *nikuleon exactly, while the honey candidates fail outright (*nūb(at)- predicts NU, *nōpet predicts NO); (C) metrology—NI carries the full small-fraction food-measure series, 20 NI+fraction co-occurrences glyph-verified (½ ⅓ ¼ ⅕ ⅙ ⅒ 1/16 1/24; HT30 NI 7+⅙, HT94a NI 3+1/16, KH8 NI ½ (erased)), matching the LB Fs practice of fraction-measured figs; (D) botanical pictograph (fig leaf/plant, CH 024 ancestor, AB30). 66 corpus records carry the NI token (HT×35, KH×22, KN×3, PH×2, ZA×2, CR×1, Tel Haror×1); 75 standalone occurrences, 66% numeric, neighbors VIN×12, CYP×8, GRA×4 || Not nūb(at) 'honey' (√n-w-b bee→honey metonymy): the HT114a quartet is non-discriminating (the LB comparandum has NI = figs); the HT51a NI ≠ TI-NI argument is circular (TI-NI is itself an unconfirmed sibling hapax); 'figs counted whole' is factually wrong for the Aegean (LB figs take fractional T/V/Z units throughout Fs); 'no honey logogram otherwise' is refuted by DI = dibšu and by LB, which spells honey syllabically (me-ri, KN Gg 702); the companion fig signs (TI, TI-NI, TE-*301) cannot corroborate it. No nūb 'bee/honey' attestation in Krahmalkov or Biella—the metonymy lacks NWS epigraphic support. || Re-open only on a publication-grade re-analysis of the LB NI/Fs series, or an LA text spelling the NI-commodity syllabically as a honey word.
entries.source: di Mino; Neumann 1957, 157–58; Montecchi 2024, 178; Salgarella 2025; V&C 1956 s.v. su-za

entries.meaning: please, pray—precative/entreaty particle used in prayer constructions before jussives and after divine addresses

cognates.Hebrew: נָא nā—precative/entreaty particle, ~400× in Hebrew Bible. Used with imperatives (Gen 18:3 nā ʾal taʿăbōr 'please do not pass by'), jussives (Num 12:13 ʾēl nā rəpā nā lāh 'O God, please heal her'), and cohortatives (Gen 18:21 ʾērdā-nnā 'let me go down')
cognates.Ugaritic: Possible cognate in Ugaritic emphatic particle n/nn, function debated (de Moor, Pardee)
cognates.Arabic: Possible reflex in Arabic ʾinnā 'indeed, verily' (weakened assertive < precative)

entries.note: Standalone NA occurs in ritual, commodity-adjacent, and administrative settings, so its functions must be distinguished contextually. KN Za 10 is not a standalone witness: GORILA IV, 8–9 reads JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA as one word across the side break, with the divider after NA. IO Za 11 has NA only at the head of ]NA-[·]-DA-DA[ (Karetsou, Godart & Olivier, Kadmos 24, 1985, 142). The secure ritual controls are PHWc40 (TI-TI-MA · NA) and KH97a (RE-A-JA · NA).

entries.meaning: pig (livestock commodity)
entries.note: Logographic abbreviation. AB58 pictographic ancestor = pig/boar (CH 035, Ferrara 2022). 7 standalone occurrences across 3 sites (KH 4×, HT 2×, ZA 1×), 85% followed by numerals. Fractional quantity on HT115a (2 ¹⁄₅) = measured commodity (processed meat/weight), not head count || ETYMOLOGY: Akkadian šaḫû (Sumerian loanword). Guttural ḫ drops → šaū contracts to šū → SU. Linear B separated pig ideogram (*85 SUS₂) from syllabogram B 58, implying AB58 served both functions in Linear A || DISTRIBUTION: Co-occurs with VIN, NI, SI, CYP on KH11

entries.meaning: honey, fruit syrup—commodity abbreviation of *dibšu; rival dblt 'fig cake'. In personnel lists a separate single-sign abbreviation

cognates.Proto-Semitic: PS *dVbš- 'honey' (SED #2737)—core vocabulary attested across all Semitic branches
cognates.Akkadian: dišpu 'honey' (CAD D 161–63); delivered with oil, EA 55:12
cognates.Hebrew: דְּבַשׁ dǝbaš 'honey'; Deut 32:13–14 beside חֶמְאַת בָּקָר (cf. DI and E on HT12)
cognates.Ugaritic (rival): dblt 'dried fig, fig cake' (DULAT 261), in commodity lists by the quarter (KTU 4.751:10; 4.60:5) beside nbt 'honey' (DULAT 610; 4.14, 4.751); Hebrew dǝbēlâ

entries.note: Two uses, all at Haghia Triada (GORILA I 7, 37, 61, 121, 123, 133, 159, 181, 209). Commodity: HT 20 .3 QE-KU-RE · DI ½ (logographic, a divisible product: Montecchi 2008, 318); HT 32 SU-RE 108, DI 65 and OLE+NE RE 104, DI 53 (each after a larger figure, so possibly a sub-entry); OLE+DI 12× on HT 12, 14, 28a, 28b, 50b, 90, 116a, 129, also OLE+QE+DI (HT 121), DI+QE (HT 101); HT 111a DI 14[ before NI. Personnel or recipient, whole numbers in name lists, a single-sign abbreviation like PA, KA, JU, KI (Montecchi 2008, 318): HT 97a .4 DI 4 under VIR+KA; HT 122b .4 DI 2 within KU-RO 65; HT 66 DI 2 after VIR; HT 85b DI 1; HT 3 DI 2; HT 69 DI 8. dibšu applies to the commodity only; rival Ug. dblt 'fig cake'. MA-DI beside DI on 4 tablets. Broken: HT 122a ]-DI, HT 128a DỊ[, HT 62+73 DI[, HT 3 .5 DỊ[, HT 69 .3 ]DI 12[. One consonant, /d/; all witnesses at HT.
entries.source: GORILA I; CAD D 161–63; DULAT 261, 610; Montecchi 2008, 318

entries.meaning: the craftsman, artisan (title)
entries.note: Hapax on HT118, where it receives 4 pigs with 1 owed, among MA-DI, QA-QA-RU (Qaqqaru) and RI-RU-MA. The qātil participle 'craftsman': Ugaritic ḥrš 'craftsman, manual worker; artisan, builder' (DULAT 366); Amorite ḥariš-, *ḥāriṯ- 'artificer, worker', from *ḥrṯ 'engrave, cut', in the Mari name Ḫa-ri-ša-an (Huffmon, APNM 205). A title in a recipient list, as QA-*310-I qaynī 'the smith' takes KI-oil on HT8a. Rivals: a personal name /ʾarīšu/ on √ʾ-r-š 'to request': Amorite Ariš-ān and Ariš-ān-u (Gelb, AS 21, nos. 2190–91), glossary ʾariśum, and ʾARUŠ-U (A-RU-SU, no. 511); A-RE-SA-NA (THE Zb 2) is read on that root. Akkadian eršu (Neo-Assyrian aršu) 'plowed and sown', substantivally 'plowed field' (CAD E, s.v. eršu B), a sense the recipient slot does not fit.

entries.meaning: twin—birth-circumstance personal name from √t-ʾ-m
entries.note: Pan-Semitic √t-ʾ-m 'twin': Akkadian tuʾāmu, Hebrew tōʾam (תֹּאֲם, Gen 25:24, 38:27), Aramaic tōmā (→ Greek Θωμᾶς 'Thomas'), Arabic tawʾam. CV mapping: tuʾma → TU-MA (medial ʾ drops by guttural transparency). On HT94b (LMIB, 1500–1450 BCE), first entry in a 5-person personnel list (qty 1 each, KU-RO 5). Birth-circumstance name 'Twin' is one of the most widespread NWS naming patterns. Cf. TU-ME = tamm- (√t-m-m)—different root despite surface similarity.

entries.meaning: young bull, young animal

cognates.Akkadian: mūru 'young animal; young bull; foal' (eBL mūru I; CAD M2 229–30)

entries.note: Syllabic spelling of the *23M logogram word: MU-RU = mūru, both syllables exact. Counted 1 on HT3 and HT46a, as *23M counts whole animals. HT30 carries the logogram *23M, not MU-RU.

alternative_readings.note: 'lord, master' (Ug. mrʾ, Aram. mārē; Amorite MRʾ, Gelb AS 21 §0.7); needs MU for ma. NWS *marʾ- 'lord, master' (Ugaritic mrʾ, Aramaic mārē). MU=/mu/ for /m/, RU=/ru/ for /rʾ/ (guttural ʾ drops). On HT3 with qty 1 on personnel roster. Alternative: opaque PN. || Third attestation HT46a; Amorite MRʾ (Gelb AS 21 §0.7). Ug mrʾ spans 'lord' (DUL mru 'commander') and 'to fatten'—the former carries here.

entries.meaning: beer, strong drink—logographic abbreviation of *śakaru/*šikaru; commodity logogram, compounded with VIN
entries.note: HT56a: paired with *188 (buṭnu). Compound forms: VIN+SA (HT131b), SA-VIN (HT114b, ZA15a), a compounded beverage 'wine-beer' (cf. the yayin/šēkār doublet, Num 6:3, Isa 5:11). PS *θVkVr- → Akk. šikaru "barley beer", Heb. śēkār "strong drink", Arab. sakar. Rival 'flax': no Semitic flax word is /sa/-initial, and Linear B writes linen syllabically. On HT 27b SA n is paired with RE m (SA 4, RE 70 on one line), a transaction notation, not beer; no reading there.

entries.meaning: herb, aromatic plant (commodity term in allocation lists)

cognates.Akkadian: šammu(m) "herb, plant, drug, aromatic"—ubiquitous in administrative/pharmaceutical texts

entries.note: Commodity reading for SA-MA on allocation tablets. HT10a: follows KU-NI-SU (emmer wheat) with qty 4 in grain register. Akkadian šammu(m) is the primary cognate (sibilant merger š→s, geminate -mm- not written). Also classified as toponym in onomasticon (qty 35 on HT6b supports settlement-level distribution)—dual identity likely, with settlement named for local product. No Proto-Semitic *š-m-m is reconstructed, and the toponym/commodity ambiguity persists.

entries.meaning: measure unit (dry/liquid capacity ≈ 1.2 liters)—metrological logographic abbreviation

cognates.Akkadian: qû B 'measuring vessel; a measure of capacity', gen. qê (CAD Q 288)
cognates.Hebrew: קַב qab 'qab-measure' (HALOT 1059; 2 Kgs 6:25 רֹבַע הַקַּב 'a quarter of a qab')

entries.note: HT Wc 3014, a roundel: side a KU-MI-NA, side b QE · CAP (GORILA II 76), QE before the caprid logogram. QE writes qê, the genitive of Akk. qû in measure phrases; Heb. qab (2 Kgs 6:25). THE Zg 16 (Akrotiri faience triton, Doumas, PAE 2019, fig. 9) opens QE · at the broken left edge. Every tablet QE is broken or dotted (HT 27a, 37, 55b, 111b, 146; KH 50). Weak points: QE, not QA, for the qa- of qab and qâ; a measure before CAP, not before the cumin of side a. Rival: QE an adjunct or abbreviation qualifying CAP. One complete attestation.

entries.meaning: light, fire (divine epithet or votive label on clay vessels)
entries.note: Sole word on both clay vessel inscriptions (Kamilari + unknown site). PS *nūr-, an exact match. Votive vessel context favors divine epithet reading—nūru "Light" as address to deity (cf. Shamash epithets). PN alternative (Nūr as theophoric element) cannot be excluded. Two attestations and no sentence context. || Huehnergard: Ug nwr /nāra/ ~ /yanūr-/ "G: to be/become bright, shine"; I-n / hollow-looking w root. G suffix nāra, prefix yanūr-. BH cognate: nēr "lamp" (Huehnergard 2012, p. 50 (line ref.); cf. BH [9])

entries.meaning: garment, textile
entries.note: PS *sū-t- "garment". ZA20 allocation list: SI-TU qty 6 alongside SI-TE-TU (feminine /sūt-tu/) qty 1. HTWa1019 nodule sealed with PA-TA-NE (PN). Consonantal skeleton s-t maps cleanly. || Huehnergard: Ug šyt /šītu/ (infinitive); /šāta/ (perfect); /yašītu/ (imperfect) "to place, put"; II-y G verb. G infinitive qitl: šītu. Perfect šāta, imperfect yašītu/yašīt, imperative šīt. BH cognate: šāt ~ yāsīt "to place" (Huehnergard 2012, pp. 42, paradigm section)

entries.meaning: cedar (wood, resin or oil; commodity); rival Luwian aruza, a measure

cognates.Hieroglyphic Luwian: aruza, a measure equated with Urartian liš, rival

entries.note: Always counted: KH 86 ]RE-ZA CYP, before the aromatic cyperus, broken before; HT 88 RE-ZA 6 before NI KI-KI-NA 7; HT 13 RE-ZA 5½, first entry of the VIN · TE list. ʾarz 'cedar', the aromatic wood, resin and oil, beside cyperus at Khania as cedar beside juniper in Hebrew (1 Kgs 5:22); RE writes ra, ZA the z. Weak point: initial ʾa- unwritten. Rival: Hieroglyphic Luwian aruza, a measure, attested later.

entries.meaning: quantified commodity; perhaps butter, ghee, or cream
entries.note: E behaves logographically: eight of ten occurrences precede numerals across Haghia Triada, Knossos, and Zakros, including E 5 and E 3 on HT91. Cross-Semitic *ḥemʾat- (Hebrew ḥemʾā, Ugaritic ḥmʾt, Akkadian ḫimētu) makes dairy fat a semantic possibility if initial laryngeal loss licenses the abbreviation, but no phonetic complement or commodity equation proves it. The corpus establishes a commodity/category, not 'ghee'.

entries.meaning: figs (logographic abbreviation of TI-NI)
entries.note: Dual-function sign: syllabogram /ti/ (AB04) + logogram TIʔIN when standalone with quantities. Abbreviation of lexicon entry TI-NI. 12 standalone across 6 sites. 58% followed by numerals. Quantities: ¼–100. Pan-Semitic *tiʔin- in Deut 8:8 Seven Species. || Against it: a standalone fig logogram collides with NI = figs (CONFIRMED); complementary distribution would let both notations stand, co-occurrence in the same lists would rule one out. HT119 TI 7 stands inside a personnel total (KU-RO 160 with VIR 68) and is not figs there.

entries.meaning: myrrh or aromatic resin (compound logogram)

cognates.Akkadian: murru "myrrh, bitter resin" (CAD M/2 222; OB medical/ritual texts, c. 2000–1600 BCE)
cognates.Egyptian: mꜣrw "myrrh" (attested from 2400 BCE, imported from Punt)

entries.note: Compound logogram (3-sign ligature). 8 tablets across 2 sites (HT×5, KH×3). Always in oil/aromatic commodity sequences alongside *308 (šamnu), OLE+NE, OLE+RI, OLE+TA, CYP, VIN. Fractional quantities (⅙, ⅓, ½) typical of aromatics. ME-MI-JA-RU on ZAZg35 may be prefixed form || ETYMOLOGY: Pan-Semitic *mrr 'bitter' → murru 'myrrh' attested in all major branches. 3-sign compound for 2-consonant root suggests ideographic rather than phonetic compound. Cf. Uluburun shipwreck (c. 1300 BCE): aromatic resins traded between Levant and Aegean || Exod 30:23 mōr-dərōr heads the anointing oil recipe in the same position MI+JA+RU occupies in LA aromatic lists

entries.meaning: dagān 'grain, cereal'
entries.note: Non-phonetic commodity ideogram denoting grain/cereal. 60 standalone, 52 in compounds, 5 sites || ETYMOLOGY: Pan-Semitic *dagān (Heb. דָּגָן, Ug. dgn, Phoen. dgn). GRA+DA compound (HT133) shows DA as phonetic complement for /da-/ of dagān. DA-KA on 5 HTWa nodules may be phonetic /daga(n)/ equivalent || 4 co-occurrences with A-DU (Storm God) confirm agricultural-cultic context. 47 tablets, 5 sites. Universal Linear B commodity logogram

entries.meaning: wayn 'wine'
entries.note: Non-phonetic commodity ideogram denoting wine. 52 standalone, 10 sites—widest commodity distribution in the corpus. On HT89 it follows KU-RO in a separate commodity section; the numeral 6 is damaged. || ETYMOLOGY: PS *wayn- (Heb. yayin, Ug. yn, Gk. oinos < *woinos). VIN+WA compound (2×, HT27b) shows WA as possible phonetic complement for /wa-/ of *wayn-. || VIN-GRA-SA triad on HT27b = canonical wine-grain-beer commodity set. || No JA-NE 'wine' occurs in the corpus, so the *wayn- etymology rests on the VIN+WA complement alone, distinct from the secure commodity function.

entries.meaning: šamnu 'oil, olive oil'
entries.note: Non-phonetic commodity ideogram denoting oil/olive oil. 21 standalone, 9 sites. PS *šamnu (Heb. šemen, Ug. šmn, Akk. šamnu). *308 = ŠAMNU already resolved as pressed oil derivative with same root—OLE is the base ideogram || COMPOUND SYSTEM: Richest of any commodity—18 types: OLE+KI standard, OLE+MI anointing, OLE+DI honey-infused, OLE+TA fine-grade, OLE+NE libation, OLE+RI aromatic. OLE+MI/OLE+KI compound system confirms base value || 20 tablets, 7 sites. Universal Linear B commodity logogram.

entries.meaning: zayt 'olive (fruit)'
entries.note: Non-phonetic commodity ideogram denoting olive fruit (distinct from OLE = šamnu 'oil'). PS *zayt (Heb. zayit, Ug. zt, Arab. zaytūn). OLIV and OLE co-occur on same tablets with separate quantities (HT50a, HT101, HT116a)—fruit vs product. HT123+124a: OLIV 31 + *308 (pressed oil) 8¼ = olive processing record. HTW231a: OLIV alone on sealing = commodity label. *OLIV+TU sub-type compound (3×). 24 standalone, 17 tablets, 5 sites. Standard commodity logogram shared with Linear B.

entries.meaning: olive commodity subtype; exact product unknown
entries.note: The compound occurs on three Haghia Triada tablets within quantified commodity lists. The OLIV host securely places it in the olive-product family, and TU distinguishes it from plain OLIV. Comparison with OLE+TU shows that the adjunct can qualify related oil/olive hosts, but neither the exact product nor a phonetic expansion of TU is established. Translate only as 'TU-qualified olive product.'

entries.meaning: parūs- 'crushed, ground (flour)'
entries.note: Single-sign commodity logogram, possibly denoting flour or ground grain. PS *parūs- 'crushed, broken' (Heb. pāras 'to break, divide'). Dual role: standalone commodity (16×, 5 sites) and compound modifier (GRA+PA 19× = ground grain/flour, *304+PA 3× = rendered fat). Clusters with TI (figs) in commodity community. ZA12a/b quantities (64, 40) indicate bulk agricultural product. No phonetic complement confirmation—single-consonant skeleton makes reading tentative. On HT8a PA takes KI-oil 3½ in a list of recipients, an abbreviation there and not the commodity.

entries.meaning: ʾaššē 'fire offering, burnt offering'
entries.note: Proto-NWS *ʾaššay- with /a/ preserved (Hebrew ʾiššēh shifted /a/>/i/ via Barth's Law). Four attestations across two sites and two registers (HT tablets, ZAZb3 vessel). On HT81, HT93a and HT132 A-SE opens an entry, followed by a divider and a commodity (MI+JA+RU myrrh, I GRA+PA, A319); on HT93a the personal name QA-QA-RU stands before the same grain, so a recipient is the rival there. Commodity co-occurrences match Biblical pattern: grain (HT93a I GRA+PA), aromatics (HT81 MI+JA+RU myrrh), oil contexts (Lev 2:1, Num 28:5). Competing hypothesis: ʾaš "who/which" (Phoenician relative pronoun ʾš), the better phonological fit. Ugaritic cognate uncertain (Huehnergard: itt /ʾiṭtātu/? with /ṭ/ not /š/).

entries.meaning: Divine Justice / ʾĪ-Mīšaru—theophoric compound: ʾī- (divine prefix) + Mīšaru (justice god, maqtal pattern of √y-š-r). Personnel category on sanctuary allocation tablet.

cognates.Akkadian: Mīšaru (d-Mīšaru)—god of justice, son of Adad and Šala, spouse of Išartu (An = Anum III). maqtal nominal of ešēru "to be straight/just" (CAD E 352). Attested: OB theophoric names, Mari, Seleucid Uruk god-lists.
cognates.Ugaritic: mšr—"justice, equity" (DUL 592); KTU 1.16 vi: mšr as divine attribute
cognates.Hebrew: mêšārîm (מֵישָׁרִים) "equity, uprightness" (Ps 9:9, 58:2, 75:3); same maqtal pattern as Akkadian Mīšaru
cognates.Phoenician: Misor (Μισωρ)—Philo of Byblos via Eusebius PE 1.10.13: father of Taautus/Thoth; paired with Sydyk (√ṣ-d-q)

entries.note: HT27a .3: I-MI-SA-RA 43[ on personnel allocation tablet headed by TI-NI-TA *307 (Tinit of the Sanctuary). The word is line-initial at an intact edge, though a carry-over from line .2 is not ruled out; the numeral meets a break, so 43 or more. CAD M/2, 118 also lists ᵈIl-mīšaru (KAV 42 i 34), which I-MI-SA-RA spells with coda l unwritten. Phonological mapping: I = /ʾī/ — the West Semitic ʾî/ỉy 'where is—?' element of liturgy and onomastics: Ugaritic ỉy 'where?' (Huehnergard 2012, in contact lexicon; DUL s.v. ỉy); cultic cry ỉy ảlỉyn bʿl 'Where is Mighty Baal?' KTU 1.6 IV (= CTA/UT 6[49].4.28–29; Pope, Song of Songs, AB 7C, p. 589); Hebrew ʾî-kāḇôd (1 Sam 4:21), ʾIyyôḇ (HALOT 38, s.v. III אִי, 2. 'where? (?)', listing אִיכָבוֹד; Noth, Die israelitischen Personennamen, on ʾî-names). Amorite i-initial name elements (Huffmon 1965, APNM: ila p.165, išar p.216, itur p.270) are congruent but include lexical elements and the Akkadian 3ms preterite i- (itur), not a distinct theophoric-prefix convention. MI = /mī/, SA = /ša/ (š→S neutralization), RA = /ru/. Clean 4-sign → 4-syllable mapping. Alternative reading: *maṣṣariya "guard/watchman" (√m-ṣ-r)—but requires three accommodations (unexplained prefix, lost geminate, lost -iya suffix) vs one for Mīšaru (theophoric prefix). Context favors divine reading: sanctuary allocation, not garrison roster. If correct, HT27a contains both members of the Akkadian justice dyad: Tinit (subsuming Išartu/Yashara as heading deity) and Mīšaru (as personnel category). Cross-reference: SA-SA-RA = Yašara(t)/Išartu, the feminine counterpart. Huehnergard: /yušru/ "uprightness" (yuCCu nominal pattern); confirms adverbial accusative with -m.

alternative_readings.note: guard, watchman (root m-ṣ-r). Requires: (1) unexplained I- prefix, (2) lost geminate ṣṣ→SA, (3) lost -iya suffix. Phonologically weaker but administratively plausible ("43 guards").

related_forms: TI-NI-TA (Tinitu/Tanit, CONFIRMED — heading deity on same tablet)

entries.meaning: ruqqû-ru 'aromatic preparation (with phonetic complement RU confirming /ru-/ onset)'
entries.note: Phonetic complement RU confirms /ru-/ onset of base *401 RUQQÛ. All 6 attestations at Khania. Fractional quantities (1/16, 1/5) confirm luxury aromatic. Co-occurs with CYP, MI+JA+RU (myrrh), *308 (šamnu), OLE+TA (fine oil). KH91 distinguishes *401+RU from *401+RO on same tablet—different compounds, not spelling variants. Related: *401+*304 (RUQQÛ+PIDRU "aromatic fat", 2× at HT+KH). KNZg57a (2025 ivory scepter ring) adds the first Knossos attestation—all prior at Khania.

entries.meaning: shade, protection (personal-name element)

cognates.Amorite: ṣill- 'shade, protection' (Huffmon, APNM 257); Ṣillī-Baʿli, Ṣill-Haddu

entries.note: Name on the HT 55a KI-RO list (SI-RU 1) and first element of HT 90 SI-RU-MA-RI-TA₂ (GORILA I 107, 143). Amorite ṣill- 'shade, protection' (Huffmon, APNM 257): Ṣillī-Baʿli (APNM 58), Ṣill-Haddu, Ṣillān (Gelb, AS 21); Hebrew ṣēl, the name Ṣillāh (Gen 4:19); Ugaritic ẓl /ẓillu/ (Huehnergard 2012). PS *ẓill-, written with SI and one RU for the geminate. Distinct from SI-RU-TE in the libation formula.

entries.meaning: one who sets in order (title or name)
entries.note: A recipient in the HT 9a/9b wine lists under SA-RO · TE · VIN (2½, 2) and on HT 122a (1), one roster in three copies, among names and titles. *324 = SO: Linear A has no other SO sign, and LA 324 may be a Haghia Triada variant of LA 363/364 (Ferrara, Montecchi & Valério 2022, 88), compared with Linear B so (ibid. 98). SO-DI-RA = sōdir, active participle of s-d-r with ō for older ā and DI for d: Akk. sadāru 'to array, set in a row' (CAD S 11); Heb. śĕdērôt 'ranks' (2 Kgs 11:8, 15). SI-DA-RE stands on the same HT 122a roster. Rivals: šōṭēr 'officer' (√š-ṭ-r; Exod 5:6–19), which needs DI for ṭ; ʾaddīr 'noble' (Ug. yn (…) l ádrm 'wine (…) for the nobles', KTU 4.246:7, DULAT 21), which needs *324 for ʾa, a value plain A already writes.

entries.meaning: star (celestial toponym; Semitic kawkab with b→p voicing)
entries.note: Pan-Semitic: Hebrew kōkāb, Akkadian kakkabu, Arabic kawkab. Functions as toponym/header on roundels with CYP. Three attestations at HT.

entries.meaning: The Hunter (PN from PS *dVhVr- "hunt"; *21F = ha speculative)
entries.note: PS *dVhVr- "hunt" (exact skeleton match). Hebrew dāhar "to gallop" (Nah 3:2). Arabic dahr "time, fate, epoch" is semantically attractive but Arabic-specific—no Hebrew/Ugaritic/Akkadian cognate with "time/fate" meaning. Ugaritic ḏhrt "vision" is interdental /ḏ/, a different root. Not √ṭ-h-r: DA sign = /d/ (not /ṭ/), and the syllabary fully distinguishes D/T. PN position on KH92 allocation list.

entries.meaning: compounded perfume, ointment (vessel label)

cognates.Akkadian: raqqû in bīt raqqî 'perfume makers' bureau' (CAD R 174)

entries.note: SY Za 11, the sole word on a stone vessel from the Syme sanctuary: · RO-QA. Heb. rōqaḥ 'compounded perfume' (Exod 30:25, 35), final ḥ unwritten; a label for the vessel's contents. Rival: rōqēaḥ 'perfumer' (Ug. rqḥ, DULAT 734), the maker or owner. One attestation.

entries.meaning: myrrh (the bitter resin)
entries.cognates: Akk. murru, Ug. mr, Heb. mōr (Exod 30:23), Ar. murr
entries.note: qaṭīl + nisbe: *marīr-ēy* 'the bitter stuff' = myrrh. Perfect consonant match. Co-occurs with SA-MA 'spice' on aromatic allocation tablet HT6. Front of same tablet (HT6a) has O-RA₂-DI-NE (possible ladanum). Song of Songs 4:14 lists mōr alongside qāneh and saffron.

entries.meaning: Beloved (personal name, widd 'love')

cognates.Amorite: JADID 'dear', IA-DI-DA, IA-DI-DU-UM (Gelb 1980, nos. 3183–3192)
cognates.Arabic: wadda (وَدَّ) 'to love', inf. n. wudd, widd, wadd; widād 'love' (Lane 2931); names wdn, wdnt (Harding 1971, 639), wdd, wddʾl (637); Wadd, a god (Faris 1952, 9)

entries.note: HT 28b: WI-DI-NA OLE+DI 3, VIN 3¼, after PU-RA₂ and JA-*21F, each with its own entry. widd 'love', the i-form of √w-d-d (Lane 2931), + -īn + -a; dd unwritten. Arabian names wdn, f. wdnt (Harding 1971, 639) share the skeleton w-d-n. Initial w- where Amorite (JADID, Gelb 1980, nos. 3183–3192), Ugaritic (ydd) and Hebrew (yādîd) have y-. Rival: Wadd, a god (Faris 1952, 9; Q 71:23), which needs WI for wa. Weak point: the -īn-a ending. Cf. WA-DI-NI (HT Wc 3007). One attestation.

entries.meaning: Yāh, divine name; deity receiving offerings alongside Baal on HT28b

cognates.Hebrew: יָהּ Yāh (Ex 15:2 ʿozzī wə-zimrāt Yāh; Ps 68:5 bə-Yāh šemō; Ex 17:16 kēs Yāh)
cognates.Egyptian: tꜣ šꜣsw yhwꜣ 'land of the Shasu of YHW' (Soleb, Amenhotep III c. 1390 BCE; Amarah West, Ramesses II)
cognates.Elephantine: yhw (5th c. BCE papyri, consistent trigrammatic form)

entries.note: Corpus form JA-*21F; *21F = HA (/h/, /ḫ/). HT28b: recipient of VIN 6, between PU-RA₂ (Baal, NI 6) and WI-DI-NA (OLE+DI 3 VIN 3¼), as in Ugaritic offering lists (KTU 1.39, 1.41). HT28a: heads its own commodity list after A-SI-JA-KA. Rival: a ya- verbal form of a /h/ root.

entries.meaning: Cat (personal name)

cognates.Akkadian: šurānu 'cat'; Šu-ra-nu, a personal name (CAD Š/3 339)

entries.note: ZA 11b: E-TO-RI-[·] *516 / SA-*301-RI GRA+PA 1 / I OLIV 1. With *301 = na, SA-NA-RI, s-n-r: the metathesized form of Arabic sinnawr, not Akkadian š-r-n. Šurānu is a personal name in Akkadian (CAD Š/3 339). Reading šannāri, nn unwritten. One attestation.

entries.meaning: young bull, head of cattle (live livestock logogram; MU-onset abbreviation of *mūru). Complementary to TU = ṯawr 'cattle products'—*23M counts live animals (whole numbers 1-5), TU measures processed portions (fractional quantities 1/16–3/4). Zero tablet overlap.
entries.note: 7 tokens across 6 tablets at 3 sites (HT 4×, KH 2×, GOW 1×). || PS RECONSTRUCTION: *muhr- (Starling #2243) / *mVrVʔ- (#2245). Akk mūru 'foal (donkey or horse); calf', from OAkk on (CAD M2 229–30; eBL mūru I 'young animal; young bull; foal'). Middle Assyrian ledgers write it with the ox determinative, {gu₄}mu-ru{nita₂} 'young bull' (MARV 2 6), and count it by head: 67 mu-ru ša MU '67 calves, yearlings' (KAJ 289:11). mīru A 'young bull' (SB, CAD M2 109; eBL mīru I 'breeding bull'). Ug mru (DLU 288, √mrʔ Hip. 'to fatten'). Heb מְרִיא mǝrīʾ 'fatted steer' (1 Kgs 1:9, Amos 5:22). MU = /mu/ spells mūru's /ū/; the calf sense runs through Middle and Neo-Assyrian, so the Cretan form needs no early equine/bovine split || Alternative: *ʾalpu 'cattle' (PS *ʾalp-, Starling #2113) if purely pictographic rather than syllabic-abbreviation

entries.meaning: recipient or section heading; perhaps an excess or surplus entry

cognates.Akkadian: watārum 'be exceeding'; watrum 'additional, in excess'; watartum/watarti 'excess, surplus, extra' (Huehnergard 1997, §10.1)

entries.language_layer: uncertain; Akkadian and Northwest Semitic comparison
entries.note: TE-RI introduces a secondary allocation on HT91, stands before one ram on PH(?)31b, and occurs in the short ARKH6 sequence. These contexts support a recipient, category, or section heading, but not one fixed gloss. The former derivation from Akkadian tārum 'return' and unattested *tēri is rejected. √w-t-r/y-t-r supplies genuine 'excess/surplus' vocabulary, but its attested forms do not yield bare TE-RI cleanly; 'surplus' remains secondary.

entries.meaning: box, basket (standardized container for measured commodity allocations)
entries.note: No QU sign in Linear A syllabary — /qu/ written as KU. Accusative *quppa(m) gives KU-PA. Diagnostic pattern: KU-PA 𐄁 GRA+PA N on both ZA11a (qty 1) and ZA11b (qty 3) — container label before measured grain. All quantities small (1-3), consistent with individual containers. Distinct from KA-PA 'village' (√k-p-r, different vowel, HT-only).

entries.meaning: principal, primary, capital (quality/grade marker on sealed goods and commodity allocations)
entries.note: 95 total attestations (91 standalone HTWa nodules + 4 multi-word). Functions as pre-commodity modifier: RO GRA = 'principal grain', RO VIN = 'principal wine'. On standalone nodules, marks sealed goods as prime/principal category. Pan-Semitic: Akk rēšu, Heb rō(ʔ)š, Ug rʔiš, Ar raʾs, Aram rēš + Ethiopic, South Arabian, Modern South Arabian.

entries.meaning: seed-grain (agricultural category marker for planting stock allocations)
entries.note: 47 total attestations (40 HTWa nodules + 6 KHWa nodules + 1 multi-word HT16). On standalone nodules, marks sealed goods as seed-grain category, distinct from GRA (harvested grain). HT16 context: SA-PO ZE 1/16 — smallest fractional allocation on a distribution tablet. Pan-Semitic: Akk zēru 'seed, acreage' (OAkk on), Heb zeraʿ 'seed', Phoen zrʕ, Aram zǝraʿ (Empire, Egyptian, Biblical, Judaic, Syriac, Mandaic). LMIB-only dating consistent with seasonal planting batch.

entries.meaning: turn away! (2mp imperative—disease expulsion command)
entries.note: Egyptian group-writing: s3bw [element 6a]. √s-b-b 'to turn, go around': Heb sābab (~163 occ., HALOT 738), 2mp imper. sōbbū (Ps 48:13 סֹבּוּ צִיּוֹן). Group-writing s3 = plain /s/, not /ṣ/—the same scribe renders Semitic ṣ as Egyptian ḏ in the adjacent word yaṣʾā (y3yd33), ruling out √ṣ-b-ʾ. Geminate -bb- invisible in group-writing (standard). Disease-expulsion doublet sabbū yaṣʾā 'Turn away! Go out!' parallels Akkadian serial motion imperatives in Udug.hul. D54 determinative is embedded in the phonogram ḏi of word 2 (Kyriakidis 2002, n. 16), not a freestanding classifier per word. Keftiu Spell #33 (samānu disease), LMP BM 10059.

entries.meaning: go out! (3ms volitive yaqtula—disease expulsion command)
entries.note: Egyptian group-writing: y3yd33 [element 6b, Det: D54 'to go']. PS *wṣʾ → NWS *yaṣʾa with diagnostic *w→y shift. Akk waṣû (CAD W 319, preserves *w-), Ug yṣʾ (DLU 946), Heb yāṣāʾ (HALOT 427). Egyptian d renders Semitic ṣ; 33 (double aleph) renders final ʾ + short a-vowel (group-writing never marks length). STEINER'S OWN ROOT: Steiner 1992 (JNES 51) identifies √y-ṣ-ʾ yaṣʾā 'go out!' in this spell. Volitive parse: yaqtula modal prefix-form in -a (Moran 1960, Orientalia 29; Amarna Canaanite, cognate w/ Arabic subjunctive, ancestral to Heb cohortative ʾeṣʾā). Energic rejected (no nasal sign); fem. perfect rejected (14th c. still -at, cf. ḥanqatu -tu in next word). Keftiu Spell #33 (samānu disease), LMP BM 10059.

entries.meaning: strangling-demon (feminine personification of disease)
entries.note: Egyptian group-writing [element 7, Det: A2 'to speak/think']. Keftiu Spell #33, LMP BM 10059 || ETYMOLOGY: *ḥanqatu 'she who strangles'—disease demon name. √ḥ-n-q: Akk. ḫanāqu (CAD Ḫ 75), Heb. ḥānaq (Nahum 2:13), Syr. ḥnaq, Ar. ḫanaqa. Egyptian h for ḥ standard. The m' in the middle is problematic (vowel marker or scribal convention) || STEINER'S READING: ḥanqatu. Samānu disease involves swelling/constriction—'strangler-demon' etiology is medically coherent

entries.meaning: my Healer (deity invocation—divine title of Rapʾu)
entries.note: Egyptian group-writing [element 8, Det: A40 'seated god' (male)]. Keftiu Spell #33, LMP BM 10059. A40 confirms divine status || ETYMOLOGY: √r-p-ʾ 'to heal' + 1cs -ī = 'my healer.' Ug. rpʾu divine title (KTU 1.108:1 rpʾu mlk ʿlm 'the Healer, eternal king'; KTU 1.20–22 rpʾīm/Rephaim), Heb. rāpāʾ (Exod 15:26 rōpʾekā; Ps 103:3), Phoen. mrpʾ month name (KAI 37:3) || STEINER'S READING: r-p-y = rpʾy. Akulov reads Erupa-j, connects to Greek Europa via Hattic *lup 'bull'—same consonantal skeleton, different etymology

entries.meaning: I cry out! / my invocation (ritual speech act)
entries.note: Egyptian group-writing: p33wry [element 9, Det: A2 'to speak/think']. √p-ʿ-r 'to open wide (the mouth)' + 1cs -ī: Heb pāʿar (Isa 5:14 ūpāʿărāh pīhā; Ps 119:131 pī pāʿartī), Ar faġara (regular ʿ→ġ). Form *paʿūr-ī (qatūl verbal noun + possessive). A2 determinative fits speech act. Alternative: √p-ʾ-r 'to glorify' (Isa 60:7). Structurally bridges the two deity names: rpʾī — paʿūrī — Mayyā = 'My Healer — I cry out to — Mayyā.' Keftiu Spell #33, LMP BM 10059.

entries.meaning: Mayyā—deified Water (deity name)
entries.note: Egyptian group-writing: m'y3 [element 10, Det: A40 'seated god' (male)]. Keftiu Spell #33, LMP BM 10059. √m-y-y: PS *maʔ-/*may- 'water' is grammatically masculine across all branches (Akk mû, Heb mayim m.pl., Ug my, Ar māʾ m.), but -ā suffix = productive NWS feminine singular marker (cf. malkā, ʾilat). Mayyā = mayy- + -ā (fem.): 'the feminine Water' = Water-Goddess || THREE SUPPORTING LINES: (1) Arabic مَيَّة (Mayya)—standard feminine PN 'water,' well-attested from pre-Islamic poetry (Dhū l-Rumma, d. 735); geminated mayy- + fem. -a(t). (2) Ugaritic divine epithet pattern—feminine deity names from common nouns with -ā/-at: ʿAṯirat-, ʿAnat- from √ʿ-n-y; hypothetical *Mayyat- follows identical formation. (3) ANE primordial water = feminine deity: Tiʾāmat (Akk, fem.), Tĕhôm (Heb, fem.), Namma (Sum, fem.) || A40 male determinative: Egyptian scribal default for foreign deities—the -ā morpheme in the NWS source already marks feminine gender. Paired with rpʾī (Healer): cure + purification. Ritual instructions: 'over liquid, fermented drink, urine'—water-based media for a water deity. Akulov reads as 'Maja,' connects to Greek Μαῖα (Pleiad)

entries.meaning: she who melts; the melting one (goddess epithet)
entries.note: tD-stem (intensive reflexive) feminine participle of √m-s-s 'to melt, dissolve' (Hebrew māsas, Akkadian masāsu). TA- = reflexive/feminine prefix, doubled -s-s- = geminate root in intensive stem, -ē = feminine participial ending. Cf. Hebrew hitpolel hitmōsēs. tD-stem prefix vowel /e/ (te-) is archaic—Akkadian/Arabic retain /a/ (ta-), Hebrew innovates to /i/ (hit-); the Theran form shows an intermediate stage. Single attestation: THE-9 (RILA-S1, Del Freo & Zurbach 2024); SigLA independently corroborates sign-by-sign (te-mu-sa-se, AB04-AB23-AB31-AB09) and supplies metadata: LM IA clay tablet, 4.6×3.8 cm — a pre-eruption Akrotiri document. RILA-S1 prints the word broken at the right, its last sign uncertain: TE-MU-SA-SẸ[.
entries.source: RILA-S1 (Del Freo & Zurbach, Études Crétoises XXI.6, 2024); di Mino

entries.meaning: who cries out, the one who implores (relative clause: √š-w-ʿ + determinative-relative dē)
entries.note: ZA Zg 35 (label): ]A-MI-JA-RU · SE-WA-AU-DE. √š-w-ʿ 'cry for help' (Heb. šiwwaʿ, Isa 58:9; šawʿâ) + -DE dē, the relative of A-TA-I-*301-DE-KA (di Mino, Ya Diktu): 'the one who cries out'. Weak point: AU is /aw/, one w more than the root. Rival: a second personal name, as on a label.

entries.meaning: personal name: 'the Just/True One' — Akkadian kīnu 'true, reliable, just'

cognates.Akkadian: kīnu 'true, reliable, just' (CAD K 391–394); kânu 'to be firm, true'; PN element in Nabû-kīn-apli, Marduk-kīn-šumi
cognates.Hebrew: kūn (כּוּן) 'to be established, firm'; nākōn (נָכוֹן) 'right, true'

entries.note: Heads commodity allocation section on ARKH3a. Note: JA-KI-SI-KI-NU (ARKHZf9) was initially parsed as containing KI-NU but is now analyzed as a verbal form *yaksīkīnū from √k-s-y "to cover" (see separate entry). East Semitic vocalism (Akkadian kīnu) rather than NWS kūn—consistent with the intra-Semitic fluidity observed in Linear A onomastics (cf. ARKH3b PI-*314 Luwian name alongside Semitic JA-PI). || DUAL-FUNCTION note: kīnu is simultaneously PN element and quality adjective 'true/standard'. On ARKH3a the heading slot admits both 'Kīnu (PN): grain 13' and 'standard-grade: grain 13'; parallels the KI dual function (kī conjunction / kīn(u) grade) and the KA-NE/qanē duality on the same tablet. Discriminating test: a second attestation in-list with quantity (PN) or heading an OLE section (grade). || Standalone KI is an administrative sign of open value; the conjunction reading kī has no GORILA basis (Gordon's I,3 and I,4:a are misread).

entries.meaning: must, new wine (unfermented or partially fermented grape juice) — commodity logogram

cognates.Hebrew: tīrōš (תִּירוֹשׁ) 'must, new wine' (HALOT 1727; Deut 7:13, 11:14, 12:17; Hos 2:10; Joel 2:19)

entries.note: Wine-variant logogram. AB131 family: VIN=wine (*wayn*), *131B=must (*tirōšu*), *131C=vinegar (ACETUM). 4 attestations across 2 sites. The biblical dāgān-tīrōš-yiṣhār triad (Deut 7:13) mirrors ARKH3a's GRA + *131B + OLIV. No syllabic spelling of the word is known. Rival: SigLA codes all four tokens VINb, a variant of VIN.

entries.meaning: sixth(?) or sixth section(?)
entries.note: Compare Ugaritic tdt /ṯādīt-/ 'sixth' (Tropper, §§63.113, 63.12). The consonantal sequence is close if Linear A T writes the interdental, but the written vowels do not reproduce Tropper's vocalization. On HT123+124b TI-DA-TA is followed by a divider, not an explicit 1/6; the tablet therefore supplies no mathematical confirmation. Single attestation. The relation to TI-TI-MA remains a project hypothesis rather than an independent control.

entries.meaning: sixty (numeral)
entries.note: Exact skeleton match to Ugaritic ttm "sixty" (Huehnergard 2012, vocalization /tittma/). PS *θitt-ūma (from *θidθ- "six" × decade suffix). Pairs with TI-DA-TA = tdt "sixth" from the same root. Third instance of the geminate-orthography law: the geminate tt is spelled with the doubled sign TI-TI. On the PHWc40 roundel with NA; a bare numeral suits the roundel unit-count convention, though the precative reading of NA sits oddly beside it—pairing unresolved. Single attestation; no independent mathematical cross-check.

entries.meaning: door, doorway
entries.note: Exact skeleton match to Ugaritic dlt "door" (Huehnergard 2012, /daltu/). PS *dalt- — one of the most stable pan-Semitic nouns (BH dēlet, Akk. daltu). JU=/lu/ gives DA-JU-TE = d-l-t. Appears as header word on HT34 (Haghia Triada, grain accounting tablet with GRA 200, KI-RO 30). First-position on admin tablets typically indicates location or distribution category; "door/doorway" as storage/distribution point parallels Akkadian administrative usage.

entries.meaning: jar, jug (liquid container)

cognates.Ugaritic: kd "jar; measure of capacity for liquids" (DULAT 424)
cognates.Akkadian: kandu "a container of earthenware or silver, mainly for wine", NB, West Semitic word (CAD K 148)

entries.note: ZA 15b: KA-DI · VIN 3, then KU-RO VIN 78. ZA 4a: KA-DI 3, the last entry of the list, after E-*82 50. Ug. kd 'jar; liquid measure' (DULAT 424), Heb. kad (Gen 24:14), Akk. kandu, a wine container, a West Semitic word (CAD K 148). KA-DI writes kadd-, the geminate unmarked. Rival on ZA 4a: a personal name among the list's entries. Two attestations, both Zakros.

entries.meaning: reed, cane; or lapis lazuli (precious stone)

cognates.Hebrew: qāneh קָנֶה "reed, cane, measuring rod" (Exod 30:23, Ezek 40:3)

entries.note: Exact skeleton match to Ugaritic qn with two senses: (A) "reed, cane" (√q-n-y, vocalization /qanē/; BH qāneh קָנֶה "reed, measuring rod," source of English "cane" and "canon"); (B) "lapis lazuli" (precious stone, Ugaritic-specific sense). On KH47 (Khania tablet) with quantity 6 in a commodity context—distributional evidence favors commodity over personal name. Khania is a western Cretan port with strong trade connections, consistent with either imported lapis lazuli or local reed/cane as accounting items. || VARIANT: KA-NA (HT23a header of aromatics ledger, HT123+124b) is the same lexeme with q→K neutralization — attestation at two sites (HT+KH) strengthens the cane reading; lapis sense disfavored there (vowel-initial iqnu predicts I-/U- spelling).

entries.meaning: fruit
entries.note: Logogram *322. 3× standalone on Khania roundels (commodity marker behavior). 1× *322-RI on HT11a with phonetic complement -RI confirming /-rī/ ending. PS *pir- (#756): Hebrew pǝrī, Ugaritic pr, Phoenician pr. Compare DUBUR and BUṬNU; *49 PALM/TREE → TAMIR remains only a candidate complement pattern. HT11a context: allocation list alongside A-RU-RA-[?] (unread) and KA-RO-NA 'horn'.

entries.meaning: a party receiving grain (name or place)
entries.note: HT 40: NU-DU-*331 · TE · GRA 207 / KI-DA-TA · GRA 134 / KU-RO; KI-DA-TA holds the slot of NU-DU-*331, a party, with its own GRA entry. HT 27a .4 KI-DA-[, broken after DA, where GORILA prefers KI-DA-TẸ[ (GORILA I 49), may be a second witness. Rival: kaddat 'jar' (Ug. kd, a jar and a measure for liquids, ca. 22 l, DULAT 424), which leaves KI for ka unexplained and does not fit a grain entry.

entries.meaning: kunāšu 'emmer wheat' (logographic abbreviation)
entries.note: GRA ideogram + KU adjunct (7 att.). Full spelling KU-NI-SU (CONFIRMED, 5 tablets) and abbreviation GRA+KU (3 tablets) at the same site in complementary distribution — full word as section heading without GRA, abbreviation inside GRA-headed allocation lists, never co-occurring. It meets Salgarella's full-spelling/monogram coexistence criterion at tablet level, the only ligature adjunct with a CONFIRMED expansion. On HT128a co-occurs with GRA+PA as distinct grain subtype.

entries.meaning: U-qualified oil subtype; exact product unknown; pressed oil is a tentative Arabic comparison
entries.note: OLE ideogram + U adjunct: 21 tokens in 13 documents. The corpus establishes a distinct oil subtype, not its name. Arabic √ʿ-ṣ-r 'squeeze, press' permits a tentative comparison with pressed oil if initial ʿ is unrepresented, but the exact noun and vocalization *ʿuṣru are unattested. Ugaritic ʿṣr denotes a bird, not 'press,' and therefore supplies no support for this commodity reading.

entries.meaning: ṭuhūru 'purified/ritually clean oil'
entries.note: OLE ideogram + TU adjunct. Acrophonic candidate ṭuhūru 'purified' (Ug ṭhr 'pure', vocalized /ṭuhūru/ per Huehnergard; Heb ṭāhôr); Linear A writes √ṭ-h-r in TU-*21F-RI-NA ṭuhārī-nā (HT129). HT23a: four oil preparations (OLE+NE, OLE+TU, OLE+RI, *308) at the same fraction under KA-NA. *OLIV+TU (HT50a, HT101, HT116a) may write the same word on the olive host.

entries.meaning: kor (dry measure); rival 'ram'
entries.note: HT 23a .5 · KO-RU 1, the last entry of side a after SI+ME 10, in a list of commodities with quantities (GORILA I 41). Akkadian kurru A 'a measure of capacity' (CAD K 564), Hebrew kōr (HALOT 496; 1 Kgs 5:2). Rival: Hebrew kar 'ram' (HALOT 496; Isa 16:1). One witness.

entries.meaning: mixed wine (wine-section heading); rival 'must'
entries.note: ZA 15a .3 ME VIN, two separate signs after I-TI-NI-SA 10, no numeral: it heads the second section of the wine list, as SA VIN heads the first (GORILA III 182–183). ME as the onset of Ugaritic msk 'mixture, mixed wine' (DULAT 575; KTU 1.19 IV 61, // yn), Hebrew mesek (HALOT 605; Ps 75:9). VIN takes single-sign qualifiers elsewhere (VIN+RA, VIN+KA, VIN+TE, VIN+WA). Rival: mrṯ 'must' (DULAT 571–572). One witness.

entries.meaning: RA-qualified wine; exact variety unknown (possibly raḥṣu 'washed/filtered wine')
entries.note: VIN ideogram + RA adjunct in four current corpus records: KE Zb 5, ZA 15b, ZA 6b, and the doubtful seal CR Zg 3. Its occurrence beside plain VIN on ZA 15b establishes a distinct wine category; ZA 6b likewise contrasts it with VIN+KA. The exact variety is unknown. Of four ra- candidates, raḥṣu 'washed/filtered' (√r-ḥ-ṣ; Ug rḥṣ, Heb rāḥaṣ) supplies a possible acrophonic expansion, but the single adjunct cannot select that word over its rivals. The uncertain etymology caps the entry at CANDIDATE.

entries.meaning: priest(s) (personnel category, ligatured onset abbreviation)
entries.note: Two-sign onset abbreviation of kumru (√k-m-r). No complete √k-m-r spelling survives: HT 96a has ]KU-MA-RO, broken before KU, and HT 24a KỊ-MA+RU[. Category label on personnel registers; meets full-spelling/abbreviation complementary distribution criterion.

entries.meaning: May he cover you (f. pl.)! (3ms G imperfect yaksī + 2fp object suffix -kin; NU writes the final nasal, as in -U-TI-NU)

cognates.Hebrew: kāsā (כָּסָה) 'to cover' (Jonah 3:6 wayekas śaq—same root with ashes in penitential context)
cognates.Ugaritic: ksy 'to cover oneself' (CUC: 2 occ., cult domain)

entries.note: ARKHZf9 (Arkhanes, bronze votive object). Word 1 of 2-word inscription JA-KI-SI-KI-NU <> MI-DA-RU-RA. Morphological parse: ya- (3ms imperfect prefix) + √k-s-y 'to cover' (III-weak, G-stem imperfect *yaksī) + -kin (2fp object suffix, addressing a group of women). Full form: *yaksīkin 'May he cover you (women)!' Not 2fs -kī + energic -nū: an energic precedes an object suffix (Ar. la-ʾuḥarriqanna-kum, Fischer 2002, §198; Heb. -ennû). Read as -kī + 1cp 'us', the 2nd person would precede the 1st, against Fischer 2002, §271; kasā's second object is the covering, MI-DA-RU-RA. Biblical parallel: Jonah 3:6 וַיְכַ֣ס שַׂ֔ק וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב עַל־הָאֵֽפֶר—√k-s-y + ashes in penitential supplication before God. Lam 3:16 הִכְפִּישַׁנִי בָּאֵפֶר—'He covered me with ashes' (√k-p-š, different root, exact semantic match). Jonah 3:8 וְיִתְכַּסּ֣וּ שַׂקִּ֗ים—hitpaʿel (tG-stem) *yitkassū "let them cover themselves," same root in reflexive ritual covering. Ugaritic ksy classified under 'cult' domain confirms ritual connotation in NWS.

entries.meaning: dust, ashes, dry earth (second accusative of √k-s-y 'cover': midr-a; or intensive midrar-)
entries.note: ARKHZf9 (Arkhanes, bronze votive object). Word 2 of 2-word inscription JA-KI-SI-KI-NU <> MI-DA-RU-RA. RILA reading updates GORILA MI-DA-MA-RA₂: sign 3 reread as RU (AB26), sign 4 as RA (AB27). Skeleton m-d-r maps to PS *midr-. Final -RA writes either: (a) accusative case ending -a on a root-final /r/ (*midr-a), or (b) geminate /rr/ in an intensive form *midrar-. Context: paired with *yaksīkīnū 'May he cover you!'—the full inscription reads 'May he cover you with dust/ashes!' Ritual use of ashes/dust in NWS: Jonah 3:6 (penitential sitting on ashes), Num 19:17 (purification ashes of red heifer), Job 2:12 (mourning dust on head), 2 Sam 13:19 (lamentation ashes). Additional parallels: Ezek 27:30 בָּאֵפֶר יִתְפַּלָּשׁוּ "they roll in ashes" (mourning), Esther 4:1 וַיִּלְבַּשׁ שַׂק וָאֵפֶר "sackcloth and ashes" (supplication), Gen 18:27 עָפָר וָאֵפֶר "dust and ashes" (Abraham's self-abasement before God), Isa 61:3 פְּאֵר תַּחַת אֵפֶר "beauty instead of ashes." A votive bronze suits both purificatory and penitential ritual readings. || 'Cover/clothe' takes two accusatives, person and covering (Fischer 2002, §374a: albasanī ṯiyābahu 'He clothed me in his garments'), so the -a has a governor in JA-KI-SI-KI-NU.

entries.meaning: My Giver / My Athena — 1cs possessive on divine epithet (√y-t-n 'to give' + -ya 'my')
entries.note: THEZb6 (Thera, clay vessel). Single-word devotional inscription. Variant of the A-TA-NA paradigm: feminine absolute A-TA-NA-TE (ZA10a, -tu; ZA9 A-TA-NA-[·] probably the same word), 1cs possessive A-TA-NA-JE (THEZb6, -ya). Two suffixed forms at two sites (Zakros, Thera) confirm productive derivation. The -JE suffix writes NWS 1cs possessive -ya, paralleling PU₂-RE-JA = burēyā 'my Creator' (same suffix on divine epithet). On a votive vessel, 'My Giver' is a natural devotional dedication—the worshiper claiming personal relationship with the goddess. √y-t-n is the Ugaritic/Phoenician (coastal NWS) form; Minoan patterns with the coastal languages.

entries.meaning: sesame (seed-spice commodity)
entries.note: Hapax on HT23a aromatics ledger (CYP, OLE+NE/TU/RI oil sub-types, VIN) measured at fraction K, as *21F-RI-TU-QA, consistent with seed-spice. The second SA is dotted, and GORILA I 41 records SA [units] ME as a less satisfactory reading. Reduplicated s-s-m skeleton matches the Semitic etymon sign-for-sign; absent final -n regular (mimation/nunation drop). LB comparandum sits in the same commodity class beside ku-mi-no (cumin — LA KU-MI-NA already PROBABLE) and ko-ri-ja-do-no (coriander) on the Ge spice tablets. A hapax: context, structure and the triple external chain converge.

entries.meaning: aromatic reed, sweet cane (commodity; spelling variant of QA-NE)

cognates.Ugaritic: qn 'reed, cane' (DULAT; also 'lapis lazuli' = iqnu, a distinct lexeme written identically)
cognates.Hebrew: qāneh קָנֶה 'reed, cane' — qəneh-bośem 'aromatic cane' Exod 30:23, anointing-oil ingredient
cognates.Linear B: cf. ko-no (σχοῖνος 'aromatic rush') — semantic parallel in Mycenaean spice accounting

entries.note: Spelling variant of QA-NE (KH47, CANDIDATE qanē) with q→K neutralization proposed under Gordon §4/§76. Cross-site comparison: HT (2×) + KH (1×). HT23a heads an aromatics ledger (CYP, oil sub-types, VIN, and SA-SA-ME sesame), providing the principal contextual support for comparison with Hebrew qāneh and qəneh-bośem. On HT123+124b KA-NA is followed by the central lacuna, probably containing a lost quantity; that tablet supports administrative recurrence but not the product identification. Lapis-lazuli (Ugaritic iqnu < Akkadian uqnû) is a rival homograph, though its vowel-initial form fits the Linear A spelling less directly.

entries.meaning: the stall, storehouse

cognates.Akkadian: abūsu 'storehouse', pl. abūsātu, ubsātu (CAD A/1 92); bēl abūsi 'overseer of the storehouse', Ras Shamra (CAD A/1 93)

entries.note: *325 = /bu/ (CANDIDATE). PS *s = [ts] takes the Z-series. HT10a: two issues (4, 14); HT85a: 6 men, beside DA-RI-DA and DA-RE, the pattern of a standing unit. The U-/A- onset against A-*325-ZA (PE2) matches Akk. ubsātu beside abūsātu. At Ras Shamra a bēl abūsi 'overseer of the storehouse' receives goods. Rival: *325 = /ḫu/, ʾuḫuzza(t) 'holding' (Heb. ʾăḥuzzâ, HALOT 32), with ZA for PS *ḏ.

entries.meaning: the stall, storehouse

cognates.Akkadian: abūsu 'storehouse', pl. abūsātu, ubsātu (CAD A/1 92); bēl abūsi 'overseer of the storehouse', Ras Shamra (CAD A/1 93)

entries.note: *325 = /bu/ (CANDIDATE). PS *s = [ts] takes the Z-series. PE2 fraction list (¼). Spells PS *ʾabūs- sign for sign. Variant of U-*325-ZA, as Akk. abūsātu beside ubsātu.

entries.meaning: possible personal name Tōmar/Tamar; palm-name

cognates.Amorite: TAMAR-U /ta-ma-ru/, a one-element personal name; also ŠUM-U*TAMAR and ŠUM-U*TAMAR-U (Gelb 1980, nos. 6027, 5716, 5715)
cognates.Hebrew: tōmer תֹּמֶר masculine palm (Judges 4:5, the Palm of Deborah) / tāmār תָּמָר feminine name
cognates.Ugaritic: syllabic /tamaru/ 'date palm' proposed for Ug. 5 137 (Huehnergard 2008, nos. 175, TMR)
cognates.Proto-Semitic: *tam(V)r- 'palm tree'; the plant word occurs in Semitic personal and place names

entries.note: Credible Semitic name candidate within the bronze-bowl scriptio continua A-RA-KO-KU-QA-WA-SA-TO-MA-RO-AU-TA-DE-PO-NI-ZA. The onomastic comparison is Bronze Age: Gelb's Amorite index gives the one-element name TAMAR-U /ta-ma-ru/ (no. 6027) and TAMAR in two compound names (nos. 5715–16). Compare also Hebrew Tāmār as a woman's name (Gen 38; 2 Sam 13), Hebrew tōmer 'palm' (Judg 4:5), and proposed syllabic Ugaritic /tamaru/ 'date palm' (Huehnergard 2008, nos. 175, TMR). TO-MA-RO can therefore represent a local Tōmar/Tamar-type name if final O is a support vowel writing coda /r/; initial /tō-/ could reflect local vocalism or *ā > ō. The limitation is epigraphic: GORILA prints no divider before or after TO-MA-RO, so its word boundary and exact vocalization remain inferred. The personal-name reading is retained as CANDIDATE; no grammatical case can be assigned from the context.

entries.meaning: linen (material adjectival base in jar labels)

cognates.Greek: χιτών via LB ki-to, here fully vocalized

entries.note: Base of KI-TA-NA-SI-JA-SE (PEZb3 clay vessel) = "linen which goes out" — commodity + disbursement marker. SI-JA-SE = šī-yāṣē (relative particle + 3ms impf. √y-ṣ-ʾ "to go out"), tagging goods for outgoing allocation. The pithos label reads: ...kitāna šī-yāṣē pidr-qê "linen which goes out, a qê-measure of fat." || LB ki-to (χιτών ← ktn) points to this word; the full form is recovered by segmentation. || Parallel: A-NA-NU-SI-JA-SE (HTZb159) uses the same -SI-JA-SE disbursement suffix on a different stem. || -t derivative: KI-TA-NI-TE kitānit "linen robe, linen cloth" (PK Zb 21 pithos).

entries.meaning: linen robe, linen cloth

cognates.Akkadian: kitītu, var. kitintu "linen robe" (eBL kitītu I); kitû "flax, linen"

entries.note: PK Zb 21 pithos, incised before firing. -t derivative of KI-TA-NA (PE Zb 3 KI-TA-NA-SI-JA-SE; KH60 RA-KI-TA-NA-SI); the recurrence of KI-TA-N- is noted by Davis (Kadmos 47, 2008), whose reading this is. Unshifted ā: the pre-Canaanite form of kətōnet. As a jar label, the stored linen goods. Rival: Driessen ME-WI-TA-NI-TE (superseded).

entries.meaning: flask, vial (small libation/oil vessel)

cognates.Hebrew: pak פַּךְ 'flask, vial' — pak ha-šemen, the anointing-oil flask (1 Sam 10:1; 2 Kgs 9:1-3)
cognates.Ugaritic: bk rb 'a large vessel' (KTU 1.3 I 12), in the passage that pairs ks // krpn

entries.note: Two spellings of one vessel word; the '/' marks the alternation. PU-KO stands alone on the HT31 vessel inventory directly before *410-VS, the only vessel on the tablet without a name ligatured to its sign. PA-KU (KNZc6 inked cup, written as one unit after DA-KI-TI) is a segment of continuous writing on a dedicatory object, where an oil-vial word fits (Hebrew pak is the vessel of royal anointing). PU-KO pukku keeps the older vowel that Hebrew pak lost after the labial; -KO writes final /-ku/, as -RO does in KU-RO. Ugaritic bk rb 'a large vessel' (KTU 1.3 I 12) stands in the same passage as krpn, the counterpart of HT31's KA-RO-PA₃. Rival: bk is commonly compared with Greek βῖκος, and Smith & Pitard (2009, 108) call it 'apparently an Indo-European Kulturwort'.

entries.meaning: refined gold
entries.note: Ugaritic pd 'refined gold' (Baal Cycle, Kothar workshop passages). Context: KH88 acquisitions ledger headed QA-NU-MA, listing *21F-*118 = ḫaṭṭu 'scepter' and NI figs 10 before PU-DE 8. Sole attestation. || Against a higher tier: the precious-goods framing needs NI = honey, but NI is figs; the etymology stands.

entries.meaning: garlic (logographic abbreviation)
entries.note: PS *ṯūm- 'garlic (Allium sativum)'; ZU carries /ṯu/ under the sibilant mergers, abbreviating ṯūm as NI abbreviates nūb(at). Context: KH91 mixed ration list — grain, wine, beans, ZU ≈⅙, cattle, honey, aromatics. Garlic between beans and beef in a ration list.

entries.meaning: cyperus, aromatic sedge (commodity logogram)
entries.note: Cyperus commodity logogram, not cypress and not copper. Khania is its principal distribution: 35× plain + 28× in fraction-ligatures (CYP+D, CYP+E; D/E are Bennett-convention fraction letters). The sign continues as the Linear B CYPERUS ideogram, associated with phonetic ku-pa-ro. On HT89 it opens the post-total commodity section at 2 + A732; ¾ is a modern fraction-model value rather than an uncontested reading. KH co-occurrence set includes aromatics (myrrh, *401+RU, fine oil).

entries.meaning: tripod cauldron (vessel logogram)
entries.note: Pictographic: hemispherical bowl on three legs with lateral handles, consistent across the 15-roundel KHWc series; an independent visual reading describes 'a three-legged cauldron'. Direct ancestor of LB *201 TRIPOD (ti-ri-po-de, PY Ta 641). All attestations are solo-sign sealed roundel receipts — bronze-vessel circulation through the Khania harbor town.

entries.meaning: Healer of Jubilation (Eshmun epithet)
entries.note: Compound epithet: vocative ʾa- + rāpiʾ (participle √r-p-ʾ 'heal'; Ug. rpu) + rinnā(h) (√r-n-n 'joyful cry, jubilation'). ZAZb3 … A-TA-I-*301-DE-KA · A-RE-PI-RE-NA · TI-TI-KU: the formula's deity slot after the A-TA-I-*301- verb, on the vessel that names A-SA-MU-NE (Eshmun). Ps 30:3 wattirpāʾēnî and 30:6 rinnâ join the two roots. Hapax. The third sign is damaged: PI favoured, MA not excluded. Rivals: Gordon (1975, 153) reads re-ma-re-na, Aramaic mārēnā 'our lord' ('for our lord Titiku'); Woudhuizen (2016, 230) a-re ma-re-na 'our guild-master'; or prosthetic A- with ʾa-rāpiʾ-ēnā 'O our Healer' (participle + 1cp suffix).

entries.meaning: the tied, sealed (packet) (?)
entries.note: HT 23a, K-fraction entry between E 17 and sesame in an aromatics ledger; RI dotted (GORILA I 41). RI-TU-QA from √r-t-q 'to tie, bind': Ug. rtq (DULAT 737); Heb. ruttəqû (Nah 3:10), rətuqôt (Isa 40:19); Ar. ratq (Q 21:30). *21F the article ha-. Weak point: *21F as an optional H-sign. One attestation.

entries.meaning: outpouring, pouring-out—(header) disbursed; (libation) may it be poured
entries.cognates: Ug. √n-t-k "pour out" (KTU 1.14 I 28-30); Heb. נָתַךְ nātak—nifal nittak (Exod 9:33, 2 Chr 34:25), Hiphil hittīkū "they disbursed" (2 Kgs 22:9), Hiphil hitaktī (Ezek 22:20-22); Akk. natāku "drip"
entries.note: Ugaritic √n-t-k 'to pour out, forth' (Huehnergard; Kirta: tntkn udmʿth km ṯqlm arṣh, 'his tears pour out like shekels to the ground,' KTU 1.14 I 28–30); Hebrew nifal nittak of rain (Exod 9:33), wrath (2 Chr 34:25), molten metal (Ezek 22:20–22); Akkadian natāku 'drip,' tabāku 'pour out' as the standard verb of commodity disbursement. Surface tt = geminate from assimilated nun, spelled with the doubled sign TI-TI (geminate-orthography law). Across genres: header of HT35, where every commodity is pourable (cyperus, myrrh, three oil grades, butter, wine, all in fractional liquid measures)—the pour-class counterpart of the given/received/counted header family; final word of the ZAZb3 wine-libation formula (wine 32, ʾaššē fire-offering, √n-w-y formula word, Eshmun epithet), closing as a libation should. Noun tittuk(u) 'outpouring' vs G imperfect tittōk 'may it be poured' left open; both fit both slots. 2 Kgs 22:9 הִתִּיכוּ hittīkū (Hiphil 3cp √n-t-k with nun→geminate): "Your servants have disbursed the silver found in the house"—the exact administrative disbursement sense on a financial report, with the same geminate /tt/ orthography. || ZAZb3 translation reads a toponym, 'from Tittiku'; the HT35 header reading 'disbursed' and the toponym remain rivals.

entries.meaning: which have been poured out—disbursed (derived-stem header); rival a heading name

cognates.Ugaritic: ntk to pour out, forth (base form TI-TI-KU)
cognates.Hebrew: hittiku they disbursed (2 Kgs 22:9, n-t-k Hiphil 3cp); paragogic nun: Job 19:2 (energic -nn- + 1cs -i)

entries.note: I- (relative or 3ms yi-) + TI-TI-KU (Nt-stem n-t-k pour out, nun assimilated to geminate /tt/) + -NI (energic nun suffix, Ug. yaqtulan(na)). HT96a context: section header on grain-allocation tablet listing PNs with GRA quantities. Base form TI-TI-KU independently attested (HT35). Amarna -ni on verbs is the 1cs object or dative suffix, often through the ventive -anni (Rainey 1996, I:72–74, II:264). The 'pour out' sense suits the liquids of HT35 better than the grain and figs of HT96a. One witness.

entries.meaning: gift

cognates.Hebrew: mattat 'gift' < *mattant (1 Kgs 13:7; Prov 25:14; Eccl 3:13; 5:18; Ezek 46:5, 11; HALOT 656)

entries.note: HT Zd 155 and HT Zd 157, each time right before A319 with no divider before MA; the cut rests on the ending the two graffiti share (Duhoux 1978, §29 A6). Heb. mattat 'gift' < *mattant, Ph. mtt (HALOT 656). MA-TI-TI writes the i-grade *mattint- > mattitt-, the final TI a dead vowel. WI-JA-SU on HT Zd 157 is likely the recipient's name. The rival √š-m-ṭ 'release' parse needs TI-TI to write a geminate.

entries.meaning: My kinsman knows (sentence name)
entries.note: Kinship-theophoric sentence name: ʿammī 'my kinsman (as divine epithet)' + dāʿ (√y-d-ʿ 'know'). Both elements independently productive—ʿammī- in ʿAmmîšaddāy (Num 1:12), ʿAmmînādāb (Exod 6:23), ʿAmmîhûd (Num 1:10), Amorite royal Ammi-ditana/Ammi-ṣaduqa; -dāʿ in ʾĂbîdāʿ and ʾEldāʿā (both Gen 25:4), ʾElyādāʿ (2 Sam 5:16), Ugaritic ydʿ attested as personal/divine name. The abī-/aḫī-/ʿammī- rotation (Abinadab, Ahinadab 1 Kgs 4:14, Amminadab—all on one base) makes ʿAmmī-dāʿ a predicted paradigm cell beside attested ʾĂbî-dāʿ. Initial ʿa- > A per guttural dropping; qty 1 on ZA10a among personal names. A-MI-DA-O (PH(?) 31b.5) is broken at the start, ]A-MI-DA-O (GORILA I 319), and is not counted. RIVAL: a Hurrian-layer name (cf. MI-TA). Cf. JA-DA-SU (yadaʿšu), same verbal root. Howard (JSS 68.1, 2023) tabulates the ʿAmmī+verb sentence-name template in the appendix (ʿAmmi-yepuʿ, kings of Talhayum, attested Mari/Terqa/Šeḥna), with ʾIli-yepaʿ at Alalah showing the first-element rotation in cuneiform.

entries.meaning: the Height (toponym of the Ramah/Ramoth type)
entries.note: Bare RU-MA-TA at HT29 (qty 2) and HT99b (qty 1, after SI+SE-NI); RU-MA-TA-SE on ZA20 (qty 3) beside DU-RE-ZA-SE: bare at home, -SE abroad. Every attestation carries a quantity: a recipient entry, not a header. √r-w-m 'to be high': *rūmat-, feminine noun of place. Hebrew toponyms רוּמָה Rûmâ (2 Kgs 23:36, the u-vowel form), אֲרוּמָה ʾĂrûmâ (Judg 9:41), רָמַת Rāmat (Josh 13:26), הָרָמָתָה hā-Rāmātâ (1 Sam 1:19), רָאמֹת Rāʾmōt (Josh 20:8); Ugaritic rm 'to go up'. Final -A is the written vowel. Aegean comparandum: LB o-ru-ma-to = *Orumanthos (PY Cn 3.6; ethnic o-ru-ma-si-ja-jo, PY An 519.12), cf. Ἐρύμανθος, a mountain; Linear A spelling hides a nasal before a stop, so RU-MA-TA may write *rumanth-. The three-consonant skeleton alone matches names no better than chance.

entries.meaning: man of Ušu (mainland Tyre)—origin-labeled worker
entries.note: Amarna {uru}Usu (ORACC qpn, 4 instances; EA 121 among them)—Ušu, the mainland twin of Tyre. Standard š→s merger; no other assumption required. Counted roster item (qty 1, within the KU-RO 10) on HT117a, where the reverse face independently labels personnel by origin (DI-KI-SE 'the Diktaian', HT117b) and U-DI-MI (ʾUdumī) sits seven lines below—an origin-labeling practice, Levantine workers on a Haghia Triada roster. The gentilic personnel practice answers the objection that a toponym cannot designate a roster person. Against 6 u-initial Amarna toponyms and 19 U-initial short word types in the corpus, the two matches fall on one tablet face. Dissolves the u- 'and' conjunctive reading of the HT117a U- words.

entries.meaning: the Udumite—man of Udum (Kirta's city)

cognates.Ugaritic: udm, a town, Kirta's city (DULAT 18); udmy 'Udumite' (DULAT 19)

entries.note: Toponym anchored twice: Ugaritic udm, Kirta's city (udm rbt 'Udum the great', KTU 1.14), and Amarna {uru}Udumu (ORACC qpn, city determinative). Weak point: the DI vowel—progressive echo, the primary dead-vowel rule, predicts U-DU-MI for the /dm/ cluster; DI requires the regressive rule outside its stated word-initial scope, or a real vowel mismatch if the Amarna medial /u/ is phonemic. The reading leans on its context: counted roster item (qty 1) beside the clean U-SU (ʾUšu, mainland Tyre), within the origin-labeling practice of HT117a/b (DI-KI-SE). A U-DU-MI variant in any join or re-reading would support this reading.

entries.meaning: flax, linseed—field-crop commodity
entries.note: Ug qṭ (I) 'flax' (DUL s.v.), n.m., attested 4× in KTU: 1.71, 1.72, 1.85 (hippiatric prescriptions—št bln qṭ, linseed ground with mixed fodder) and 2.36 (ḥwt qṭ 'the land of flax' beside ḥwt ugrt—a known crux, possibly Egypt). Wanderwort family *kito- 'flax/linen': Akk kitû, Aram kittānā, Sum gada, Gk χιτών; Ugaritic branch shows q for k. || *118 = ṭa, a speculative value, stands where the root demands the emphatic. || CONTEXT: KH10 (Khania grain ledger, GRA 10 … A-KI-PI-E-TE GRA 90); flax recorded beside grain matches Ugaritic field-crop practice, but the visible ideogram is GRA—the reading rides on the lexical match.

entries.meaning: attendant, lad (personnel designation on administrative sealings)
entries.note: Contingent on *86 = /na/, a proposed value. Reading: na-ro → naʿaru with guttural ʿayin elided per standard CV spelling rules. Cognate: Ugaritic nʿr "lad, attendant, apprentice" (personnel-class term in administrative/ration contexts), Hebrew naʿar נַעַר "youth, servant, attendant."
