Context: sole word on four Khania LMIB nodules, one scribe—administrative sealings. The two signs stand on different faces, *86 on face a and RO on face g, read together as *86-RO. Sister nodules at same site carry commodity designations (ZE "seed-grain" ×6, *301 "pastureland" ×3) and fractions, establishing the genre as category labels on sealed goods. Four identical attestations from one site = consistent administrative usage, not a rare personal name.

entries.meaning: She-of-the-Bull (feminine personal/divine name)
entries.cognates: PS *ṯawr- "bull, ox" (#269); Ug. ṯr/ṯrn "bull" (KTU deity epithet, PN element); Heb. שׁוֹר šōr "ox" (< *ṯawr with interdental→sibilant); Ar. ṯawr "bull"
entries.note: Feminine counterpart of ZU-RI-NI-MA (KN Zb 52, masculine with mimation). I- = prosthetic vowel (cf. I-DA-MA-TE vs DA-MA-TE); ZU-RI-NI = base *ṯawrīn-* (bull + relational -īn); -TA = feminine -t (replacing masculine -MA). Context on PH6: governed by A-RI = harrī "mountain of" (the "lion" flanking reading is circular support). Final -TA where the construct chain expects genitive -TI remains an open caveat: the gentilic family shows both -TA (HT25a, ZA8) and -TI (KHWc2005 kanaʿanītī), and divine names may stand diptotic/frozen. ZU = /ṯu/ (a proposed value). The masculine parallel, the A-RI context and the regular morphological pattern place it above SPECULATIVE.

entries.meaning: Dwelling/endurance of Anat (theophoric compound PN: √DWR + goddess ʿAnatu); rivals Egyptian Neith (Nt) as the second element, a simplex feminine name

cognates.Amorite: Dāra 'see DWR' (Gelb 1980); also Dāra as DN
cognates.Akkadian: dūru 'wall, fortress, city wall' (CAD D 196); dāru 'to last, endure' (CAD D 114)
cognates.Hebrew: דּוֹר dōr 'generation, period' (BDB 189); דּוּר dūr 'to dwell' (Aramaic, rare in BH)
cognates.Egyptian: Nt 'Neith' as the second element of personal names: sꜣ-nt, wsr-nt, rdj-nt, ḥtp-nt (PNM v6)

entries.note: HT98b .2 (Haghia Triada, tablet): recipient of K (1/10), after ]VIN ¾ and ]*188[ (GORILA I 161). Hapax. Both elements recur: DA-RU- in DA-RU-*329 (HT7b, a recipient of 2) and -NE-TE in KA-KU-NE-TE (ZA10b, a name list beside the Egyptian PA-JA-RE). Dāru-ʿAnēt needs an unwritten ʿa-, and I-NA-TA-I ʿInatī (IOZa6) writes Anat NA-TA; rival Egyptian Neith (Nt), the second element of sꜣ-nt 'son of Neith', wsr-nt 'Neith is strong', rdj-nt 'Neith gives', ḥtp-nt 'Neith is content' (PNM v6). First element Dāru: Amorite noun/DN (Gelb 1980), √DWR 'to turn, dwell, endure.' Akkadian dūru 'wall, fortress,' Hebrew dōr 'generation.' Second element -NE-TE = ʿAnēt(u), the goddess Anat (Huffmon 1965 APNM p. 200: Hanat/ʿAnat, well-attested NWS theophoric element). Amorite parallels: Ḥabdu-ᵈḤanat, Zikri-Ḥanat, ʿAbdi-ʿAnati, Šūm-ʿAnati. Phoenician: ʿBDʿNT. Alternative parse: Dārunēt as simple feminine (√DWR + -at feminine suffix with epenthetic -n-), 'she who endures.' Theophoric compound preferred: (1) 4-syllable name in accounting list, (2) -NE-TE may be compared with the CANDIDATE I-NA-TA-I = ʿInatī at IOZa6, (3) element + DN is the productive Amorite pattern.

entries.meaning: Weapon of Anat (theophoric compound PN: kakkum 'weapon' + goddess ʿAnatu)

cognates.Akkadian: kakkum (kakku) 'weapon, arms' (CAD K 52); also DN Kakka
cognates.Amorite: kakka 'weapon' (Gelb 1980); KAKKAR-I (PN)
cognates.Hebrew: כְּלִי kĕlî 'weapon, vessel' (different root, but same semantic field)
cognates.Ugaritic: ʿnt bnʿmt 'Anat of the peoples' — Anat as warrior-goddess

entries.note: ZA10b (Zakros, tablet): name-list position among 10+ names with quantities, co-occurs with PA-JA-RE (Payare, Egyptian theophoric) and DU (relative pronoun). First element Kakku: Akkadian kakkum 'weapon' (CAD K 52), also a divine name Kakka (Gelb 1980: 'kakkum, fem. kakka "weapon"; cf. also Kakka, DN'). Amorite KAKKAR-I attested as PN. Second element -NE-TE = ʿAnēt(u), the goddess Anat. Anat as warrior-goddess is iconographically associated with weapons at Ugarit and in Egyptian sources (Papyrus Chester Beatty VII: 'Anat, the victorious goddess, the woman who acts as a warrior'). 'Weapon of Anat' fits the martial divine epithet tradition. Alternative parse: Kakkun-ēt as simple feminine, 'little weapon' or 'weaponess.' Theophoric compound preferred for same reasons as DA-RU-NE-TE.

entries.meaning: the wool (substrate commodity noun with Semitic mimation)

cognates.Greek: μαλλός (mallos) 'flock of wool' < Minoan /maru/ (Salgarella 2022; Nosch & Weilhartner 2026)
cognates.Linear A: A559 = MA+RU composite wool logogram (*146 Raison-Pope)

entries.note: HT 24a writes the word with the wool ligature MA+RU (A559) followed by ME (GORILA I 43): .2 MA+RU-ME 10, .3 MA+RU-MẸ 6, .4 PA-SA-RI-JA · MA+RU-MẸ[, broken after ME. The ligature is the logogram MARU 'wool' (Salgarella 2022, Mix and Match; Nosch & Weilhartner 2026), the Minoan wool word /maru/ that passed into Greek as μαλλός, and -ME adds mimation, the spelling convention of JA-SA-SA-RA-ME = yaššaram. The two complete entries carry quantities (10, 6) under two section headings, a commodity distribution, not a personal name. Mimation doublet with syllabic MA-RU (HT117a). Context: wool allocations under the Kubaba-adjective heading KU-PA₃-RI-JA, cf. the Knossos Linear B wool series for religious dependents.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'the Protector heals' (√r-p-ʾ + √ḏ-m-r)

cognates.Amorite: RIPʾ-I+DN names, RI-IP-I-D-DA-GAN, RI-IP-E-D-IM (Gelb 1980, nos. 5272, 5287–5293); IR-PA-D-IM (no. 3757); ḍimrum 'protection', DIMR- names

entries.note: PE 2: RU-PI-*305-MI 1⅛, after a broken line, followed by A-*325-ZA, A-RI-PA, QA-QA-DA, TO-ME, TO-*49-RE. RU-PI is the Amorite RIPʾ- 'heal' name element (Gelb 1980, nos. 5272, 5287–5293). *305-MI read ḏa-mi(r), √ḏ-m-r 'protect', final r unwritten. Amorite has DIMR- only as a first element. Weak point: *305 = ḏa is speculative; with da, *305-MI is DA-MI. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Kikkina, recipient or named administrative entity

cognates.Amorite: KIKKIN-I (KI-IK-KI-NI), KIKKIN-U (KI-IK-KI-NU), KIKKIN-UM (KI-IK-KI-NUM), with KI-KI-NU-UM and KI-IK-KI-NI-IM variants
cognates.Ugaritic: kkn, personal name of uncertain etymology; distinct kknt 'pot/vessel' has final -t

entries.note: HT88 places KI-KI-NA after the NI fig logogram and before the quantity 7, favoring a recipient, group, or other named entity. Gelb's Amorite onomasticon repeatedly writes the close KIKKIN name as KI-IK-KI-NI, KI-IK-KI-NU and KI-(IK)-KI-NU-UM. The former vessel comparison is rejected: the Ugaritic word is kknt, with final -t, and Huehnergard notes that it may be an error for kkbt. Ugaritic kkn is instead catalogued as a personal name of uncertain etymology. Translate 'figs—Kikkina(?), 7,' not 'seven pots.'

entries.meaning: box, chest, basket (container or unit)

cognates.Akkadian: quppatu 'box, basket'; quppu A 'wicker basket or wooden chest' (CAD Q 307)

entries.note: HT 6a, after DA-QE-RA: QE-PI-TA 22¾, counted in quarters, a container or unit. Ug. qpt 'box, chest, basket' (DULAT 696); Akk. quppatu, quppu (CAD Q 307). Weak point: QE-PI for the u-a of quppatu. One attestation.

entries.meaning: waitress, girl (?) (DULAT p.886; Hurro-Hittite loan from šiduri 'girl, young woman')
entries.note: Exact interdental skeleton. Two roundels in the HTWc series (HTWc3011, HTWc3012) (administrative genre). Dual reading: common noun 'waitress/girl' OR Hurrian feminine PN Šiduri (see onomasticon entry). Contact layer—word is a Hurro-Hittite loan into Ugaritic (Laroche GLH 229, CAD Š/2 408); reaches Crete via Hurrian or Ugaritic channel. DULAT's own gloss carries '(?)'—marginality at Ugarit (2 attestations, both Hurrian-context texts). The Ashtart rival fails on orthographic grounds.

entries.meaning: righteous one (PN)
entries.note: SA=ṣ, KA=q via emphatic neutralization. Amorite PN şadaqa (√ṣ-d-q). Mallia roundels, administrative grain context. Cf. Zadok, Zedekiah, Melchizedek. The initial A- needs a prothetic vowel. Rival: Hurrian aštaga 'woman', the diminutive in -(a)ga of ašte 'woman' (Wilhelm, "Hurrian," 103; Laroche 1980, 61–62), written aš-ta-ka (Meskene) and aš-da-a-ga-bi (KUB XXIX 8 IV 23): coda š with a dead A, as A-SA-MU-NE, accounts for every sign.

entries.meaning: personal name, ʾAmar- 'he has spoken, seen' with -ānu

cognates.Amorite: ʾAMAR+ʾIL-I (Gelb AS 21 no. 408); ʾAMAR-A+HADD-U, ʾAMAR-U (nos. 720, 724); ʾMR 'to see, to command, to speak' (p. 14)

entries.note: SK Zb 1, a clay vessel from Skhinia, the word alone. A-MA-RA-NE writes ʾAmarānu, the ʾAmar- names of Amorite (ʾAMAR-ʾILI, ʾAMAR-ADDU, ʾAMAR-U; Gelb AS 21 nos. 408, 720, 724) with -ānu. Weak point: the final E. Rival: marʾānu 'lordly one' (PS *marʾ-), with A- unexplained. One attestation.

entries.meaning: and the bahaq-rash (wa- + pan-Semitic skin-disease noun—rubric disease name)
entries.note: Egyptian group-writing: wbqy [rubric element 4, Akulov 2023, 3], disease determinative; Kyriakidis reads final sign as l (w-b-ql), Steiner w-b-qi(?). Read as wa- 'and' + *b(u)haq-ī: SED #135 *bahaḳ- '(kind of) skin disease'—Heb bōhaq 'tetter' (Lev 13:39), JAram bōhăqā, Syr behqītā 'scabies', Mandaic baqiata 'decay, gangrene' (h-less, precedent for unwritten h here), Arab bahaq (still clinical for vitiligo), Mehri/Harsusi/Jibbali white-patch terms, Tigre bähaq 'blisters'. Names a skin disease beside samāwnā (Akk sāmānu 'the red one') in a skin-disease papyrus. Rivals: Arabic-only √w-b-q 'perish' (Q 18:52, 42:34—'the Perdition'); Akulov's Eg. wbnw 'wound' (n→q unexplained). Kyriakidis 2002, 215: 'the combination wbq may suggest a Semitic language'. Steiner left unread. Weak points: unwritten medial h; the final sign is disputed.

entries.meaning: the śĕʾēt-mark (skin-disease term—rubric disease name)
entries.note: Egyptian group-writing: s3t [rubric element 5, Akulov 2023, 3]; final loaf sign is the Egyptian word t(i) 'bread' used phonetically (Kyriakidis 2002 n. 15, Helck's whole-word principle)—no semantic determinative from it; Akulov 2023 alone adds land + plurality dets (not in Steiner or Kyriakidis). Orthography s-ꜣ-t writes ś-ʾ-t with the aleph: Heb שְׂאֵת śĕʾēt, technical skin-disease term (Lev 13:2, 10, 19, 28, 43; 14:56)—rabbis 'swelling' (< nāśāʾ 'lift', Sipra; b. Šebu. 6b), Tgs 'mark/prominent spot', Milgrom (AB Leviticus, 773) 'discoloration'. Root √n-ś-ʾ pan-Semitic (Ug nšʾ, Akk našû, Arab nasaʾa, Gz naśʾa); the noun is Hebrew-technical. With WBQY, the rubric names the disease in Lev 13 diagnostic vocabulary (śĕʾēt 13:2 + bōhaq 13:39). Rival: Eg. s3tw 'soil' (Akulov 2023, 4—favored if the land determinative is genuine). Steiner left unread.

entries.meaning: the dwelling, abode (sanctuary as divine habitation)

cognates.Amorite: nawûm 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)' (Huffmon, APNM 237)
cognates.Hebrew: nāweh (נָוֶה) 'habitation, pasture-land; temple, shrine' (Exod 15:13 אֶל־נְוֵה קׇדְשֶׁךָ)

entries.note: The nominal core of the libation formula: A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA = ʾata-i-nawa-ya 'I make myself a dwelling' (CONFIRMED, 11× at five peak sanctuaries) conjugates this noun, and *301-WA = nawā (PROBABLE, IOZa4) writes it with the rebus sign *301 = /na/ that derives from this very root. PH6 (MM IIB) spells it phonetically with plain NA—the tablet predates the *301 rebus convention, making this the earliest witness of √n-w-y in the corpus. ʾi- = prosthetic vowel (cf. I-ZU-RI-NI-TA, I-DA-MA-TE vs DA-MA-TE). Set off by word-divider 𐄁 as heading of the PH6 dedication.

entries.meaning: mountain of (construct state before divine names)

cognates.Hebrew: har (הַר) 'mountain' (< *harr-); construct har- as in har Sinai, har Tsiyyon

entries.note: Initial h- carried by plain vowel sign per guttural-carrier convention; genitive -ī as the construct chain requires (nawā harrī DN 'dwelling of the mountain of DN'). harrī is preferred over ʿalē 'upon, for' and ʾarī 'lion': the A-RA/A-RI/A-RU full u/i/a triple argues nominal inflection against a frozen preposition, and the house dative is la- (RE/RA). A higher tier needs an undamaged A-RI + established toponym, identification of RU-DI (HT141, damaged context [...] 1 A-RI RU-DI [...]), or governed -TA proper-name parallels. PH28a (same site and period) has A-RI-JA-[, broken after JA.

entries.meaning: Ida, in righteousness (toponym + prepositional phrase written as one word)
entries.note: Segmentation: I-DA (Mount Ida, PROBABLE) + PA₃-I-SA-RI = bi-ʾišarī 'in righteousness'—the b= proclitic spelled with PA₃ = /ba/ (dead vowel), medial I carrying the ʾ of ʾišar-, and genitive -ī after the preposition exactly as la-piṭrī (PKZa11). Same √y-š-r as the formula's yaššaram (JA-SA-SA-RA-ME, CONFIRMED)—PH6 renders the concept with b= + genitive where the LM I vessels use the adverbial accusative with mimation. Components entered separately: I-DA (PH6 added to attestations), PA₃ (b= proclitic), I-SA-RI (ʾišarī).

entries.meaning: uprightness, righteousness (genitive after the b= proclitic)
entries.note: Attested only within I-DA-PA₃-I-SA-RI (PH6), following the b= proclitic; the medial I carries the ʾ of ʾišar-, and the final -ī is the genitive a preposition governs (cf. la-piṭrī, PKZa11). Same √y-š-r as the formula's yaššaram (JA-SA-SA-RA-ME, CONFIRMED)—PH6 renders 'in righteousness' with b= + genitive where the LM I vessels use the adverbial accusative with mimation. Nominal shape closest to Akk. išaru.

entries.meaning: in, with, by; on HT103 perhaps administrative ‘in the charge of’

cognates.Phoenician: b 'in, from'; bd ‘in the charge of’

entries.note: A single-consonant proclitic cannot be written bare in a CV syllabary: PA₃ = /ba/ spends its vowel slot as a dead vowel, the reconstruction following PS/Ug. bi=. The damaged APZa2 sequence ]PI-MI-NA-TE does not independently establish PI = bī. The prepositional value rests chiefly on PH6 I-DA-PA₃-I-SA-RI = ʾIdā bi-ʾišarī. On HT9b PA₃ stands between dividers before WA-JA-PI, a transaction sign like TE in the HT9a heading, and is no witness. If PA₃ is independent on HT103, its position before a probable personal name and quantity has a close administrative parallel in Ugaritic/Phoenician bd /bādi/ or /bīdi/ ‘in the charge/custody of’ (< *bi-yadi): Kition no. 84 repeats bd + personal name + counted workmen (Krahmalkov 2000, 97), and CAT 4.145:9–10 uses bd rb hršm ‘in the custody of the chief of the craftsmen’ (Huehnergard 2012, 76, 94). Akkadian likewise writes ša qāti ‘in the charge of’ with the single logogram NĪG.ŠU before personal names (Huehnergard 1997, 276). PA₃ could therefore be ordinary b- ‘in/by’ or a local administrative shorthand for bād(i), but no Semitic source yet proves the abbreviation bd > b, and the standard Linear B coda-omission rule does not cover final /d/. Linear B pa-ro + personal name ‘in whose care/in the charge of’ supplies a functional Aegean parallel (Killen 2024, 103). Other standalone PA₃ tokens need not share this function.
entries.root_meaning: in, with, by (PS proclitic preposition bi=)

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Wool' (substrate maru 'wool')
entries.note: Bare form of the mimation doublet MA-RU/MA+RU-ME (HT24a 'the wool'). On HT117a one of ten entries counted 1 each under MA-KA-RI-TE 'merchants' (KU-RO 10), between KU-RA-MU (Kurmu) and KU-PA₃-NU (Kubānu): a name on the noun, as Tēnā 'Fig' (TE-*301). Linear B ma-ro-ne, a man's name in the dative, receives oil at KN Fh 347 (DMic s.v.). The wool word is anchored by logogram A559 = MA+RU composite (Salgarella 2022; Nosch & Weilhartner 2026), source of Greek μαλλός.

entries.meaning: Kulelu (personal name; cf. Middle Assyrian Kulilu)

cognates.Middle Assyrian: Kulilu, written {m}ki-li-lu, T 98-038 obv. 4', Dunni-Aššur/Tell Sabi Abyad (ORACC P532066)
cognates.Amorite: KU-LA-IL-E and KI+L-I+IL (secondary k-l-l name-family comparisons; Gelb, AS 21 nos. 4114, 4065–66)

entries.note: The HT117b roster fixes the personal-name slot; KU-RE-JU also takes quantity 8 on HT39. With R/L neutralization and JU=/lu/, the spelling permits /Kulelu/. The strongest external formal parallel is the Middle Assyrian personal name Kulilu, written {m}ki-li-lu at Dunni-Aššur (Tell Sabi Abyad), T 98-038 obv. 4' (ORACC tcma/tsa1, P532066). The later personal name Kullulu is written {1}ku-lu-lu in SAA 6 22 rev. 9'. Amorite KU-LA-IL-E and KI+L-I+IL provide secondary k-l-l name-family comparisons, but neither the root nor the meaning 'El is perfection' is established for the Linear A name. Rival: kᵉlûlâ 'betrothal, being a bride' (HALOT; Jer 2:2), as the pair of *21F-TU-NE 'bridegroom' on HT 117b; the quantity 8 on HT 39 and DI-KI-SE, a name in the same layout, favour a name. Both readings take JU = /lu/.

entries.meaning: Dūmatī (personal name—'the Enduring One', √dwm hypocoristic)

cognates.Amorite: Dūmat-An (DU-MA-TA-AN), Gelb AS 21 no. 1581—u-vocalized dūmat- name element
cognates.Hebrew: דּוּמָה Dūmāh, Ishmaelite eponym (Gen 25:14); cf. Dūmat al-Jandal
cognates.Arabian: dmt / dwmt / dymt / dwmn name cluster under dm 'enduring' (Harding 1971, p. 242)
cognates.Sabaic: dwm 'lasting, permanent'; dwmm 'forever' (Beeston 1982, p. 36; Biella 1982, p. 81)

entries.note: Third-slot recipient on HT19, the same-scribe minimal pair of HT17 whose identical slot holds Siddāru (SI-DA-RE, HT122a roster control)—name for name across the sister tablets. Spelling is the cleanest on offer: first vowel etymological (ū of √dwm), ME a dead vowel, -DI = /tī/ one voicing step in the post-nasal cluster. Cross-Semitic dūmat- name family: Amorite Dūmat-An (DU-MA-TA-AN, Gelb AS 21 no. 1581, Mari XIV 47:19—vocalization cuneiform-explicit), Hebrew Dūmāh the Ishmaelite eponym (Gen 25:14), Harding p. 242 cluster dmt/dwmt/dymt/dwmn under dm 'enduring', Sabaic dwm 'lasting, permanent' productive (Beeston p. 36, Biella p. 81). -ī hypocoristic per QA-*310-I = qaynī. Rival: Dimtu-oblique 'the Tower-estate' (DE-ME-TE is no support: HT 94b reads RA-[?]-DE-ME-TE, one word with a sign lost after RA), on Ug. dmt 'tower' + dmt toponym (DULAT 272), Akk. dimtum 'tower; fortified settlement, district' (Huehnergard GAk), and CAD D s.v. dimtu confirms the voiced by-form dindu alongside dintu (pp. 144-147; dindu BBSt No. 8 i 27 + NB Elam toponyms)—so the rival's -DI spelling is orthographically regular, not a strike against it; it would lead if a second dmt-form turns up in a heading/destination slot. OSA ḍmd 'friend' is an exact skeleton match too.

entries.meaning: ʿAttiru (divine name ʿAṯtar, assimilated—or theophoric ʿAttirī 'man of ʿAṯtar')

cognates.Amorite: Aštar divine element (Gelb AS 21; cuneiform š for /ṯ/); assimilated Attar in [A]t-ta-ri-ša-du-u[q] (Huffmon 1965, 173)
cognates.Sabaic: ʿṯtr, chief deity of the South Arabian pantheon

entries.note: ZA4a (Zakros tablet) roster slot, 4 units, directly before the personal name JA-PA. PS ʿAṯtar- with ṯt→tt assimilation, as in Amorite [A]t-ta-ri-ša-du-u[q] (Huffmon 1965, 173: "perhaps an assimilated form representing *Attar"); geminate unwritten, ʿayin on the plain vowel sign. NOT *ʿAštar-: the ṯ→š merger is post-Bronze Canaanite. Second-syllable i has in-family precedent (Akk. Ištar, Ebla Išdar) or marks the nisbe ʿAttirī, which the roster slot favors. Rival: ʿatīru 'entreated' (√ʿ-t-r; Gen 25:21 wayyēʿāter), which fits a-ti-ru as written.

entries.meaning: with, at (comitative preposition); IOZa12 possibly ʔittī 'with me'
entries.note: Comitative preposition < PS *ʔin-t- 'with, at, via' (Huehnergard 2019 §3.6), extended form of *ʔin. CV fit exact: n-assimilation (*ʔinti > ʔitti) orthographically invisible, geminate written single, glottal onset carried by the bare vowel sign || HT25b: WI-TE-RO 𐄁 I-TI VIR 28 / VIR 24 / KU-RO 52 (28+24=52 exact)—I-TI marks only the first personnel entry, matching Akkadian ledger itti 'with, including' flagging an included subgroup; rival reading: personal name (NAME VIR n roster syntax) || IOZa12: ]𐄁 ]𐄁 JA-SA-SA-RA-ME 𐄁 I-TI[—word divider rules out a suffix parse; either bare ʔitt- 'with' (complement lost in the lacuna after I-TI) or suffixed ʔittī 'with me' (Heb. ʔittī; formula word + 'with'+suffix predication, the ʕimmānû-ʔēl construction type) || Isogloss note: Ugaritic prefers ʕm 'with'; ʔitt- sits on the Akkadian/Canaanite side—retention of a form Huehnergard reconstructs to PS itself, a peripheral archaism, not a borrowing marker

entries.meaning: may you (f.) answer us (N-stem of √ʿ-n-y in the TA-NA-[X]-U-TI-NU frame: 2fs prefix + indicative -u + subject clitic -tī + 1cp object -n)
entries.cognates: Hebrew עָנָה (ʿānāh) 'answer'; Ugaritic ʿny 'answer'; Amarna Canaanite ʿ-n-y forms
entries.note: Paradigm entry for the √ʿ-n-y verbal family (*301=NA writes the proposed N-stem marker + root); conjugations are recorded here, not as separate entries. Members: TA-NA-I-*301-(TI/E) (PSZa2, CANDIDATE; the last sign is an uncertain TI in GORILA, E in Ferrara, Montecchi, and Valério 2022, 87) = if TI, 'may you (f.) answer'; if E, 'may she/you answer'; A-TA-I-*301-DE-KA (ZAZb3, PROBABLE) = 'who-answered-for-you'. Template parallel: TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU (IOZa2, √r-ṣ-y)—same TA+NA+ROOT+U-TI-NU frame with the root slot swapped. Ugaritic tʿnyn /taʿniyūna/ (KTU 1.23:12) supports the root and a t-…-n profile, not the segmentation. On IOZa6 the proposed 2fs verb addresses and puns on the following theonym I-NA-TA-I (ʿInatī, 'my Anat'). Position 1 of the IOZa6 libation formula.

entries.meaning: in, at (preposition)
entries.cognates: Hebrew בְּ- (bə-); Ugaritic b-; Amarna Canaanite bi-; Phoenician b-
entries.note: Possible standalone spelling of the b- preposition (PA₃ = /ba~be/ + E); cf. Hebrew bə-, Ugaritic b-, Amarna bi-. A divider follows PA₃-E on PKZa8, whereas the Semitic preposition is normally proclitic, and the following group is presently read as the vocative yā Diqqite. The exact syntax is therefore unresolved; translate only as fragmentary 'in/at …' rather than joining it confidently to Dikte.

entries.meaning: personal name ʿAnānu; rival Ḥanānu
entries.cognates: Hebrew עָנָן (ʿānān) 'cloud'; biblical PN עָנָן (ʿĀnān, Neh 10:27; HALOT 858); Amorite A-NA-NU-UM-DINGIR (Gelb 1980, no. 476a), written as A-NA-NU; PS *ʿanan-; rival: Amorite Ḥanan-a, Ḥanan-at-um, Ḥanan-im (Gelb, AS 21, nos. 475–478), biblical PN חָנָן (Ḥānān, Neh 10:27; HALOT 335)
entries.note: Owner/recipient name on a painted pithos, base of A-NA-NU-SI-JA-SE (HTZb159)—the 'cloud' substantive is the etymology, not the function. -SI-JA-SE is the vessel-label adjectival formation shared with KI-TA-NA-SI-JA-SE (PEZb3). Amorite A-NA-NU-UM-DINGIR (Gelb 1980, no. 476a) has the same spelling; cuneiform does not tell ʿ from ḥ. Rival: Ḥanānu, √ḥ-n-n 'be gracious'; Amorite Ḥanan- (Gelb, AS 21, nos. 475–478), and Neh 10:27 names Ḥānān beside ʿĀnān.

entries.meaning: In the charge of Našūka ('the Bitten one')—custody formula + personal name on a sealed receipt

cognates.Ugaritic: bd 'in the hand, charge of' (< bi-yadi) (Huehnergard 2012, glossary); nṯk (I) 'biter' (DULAT 643)
cognates.Akkadian: ina qāt 'in the charge of' (functional parallel); našāku 'to bite' (CAD N/2 53)

entries.note: HT Wc 3010, a roundel: *333-DI-NA-SU-KA alone. With *333 = bi, bīdi 'in the charge of' (Ug. bd < bi-yadi, the custody preposition of administrative receipts) + Našūka, qatūl of √n-š-k, 'the Bitten one'; cf. the serpent names Naḥash (1 Sam 11:1) and Naḥshon. Pair of HT Wc 3009 *333-DI-SU-KA: the same frame, another name. Weak points: *333 = bi rests on its three words; -KA where the genitive wants -ki. Rival: the whole group a personal name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: In the charge of Sūka—custody formula + personal name on a sealed receipt

cognates.Ugaritic: bd 'in the hand, charge of' (< bi-yadi) (Huehnergard 2012, glossary)

entries.note: HT Wc 3009, a roundel: *333-DI-SU-KA *188. With *333 = bi, bīdi 'in the charge of' (Ug. bd) + Sūka, a name without a secure etymology. Pair of HT Wc 3010 *333-DI-NA-SU-KA. Weak point: *333 = bi rests on its three words. Rival: the whole group a personal name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Balsam, perfume—aromatic personal name (cf. Basemath) on a metal ornament
entries.note: MO Zf 1, a metal ornament from Mokhlos, the word alone. With *333 = bi, *333-SA-MU writes biśāmu 'balsam', before the Canaanite shift of ā (Heb. bōśem); a name of the aromatic class, cf. Basemath (Gen 26:34). Weak point: *333 = bi is a working value. Rival: a label for the object, or a non-Semitic name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: may that which goes out glorify—volitive yaqtula √p-ʾ-r + √y-ṣ-ʾ participle/imperfect (the outpoured libation as subject)
entries.cognates: Hebrew פָּאַר (pāʾar) "glorify, beautify" (Isa 60:7, 13; hitpaʿel Isa 60:21, 61:3), פְּאֵר (pəʾēr) "diadem, headdress", תִּפְאֶרֶת (tipʾart) "beauty, splendor"; Akkadian apāru "to cap, crown" (CAD A/2 166–67; āpirat agê bēlūti of Ištar, STC 2 75:7); Hebrew יָצָא/יֹצֵא (yāṣāʾ/yōṣē) "go out"; Akkadian (w)aṣû "go out", ṣītu "outflow, disbursement"
entries.note: The Syme sanctuary's one otherwise unread word (first edition, transcription only: Muhly & Olivier 2008, 212–13, HM 5585, found 1987—no prior semantic interpretation). Segmentation JA-PA-RA | JA-SE: two words, every morpheme attested elsewhere in the lexicon. (1) JA-PA-RA = yapʾara, ya- 3ms prefix conjugation + √p-ʾ-r with unwritten ʾ—spelling parallel JA-PA-QA = yapqaḥ (PKZa11/12, three signs write y-p-q-ḥ). Final -A = volitive yaqtula, apt in prayer. (2) JA-SE = yāṣē, identical to the yāṣē of SI-JA-SE (šī-yāṣē "which goes out", HTZb159/PEZb3)—administrative disbursement marker there, the outpoured libation here. || Verb-first NWS syntax: "may that which is poured out glorify (her)"—cf. Isa 60:13 לְפָאֵר מְקוֹם מִקְדָּשִׁי "to beautify the place of my sanctuary"; hitpaʿel liturgical register Isa 60:21, 61:3; Ben Sira 50:20 (MS B) ובשם ייי התפאר. || Rivals: Ugaritic pʿr "proclaim (a name)" (ypʿr šmthm, KTU 1.2 IV 11, 18) is orthographically identical (ʿ drops like ʾ) but attested only with šm "name" as complement, absent here; PS *wpr "pilgrimage" has a nominal gloss, no attested denominal verb, and an initial-w assimilation problem. || A hapax: √p-ʾ-r has no second corpus attestation yet. Support comes from yāṣē (×2 sites) and the ya- prefix paradigm. || √p-ʾ-r also gives pəʾēr "diadem" and tipʾart "splendor".
entries.root_meaning: to glorify, beautify, adorn + to go out

entries.meaning: may he/it glorify, adorn (3ms volitive yaqtula √p-ʾ-r; guttural ʾ unwritten)
entries.cognates: Hebrew פָּאַר (pāʾar) "glorify, beautify", פְּאֵר (pəʾēr) "diadem" (Exod 39:28; Isa 61:3), תִּפְאֶרֶת (tipʾart) "beauty, splendor"; Akkadian apāru "to cap, crown"—metathesis sibling (BDB s.v. פְּאֵר compares Assyrian ipru, ēpartu; inner-Hebrew doublet אֲפֵר ʾăpēr "headband", 1 Kgs 20:38, 41)
entries.note: Component of JA-PA-RA-JA-SE (SYZa9)—see that entry; not attested standalone. Spelling parallel: JA-PA-QA = yapqaḥ (PKZa11/12), same ya- + p-initial root with dropped guttural.
entries.root_meaning: to glorify, beautify, adorn; nominal: diadem, headdress

entries.meaning: that which goes out, it goes out (3ms imperfect/participle √y-ṣ-ʾ with ʾaleph-III loss)
entries.cognates: Hebrew יָצָא (yāṣāʾ) "go out", participle יֹצֵא (yōṣē); Ugaritic √yṣʾ "go out, appear"; Akkadian (w)aṣû "go out", ṣītu "expenditure, outflow"
entries.note: Component morpheme, broken out on its second compound attestation: within SI-JA-SE = šī-yāṣē "which goes out" (HTZb159, PEZb3—disbursement marker on jar labels) and now bare within JA-PA-RA-JA-SE (SYZa9—the libation as "that which goes out" of the vessel). Same two signs, same reading, two genres: what administration marks as outgoing goods, liturgy pours as the outgoing libation. Cf. Hebrew אֲשֶׁר־יֵצֵא (2 Kgs 12:13, Temple expenditure) for the administrative use; the cultic use has no direct biblical parallel—the poured offering as grammatical subject is Minoan.

entries.meaning: 'The Requested One'—votive birth-name from √ʾ-r-š "to request, desire" + hypocoristic -ān; the child asked of the goddess, the name a receipt

cognates.Amorite: ARIŠ-AN (Gelb AS 21 §6 Index of Names no. 2190), ARIŠ-AN-U no. 2191 (frozen -u), A-ru-si-AN (Huffmon APNM p. 22), Ḥa-ri-ša-an—all within d 0.1
cognates.Ugaritic: ʾrš 'to request, wish, demand, claim' (CUC); irš 'demand' (DULAT)
cognates.Akkadian: erēšu 'to request'—the Erišti-DN class ('Requested-of-DN', e.g. Erišti-Aya) among the commonest OB female names
cognates.Safaitic: ʾrš ×12 + ʾršt ×11 + ʾršn—the exact shape ʾAriš-ān (Harding 1971 p. 37)
cognates.Hebrew: ʾărešet 'request' (Ps 21:3, hapax); naming-motif parallel Šāʾûl 'Asked-For' and Hannah's Samuel etymology (1 Sam 1:20)

entries.note: Sole word on THEZb2, an Akrotiri clay vessel—the owner/dedicant slot. Weak points: hapax; final -a where ARIŠ-AN-U freezes -u (the Yarīmān -ē caveat); RE = /ri/ by the routine e/i wobble. A votive Semitic name on a Theran vessel.

entries.meaning: O Beloved!—vocative of the reduplicative divine epithet (with i- prosthesis)

cognates.Amorite: dad- 'favorite' (Huffmon 1965, 181); dādum 'beloved' (Gelb 1980)

entries.note: CR Zg 4: I-DA-DA, with A-RO-TE on line 2. Cf. Ugaritic dd 'loved one', ydd 'beloved'; Amorite dad- 'favorite' (Huffmon 1965, 181). The IO Za 11 DA-DA parallel fails: IO Za 11 reads ]NA-[·]-DA-DA[ as one broken group (Karetsou, Godart & Olivier, Kadmos 24, 1985, 142). Weak point: dād- has no initial cluster to call for a prosthetic I-. Rival: a personal name.

entries.meaning: Salvation—votive exclamation/dedication term
entries.note: Cross-site paradigm JA-SI (KNZb4, PEZc4) ~ JA-SI-E (KEZb4 lamp dedication) + the JA- vocative frame. On KNZb4 read inside the votive frame JU 𐄁 JA-SI 𐄁 SI = l(u) 'for' + yašīʕ + šay 'tribute' (JU votive arm); on PEZc4 paired with A-JA: 'Life! — he saves!'.

entries.meaning: townsmen, citizens (heading before the logogram for men); rival Semitic nātîn 'those given'

cognates.Egyptian: nʾ.tjw 'townsmen; citizens', nisbe of nʾ.t 'town' (AED lemma 81110; Wb 2, 213.1–4); as a personal name Nʾ.tjw (RPN I 169.6)

entries.note: HT 84 *21F-JA-DU / NU-TI · VIR+[?], whole, a heading directly before the logogram for men; ZA 9 ]-NU-TI ·, broken before NU, heads an allocation list (RA, ]RO-SI-RA, A-TA-NA-[·], [·]-MA-JU, WI-RA-RE-MI-TE with QI+SI and *21F). Egyptian nʾ.tjw 'townsmen; citizens' (AED lemma 81110; Wb 2, 213.1–4), n-w-t consonant for consonant, as PA-JA-RE and JA-MI-DA-RE stand on Haghia Triada lists. Rival: √n-t-n 'those given', Ugaritic ytnm 'temple slaves' (DULAT 977), Aramaic nātîn 'temple servant', which needs a final -n unwritten and mismatches the first vowel. Ugaritic únt 'corvée' would be spelled U-NU-TI.

entries.meaning: O Salvation—vocative/petitionary extension of yašīʿ
entries.note: KEZb4 (Kea lamp): single-word lamp dedication. Completes the three-member mini-paradigm with JA-SI (KNZb4 'Salvation' dedication term, PEZc4 'he saves')—same √y-š-ʿ across three sites, Rendsburg paradigm criterion. JA- vocative frame established (JA-DI-KI-TU 'O Diktu!' PROBABLE, IOZa2). Phonology rule-standard: š→S-class, final ʿ dropped. Open morphological question: the -E extension (vocative/petitionary?) vs bare JA-SI—recorded, not resolved.

entries.meaning: the Tylissian (f.): provenance label on a jar

cognates.Hebrew: ha-kkĕnaʿănît 'the Canaanite (woman)' (Gen 46:10; Exod 6:15; 1 Chr 2:3), ha-mmôʾābît (2 Chr 24:26): article + feminine gentilic -ît
cognates.Ugaritic: ḫtyt GN f. 'Hittite', hmš ddm l ḫtyt 'five cauldronsful for the Hittite (people?)', KTU 4.269:3 (DULAT 409); kd (I) n. f. 'jar' (DULAT 424)
cognates.Amorite: GUBL-AJIT-UM, Gu-ub-la-ji-tum 'the Byblian (woman)' (Gelb 1980, no. 1795)
cognates.Linear B: tu-ri-so Tylissos (KN Ce 59, Da, Db, Dd, Dh); ethnic tu-ri-si-jo (KN E 668, Og 833), fem. tu-ri-si-ja (KN Lc 533)

entries.note: KN Zb 5, a clay vessel (MM IIIB), the single word A-TU-RI-SI-TI ·. Pre-Greek Turis- (LB tu-ri-so, Tylissos) with the NWS article ha- (h dropped to A, as A-KI-DA-RO) and the feminine gentilic -īt, as KA-NA-NI-TI kanaʿanītī. The feminine agrees with the jar (Ug. kd n. f., KA-DI kadd): a provenance label of the SU-KI-RI-TE-I-JA genre. Linear B writes the same feminine ethnic with Greek -ia, tu-ri-si-ja. A Semitic formation on a pre-Greek stem.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'hidden one' (?)
entries.note: HT 117a: TU-JU-MA 1 in the roster under MA-KA-RI-TE, 'merchants'. √ʿ-l-m 'to hide', ʿ unwritten, with JU = /lu/. Rival: √t-l-m, Heb. telem 'furrow' (HALOT 1740). One attestation.

entries.meaning: fire offering(s)
entries.note: KH9 MI I-SI CYP+D ½ 2 (cyperus); PYRWc4 roundel TI (figs) I-SI. Hebrew ʾiššeh 'offering by fire' (BDB; H0801). /i/-vocalized counterpart of A-SE ʾaššē; the two spellings do not share a site (A-SE: HT, ZA; I-SI: KH, PYR). One-consonant skeleton—reading rests on offering-commodity context alone.

entries.meaning: pasture, meadow (estate heading)

cognates.Hebrew: כַּר kar 'pasture, meadow' (Isa 30:23 kar nirḥāb; Ps 65:14); also 'lamb, ram' (Deut 32:14; Amos 6:4)

entries.note: HT97a KA-RU · *307+*307 · VIR+KA 82 / *327 33 / KA-NU-TI 25 / PA-I-TO 6 … — heading slot of HT85a A-DU · *307+*307 · VIR: 'pasture-sanctuary: men'. HT75 bare (KA-RU / — / [break]); one informative context. Geminate karr- written single. Rivals: Akkadian kāru 'quay, trading station' (East Semitic loan only; Kommos harbour), and a divine name (A-DU parallel). Two-consonant skeleton. Not KU-RA (first-syllable vowel).

entries.meaning: (to) the lord / lords—recipient entry; written only as WA-DU-NI-MI 'and (to) the lord(s)'

cognates.Amorite: ʾadun- in PNs: ʾADUN-UM A-DU-NU-UM (Gelb AS 21 no. 199); LA+ʾADON-IM LA-DU-NIM, genitive (no. 4246, Mari); A-du-na-dIM (Huffmon APNM p. 20). Huffmon p. 159: the names favour Albright's *ʾadun- 'lord' over Gelb's *ʾadān-
cognates.Amarna: Aduna, ruler of Irqata (EA 75:25; EA 140:10); Moran 1992: 380 'WS hypo. "father" or "lord"'
cognates.Ugaritic: ʾadn /ʔadānu/ 'father, lord'; PN A-du-ni-dU (PRU III 15.42 ii 20′, via Huffmon p. 159)
cognates.Hebrew: אָדוֹן ʾādôn, pl. אֲדֹנִים ʾădōnîm (< *ʾadān- by the Canaanite shift)

entries.note: HT6b WA-DU-NI-MI 3 + fractions, first line of the verso; HT85b ninth of eleven entries, each 1, the others names or places (Scribe 9). WA- = wa- 'and', allomorph of U; list entries otherwise carry no conjunction. Initial ʾa- absorbed after the particle, as in Amorite LA-DU-NIM la-ʾadun-im. -NI-MI: gen. sg. -im or pl. -īm, not distinguished by the script. No DO sign, so ʾadun- and ʾadōn- both write DU. If ʾadun- holds, A-DU-NI-TA-NA (ARKH5) admits ʾadun-nittan 'the lord gave'. HT127a ]DU-NE-MI is excluded: it is broken before DU and NE cannot be equated with NI.

entries.meaning: personal name: 'my kinsman / my (paternal) uncle'

cognates.Amorite: ʿAMM-IJA AM-MI-IA (Gelb AS 21 no. 735); ʿAMM-I+HADD-U AM-MI-A-DU, AM-MI-AD-DU (nos. 726–727); ʿAMM-I+DANN-U AM-MI-DA-NU (no. 728); ḥamm- 'paternal uncle' (Huffmon APNM 196)

entries.note: HT 115b *306+MI 1, a recipient after *306-TU-JA 1 and A-I 1. Ligature ʿA+MI: ʿAmmī, the geminate unwritten, the -ī of 'my'; a hypocoristic of the ʿAmmī-DN names, cf. Amorite ʿAMM-IJA (Gelb AS 21 no. 735). One attestation.

entries.meaning: (man) of the encampment, herdsman?—qualifier after a personal name

cognates.Amorite: NW *naw(u)-, *nawiy- 'steppe; encampment (man and beast)'; Mari nawûm, feminine (Huffmon APNM p. 237)
cognates.Hebrew: נָוֶה nāweh 'pasture, abode'; construct נְוֵה nᵊwēh, as נְוֵה רֹעִים 'abode of shepherds' (Jer 33:12)

entries.note: HT115b TI-NU-JA · NU-WI · GRA ½; HT115a RI-TA-MA / NU-WI 2 (line break on the GORILA facsimile). Two recipients, one scribe (Scribe 8), under a GRA+BOSm (grain + cattle) heading. No NO, WE or WO signs: NU-WI covers nō-wē and a cluster nw- (cf. Linear B pe-ru-si-nu-wo perusinwos, ke-se-nu-wi-ja ksenwia). Needs ā→ō (participle nōwē) or first-vowel reduction (construct nᵊwē). Rivals: (ʿa)nwī 'the humble, dependent' √ʿ-n-w (Hebrew ʿānāw, Ugaritic ʿnw), with initial ʿa- lost as in A-PA-RA-NE/PA-RA-NE; a patronymic '(son of) Nuwī' (Arabian PN nwy, Harding 1971: 604). Rejected: Hurrian genitive -we/-wi (NU-WI stands as a word on HT115b).

entries.meaning: Rimši; a personnel group named with the Amorite element rimši (Ugaritic DN rmš)

cognates.Amorite: Gelb AS 21 root RMS (unglossed): Rimši-ʾIl RI-IM-SI-DINGIR (no. 5285) and Rimši-ʾIli RI-IM-SI-I₃-LI₂ (no. 5286), Mari; feminine ʾAnnu-rimši AN-NU-RI-IM-SI (no. 831, Mari) and Kakka-rimši KA-AK-KA-RI-IM-ŠI (no. 3912); same root Ramaši RA-MA-SI (FN), Ramišum RA-MI-SUM

entries.note: HT119 RI-MI-SI 13, a group in a personnel list. /rimši/ matches the Amorite element in Rimši-ʾIl, Rimši-ʾIli, ʾAnnu-rimši, Kakka-rimši (Gelb, AS 21, nos. 5285–86, 831, 3912); Gelb leaves RMŠ unglossed. Ugaritic rmš is a divine name receiving a ram (š l rmš) in KTU 1.46:13, 1.109:7, 1.130:21 (DULAT 730). One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, Amorite type (element quwy-: 'wait for, hope' or 'be strong')

cognates.Amorite: Gelb AS 21 root QWJ (unglossed): Quwyum KU-IA-UM (no. 4109), KU-WU-UM (no. 4188); -at- form Kuyatum KU-IA-TUM (no. 4108); theophorics Quwi-Dagan KU-U₂-D-DA-GAN (no. 4145), Quwi-Haddu KU-U₂-D-IM (no. 4146, Mari), Quwi-Yaraḫ KU-WE-RA-AH (no. 4187), KU-UM-D-U (no. 4162, Ugarit MRS XVI 9:7)
cognates.Hebrew: קָוָה qāwāh 'wait for, hope' (HALOT 1082); קַוֵּה אֶל־יְהוָה 'wait for YHWH' (Ps 27:14)

entries.note: HT119 KO-JA 10, second named entry of a personnel list (Scribe 9). Hypocoristic qōy-/quy- + -a (cf. Amorite -ya hypocoristics). Cuneiform has no o-vowel, so Gelb's KU- spellings fit /qō/ as well as /qu/; KO-JA needs /qō/ (from *qaw- with aw > ō) or a Minoan o/u interchange. Root gloss open: 'wait for, hope' (Hebrew qāwāh, as קַוֵּה אֶל־יְהוָה Ps 27:14, matching the imperative + DN shape of Quwi-Haddu; Akkadian quʾʾû 'await') or 'be strong' (Arabic qawiya). Weak points: two signs, vowel mismatch. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Kiriš, divine name (Amorite DN Kiriš/Kirišu) or theophoric short name; oil recipient

cognates.Amorite: Gelb AS 21 glossary 'Kiriš, Kirišu, DN' (root KRS); ʾAwij-Kiriš A-WI-KI-RI-IŠ (no. 563; ARM XIV 106:18) and Iluna-Kiriš (no. 2556; ARM XIII 8:19 = LAPO 16 no. 104), Mari, Zimri-Lim era. Kiri(š) in 2 women's and 5 men's name types (Nakata 1995, Orient 30–31, charts pp. 251–252); seal of Iluna-Kiriš, servant of Zimri-Lim (Topçuoğlu 2016 no. 251 = Otto 2000 fig. 435)
cognates.Linear B: qe-ra-si-ja (KN Fp 1+31, 5, 6, 13, 14, 48; fem. dat., oil offerings beside pa-si-te-o-i), masc. qe-ra-si-jo (KN Fp 16.2): comparandum, not identity (KI/QE, RI/RA)
cognates.Hurrian: Gelb 1944 (Hurrians and Subarians, 113) parses Ur III Pudum-kiriš as Hurrian kir + -š

entries.note: TY3b (Tylissos, LM IB) KI-RI-SI OLE+MI 6 heads side b of an oil-distribution tablet (other recipients: PI-KU-ZU, ZA-*321, A-DU, A-DA, KO-A-DU-WA). Final SI writes -š (sibilant merger), matching Amorite Kiriš. Kiri(š) is a productive Mari theophoric element; Nakata never marks it female, so likely a male god of unknown identity and function. No published equation with Elamite Kiririša: separate deity. Rival: Hurrian kir + -š (Gelb 1944: 113)—Linear A's Hurrian layer makes that parse equally available. Oil recipient parallels Linear B qe-ra-si-ja at Knossos, but Kiriš has ri where qe-ra- has ra. Weak points: one attestation; may be a personal name.

entries.meaning: Setoiya (Knossian place name)
entries.note: Same spelling as Linear B se-to-i-ja, 17 Knossos tablets (As 40+5093, As 1516, Dc 5687+, Lc 525, Le 654, Mc 4464+, Sd 4407+ and others). PR Za 1 formula slot 2, the site-specific slot (cf. TU-RU-SA at Kophinas, O-SU-QA-RE at Tylissos, I-DA-MI at Syme). Locative ("at Setoiya") or epithet ("she of Setoiya") open.

entries.meaning: personal name: 'Sîn has gathered in / laid up (the child)'—verb + DN sentence name

cognates.Akkadian: kamāsu A 'to gather in', D kummusu (CAD K 114); moon-god Suen/Sîn, OB {d}suen, su₂-en, zu-en.
cognates.Amorite: Gelb AS 21 glossary KMS "to hide"; nouns kamisum, kumisum, kumsum; names KAMIS-UM (nos. 1745, 3971, 3972), JA-KMIS-I Yakmisi (no. 2910), KUMS-AJA (no. 4163). Sîn in Amorite names is a Mesopotamian borrowing: cult at Mari, treaty in his temple at Ḥarran, Ḥa-an-na-EN.ZU (Huffmon 1965, 35, 273).
cognates.Hebrew: kāmus "laid up" // ḥātûm "sealed" (Deut 32:34; HALOT 481); sense parallel Ṣəpanyāh "Yah has treasured" (√ṣ-p-n).

entries.note: PK1.3–4, one-each roster sorted by first sign. SI written on the right edge, word finished I-NA at the left margin (GORILA I 280–281; SigLA lists the SI as side b). O = u- of the D preterite, KA-MI = kamm- (geminate written single), ZA = final s + dead vowel; SI-I-NA = Sîn with two vowel slots (Suen > Sîn). Sibling frame U-KA-RE-A-SE-SI-NA (PE1 heading). Weak points: O for /u/ where Linear A has U (only PE1 U-KA- supports the swap); kamāsu otherwise unattested in Akkadian name formation; Sîn not in Ugaritic (moon-god Yariḫ), so the name implies a Mesopotamian-facing channel. One attestation.

entries.meaning: I weep (G prefix form, 1cs); rival ʾabakki (G present)

cognates.Hebrew: G 1cs ʾebkeh 'I weep' (Isa 16:9; Jer 48:32); wāʾebkeh 'and I wept' beside prayer (Neh 1:4); D-stem bikkâ 'bewail': məbakkôt ʾet-hattammûz, women bewailing Tammuz (Ezek 8:14)
cognates.Akkadian: bakû 'weep' (ORACC CAMS; 3cs preterite ibki, so 1cs abki); a-bak-ki = G present 1cs abakki (ORACC P273162, P338383)
cognates.Geʿez: bäkäyä 'flere, plorare, lamentari' (Dillmann 1865, no. 4035), imperfect of the yəqättəl type

entries.note: KN Zb 40 line 1, incised on a pithoid jar. A = 1cs ʾa- (as in ʾata-inawaya), PA = b with a dead vowel, KI = kī: ʾabkī, the G prefix form, Hebrew ʾebkeh 'I weep' (Isa 16:9; Jer 48:32). Not D: a D 1cs takes ʾu- (Ar. ʾu-, Fischer 2002, §211b; Akk. ubakka). Rival: the G present ʾabakki, which fills every vowel: Akk. a-bak-ki (ORACC P273162, P338383); Geʿez bäkäyä 'flere, lamentari' (Dillmann 1865, no. 4035), yəqättəl imperfect (Gragg 1997, Table 13.3). The G present is East and South Semitic; Central Semitic lost it. Findspot: Unexplored Mansion, Knossos; LM II destruction deposit, jar typologically LM I, inscription probably LM IB (Popham, Pope & Raison 1976, Kadmos 15; Owens 1998–99, Talanta 30–31, 147–48); the Mansion's upper floor held a domestic shrine with a goddess figurine (Owens). Weak points: one attestation; a lament on a household storage jar needs the shrine context to carry it. Rival: ʾa-pak- "jug, bottle" (Heb. pak, a small flask, poor fit for a pithoid jar; Ug. bk "beaker").

entries.meaning: and here, hither

cognates.Ugaritic: hnh 'hither?' (reading uncertain; possibly hn + terminative -h), beside hnn 'here' (Tropper §81.11a-b)

entries.note: KN Zb 40 .2, under A-PA-KI. U-NA- as in U-NA-KA-NA-SI and U-NA-RU-KA-NA-TI, w- + hn (di Mino, Ya Diktu); final A = -ā(h), as Hebrew hēnnâ 'here, hither' (Gen 45:8), Ugaritic hnh 'hither?' (Tropper §81.11a). Rival: hunāha without the conjunction.

entries.meaning: of the (olive-)press, press-estate (nisbe -ī on gitt- 'press; farmstead, estate')

cognates.Ugaritic: gt /gittu/ 'wine or olive press; farmstead, estate' (DULAT 307)
cognates.Hebrew: gat (גַּת) 'winepress'; gittî 'Gittite, of Gath' (2 Sam 6:10), pl. gittîm (2 Sam 15:18), the same nisbe

entries.note: KI for /gi/, TA for /tt/, -I for the nisbe -ī. HT 123+124a, two joining palimpsest fragments (GORILA I 210–211): KI-TA-I · OLIV 31, *308 8¼, KI-RO 1, the first of four parties in an olive and pressed-oil account beside PU-*131A, SA-RU (šarru) and DA-TU; KU-RO OLIV 93½. A press-estate fits as a party beside a royal establishment: Ug. gt 'press; farmstead, estate' (DULAT 307). Rival: a personal or institutional name. One attestation; HT 29 has [?]-KI-TA, a name.

entries.meaning: provisions (cf. Heb. ṣêdâ, travelling provision)
entries.note: ARKH 2 .1, intact: SI-DA-TE heads the tablet without a numeral over a must list, KU-RA *131B 5, then A-SI-DA-TO-I 12, ZU-*301-SE-DE-*21F-*118 6, A-SU-PU-WA 4, RU-MI[ (GORILA III 7). Heb. ṣêdâ 'provisions' (Gen 42:25; Josh 1:11), Ug. ṣd. SI writes ṣē, contracted from *ṣayd-; TE the feminine -t. Weak point: SI for ṣē. Rival: a personal name or party heading, as on HT 20 and HT 16; cf. SI-DA-RE (HT 17, HT 122a). One attestation.

entries.meaning: Arwad (island city of the Phoenician coast), an entity in a transfer
entries.note: RA-U writes /raw/, as A-I writes /ay/: all four consonants ʾ-r-w-d stand in order, and SigLA reads U (AB10), not AU. KH 5: A-DA-KI-SI-KA · A-RA-U-DA · over WI-SA-SA-NE CYP+E 2, VINb+WI 2, then WI-NA-DU · *301-NA ·, KU-PA-ZU CYP 3. Hogan takes the tablet as perhaps one transfer of CYP+E and VINb+WI to several entities, A-RA-U-DA among them (Hogan, in Salgarella and Petrakis, The Wor(l)ds of Linear A, 81): an entity slot, which a place fills. Late Bronze Ugarit writes the gentilic {iri}a-ru-a-di-yu (RS 19.0042) with the same u for w. Rival: the personal name ʾArōd (Num 26:17). One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name (cf. Hebrew ʿAttay)
entries.note: *306 = ʿA; TU writes -tu with the geminate unwritten. A recipient on three documents: the HT 9a/9b wine roster (10; 8), the same roster on HT 122a (1[, beside PA-DE and *324-DI-RA), and HT 119 (2, before *327-JU 8 and KU-RO 160). The name slot is secure; the etymology rests on two consonants. Two independent lists: the HT 9a/9b roster (recopied on HT 122a) and the HT 119 personnel count (KU-RO 160). With ʿ the Hurrian attai 'father' (Laroche 1980, 63) is excluded. *306-TU-JA (HT 115b) is the same name with hypocoristic -ya.

entries.meaning: personal name, hypocoristic of *306-TU in -ya
entries.note: HT 115b *306-TU-JA 1, whole and undotted, between KU-RU-MA · I ½ and A-Ị-[··] 1̣, on a palimpsest (GORILA I 191); *306+MI stands on the same face. *306-TU (HT 9a, 9b, 119, 122a) with hypocoristic -ya, cf. Heb. ʿAttay (1 Chr 2:35). Weak point: -ya is also Hurrian and Akkadian. Rival: a Hurrian name in -ya. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, Amorite type (yaqtul of QWJ)

cognates.Amorite: JA-QWUJ-U, written ia-ku-ú (Gelb 1980, no. 3314); JA-QWUJ-UM, ia-ku-ú-um and ia-ku-um (nos. 3315, 3317); JA-QWUJ-JA, ia-ku-ia (nos. 3300–3301)

entries.note: MA 2b: ]-RE-TI 4, ]TI 1, JA-KU 2, TI[, a roster of small whole numbers on a three-sided bar (DU-RA 5 on face a). JA-KU matches Amorite ia-ku-ú (Gelb 1980, no. 3314) sign for sign: final *-y is lost in both, and /qu/ is written KU. Same root as KO-JA. JA-KU-TI (KN 1a) carries the same base. Rival: JA-KWUN-U, ia-ku-nu (Gelb 1980, no. 3309), with final n unwritten. Two signs, one attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, Amorite type: base JA-KU with -TI

cognates.Amorite: JA-QWUJ-U, written ia-ku-ú (Gelb 1980, no. 3314)

entries.note: KN 1a: JA-KU-TI E 240; the verso has JA-DU-RA-TI E 105 in the same layout (SigLA reads AB38, E, on both faces), so both are names. Base JA-KU (MA 2b), Amorite ia-ku-ú (Gelb 1980, no. 3314). JA-DU-RA-TI carries the same ending -TI; its function is open. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name (Amorite Kakku)

cognates.Amorite: KAKK-U, written ka-ak-ku, a woman's name (Gelb 1980, no. 3913); KAKK-A+ compounds (nos. 3905–3912); kakkum, fem. kakka 'weapon', and the god Kakka (Gelb 1980, glossary)

entries.note: HT 62 .2 (GORILA I 117): ][·]-NA GRA 15¼ KA-KU 7[, a recipient after a grain entry; the 7 is Pugliese Carratelli's reading, four strokes now. Matches Amorite KAKK-U, ka-ak-ku (Gelb 1980, no. 3913), with the geminate unwritten. The same element stands first in KA-KU-NE-TE (ZA 10b). Rival: kakkum 'weapon' as a commodity, which the recipient slot does not favour. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal or clan name, 'Flea'

cognates.Hebrew: Parʿōš (פַּרְעֹשׁ), a clan, 'the sons of Parʿōš' (Ezra 2:3; HALOT 971); parʿōš 'flea' (1 Sam 24:15)
cognates.Amorite: purʿušum 'flea', in names (Gelb 1980, glossary)

entries.note: HT 20 (GORILA I 37): PA-RO-SU · heads six fraction entries (KU-MA-JU ¼, QE-KU-RE · DI ½, *21M ⅛, SA-RE-JU ⅛, WA ¼, *188+KU ½). The same scribe's HT 16 has the same layout under KA-KU-PA ·, a party, so the heading names the recipient. RO writes rʿō with ʿ lost. Rival: parsu 'portion, dry measure' (Ug. prs, DULAT 671), which leaves RO unexplained. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name, hypocoristic in -aya (cf. Hebrew ʾIttay)

cognates.Hebrew: ʾIttay (אִתַּי), Ittai the Gittite (2 Sam 15:19; HALOT 102); Ittai son of Ribai (2 Sam 23:29)
cognates.Linear B: i-ta-ja, a woman (KN Ap 769.2); o-pi i-ta-ja[ (KN Od 537.3)

entries.note: HT 28a: I-TA-JA OLE+DI 10, the last recipient of the A-SI-JA-KA list, after A-RU-DA-RA GRA 5. Gemination unwritten; -aya written JA. Hebrew ʾIttay, Ittai the Gittite, who marches with the Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Sam 15:18–19). Linear B i-ta-ja is a woman's name at Knossos (KN Ap 769.2): the name outlives Linear A on Crete, which fixes the name but not its language. Two consonants, one attestation.

entries.meaning: (men) of the Kikkar, 'round district' (gentilic heading of a head-count roster)

cognates.Hebrew: kikkār (כִּכָּר) 'round district' (Gen 13:12; Neh 12:28); ʾanšê hakkikkār 'the men of the Kikkar' (Neh 3:22); also 'round loaf' (1 Sam 2:36)

entries.note: HT 85b: KI-KI-RA-JA · heads the face over eleven entries of one unit each (KI-RE-TA₂ 1, QE-KA 1 … WA-DU-NI-MI 1, MA-DI 1, QA-*310-I 1). HT 85a is headed A-DU · *307+*307 · VIR+[?], so the tablet counts men, and a group label fits the heading. -JA writes the gentilic -āya. Weak point: KI-KI-RA leaves the a of kikkār unwritten or writes it i. Rivals: kikkār 'round loaf' (1 Sam 2:36), one to each man; a personal name heading the roster. KE-KI-RU (HT 94b) is on the same root. One attestation.

entries.meaning: large vessel (vessel label)

cognates.Akkadian: kirru A (DUG.KIR) 'a large vessel of earthenware, metal or stone', from Old Akkadian on (CAD K 408–410)
cognates.Hebrew: kiyyôr (כִּיֹּר) 'pot, basin, laver' (1 Sam 2:14; Exod 30:18), rival

entries.note: MI Zb 1, incised on the base of a clay vase (Copenhagen NM 6960): KI-RU, two signs, nothing else (GORILA IV 91). Akk. kirru A, a large vessel of earthenware, metal or stone for water, beer, oil, wine, honey or perfume, from Old Akkadian on; perfume kirrātu among Tušratta's gifts (EA 22 iii 36) (CAD K 408–410). KI-RU writes kirru, the geminate unmarked. Rival: Heb. kiyyôr 'basin, laver' (Exod 30:18), Akk. kiūru 'metal cauldron', a Neo-Assyrian foreign word (CAD K 476), which needs an unwritten y; or an owner's mark. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name; compare Linear B ta-ta-ro
entries.note: PK 1 .2 TA₂-TA-RE 1, a single-unit entry in a column of names, TA₂ distinct from TA (GORILA I 281). Linear B ta-ta-ro is a man on the Knossos roster KN As(1) 607.2 (VIR 1), also KN Pp 498, Xd 8605 and PY Eb 874, Ep 301.6, Eo 224.7. Final -RE answers Linear B -ro as in A-RA-NA-RE / a-ra-na-ro (KN As 1516), PA-JA-RE / pa-ja-ro (KN As 1519) and NA-DA-RE / no-da-ro (KN As 609), all on the same roster series. The Greek gloss Tantalos is the Mycenologists'; no Semitic etymology; possibly a name from another language of Crete. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Beloved (personal name, √d-w-d + -ma); rival the Aegean name of the Keftiu board and Linear B di-du-me

cognates.Hebrew: dûdāʾîm 'mandrakes, love-apples' (Gen 30:14; Song 7:14), the u-ā form of √d-w-d
cognates.Amorite: DAWD-U*MA, DA-DU-MA (Gelb 1980, no. 1433); DAWD-A (no. 1413)
cognates.Egyptian: {d-j}-d-ȝ-d-ȝ-m{a}, an 'Aegean' beneficiary of a wine account, BM EA 5647 v. I 3a (Dautais & Gabolde 2025, 14–15)
cognates.Linear B: di-du-me (KN L 588), di-du-mo (KN X 5751, MY Oe 129) (Dautais & Gabolde 2025, Table 1)

entries.note: HT 6b .4 DU-DA-MA 66, the largest entry in a list of names, on a face written over an erasure; DU-DA-MA itself shows no undertext (GORILA I 13). dū-dā-ma, the vowels of Heb. dûdāʾîm 'love-apples', √d-w-d 'beloved', + -ma as in the Amorite name DA-DU-MA, Dawdu-ma (Gelb 1980, no. 1433). The same name has the consonants d-d-m in three scripts: Egyptian d-ȝ-d-ȝ-m of the Keftiu writing board and Linear B di-du-me, di-du-mo (Dautais & Gabolde 2025, 14–15). Not DA-DU-MA-TA dadmatu (√d-d-m). One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name; compare Linear B ka-sa-ro
entries.note: HT 10b .3 KA-SA-RU 6, a personnel entry on a face written over an erasure; the three signs are clear (GORILA I 21). Linear B ka-sa-ro is a man's name at Knossos (KN C(2) 912.8, Dv 1450), with no Greek interpretation. Final -RU against Linear B -ro, as I-TA-NU against u-ta-no. Ugarit has DUMU ka-ša₂-ri (ORACC P503760). The root is open (k-š-r, q-ṣ-r, g-z-r); a reading as Kothar would need S for ṯ, against KA-TA-RE. One attestation.
entries.source: KN C(2) 912.8; KN Dv 1450; di Mino

entries.meaning: provisions (list heading); rival a personal name, cf. Linear B ma-si-dwo
entries.note: HT 43 .1 MA-SI-DU ·, all three signs whole, heading the tablet before PA-*342-I · I GRA+PA 5̣[ (GORILA I 83). maṣīdu 'provisions': Ug. mṣd '(feast of) game' (DULAT 578), Heb. ṣêdâ 'provisions' (HALOT 1021); SI writes ṣi. Rival: a personal name, cf. Linear B ma-si-dwo, a man at Knossos (KN Fh 360.b; DMic I s.v.), with -Cu for Linear B -Co (Woudhuizen 2016, 218). One attestation.

entries.meaning: dignitary, prince (title of a recipient); rival a personal name
entries.note: HT 11b .4 RU-ZU-NA KA 30, whole and undotted (GORILA I 23), the fourth of five KA entries that KU-RO 180 totals, before SA-QE-RI · KA 30. Heb. rōzēn 'dignitary, prince' (HALOT 1210); Ar. razuna 'was weighty, grave' (Lane 1079) fixes the PS *z, which ZU writes beside ṯ. Woudhuizen (2016, 223–224) reads the same word. Rival: a personal name. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name; compare Egyptian rw-sȝ, one of the 'names of Crete' on BM EA 5647
entries.note: HT 96a .3 RU-SA 4, whole and undotted, after SI-MI-TA GRA 5 and before *323-*317 1, with no logogram of its own (GORILA I 157). The writing board BM EA 5647 heads seven names 'making names of Crete' (jr.t rn.w n[y.w] kftjw); the seventh, rw-sȝ (r. I 7), is ru-sa sign for sign (Dautais & Gabolde 2025, 9, 14, Table 2 p. 15). Linear B has ru-si at Knossos (KN Ak 634) and ru-si-qe on KN L 588.1, the tablet that has di-du-me on .3, the name the board's {d-j}-d-ȝ-d-ȝ-m and DU-DA-MA match (DMic II s.v. ru-si). No etymology is adopted here. The final vowel differs from Linear B (a against i). Two signs; one attestation.
entries.source: Dautais & Gabolde 2025, 9, 14–15; DMic II s.v. ru-si; di Mino

entries.meaning: personal name; compare Linear B a-ti-ka
entries.note: ZA Wc 2, a Zakros roundel: .1 A-TI-KA-A, .2 DỤ-KO-⟦MI⟧, the erasure brackets dotted; GORILA divides A-TI-KA · A-DU-KO-⟦MI⟧, though the four signs of .1 are evenly spaced (GORILA II 98). Linear B a-ti-ka is a man in a catalogue of men at Knossos (KN V 831.4; DMic I 119). Anastasiadou (2026, 40–41) makes the comparison and reports the rival divisions: Hallager reads one word A-TI-KA-A-DU-KO with the last sign the numeral 2, and Petrakis sees no epigraphic break after KA. GORILA draws the last sign as MI. No etymology is adopted. One attestation.
entries.source: DMic I 119; Anastasiadou 2026, 40–41, in Salgarella & Petrakis (eds.) 2026; di Mino

entries.meaning: bundle, bag (commodity or container)
entries.note: HT 30 .3 SA-RA-RA ½: three separate signs, both RA of the plain form (RA₂ in SA-RA₂ on .1), on a tablet written over an erasure, between QA2+[?]+PU ⅕ and *23M 1 (GORILA I 57). The tablet lists commodities with fractions and no names. Heb. I צְרוֹר 'little pack, bag', for money (Gen 42:35) and myrrh (Song 1:13), JArm. Syr. ṣərārā 'bundle, bag', Arab. ṣurrat 'purse' (HALOT 1054); Ug. mṣrr(t), a piece of fabric or a garment (DULAT 581). Rival: a personal name (Heb. Šārār, 2 Sam 23:33), against the slot. One attestation.

entries.meaning: personal name; compare the Ugaritic personal name kṯn
entries.note: HT 13 KU-ZU-NI 18, in the KA-U-DE-TA wine list; HT 85a KU-ZU-NI 5, in a roster counted in men; both tablets also list DA-SI-*118. ZU = /ṯu/: kuṯ(i)n-. Ugarit has the personal name kṯn, syllabic ki-še-na, ki-ši-na, ku-ši-nu, etym. unc. (DULAT s.v. kṯn (I), citing Huehnergard UVST 231 nn. 91 f.). Rival: Ug. ktn 'tunic' (DULAT 464), which has t, not ṯ. Weak point: ZU = /ṯu/ is a proposed value.

entries.meaning: personal name; Egyptian Pꜣjj, the first element of PA-JA-RE
entries.note: HT 41a .4 MI-DA-NI · PA-JA 2 and two fraction signs, both signs whole and undotted, the last line of the face (GORILA I 79). Egyptian Pꜣjj is a common name, borne under Thutmose III and Amenhotep II among others (PNM v6, s.v. pꜣjj); PA-JA-RE (HT 8b, 29, 88, ZA 10b) reads Pꜣjj-Rꜥ with the same JA. Egyptian two-consonant names are many, so the match rests on the identity with PA-JA-RE. Rival: a Semitic hypocoristic. Two signs; one attestation.
entries.source: Ilin-Tomich 2025 (PNM v6), s.v. pꜣjj; di Mino

entries.meaning: personal name 'redeemed' (p-d-y); recipient of wine
entries.note: HT 9a SA-RO · TE · VIN · PA-DE · 5¾, the first entry of the wine roster; HT 9b PẠ-DẸ 3, both signs dotted (GORILA I 18–19); HT 122a PA-DE 1. HT 122a recopies the HT 9 roster, so the three are one context. Ugaritic pdy (II) is a personal name, spelled syllabically pa-di, pa-di-ya (DULAT 653); Padi is also the king of Ekron in Neo-Assyrian texts (ORACC). DE writes the final ī. Rival: pa-de, a divine recipient at Knossos (KN Fp 1, Fp 48), which Landau compares with Linear A PA-DE (DMic II s.v.).
entries.source: DULAT 653 s.v. pdy (II); DMic II s.v. pa-de; di Mino

entries.meaning: Taanach (place name), or a personal name
entries.note: HT Wc 3004 and HT Wc 3005, two roundels by one scribe, each reading TA-NI-KA with SE (GORILA II 73): one context. Taanach is Hebrew Taʿnak (HALOT 1770; Josh 12:21; 17:11; 21:25; Judg 1:27) and Amarna URU Taḫnaka, EA 248:14, 'perhaps biblical Taanach' (Moran 1992, index). ʿ is unwritten, NI writes the a, and a Canaanite town on Haghia Triada roundels is unexplained. Rival: a local personal name.

entries.meaning: personal name '(DN) has helped', hypocoristic
entries.note: KN Zg 55, a steatite disk seal (CMS II 2, no. 213): face a a boar's head and knife, face b JA-SA-JA, the whole text, SA underlined in Younger's text (Younger, Linear A Texts). Amorite JŠʿ 'to help', jišʿum 'help', and the hypocoristic name Jišʿ-ija (Gelb 1980, glossary; no. 3768): ʿ unwritten, -JA the hypocoristic ending. Rival: an abbreviation of JA-SA-SA-RA (Younger). One attestation.
entries.source: Gelb 1980, glossary s.v. JŠʿ and no. 3768; Younger, Linear A Texts; di Mino

entries.meaning: Lyktos (place name); compare Egyptian Ri-ka-ta
entries.note: HT 146 .4 RI-KA-TA 30, the last of four entries of 30 (]QE[ 30, RI-*305 30, MA 30); RI word-initial, TA dotted (GORILA I 241). The Kom el-Hetan list of Amenhotep III (statue base C, no. 9) writes Ri-ka-ta beside the names read as Amnisos and Knossos; Astour takes it as 'most probably identical with the Cretan Lyktos' and explains Likata as a status absolutus beside LB ru-ki-to (Astour 1966, AJA 70, 317). r/l merger; the three vowels match the Egyptian form, not LB ru-ki-to. Lyktos lies far from Haghia Triada. Rests on the dotted TA. One attestation.

entries.meaning: offering pit (for the dead)

cognates.Akkadian: apu B 'hole, opening in the ground', NA ritual pit for offerings to the dead (CAD A/2 201)
cognates.Hebrew: II ʾôb 'spirit of the dead' (HALOT s.v.); baʿălat ʾôb (1 Sam 28:7)
cognates.Hurrian: abi 'trou, fosse' (Laroche 1980, 34)
cognates.Hittite: a-a-pi 'sacrificial pit' (HALOT s.v. II ʾôb, after Rabin)

entries.note: KN Ze 16, the only word, incised at eye level on the last block of the dromos of the Kephala tholos, before the burial chamber (GORILA IV 138; Owens 1998–99, 148–149). A and PI clear; nothing before A or after PI, and the divider Owens reports after PI is not drawn. Akkadian apu B 'hole, opening in the ground', the NA ritual pit where food for the spirits of the dead is laid and honey, oil, beer and wine poured (CAD A/2 201); at Emar an offering is made before the abū (Milgrom 2000, 1768); Hebrew II ʾôb 'spirit of the dead', which Rabin derives from Hittite a-a-pi 'sacrificial pit' (HALOT s.v.; baʿălat ʾôb, 1 Sam 28:7). The word travels (Hurrian abi, Laroche 1980, 34; Hittite a-a-pi; Luwian āpit-), so it names the pit, not the writer's language; final I matches abi and needs the genitive -i in Akkadian. Rival: a personal name. Hapax.

entries.meaning: the Byblian, (wool) of Byblos: a section heading
entries.note: HT 24a .1 KU-PA₃-RI-JA · KI-MA+RU[, the heading of a wool inventory; PA-SA-RI-JA heads the second section at .4. Gubla with the gentilic -iya: Amorite GUBL-AJ-I and GUBL-AJIT-UM (Gelb 1980, nos. 1793–1795) and Gubla in Gelb's glossary; Akkadian Gublaya 'Byblian' at Ugarit (ORACC P503838); Hebrew gibli 'Gebalite'; Ugaritic gbl 'Byblos' (DULAT 290). KU writes g, PA₃ b, RI l. Rival: the Ugaritic place kbry, syllabic URU ku-ba-ri-ia-a (DULAT 424). One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'burning, kindled'
entries.note: HT 93a .6 DE-JU-KU 1½, whole and undotted, in a grain list between VIR+[·]-I 6 and O-TI-[·] 3 (GORILA I 147). Amorite DALQ-UM and DALAQ-UM (Gelb 1980, nos. 1396, 1462) and the root DLQ 'to burn' in Gelb's glossary; Hebrew dālaq 'burn'. JU writes l. Rival: √d-l-g 'leap' (Hebrew dālag), with KU for g. One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'glory' (feminine)
entries.note: ZA 10b .3 MA-KI-DE-TE 5, intact, between MA-ZA 5 and SA-MA 5 in a name list (GORILA III 171). Safaitic MJDT beside MJD (Harding 1971, 528); Hebrew meged 'excellence' and Magdîʾēl (Gen 36:43). With ME-KI-DI (ZA 14) the feminine and masculine of one name at one site, as Harding's MJDT and MJD. Rival: Arabian MQʿDT 'posterior, seat' (Harding 1971, 560), with ʿ unwritten. One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'glory' (masculine)
entries.note: ZA 14 .1 ME-KI-DI 1, intact, the first entry of a name list, before *21F-*118 1 and QA-TI-JU 8 (GORILA III 181). Safaitic MJD (Harding 1971, 528); Hebrew meged 'excellence'. The masculine of MA-KI-DE-TE (ZA 10b). Rival: Ugaritic mkt 'immolation, offering (?)'. One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, hypocoristic in -ya
entries.note: HT 6a .2–3 PI-TA-JA 24, intact, in a fig list after DA-TA-RA · TE · NI 15 (GORILA I 13). Amorite PATIJ-UM (Gelb 1980, nos. 5160, 5162); or √p-t-ḥ 'open' with ḥ unwritten, as PTḤ in Gelb's glossary and Hebrew Pəṯaḥyāh. Rival: the Egyptian personal name ptjj (PNM). One document.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'bear' with -ān
entries.note: HT 115b .2 DU-PA₃-NA 1, whole and undotted, after TI-NU-JA · NU-WI · GRA ½ and before KU-RU-MA · I ½, on a palimpsest (GORILA I 191). Amorite DABIN-UM (Gelb 1980, no. 1411) and the root DBB in Gelb's glossary; Arabian DBN (Harding 1971, 234). Rival: Harding's own gloss, dibbān 'fly'. One document.

entries.meaning: personal name
entries.note: An entry with a numeral on four Haghia Triada tablets: HT 10a DA-RI-DA 8 before ME-ZA 3, in the KU-NI-SU list (GORILA I 21); HT 85a DA-RI-DA 12, first under A-DU · *307+*307 · VIR+[·] (GORILA I 131); HT 122a DA-RI-DA 1, last before KU-RO 31 (GORILA I 207); HT 93a DA-RI-DA *406VS 2 (GORILA I 147). Hebrew Dardaʿ (1 Kgs 4:31), with ʿ unwritten. Rival: a place or work unit, since 12 on HT 85a stands against 1 on HT 122a.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'antelope'
entries.note: HT 108 .2 DI-NA-RO 2 DU-SU-NI 4[, whole and undotted, a recipient in the grain list under KI-RE-TA-NA (GORILA I 175). Hebrew Dîšôn and Dîšān, clans of Seir (Gen 36:21), and dîšôn 'antelope' (Deut 14:5). Rival: a Hurrian name in -nni, as DA-KU-SE-NE. One document.

entries.meaning: personal name
entries.note: HT 1 .2 ZU-SU 70, whole and undotted, the second entry under QE-RA₂-U, after KI-RO 197 and before DỊ-DI-ZA-KE 52 (GORILA I 3). The personal name Zuzu at Late Bronze Ugarit (RSO 7, 3, lower edge 3; ORACC P347841). SU for the second z stands against ZU for the first. Rival: an institutional name in the same quantified slot. One document.

entries.meaning: personal or institutional name, a recipient
entries.note: A recipient at two sites: HT 123+124b .2 PI-SA 4 in a terebinth list, clean on a palimpsest face (GORILA I 213), and KH 6 .6 PI-SA[ at a line end, broken after, before CYP+D ½ (GORILA III 27). Amorite Bu-ṣí (Huffmon 1965, 303), with PI for b and SA for ṣ. Rival: an institution receiving allocations.

entries.meaning: entity name: yidu 'strength' with TI
entries.note: HT 104 .2–3 I-DU-TI 20 ½, I at the end of .2, DU-TI at the head of .3, all three signs whole and undotted, the ½ dotted (GORILA I 171). Eblaite names built on yidu 'strength', as yidu-na 'our strength' (Pagan 1998, Ebla personal names, row 2466); TI is unexplained. Rivals: I-DU followed by TI as an ideogram, which GORILA's note allows; Ida, written I-DA-A on KO Za 1. One document.

entries.meaning: ring text ending with the personal name ʾAyaku
entries.note: KN Zf 13, gold ring HM 530: 19 signs in a spiral from the outer band inward, no dividers; RI (12, 15), MU (16) and KU (19) underdotted (GORILA IV 152–153). The last four signs are A-JA-KU, ʾAyaku (Amorite ʾAjak-u, Gelb 1980, no. 320); the first fifteen carry no reading, and the segmentation is not marked. Rival for the ending: Akkadian ajakku, a temple structure (CAD A/1, 224–25). One document.

entries.meaning: skin, fleece (a hide with its wool); rival 'hair'

cognates.Akkadian: paru A (parru, baru) 'skin, hide' (CAD P 209); pāru, parru, bāru 'Haut' (AHw 836)
cognates.Arabic: farw- 'fur'; farwa 'a skin, but not unless having upon it fur or wool' (Lane 2390)
cognates.Syriac: partā, pl. parrē 'bran, husk; scurf of the head' (Brock. 591)

entries.note: PH 3a .3 ]MA+RU ⅓ · PẠ-RẠ ⅓ (GORILA I 291): after the wool ligature MA+RU and the MA ligatures *556, *557 and *563, with the wool entry's ⅓ measure; a fractional measure fits a material counted by weight. PA and RA at their primary values, the geminate unwritten. Both signs dotted. Rivals: *parʕ- '(loose) hair of the head' (Akk. pērtu, Hbr. päraʕ; SED I No. 218), head hair rather than a traded material; *ɣapar- 'stiff hair' (Kogan 2011, 223) with its first syllable unwritten. HT 128a .1 *326 PA-RA TU-RU-NU-SE-ME GRA 10, with no quantity of its own (GORILA I 221): there a personal name, or *barr- 'wheat' (Hbr. bār, Akk. burru, CAD B 330) with PA for /b/. A two-sign word: the PH 3a context, not the spelling, selects the sense.

entries.meaning: Tegi 'Beautiful' (personal name; Hurrian tagi/tegi 'beautiful')

cognates.Hurrian: tagi 'beau', RS voc. te-gi-še 'beau prix'; onom. Tagi(b)-šarri, Tagu(b)-šini, Taguya (Laroche 1980, 249–50)

entries.note: HT 13 .3–4 TE-KI 27½, after TE-TU 56 and before KU-ZU-NI 18, under KA-U-DE-TA VIN · TE · (GORILA I 27). HT 122a .3 TE-KI 2, before QA-*310-I 3 (GORILA I 207). HT 85a writes TE-KE 3 in the same set of units (DA-SI-*118, KU-ZU-NI), counted under VIR. Hurrian tagi 'beautiful' as a bare-stem name; the Ras Shamra form te-gi-še has e in the first syllable, as TE-KI does. Rival: PS *diḳ(ḳ)- 'small' (Ug. dḳ, DULAT 275). A two-sign name: the vowel match, not the consonants, separates it from chance.

entries.meaning: Tegi (personal name; spelling of TE-KI)
entries.note: HT 85a .5 TE-KE 3, whole and undotted, sixth of seven entries under A-DU · *307+*307 · VIR+[?] ·, after KU-ZU-NI 5 (GORILA I 131). HT 13 lists DA-SI-*118, KU-ZU-NI and TE-KI in the same order; TE-KE is TE-KI with the e/i alternation. See TE-KI.

entries.meaning: official, commissioner (title); rival: the personal name Qīpu

cognates.Akkadian: qīpu (qēpu) s. 'official; administrator of a region, a city, a temple', from MB on, Ass. qēpu, lex. LÚ qe-e-pu (CAD Q 264); qīpu adj. 'trustworthy, trusted (person)' (CAD Q 263); qiāpu 'to believe, trust'
cognates.Nuzi: QĪPU, Ki-pu, slave of the palace (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 88)

entries.note: HT 9a and 9b, the wine roster: QE-PU 2 on both faces, one of two entries unchanged (with DI-NA-U 4) while the total falls from 31¾ to 24 (GORILA I 19). QE writes q and the Assyrian ē, PU the -pu. An Akkadian title in a recipient slot beside the names Padī and Dīnāyu. Rival: the name Qīpu.

entries.meaning: Paššiya (personal name; Hurrian hypocoristic on pašš- 'send')

cognates.Nuzi: PAŠŠIJA, Pa-aš-ši-ia, two bearers, one the son of Pula-ḫali who also bears Pašši-tilla (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 112); "Hypocoristic for Paššip-tilla" (ibid., 243)
cognates.Hurrian: pašš- 'mander', Mitanni letter pa-aš-ši-en; paššithi 'messager' (Laroche 1980, 197–99)

entries.note: The matched roundel pair HT Wc 3001 (PA-SE-JA ½) and 3002 (PA-SE-JA), Scribe 107 (GORILA II 72): one context. HT 93a .8 ]PA-SE-JA 20, broken before, PA dotted, ]PI-SE-JA possible (GORILA I 147). The base PA-SE heads HT 18 and stands on HT 27b as an entry parallel to MI-DA (· VIN+WA · SA n): name and -ya short form in one archive, as Pašši-tilla and Paššiya at Nuzi. SE writes the stem vowel i. Rival: the Semitic nisba -iya, 'the one of PA-SE', as KU-PA₃-RI-JA Gubliya, with PA-SE unexplained. Cf. LB pa-sa-ja, a spice recipient (KN Ga 953).
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943; Laroche 1980

entries.meaning: Dašurat 'Old (f.)' (woman's name; Amorite dašuratum 'old')

cognates.Amorite: DAŠUR-AT-UM, DA-ŠU-RA-TUM, FN (YOS VIII 51 2, 14; Gelb 1980 no. 1489); DAŠUR-UM, DA-ŠU-RU-UM (no. 1490); DAŠUR-AH+ʿAŠTAR, DA-ŠU-RA-EŠ₄-DAR, FN (no. 1488); ʿAMM-I+DAŠUR, AM-MI-DA-ŠUR? (no. 729); dašurum, dušurum, fem. dašuratum, dašura 'old' (Gelb 1980, 17)
cognates.Arabic: daṯara, aor. -ṯuru, inf. duṯūr, of a trace of a dwelling 'it became effaced… and it became old'; of a man 'he became overcome by old age and emaciation'; dāṯir 'effaced' (Lane 851)

entries.note: SY Za 6, on the wall of a chalice-shaped serpentine libation table below the rim: one group of four signs, no divider (Muhly and Olivier 2008, 209–210). SE uncertain; DA (SA not excluded), RA and TE probable. DA-SE-RA-TE writes DA-ŠU-RA-TUM sign for sign without mimation: SE writes š, TE the feminine -t. Amorite š writes PS *ṯ, so dašur- is Arabic daṯara 'became old'; Gelb gives no root. The sole word on a libation table: the dedicant's name, or 'the Old One (f.)' as an epithet. Rival: SA for DA. One attestation.

entries.meaning: Ar-tae (personal name; Hurrian ar- 'give')

cognates.Nuzi: AR-TAE, A-ar-ta-e, var. Ar-ta-e, Ar-ta-a-e, A-ar-da-e (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 33); ar- with -tae, from ar 'give' (ibid., 203)

entries.note: HT 29 .5 A-RE-DA-I 2, whole and undotted, RE written over an erased sign, the whole tablet over an erasure (GORILA I 55). An entry of two units after [?]-KI-TA 2 and before KA-DU-MA-NE 1, on a tablet with PA-JA-RE. Nuzi writes the name A-ar-da-e beside A-ar-ta-e: RE writes ar- with a dead vowel, DA the -da- of that spelling. Rival: DA-I dayu as a second element, with A-RE unexplained.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943

entries.meaning: the one of Šakmu (Shechem) (gentilic in -SE on the toponym)

cognates.Hebrew: šǝkem 'shoulder, mountain ridge'; Šǝkem Shechem, gentilic haš-šikmî (Num 26:31)
cognates.Amarna: KUR ša-ak-mi 'the land of Šakmu', Shechem (EA 289)
cognates.Amorite: ŠKM: Šākim, DN (Gelb 1980, 33); ŠAKIM-UM, ŠA-KI-MU-UM (no. 5804)

entries.note: ZA 15a .7 *363-KE-MA-SE 5, the last entry of the wine issue headed *47-KU-NA, after SA-MI-DA-E 4 (GORILA III 183). Intact, no dots. *363 at its proposed value SO: so-ke-ma writes škm, the Hebrew and Akkadian reflex of PS *ṯkm; the rival value ṮA gives the same root. -SE as on RU-MA-TA-SE beside bare RU-MA-TA, and on MI-ZA-SE on the same face: town and gentilic, as Šǝkem and šikmî. Rival: the Amorite name Šakim (ŠA-KI-MU-UM). *363 unresolved.

entries.meaning: ʾAkiru (personal name; Amorite ʾAkir-, cf. ʾikkār 'plowman')

cognates.Amorite: ʾAKIR-UM, A-KI-RU-UM (KISURRA B 7+); ʾAKIR-I, A-KI-RI (VAS VIII 14 37); ʾAKIR-AH, A-KI-RA, FN (Gelb 1980 nos. 338–340)
cognates.Akkadian: ikkaru 'plowman, farm laborer; farmer', Sum. lw. (CAD I/J s.v.)

entries.note: ARKH 4b .4 A-KI-RO 3, after the numeral ]9 that closes the entry of .3–4 and before ZA-SI-ZU[ ]3, in a list of whole-number entries with no logogram on the face (GORILA III 14–15). Intact and undotted. A-KI-RO spells A-KI-RU-UM / A-KI-RI / A-KI-RA sign for sign, RO for the case vowel. The noun ʾikkār behind the name is this lexicon's analysis, not Gelb's. Rivals: the Akkadian name Ikkaru; A + KI-RO 'owed'.

entries.meaning: Azzuya (woman's name; Hurrian hypocoristic on az(z)-)

cognates.Nuzi: AZ(Z)UIA, A-zu-ia, var. Az-zu-ia, a woman (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 41); az(z), Hurrian, in women's names (ibid., 208)

entries.note: HT 11a .3–4 A-SU-JA 1, A at the end of .3 and SU-JA on .4, whole and undotted, the first entry after KU-RO 10 (GORILA I 23). Spelled as Nuzi A-zu-ia: SU writes zu, JA the hypocoristic -ya. Rival: Ugaritic PN ùsy (DULAT 111).
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943

entries.meaning: corvée workers, labour gang (personnel term)

cognates.Proto-Semitic: *mass- 'forced labor, corvée levy, labor gang' (semitic_roots S31)
cognates.Akkadian: massu 'corvée worker': idi LÚ.MEŠ ma-zi 'wages for the corvée workers' (Wiseman Alalakh 246:6; CAD M/1 s.v.)
cognates.Hebrew: mas מַס 'corvée, labour gang': wayyaʿal ham-melek šəlōmōh mas 'King Solomon raised a levy' (1 Kgs 5:27)

entries.note: ZA 10b .2–3 MA-ZA 5, after U-*49 6 and before MA-KI-DE-TE 5 (GORILA III 171), in a list that counts A-MI-TA ʾamita 'handmaid' 3. MA-ZA writes ma-za on primary values: Alalakh's z spelling, the geminate unwritten. A labour gang issued in a list, as Alalakh issues wages to the ma-zi. Rivals: the Eblaite name ma-za (Pagan 1998); the Hurrian name mzy, ma-zi-i (DULAT 600).

entries.meaning: messenger, courier (title)

cognates.Akkadian: kallû 'messenger', LÚ ka-al-la at Ugarit (RS 16.188 r. 7; CAD K 83–84)

entries.note: HT 88 .4 KA-JU 1, both signs whole and undotted, the second of six one-unit entries after KI-RO, between KU-PA₃-PA₃ 1 and KU-PA₃-NU 1 (GORILA I 139). JU at its primary value lu: ka-lu, the geminate unwritten. A title in a roster of one-unit entries, as Ugarit issues wine to the courier. Rivals: Ugaritic qallu, with KA for q; kalû 'lamentation priest' (CAD K 91).

entries.meaning: trader, merchant (title); rival rōqēaḥ 'perfumer'

cognates.Hebrew: rōkēl 'trader': hā-rōkĕlîm beside the goldsmiths (Neh 3:31–32); ʾabqat rôkēl 'the merchant's powders' (Song 3:6)

entries.note: HT 98a .4 RO-KE ½, whole and undotted, between TE-*301 ¾ and KA-RI-*310-I ¼, in a list of fractional issues with TA-NA-TI; wine on face b (GORILA I 161). The qōṭēl participle with Canaanite ō, as RO-E rōʿē; KE at its primary value k. The final l goes unwritten, as Linear B drops a word-final liquid: ma-te mātēr, pa-te patēr (PY An 607), and Linear A KA-PA kapa(r). Rival: rōqēaḥ 'perfumer', which needs KE for q.

entries.meaning: land labourer, field worker; rival the personal name Šadī

cognates.Ugaritic: šdy (I) 'land labourer', nʿrm šdym (KTU 4.868:4); PN šdy (II), syll. ša-de₄-ya (DULAT 799)

entries.note: HT 111b .1 SA-DI 4[, whole and undotted, the numeral broken after (GORILA I 181), on a fragment broken above and below. SA writes š in the S-class merger. A count of four fits a term for workers; the fragment gives no heading to choose between the occupation and the name. Rival: the name Šadī (Ugaritic šdy (II); Amorite šad- 'mountain').

entries.meaning: (portion) of the fire offering (-iya derivative of A-SE)
entries.note: HT 115a .4 A-SE-JA with four fraction signs, whole and undotted, after PA-RA-NE 1, on a palimpsest whose heading carries GRA+BOSm (GORILA I 189). The base A-SE ʾaššē opens grain and commodity entries on HT 81, HT 93a and HT 132; -JA forms the derivative as in PA-SE / PA-SE-JA. Rivals: the Nuzi name Aziya, A-zi-ia (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, 41); the Ugaritic name ùsy (DULAT 111).

entries.meaning: siddāru 'Arranger' (personal name; spelling of SI-DA-RE)
entries.note: GO 2 recto .3 SI-DA-RO with ¼, broken after the fraction, below single-sign entries SI[, KA ⅛, SI 2 and DA[ (Younger, Linear A Texts). SI-DA-RE (HT 17, HT 122a) with the final vowel o; JA-SI-DA-RA (PH 7a) carries the same stem. A second site, not a second context for SI-DA-RE. Rival: a commodity term, as the single-sign entries around it are. See SI-DA-RE.

entries.meaning: Dimenu (personal name; Ugaritic name type dmn)

cognates.Ugaritic: dmn PN (etym. unc.), syll. ZI-me-ni, ZI-me-nu (RS 34.169:2) (DULAT 283); tmn (II) PN (etym. unc.), syll. ta-me-nu (RS 34.169:5) (DULAT 858)

entries.note: HT 117a .8 DA-MI-NU 1, whole and undotted, in the second list headed SA-TA, before DA-NE-KU-TI 1 (GORILA I 197). DA at its primary value d gives dmn; the syllabic ZI-me-nu has the same three syllables. DULAT gives no etymology, so the language stays open. Rival: Ugaritic tmn (II), ta-me-nu, which needs DA for t. Second analysis: DA = the determinative-relative ḏā 'the one of' + MI-NU, a 'he of X' name written as one word, as DU-RU-WI ḏu-lēwī is. The type: Amorite Zu-i-la 'He of God' (Gelb no. 6596), Zu-dIš-ḫa-ra 'He of Išḫara' (no. 6598), on ḏu 'he/she of', written ZU (Gelb 1980, 18); Nabataean dwšrʾ, Δουσαρης 'He of the Šarā', probably dišar (Macdonald, in Al-Jallad 2022, 95–96); Hebrew zeh sînay 'the One of Sinai' (Judg 5:5). MI-NU is from √m-n-y 'count, allot', the portion and fate (PS *maniy-at-, no. 2703): Amorite manawum, manūtum (Gelb 1980, 25), Arab. Manāt (Q 53:20); cf. MI-NE Mīnō in DA-DU-MI-NE. Or from √m-n-n 'bestow, favor': Heb. mān 'manna' (Exod 16:31). Hence dā-Mīnu 'He of the Portion' or 'He of the Favor'. MI- stands for Amorite ma-, as in MI-NU-TE against Ma-nu-tum (Gelb no. 4528). Cf. LB da-mi-ni-jo, a shepherd at Knossos (DMic I).

entries.meaning: He of Naśiʾ (personal name heading HT 126a)

cognates.Amorite: Naśiʾ DN, written NA-SI: Niqmi-la-Naśiʾ NI-IQ-MI-LA-NA-SI (Gelb no. 5051), Yadur-Naśiʾ IA-DU-UR-NA-SI (no. 3218); ḏu 'he/she of', written ZU (Gelb 1980, 18)
cognates.Hebrew: nāśîʾ נָשִׂיא 'leader, prince' (HALOT 727): nəśîʾ ʾĕlōhîm נְשִׂיא אֱלֹהִים 'a prince of God' (Gen 23:6), wə-nāśîʾ bə-ʿammǝkā lōʾ tāʾōr וְנָשִׂיא בְעַמְּךָ לֹא תָאֹר (Exod 22:27), nəśîʾê maṭṭôt נְשִׂיאֵי מַטּוֹת (Num 1:16)

entries.note: HT 126a .1 DA-NA-SI · *318 ·, heading the tablet, before A-NA-[·] 1 and SI-DI-JA 1 (GORILA I 217). ḏā 'the one of', as in DA-MI-NU, + Naśiʾ, the Amorite god 'the Exalted One', whom Gelb's names write NA-SI sign for sign: 'He of Naśiʾ', the type of Amorite Zu-dIš-ḫa-ra 'He of Išḫara' (Gelb no. 6598). NA-SI also closes U-MI-NA-SI, the heading of HT 117a and HT 28b. Rival: ḏā-Nasr, the god Nasr of Ḥimyar (Q 71:23; Faris 1952, 10), with r unwritten.

entries.meaning: He of the speckled (flock) (personal name); rival 'He of the head shepherd'

cognates.Ugaritic: ksp d nqdm 'silver of the head shepherds' (KTU 4.369:8); nqd 'head shepherd' (DULAT 630); syll. mu-qa-dī 'grazing rights' (PRU 6 116; UVST NQD¹)
cognates.Hebrew: nōqēd נֹקֵד 'sheep-breeder', of Mesha (2 Kgs 3:4); nāqōd נָקֹד 'speckled' (Gen 30:32)

entries.note: HT 117a .8–9 DA-NE-KU-TI 1, after DA-MI-NU 1 and before KI-DA-RO 1, in the second list headed SA-TA (GORILA I 197). ḏā 'the one of', as in DA-MI-NU, + naquddi, genitive of naqudd- 'speckled', Jacob's flock (Gen 30:32), TI writing di: 'He of the speckled (flock)'. KU-TI answers to -qudd-, as Hebrew nəquddîm (Gen 30:39). Ugaritic joins the same d to nqdm in ksp d nqdm (KTU 4.369:8); Safaitic has the name Nqd (Harding 1971, 597). DA-MI-NU beside it answers to LB da-mi-ni-jo, a shepherd at Knossos. Rivals: nāqidi 'head shepherd' (Ebla na-gi-du-um), whose a-i vowels miss NE-KU; DA-NE + KU-TI, neither part attested alone.

entries.meaning: Old (man's name); rival 'He of the gate'

cognates.Amorite: DAŠUR-UM, DA-ŠU-RU-UM (Gelb 1980 no. 1490); fem. DA-ŠU-RA-TUM (no. 1489); dašurum 'old' (Gelb 1980, 17)
cognates.Arabic: daṯara 'became old', of a man 'overcome by old age' (Lane 851)

entries.note: HT 6a .1–2 KA-PA · DA-TA-RA · TE · NI 15, heading a fig entry (GORILA I 13).
