HT 88 .6 DA-TA-RE 1, in the KI-RO roster before KU-RO 6 (GORILA I 139), the same name. daṯar 'old', the masculine of DA-SE-RA-TE Dašurat: Amorite DA-ŠU-RU-UM beside fem. DA-ŠU-RA-TUM (Gelb nos. 1490, 1489). TA writes ṯ as in TA-RA ṯa(ġ)ra, where DA-SE-RA-TE writes it SE. Rival: ḏā-ṯaġri 'He of the gate', ḏā as in DA-MI-NU + ṯaġr- as in TA-RA, a type with no attested name.

entries.meaning: Good (f.) (personal name)

cognates.Amorite: ṬAJB-AT-UM, DA-BA-TUM, a woman (Gelb 1980 no. 1409); ṭābum, fem. ṭābatum 'good' (Gelb 1980, 35)

entries.note: ZA 10a .4–5 DA-I-PI-TA 1, in a name list after A-DU-KU-MI-NA 1 (GORILA III 169); ZA 8 DA-I-PI-TA 2½, before KA-I-RO 4, by another scribe (GORILA III 165). ṭayyibat- 'good (f.)', fem. of qattil ṭayyib-: DA writes ṭ as in Amorite DA-BA-TUM Ṭaybatum (Gelb no. 1409) and Ebla da-bù 'good'; I writes yyi, the gemination unmarked. LB da-i-pi-ta heads a list of men at Knossos (KN Bk 799), non-Greek (Docs² 537): the name carried into Mycenaean Crete. Rivals: DA-I + PI-TA, DA-I dayyu 'enough' (HT 12) with PI-TA otherwise only inside PI-TA-JA; DA + I-PI-TA, I-PI-TA unattested.

entries.meaning: Timar the Levite (f.), priestess (woman's name and title); rival Tamar + WI-TE

cognates.Hebrew: timmōrāh תִּמֹרָה 'palm figure', carved with cherubim in Solomon's temple (1 Kgs 6:29, 32, 35); PN Tamar תָּמָר (Gen 38:6); Lēwî, named by his mother Leah (Gen 29:34)
cognates.Minaean: lwʾt 'priestess': lwʾtn S¹lmy 'the priestess Salmay', daughter of a priestess (M 333, RES 3357); lwʾtn Mwʾl 'the priestess Mwʾl' and her property (M 358, RES 3697), Dedan (DASI)
cognates.Amorite: TAMAR-U, TA-MA-RU (Gelb 1980 no. 6027)

entries.note: PY R 1 .1–2 TI-MA-RU-WI-TE, a ligature and VIN 90, the only entry (GORILA I 322). TI-MA = Tīmar 'palm', final r unwritten before the l of lēwīt, both in the R-series; the i as Heb. timmōrāh. RU-WI-TE = lēwīt, fem. of lēwī as in DU-RU-WI and U-RE-WI (HT 25a). Name + title, as Minaean lwʾtn S¹lmy 'the priestess Salmay', a priestess's daughter (M 333). Rival: TI-MA-RU Tamar, Amorite TA-MA-RU (Gelb no. 6027), + WI-TE, perhaps √w-d-d as in WI-TE-JA-MU.

entries.meaning: Strength is alive, the arm thrives (personal name); rival Yidu-nešše, Hurrian 'prosperity'

cognates.Eblaite: i-du na-sa, yidu-naḥša 'strength is alive'; i-du na, yidu-na 'our strength' (Pagan 1998, rows 2469, 2466)
cognates.Akkadian: naḫāšu 'to prosper' (CAD N/1 133); naḫšu 'healthy, prosperous', PN Na-aḫ-šum (CAD N/1 142)
cognates.Hurrian: nešše 'prospérité', ne-eš-ši (Laroche, GLH 181), rival

entries.note: HT 13 .5–6 I-DU-NE-SI 5, the last recipient in the VIN · TE list headed KA-U-DE-TA, after TE-KI 27½, KU-ZU-NI 18, DA-SI-ṬA 19, before KU-RO 130½; lines .4–7 over an erasure (GORILA I 27). I-DU = yidu 'arm, strength', as in I-DU-TI; NE-SI = naḥši, ḥ unwritten: the Eblaite name i-du na-sa yidu-naḥša 'strength is alive' word for word. Cf. Amorite E-DU-NA-SA (Gelb no. 1599), unanalysed. Rivals: Hurrian nešše 'prosperity', vowels exact, beside Hurrian TE-KI; Naśiʾ, the god of DA-NA-SI, 'Naśiʾ is strength'.

entries.meaning: (Little) kinsman (personal name, hypocoristic); rival ʾAmaya 'maidservant'

cognates.Ugaritic: PN ʿmy ʿAmmaya (KTU 3.10:9); PN ảmy (KTU 2.76:3), syll. am-ma-ia (RS 88.2158:31') (DULAT 73)
cognates.Amorite: ʾAMAT-AN, A-MA-TA-AN (Gelb 1980 no. 404), rival

entries.note: KH 14 .1 ]RA · A-MA-JA · CYP 6[, whole and undotted between dividers, a cyperus recipient (GORILA III 45). A-MA ʿamma 'kinsman' + hypocoristic -ya, as A-SU-JA, PA-SE-JA: the Ugaritic name ʿmy ʿAmmaya (KTU 3.10:9), syllabic am-ma-ia (DULAT 73). Rival: ʾAmaya, short for ʾamat- 'maidservant' (Ug. amt, DULAT 71), with t lost.

entries.meaning: House of the Throne, the crown estate (institution heading); rival the Hurrian name of PI-TA-KE-SI

cognates.Akkadian: bīt kussî, É.GIŠ.GU.ZA, '1. royal property (real estate), 2. royal service' (CAD K 593); grain to PN ša GIŠ.GU.ZA (CAD K 592)

entries.note: HT 21 PI-TA-KA-SE · TE · GRA 161, then OLE+U 11, OLE+E 3¾, *304 7¾, OLIV 1¼, the heading of a grain and oil account (GORILA I 39). bīt 'house of' + kissē 'throne': Akk. bīt kussî 'royal property' (CAD K 593), and grain booked to persons ša kussî 'belonging to the crown' (CAD K 592). PI writes bi as in DA-I-PI-TA. Its man is PI-TA-KE-SI (HT 87), bīt-kissi with the genitive. Rival: the Hurrian name Pidi-kešḫi.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'El is king'; rival Hurrian Šar-elli

cognates.Amorite: ŚARR-A+ʾIL, ŠAR-RA-DINGIR, Alalakh IV (Gelb 1980 no. 5846)
cognates.Hebrew: Malkîʾēl, the same sentence with mlk (Gen 46:17)
cognates.Hurrian: Šar-elli, the queen ṯryl, syll. šar-e-li (DULAT s.v. ṯryl; Laroche GLH 78), rival

entries.note: HT 20 .4 SA-RE-JU ⅛, after CAPm ⅛ and before TELA, in the list under PA-RO-SU beside KU-MA-JU and QE-KU-RE (GORILA I 36–37). ša-r(ʾ)ē-lu sign for sign: JU writes lu, the nominative of ʾēlu, and RE carries the ē once the ʾ drops at the join. Weak point: Northwest Semitic 'king' is mlk, šarru is the Akkadian and Amorite word, and Hebrew śar is 'prince'. Rival: Hurrian Šar-elli, syll. šar-e-li (DULAT s.v. ṯryl; Laroche GLH 78), whose -li mismatches JU. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Offspring of El'; rival 'Fruit of El'

cognates.Akkadian: pirʾu, pirḫu '1. shoot, 2. offspring' (CAD P 416); Pir-ḫi-ì-lí-šu 'Offspring-of-His-God', wr. Pi-ir-i-ì-lí-šu (CAD P 418)

entries.note: PH 2 .3 PI-RU-E-JU 60, between RA-O-DI-KI 60 and SE-SA-PA₃ 60, under the heading A-SE-TU-*21F 1 (GORILA I 288–289). pirʾ(u) + ʾēlu: the ʾ of pirʾu goes unwritten, and E-JU writes ʾē-lu as in SA-RE-JU. The name type is Akkadian Pirḫi-ilišu 'Offspring-of-His-God', also written Pi-ir-i-ì-lí-šu (CAD P 418). Rival: pir- 'fruit', 'Fruit of El', a type with no attested name. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'She is gracious'

cognates.Amorite: NAʿM-IJA, NA-MI-IA, fem. (Gelb 1980 no. 5001); 3 f. sg. ta- in TA-BNIJ+ʿAŠTAR, TAB-NI-EŠ₄-DAR, fem. (no. 6055)

entries.note: PE 6 .2 TA-NA-MA-JE, alone on the line below the ruling, under .1 I-NA-[?]-TE (Younger). ta-nʿam-ay: ta- the 3 f. sg. prefix of women's names such as Amorite TAB-NI-EŠ₄-DAR (Gelb no. 6055), √n-ʿ-m with the ʿ unwritten, -ay the hypocoristic of Ugaritic nʿmy, nu-ú-ma-ya (DULAT 607). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Calm, at rest'; rival Zakūtu 'pure, innocent'

cognates.Proto-Semitic: *škt 'to be silent, quiet; to rest' (semitic_roots no. 3250)
cognates.Amorite: Ya-ās-qī-iṭ-AN, 'rest' in a name, where Huffmon allows skt 'be calm' (Huffmon, APNM 253)

entries.note: HT 115a .3 SE-KU-TU ½, between NA-*21F-NE-MI-NA 1 and PA-RA-NE 1, a recipient (GORILA I 188–189). šakūt-u, a qatūl adjective of √š-k-t 'be quiet, rest', on primary values. Rival: Zakūtu 'pure, innocent', the Ebla name za-ku-tu and the Neo-Assyrian queen Zakūtu, which needs SE for ḏ where the lexicon writes z with the Z signs. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; CAD S; Huffmon; Pagan 1998

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Pampered'; rival Amorite Banuq

cognates.Amorite: BANUQ-UM, BA-NU-KU-UM, and BANUQ-AN, BA-NU-KA-AN (Gelb 1980 nos. 1132, 1131), rival

entries.note: ZA 14 .4 PA-NU-QE 2, after TU-MI-TI-ZA-SE 45 and before JA-WI[, a recipient among names (GORILA III 181). panūq, a qatūl passive of √p-n-q 'pamper, indulge' on primary values (Heb. pānaq, BDB 819; Syr. paneq 'pamper', Payne Smith 451). Rival: the Amorite name Banuq, BA-NU-KU-UM (Gelb no. 1132), which reads PA as ba. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Second(-born)'; rival Dīnuya

cognates.Amorite: Dīnuya, √d-y-n 'judge' (no. S36), rival

entries.note: HT 115b .2 TI-NU-JA · NU-WI · GRA ½, the frame of side a's *47-NU-RA-JA · I · GRA+BOSm / NU-WI, so a person (GORILA I 191). ṯan-iya, ṯ-n-y 'second' + hypocoristic -ya as in *306-TU-JA on the same tablet. Weak point: TI for ṯ is unestablished, and no Semitic root reads the word on TI's primary value. Rival: Dīnuya, √d-y-n 'judge', which needs TI = d, while the judge words here are written DI (DI-NA). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name (f.), on √ś-y-m 'to place, fix'; rival Šimʿat

cognates.Amorite: ŚIJM-AT-UM, ŠI-MA-TUM, fem.; ŚIJM-AT+DAGAN, ŠI-MA-AT-D-DA-GAN, fem. (Gelb 1980 nos. 5893, 5888)

entries.note: HT 96a .2 SI-MI-TA GRA 5, the first recipient under I-TI-TI-KU-NI · A-PA-RA-NE · A-*123-TE (GORILA I 156). śīmat, the women's name of Amorite ŚIJM-AT-UM, ŠI-MA-TUM (Gelb no. 5893): SI writes ś, which merges into the S series, and MI for ma is a vowel mismatch only. Rival: Hebrew Šimʿat (2 Kgs 12:22), with the ʿ unwritten. One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name; compare Amorite ʾAkkatum

cognates.Amorite: ʾAKK-AT-UM, A-KA-TUM (Gelb 1980 no. 329); fem. ʾAKK-AT-IJA (nos. 327–28); ʾAKK-ATAN-UM, A-KA-TA-A-NU-UM (no. 326)
cognates.Linear B: a-ka-ta-jo, a man's name (PY Eo 269, KN Dv 1331; DMic I 34)

entries.note: KN 32a .2 A-KA-TA, whole at the left edge, broken after (GORILA I 264–65). Sign for sign the Amorite name ʾAKK-AT-UM, A-KA-TUM (Gelb no. 329), with the stem of ʾAKK-AT-IJA and ʾAKK-ATAN-UM; Gelb gives the element no meaning. Linear B a-ka-ta-jo, a man's name at Pylos and Knossos (DMic I 34). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'the Hired' (article ha- + SI-KI-RA); rival haśkira 'he rewarded'

cognates.Hebrew: Śākār, PN (1 Chr 11:35); names with the article, haq-Qôṣ (1 Chr 24:10), hal-Lôḥēš (Neh 3:12)
cognates.Amorite: ʾAškur, DN, AŠ-KU-RA-AN, AŠ-KUR-ᵈIM (Gelb 1980 nos. 947, 950), 'of uncertain origin' (Huffmon, APNM 172), rival

entries.note: KH 20 .1 A-SI-KI-RA · CYP+E ⅓, an entry before cyperus, parallel to ]DU-RE-ZA · CYP+E ½ (GORILA III 51). The article ha- (A, h unwritten, as in A-TU-RI-SI-TI) + SI-KI-RA Śikira 'Hired' (HT 8a), the pair of A-KI-DA-RO beside KI-DA-RO; Hebrew names take the article, haq-Qôṣ (1 Chr 24:10). Rival: haśkira 'he rewarded', an H-stem of the same root, and the Amorite DN ʾAškur (Gelb nos. 947, 950). One witness.

entries.meaning: woven (cloth), a textile entry; rival šittātu 'remainder'

cognates.Ugaritic: štt adj. f. 'spun, woven'; RS Akk. TÚG še-ta-ti (DULAT 839)
cognates.Akkadian: šatû adj. 'woven (cloth)' (CAD Š/2 207); šittātu 'remainder', pl. of šittu A (CAD Š/3 136), rival

entries.note: ZA 20 .2 SI-TE-TU 1, after DU-RE-ZA-SE MI · 4 and before SI-TU 6, in a list ending KU-RA 130 (GORILA III 193). šetātu, the feminine of Ugaritic štt 'spun, woven', written TÚG še-ta-ti at Ras Shamra (DULAT 839), beside SI-TU sūt 'garment' on the next line. Rival: šittātu 'remainder' (CAD Š/3 136). One witness.

entries.meaning: flute; here the flautist, a qualifier after the name TU-QE-NU; rival Hurrian Tulbiya

cognates.Ugaritic: ṯlb 'flute', b knr w b ṯlb 'with the lyre and the flute' (KTU 1.108:4; DULAT 892)
cognates.Akkadian: šulpu 'stalk, a flute or other reed instrument' (CAD Š/3 256)
cognates.Hurrian: tlby, syll. tu-ul-bi-ia, PN (DULAT 856), rival

entries.note: HT 25a .3–4 TU-QE-NU / ZU-JU-PU₂ 1, the pattern of .4–5 DU-RU-WI / I-KI-RA 1: a name at the line end, then a qualifier and one unit (GORILA I 44–45). ṯu-lu-bu sign for sign: ZU writes ṯu, JU lu, PU₂ bu. Ugaritic ṯlb 'flute' (DULAT 892), from Akk. šulpu (CAD Š/3 256). GORILA's tabular copy dots ZU and PU₂, and the left margin beside ZU is abraded. Rival: the Hurrian name tlby, tu-ul-bi-ia (DULAT 856), which needs ZU = tu. One witness.

entries.meaning: store(house), an entry under SI-DA-TE 'provisions'; rival a personal designation in -uwa

cognates.Hebrew: bêt hāʾăsuppîm 'the house of the stores' (1 Chr 26:15); ʾăsuppê 'storehouses of' (Neh 12:25)

entries.note: ARKH 2 .5–6 A-SU-PU-WA 4, the final WA over an erasure, an entry under the heading SI-DA-TE ṣēdat 'provisions', after ZU-*301-SE-DE-*21F-*118 6 (GORILA III 6–7). ʾa-su-pp-ū-a, the ʾăsuppîm 'stores' of 1 Chr 26:15, √ʾ-s-p 'gather'. -PU-WA writes the glide before a final -a, as A-SI-SU-PO-A writes -PO-A (KH 9), and QA-RA₂-WA stands beside QE-RA₂-U. Rival: a personal designation in -uwa, since A-SI-SU-PO-A stands beside the person sign VIR+*307. One witness.

entries.meaning: corvée gang, labour gang (personnel term); the word of MA-ZA

cognates.Proto-Semitic: *mass- 'forced labor, corvée levy, labor gang' (semitic_roots S31)
cognates.Akkadian: massu 'corvée worker': idi LÚ.MEŠ ma-zi 'wages for the corvée workers' (Wiseman Alalakh 246:6); LÚ.MEŠ ma-as-sa.MEŠ (EA 365:14) (CAD M/1 327)

entries.note: HT 10a .8 ME-ZA 3, the last issue of emmer under KU-NI-SU, after DA-RE 16½, U-*325-ZA and DA-RI-DA 8 (GORILA I 20–21); HT 85b ME-ZA 1, among single entries under KI-KI-RA-JA beside QA-*310-I qaynī 'smith' (GORILA I 130–131). Alalakh writes the gang ma-zi and issues it grain (CAD M/1 327), as HT 10a issues ME-ZA emmer. The word of MA-ZA mazza (ZA 10b); ME for ma is a vowel mismatch only. Rival: the Hurrian name mzy, ma-zi-i (DULAT 600).

entries.meaning: partners, the heading of a shares account

cognates.Akkadian: tappû, tappāu 'partner, colleague … business partner'; Bogh. and Alalakh tappûtu (CAD T 184)
cognates.Eblaite: da-ba-u₃ tappāʾu 'comrade', a personal name (Pagan 1998, row 1378)

entries.note: HT 104 .1 TA-PA · *505 ·, heading three entries, DA-KU-SE-NE-TI 45½, I-DU-TI 20½ and PA-DA-SU-TI 29, whose sum is KU-RO 95 (GORILA I 170–171). ta-pa(ʾu) on primary values, the geminate and final ʾu unwritten: the partners in a divided account, as Akk. tappû 'business partner' (CAD T 184). Rival: ṭap 'children' (semitic_roots no. 66), TA writing ṭ. One witness.

entries.meaning: herdsman, shepherd (title on a label)

cognates.Ugaritic: rʿy 'shepherd', in ration lists: rʿym tlt ddm 'shepherds: three cauldronsful (of flour)' (DULAT 716)

entries.note: PH 24, an MM II label, RO-E the only group, whole and undotted (GORILA I 310–311). rō-ʿē, the qōtēl participle as in RO-KE rōkēl, ʿ unwritten: Heb. rōʿeh, Ug. rʿy 'shepherd' (DULAT 716). Rival: rōʾē 'seer' (semitic_roots no. 627). One witness.

entries.meaning: Father (hypocoristic personal name, ʾAdday); rival the kin title ʾad 'father'

cognates.Ugaritic: ʾad 'father', par. um 'mother' (DULAT 16); PN ʾady, syll. a-da-a-a, ad-di-ya (DULAT 23)
cognates.Amorite: /ʔad/ 'lord, father' (Huffmon APNMT 156, apud DULAT 16)

entries.note: ZA 10b .4 A-DE 4, whole, between SA-MA 5 and A-MI-TA ʾamita 'handmaid' 3, in a list that also counts U-*49 ʾummi 'mother' 6 (GORILA III 171). ʾAddē, Ugaritic ʾady, syll. a-da-a-a (DULAT 23): hypocoristic -ay contracted to -ē, the geminate unwritten. Rival: the kin title ʾad 'father' (DULAT 16), as U-*49 is 'mother' in the same list. One witness.

entries.meaning: provisions (section heading); same word as SI-DA-TE ṣēdat

cognates.Hebrew: ṣēdâ 'provisions': lātēt lāhem ṣēdâ laddārek 'to give them provisions for the way' (Gen 42:25); lāqaḥat ṣēdâ lāʿām 'to fetch provisions for the people' (Judg 20:10)

entries.note: KH 7a .4 SE-*305 ·, whole, heading the third section, KU-[·]-KO-E VIR+*313b [ ]18 / CYP+D 1, in the slot of E-NA-SI naḥāši and I-JA-PA-ME · TA-TA (GORILA III 29). ṣē-dā with *305 = da, the live alternate of its sign record, since ḏa gives no root. The heading word of SI-DA-TE ṣēdat (ARKH 2) and MA-SI-DU maṣīdu (HT 43), √ṣ-y-d. Rival: the name of the section's leader. One witness.

entries.meaning: Height (toponym), the bare form of RU-MA-TA rūmatā

cognates.Amorite: RUWM-AT-UM, RU-MA-TUM, personal name (Gelb 1980, no. 5306)

entries.note: HT 64 .2 ]NA 2 RU-MA, whole against the tablet's right edge; only GORILA's normalized box adds the bracket (GORILA I 118–119). rū-ma sign for sign as Heb. Rûmâ (2 Kgs 23:36). The bare form of RU-MA-TA rūmatā 'the Height' (HT 29, HT 99b), √r-w-m. Rival: a personal name of the Amorite RU-MA-TUM type (Gelb 1980, no. 5306). One witness.

entries.meaning: Female (Hurrian personal name); rival the line as a heading, 'female (ones)'

cognates.Hurrian: aštuḫḫi 'féminin', opp. turuḫḫi 'masculin', from ašte 'femme'; instr. aš-tu-uḫ-ḫa-a-i (Laroche GLH 62); Ugaritic alphabetic aštḫ-n (GLH 63); Nuzi ᶠAš-du-uḫ-ḫa-a-a (NPN 37, 206)

entries.note: PH 2 .1 A-SE-TU-*21F 1, the first entry, above RA-O-DI-KI 60, PI-RU-E-JU 60 and SE-SA-PA₃ 60, whole and undotted (GORILA I 288–289). aš-tu-ḫa with *21F = ḫa, SE writing š with the e of ašte: the Nuzi woman's name ᶠAš-du-uḫ-ḫa-a-a (NPN 37), Hurrian aštuḫḫi 'feminine' (Laroche GLH 62). Rivals: the line as a heading, 'female (ones)', if GORILA's 1 is the first stroke of RA (Younger, Linear A Texts); A-SE ʾaššē + an unread TU-*21F. One witness.

entries.meaning: Ḫaru (Hurrian personal name); rival the Semitic name Ḫayru 'Excellent'

cognates.Hurrian: Nuzi Ḫa-a-ru, [Ḫa]-a-ru(m), f. of Alkiya (NPN 55); element ḫaru 'H.? Anatolian?' (NPN 214)
cognates.Eblaite: ha-ru₁₂ ḫayru 'excellent', the rival (Pagan 1998, row 2259); *ḫVyVr- 'be favourable' (semitic_roots no. 988)

entries.note: HT 9a A-RU 4¼, the last recipient of the wine list under SA-RO · TE · VIN, before KU-RO 31¾; HT 49a A-RU 1 in a name list with TU-SU-PU₂ Tešub. ḫa-ru sign for sign, ḫ unwritten as in E-PA-TU Ḫebat: the Nuzi name Ḫa-a-ru (NPN 55), an element NPN marks 'H.? Anatolian?' (NPN 214). Rival: the Eblaite name ha-ru₁₂ ḫayru 'excellent' (Pagan 1998, row 2259), which needs the coda y unwritten.

entries.meaning: Hand (personal name); rivals Yadīn 'he judges', Yadiʿ 'he knows'

cognates.Amorite: JAD-IM, IA-DI-IM (Gelb 1980, no. 3205); JA-DJIN+HADD-U, IA-DI-IN-D-IM (no. 3206), the Yadīn rival

entries.note: PH Wc 39, an MM II roundel from Vano LI, JA-DI on face a, RO rōš on face b, whole and undotted (GORILA II 94). ya-di sign for sign as the Amorite name IA-DI-IM (Gelb 1980, no. 3205), mimation unwritten, *yad- 'hand'. Rivals: Yadīn 'he judges' (Gelb no. 3206 IA-DI-IN-), Yadiʿ 'he knows', each with a final consonant unwritten. Not JA-DI-KI-TU, which divides JA | DI-KI-TU. One witness.

entries.meaning: Tuya (personal name, hypocoristic in -ya); rival Ḏū-Yā 'He of Yah'

cognates.Nuzi: TUIA, Tu-ú-ia, var. Tu-ú?-ia (NPN 156); -tuja 'H. Perhaps a formative in Akituja' (NPN 268)

entries.note: HT 7a .3 DU-JA 4, whole and undotted, under QE-TI · VIR after I-RU-JA 3, a Hurrian -ja hypocoristic (GORILA I 15). tu-ya sign for sign as the Nuzi name Tu-ú-ia (NPN 156), its element -tuja Hurrian (NPN 268). Rival: Ḏū-Yā 'He of Yah', ḏū as in DU-RU-WI ḏu-lēwī and DA-NA-SI Ḏā-Naśiʾ, + JA = Yā(h), as JA-*21F Yāh (HT 28b). One witness.

entries.meaning: lord, master (title, an entry in a KI-RO roster); rival a personal name
entries.note: HT 55a .1 ]KI-RO · MA-RE 1, whole and undotted, the first of single entries owed (GORILA I 106–107). mā-rē, the -MA-RE of JI-NU-MA-RE 'wine-lords'; Ebla mar-a 'the lord' (Pagan 1998, row 3651). Ugaritic has no mrʾ 'lord' (DULAT 562). Rival: a personal name. One witness.

entries.meaning: Šata (personal name, heading the second section); rival śadā '(those of) the field'

cognates.Nuzi: ŠATA, Ša-a-ta, var. Ša-ta, f. of Urḫi-tešup (NPN 126)
cognates.Ugaritic: šd (I) 'open field; field, plot, estate' (DULAT 795), the rival

entries.note: HT 117a .7 SA-TA ·, whole and undotted, heading the second section over five names with 1 each, in the place MA-KA-RI-TE · KI-RO · U-MI-NA-SI holds in the first (GORILA I 197). ša-ta on primary values, sign for sign as the Nuzi name Ša-a-ta, Ša-ta (NPN 126), which NPN leaves unclassed. Rival: śadā '(those of) the field', TA writing d as the T class allows, the root of SA-DI šadī (semitic_roots no. 1804; DULAT 795), since HT 87 and HT 117b put group terms in this slot. One witness.

entries.meaning: Tunu (Hurrian personal name, owner's name on a double axe)

cognates.Hurrian: element tun- 'H.', cf. tu-u-ni, du-u-ni (KUB XXV 44, 45) (NPN 269); Nuzi TUN-TEŠUP, Du-un-te-šu-up, var. Du-un-te-šup, f. of Arbi (NPN 158)

entries.note: KA Zf 1, a bronze double axe from Kardamoutsa (BM 1954,10-20.1), TU and NU · on either side of the shaft hole, whole and undotted (GORILA IV 149). tu-nu on primary values: the Hurrian element tun- (NPN 269), as in the Nuzi name Tun-tešup (NPN 158). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'He is light'; rival mənōrāya 'lampstand (man)'

cognates.Ugaritic: PN nryn, syll. nu-ri-ia-nu, short form nu-ri-ia (DULAT 634)
cognates.Eblaite: su-nu-ri₂ šū-nūrī 'he is my light' (Pagan 1998, row 4282)
cognates.Amorite: NU-RA nūram (Gelb no. 5085)

entries.note: HT 115a .1 *47-NU-RA-JA · I · GRA+BOSm, whole and undotted, the first entry of a palimpsest (GORILA I 189); HT 115b repeats the frame with TI-NU-JA, a person. NU-RA-JA is nūr-aya, as Ugaritic nu-ri-ia beside nu-ri-ia-nu (DULAT 634). With *47 = so: šū 'he', as Ebla su-nu-ri₂ šū-nūrī 'He is my light' (Pagan 1998, row 4282); SO for šū is a vowel mismatch only. Rival: with *47 = mo, mənōrā 'lampstand' (Ug. mnrt, DULAT 558) + -aya. One witness.

entries.meaning: rounds, round cakes of (a commodity); talent; rival the personal name Qaqqaru

cognates.Ugaritic: kkr 'talent' (DULAT 430–31); kkr ḥlb 'a talent of cheese' (DULAT 355)

entries.note: HT 20 .2–.3 QE-KU-RE · DI ½, whole and undotted, the second entry under PA-RO-SU in a list where every entry takes a fraction (GORILA I 37). kik-kᵊrē, a construct before the commodity sign DI, as Hebrew kikkᵊrê kesep 'talents of silver' (2 Kgs 5:5). QE writes k, its listed alternate; Ugarit writes the word with ka₄, the QA sign (DULAT 430–31). Rival: the name Qaqqaru, spelled QA-QA-RU elsewhere at Haghia Triada. One witness.

entries.meaning: rounds of (a commodity); talent
entries.note: HT Wc 3017, a roundel, face a QA-KU-RE · DI-*306 ·, face b CYP+D · *304+PA, all signs whole and undotted (GORILA II 77). The a-vowel form of QE-KU-RE kikkᵊrē, again before a DI- word. QA for k as Ugarit's ka₄-ka₄-r[u] (DULAT 430–31). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'My judgment' (short form of a √d-y-n name); rival the whole group WA-DI-NI, Ugaritic PN wdny

cognates.Amorite: Dīnī-Haddu, DI-NI-A-DU, DI-NA-A-DU (Gelb nos. 1513, 1512)
cognates.Linear A: DI-NA-U Dīnāyu beside WA on HT 16

entries.note: HT Wc 3007 WA-DI-NI, the only text; HT Wc 3008 face a WA · DI-NI, the point after WA in GORILA's transcription, face b RU-JA-TA-DI; all signs whole and undotted (GORILA II 74). WA is the cloth sign, alone on HT Wc 3019 (WA ¼) and KH Wc 2124, and beside DI-NA-U Dīnāyu on HT 16. dī-nī 'my judgment', as Alalakh Dīnī-Haddu, DI-NI-A-DU (Gelb no. 1513). Rival: one word, Ugaritic PN wdny, 'etym. unc.' (DULAT 929). Two witnesses.

entries.meaning: Ḫaluti (woman's name, seal owner); rival ʾālôt 'oaths, curses'

cognates.Nuzi: Ha-lu-ti, var. Ha-lu-u-ti, a woman's name (NPN 51)
cognates.Hebrew: ʾālāh, pl. ʾālôt 'oaths, curses' (Deut 29:20; 30:7; 2 Chr 34:24), the rival

entries.note: CR Zg 4, a steatite reel seal (CMS XII 96), face b A-RO-TE under a lozenge-net relief, face a I-DA-DA, read from the impression, the signs whole (Younger, Linear A Texts, citing Raison–Pope 1994, 242–43). A seal names its owner: Ḫaluti, the Nuzi woman's name Ha-lu-ti (NPN 51), with A for ḫa as in A-RU Ḫaru; TE for ti is a vowel mismatch only. Linear B a-ro-te (PY La 622) is obscure (Killen). Rival: ʾālôt 'oaths, curses' on primary values, the plural of ʾālāh (Deut 29:20; 2 Chr 34:24), whose ō needs the Canaanite shift. One witness.

entries.meaning: Kutukkore (Hurrian personal name)

cognates.Hurrian: Nuzi KUTUKKA, Ku-duq-qa, var. Ku-tu-ug-ga, Ku-tu-uq-qa (NPN 93), the element kutukka H., cf. ku-du-uk-ku KUB XXVII 38 ii 10 (NPN 231; Laroche GLH 150); Kutukkeja, Ku-dug-ge-ia (NPN 93); -re 'H.? … Probably identical with -ri' (NPN 248)

entries.note: ZA 8 .2 KU-TU-KO-RE with a fraction, whole and undotted, an entry in the fig issue headed KI-RA · (GORILA III 165). ku-tu-k(k)o-re: the Hurrian base kutukk- of Nuzi Kutukka (NPN 93), with the suffix -re of Antare and Humere (NPN 248), the geminate unwritten. Base and suffix are each attested, not together. One witness.

entries.meaning: Tati-te, '(Teššup) loved' (Hurrian personal name, hypocoristic)

cognates.Hurrian: tad- 'aimer' (Laroche GLH 248); tat 'H. … Cf. tat, "love," in Tuš.' (NPN 263); Nuzi TATI, Ta-ti, and TATIP-TEŠUP, Ta-ti-ip-te-šup (NPN 150); -te, the 'shortened var.' of -teja, itself the hypocoristic of -tešup (NPN 264)

entries.note: PK 1 .3 TA₂-TI-TE 1, whole and undotted, before O-KA-MI-ZA-SI-I-NA, in a roster of names each counted 1 (GORILA I 281). ta-ti-te: Nuzi Ta-ti beside Tatip-tešup (NPN 150), with -te for -tešup (NPN 264), 'Teššup loved'. TA₂ writes a t-, its vowel open. One witness.

entries.meaning: Akipe-te, '(Teššup) brought' (Hurrian personal name, hypocoristic)

cognates.Hurrian: ag- 'amener, apporter', agi-, agib- in names, Akib-Tešub (Laroche GLH 36); Nuzi Akipei, A-ki-be-e-i, 'Probably < akip-' (NPN 14, 198); [A-ki]p-te-ia, A-ki-te-ia, and A-kip-te-šup (NPN 198); -te, the 'shortened var.' of -teja (NPN 264)

entries.note: KH 10 .3–4 A-KI-PI | E-TE GRA 90, run over the line end and printed as one word in GORILA's normalized line, after I-PA-SA-JA Ipšaja · QA-*118 (GORILA III 36–37). a-ki-pe-te: the Hurrian stem akip- 'brought' of Akip-tešup (Laroche GLH 36), A-KI-PI-E sign for sign as Nuzi Akipei, A-ki-be-e-i (NPN 14), + -te for -teja (NPN 264), as Nuzi [A-ki]p-te-ia (NPN 198). A recipient of grain beside the Hurrian Ipšaja. One witness.

entries.meaning: Ṣubʾu (personal name); rival ṣābu 'workers, troop'

cognates.Amorite: ṢUBUʾ-UM, ZU-BU-U₂-UM and ZU-BU-UM (Gelb 1980, AS 21, 652, nos. 6581–6582)

entries.note: HT 63 .1 SU-PU₂, whole and undotted, the third entry under *305 · TE 1, after KA-TI 1, against the tablet's upper right corner; no numeral survives, and GORILA's normalized line brackets the end, SU-PU₂[ (GORILA I 118–119). ṣu-bu, PU₂ for bu as in DU-PU₂-RE dubur, the final ʾu unwritten as in TA-PA tappāʾu: the Amorite name Ṣubʾu (Gelb 1980, AS 21, 652). Linear B su-po (KN Dc 5812) and su-pu-wo (KN C 912) are men's names at Knossos (DMic II 304). HT 8b .1 SU-PU₂ *188 1 may be the same word before the logogram (SU-PU₂-*188). Rival: ṣābu 'workers, troop' (semitic_roots no. 1333), a collective under the personnel sign *305. One witness.
entries.source: di Mino; Gelb 1980; Pagan 1998; DMic II
